code.title: id: embedded presenter slice 1 — round-panel hello-world presenter (GC9A01 + CST816S, bridge-fed glance card, touch back-channel)
code.body:
## Origin

Filed from the #13630 research (embedded display tier — ESP32 screens as world presenters), per the research-issue rule: build slices are filed from the research, as #13623 was filed from #5971. The research record (doc PR for #13630) carries the full evidence: hardware envelope, rendering path, connectivity tracks, UI model, licensing inventory.

**Not enqueued as a pilot task:** the shortlist is operator-managed (the #13342 pattern) — Felix/Drewry draw slices deliberately. This slice additionally waits on the physical board being on the desk.

## Scope

ESP-IDF firmware for the **Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-1.28** (ESP32-S3R2, GC9A01 round 240×240 over SPI, CST816S touch over I2C) that acts as the first embedded world presenter, bridge track:

1. **Panel + touch bring-up.** `espressif/esp_lcd_gc9a01` for the panel, `espressif/esp_lcd_touch_cst816s` for touch, LVGL 9 via `espressif/esp_lvgl_port`. Partial rendering with double draw buffers in DMA-capable internal SRAM (PSRAM is for assets, not flush buffers — research §2).
2. **Round-safe glance card.** One card from a bounded, test-owned view fixture: a headline state value plus one label line, laid out inside the 170×170 px inscribed safe square of the round panel (research §5). Corners carry no text and no touch targets.
3. **Bridge feed.** WiFi join, then a WebSocket (`espressif/esp_websocket_client`, WSS) to a bridge stub on the LAN. The stub serves the recorded view fixture and logs everything it receives. No real world session in this slice.
4. **Touch back-channel.** The CST816S hardware gesture set mapped to the research record's six-verb vocabulary — tap (select/ack), double-tap (secondary), long-press (back/context), swipe ←/→ (prev/next card), swipe ↑/↓ (within-card) — sent to the bridge as typed input events. Swipe ←/→ switches between at least two fixture cards.
5. **Refresh/power discipline.** Flush only dirty regions; coalesce fixture updates; backlight dims after an idle timeout and the touch interrupt wakes it.

## Acceptance

- `idf.py build` succeeds for target `esp32s3` with the pinned component set; the component manifest is recorded on this issue (it feeds the license checker, #5985).
- On the physical board: the fixture card renders inside the safe square; swipe ←/→ changes cards; every gesture in the vocabulary appears in the bridge stub's log as the corresponding typed input event.
- Hardware evidence attached to this issue (photo or short recording of the board + the bridge log), in the spirit of the #786 transcript harness: behavior on the device, not only a build log.

## Non-goals

- No native iroh on-device (research track 2; gated on its own Rust-on-IDF spike).
- No real world session or world-side view contract — bridge stub + fixture only. The glanceable view contract is separate design work named in the research record's open questions.
- No other panels (ST7789 rectangle and SSD1306 very-small are envelope checks for a later slice).
- No text entry, no pinch, no drag — the vocabulary is the six verbs.

## Components (from the research record's licensing inventory — nothing blocks bundling)

ESP-IDF (Apache-2.0), `espressif/esp_lcd_gc9a01` (Apache-2.0), `espressif/esp_lcd_touch_cst816s` (Apache-2.0), `espressif/esp_lvgl_port` (Apache-2.0), LVGL (MIT), `espressif/esp_websocket_client` (Apache-2.0).

code.title: id: build: presenter-side kitty graphics stills pipeline (from #5971 research)
code.body:
First build slice from the #5971 conversion research (doc/2026-11-23T18-32-12Z_research_id5971_image_video_conversion_tooling/, PR #13621). Parent context: worlds program #5955; assets design #5970; rendering ladder #6011 (closed); capability tiers #786.

## Scope

The presenter-side kitty graphics stills pipeline in pkgs/id (id-worlds presenter surface):

1. Shared converter front half: decode a bounded image asset (by content ID) with the image crate, enforce pixel/size caps, resize to the negotiated cell geometry × probed cell pixel size (geometry treated as probed-with-fallback).
2. Hand-rolled kitty APC encoder per research §6.2: PNG payload (f=100) passthrough when geometry already fits, otherwise re-encode; RGBA+zlib (f=32, o=z) for changing frames; 4096-character chunking with m= continuation; image IDs and placements; direct medium (t=d) only.
3. Gating on the existing capability probe: emit kitty bytes only when the connection's kitty_graphics bit is set AND an a=q query round-trip accepts the payload class — detection alone is not support (research §2.1, §2.3 multiplexer caveat).
4. Boundary held: guests/worlds never supply escape bytes; the encoder is presenter-owned (per doc/2026-11-01_design_id786.md).

## Acceptance

- Golden-fixture tests against a bounded, test-owned image fixture, compared against icat/chafa reference output for the same input.
- Unit tests: chunking boundaries, ID/placement emission, query-gating refusal paths (no bytes emitted when the bit or the query fails).
- No new dependencies beyond the image crate if it is not already in the id workspace graph (report any addition explicitly).
- Symbols/ASCII sampling, sixel, and animation frame sets are NOT this slice (research §7 sequences them after).

## Filing note

Filed by lane felix from the #5971 research pass. Not enqueued with a pilot packet: Felix's shortlist is operator-managed (the #13342 pattern); Felix sequences this against #5970's ratification of the research recommendations.

code.title: id/atlas: define and verify visibility of derived graph and search results per reader profile
code.body:
A proposed cross-host conformance fixture from the ID R&D program (#13240). Decide and test which *derived observations* each reader or replication peer may receive. Scope the test to a small fixed corpus. The change should reuse the existing ID authority, graph and publication semantics.

## Why this needs its own proof

The native implicit-trust exchange sends an inventory summary during the greeting before planning scoped offers. The scoped snapshot design already defines an included-only manifest. Atlas applies result filters and orders FTS candidates with BM25. Authorization of result rows, disclosure of replication metadata and influence of aggregate ranking statistics are different contracts. The present source evidence establishes these boundaries. No production exposure is asserted.

## Acceptance

1. Name each applicable reader/peer class, the metadata it is allowed to receive and the expected behavior for result order, counts, cursor existence and topology. Full-trust replication may admit more than a restricted reader. Record any accepted shared-statistics policy.
2. Specify two small stores with identical material authorized to the reader and a different restricted record. Derive the expected visible nodes, edges and counts independently. Under a strict ranking profile, specify the corpus used for lexical statistics and compare ranking at the same visible cut.
3. Supply deterministic expected observations through one existing query adapter and the intended federation or export adapter. code.title: fleet queue: make packet repair atomic and preserve independent holds
code.body:
# Queue repair transaction — decision packet

2026-11-23. Scope owner pending. Reference branch main at 1f9bc15391ca1c2efa639463a6369392456c27e5. This is a private design for a separate hardening item. Original repair implementation claim: developing-today/code#13191 comment 7098097864. Production receipt: comment 7105556112. Preserve that operator record and leave those rows alone.

## Source premise

In pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/turso_queue/repair.rs, verb_repair performs the Rust work_identity/live_identity_holder check, the queue-scoped dedupe key check, packet reconstruction and validation. It then updates the entire payload conditional on ID/status, performs the event insert separately and re-reads the task. For a blocked row it clears last_error and releases the row when dep_block_active is false. A manual or lane hold can therefore be cleared. This is a source-level possibility, without evidence of production loss.

core.rs::pipeline sends separate execute requests followed by close. exec_batch is a transport roundtrip optimization. Appending COMMIT to a list of independent execute requests could commit a preceding update even if the intervening event insert failed. Current mocked tests intentionally exercise six separate response groups for a successful repair, so their HTTP request counts must change with transaction semantics.

## Proposed implementation

1. Preserve the public repair vocabulary and dry-run reply. Compare eligibility using the existing validator, work_identity, family and PR normalization, and per-queue dedupe key. Keep the existing policy on eligible invalid non-blocked rows.
2. Scope the database read/write transaction to one repair request. Strictly bind statement execution to one Hrana stream until commit or rollback. Keep token, baton, and any service routing private. Use the same provider connection policy as the existing transport. No auth headers forwarded to an unverified origin. No GitHub, secret provider, or other external calls while the writer is held. Bound transaction time by the managed stream lifetime; rollback after validation, contention, storage failure, or refusal.
3. Under that transaction, load the raw target plus latest disposition event (reuse admin.rs::quarantine_select), leases, and eligible identity/key peers. Refuse active ownership or terminal state. Reconcile status, blocked_deps, progress, result, last_error, lease table and latest event. Positive claim-quarantine provenance from quarantine_transition.sql is necessary for automatic release. Repairing the payload under an independent hold preserves its status and reason. If provenance is missing, retain the block and report that a separate release requires human/lane reconciliation.
4. Preserve row identity and unrelated fields. Update the dedupe stamp only after a successful check and validation. Write a single repaired event on the same transaction and expose the committed event ID. Return the row captured in the transaction after commit. A dropped commit response is ambiguous: reconcile by stable operation identity/receipt, never silently replay against a new generation of the task. Keep the existing no_defects result for genuinely unrelated callers.
5. Reuse repair.rs fixtures alongside a disposable rusqlite-backed Hrana test double or isolated compatible server. Add actual transaction-state and multi-connection tests; statement-string matches alone do not establish rollback. No production DB, network probes or live work IDs in these oracles.

| Input or fault | Observable result |
|---|---|
| Blocked claim-quarantine with provenance, no competing holder or lease | Exactly one valid packet, released to queued, exactly one matching event |
| Active manual/lane/dependency hold, including fossil quarantine error | Valid packet can be restored while status, recorded reason and all blocker metadata survive |
| Claimed/terminal row, stale worker or live lease despite unclaimed status | Refusal with no changed metadata/event |
| Independent same-status payload edit during repair | The serial ordering preserves the other committed edit or repair refuses; no overwrite |
| New valid peer with same work identity in another queue or same key in same queue | Check runs at writer state; second conflicting repair cannot produce a false attestation |
| Event insert rejected by a disposable DB trigger, or transport fails before commit | Original payload, status and event count survive |
| Commit succeeds and response is lost | Retry retrieves existing committed result or reports ambiguity with a stable reconciliation reference; no second mutation |
| Dry run, no defects or refused malformed packet | No task mutation or durable audit event |

## Verification route

Target the immutable candidate ref via fleet queue dispatch on an included GitHub runner with queue-broker features and narrow tests. Run the same-change reference and queue-lifecycle book checks. Capture provider run and attempt, test count, broker API response and independent disposable table observations. Release publication and deployment are separate from merging. An offline SQLite test cannot establish managed Turso failover durability.

Property/scenario coverage at the fold layer is deep (`pkgs/id/crates/id-events/src/groups/tests.rs`, `voiding_scenarios.rs`, `membership_properties.rs`, …), but the actual `id delegate` / `id revoke` commands have only 2 CLI-level tests (`pkgs/id/tests/cli_delegation.rs`, verified 2026-11-23 against origin/main).

Add CLI scenario tests for the four named scenarios, exercising the real commands end to end:

1. **Attenuation refusal** — delegating a scope the grantor does not hold at that position is refused.
2. **Veto by non-manager refusal** — `id revoke` by an account without Manage (and not the grant's grantor, unless/until the #6379 F2 implementation changes that rule) is refused.
3. **Cross-world cap** — a cross-world grant above Write, or naming an empty world, is refused.
4. **Device scope cap** — a device acting for an account above its device scope is refused.

code.title: id: verify the ingest funnel and key custody end to end (#6379 F3+F4)
code.body:
Stage-2 verification packet for #6379 (findings F3 + F4 from the stage-1 audit, task 14441; routed by the 2026-11-17 triage, task 18481). Verification only — any bypass or custody defect found is filed separately and treated as fail-closed until fixed; do not fix in this packet.

## F3 — the fold trusts ingested events; verify the funnel is total

`pkgs/id/crates/id-events/src/groups/*` contains no signature verification; authenticity rests entirely on every write path funnelling through event-store ingest (`pkgs/id/crates/id-events/src/event_store/ingest.rs`, `verify_strict`; bytes that do not verify are refused and change nothing).

Trace end to end, per path, whether any route writes the group log bypassing ingest verification:
- local CLI writes (`id-cli` commands),
- sync ingest (`event_store/sync.rs`),
- hosted ingest (`pkgs/id/src/hosted_ingest.rs` and the hosted bridge surface),
- relay/envelope delivery paths.

Acceptance: a per-path verdict recorded on this issue (funnels through ingest / bypasses — with the bypass's code path named). A confirmed bypass is a separate security issue, filed in the same pass.

## F4 — key custody at the account boundary

The CLI identity is the local keypair file (`load_or_create_keypair`, now in `pkgs/id/crates/id-store/src/store.rs`; creation goes through `write_private_file` + `restrict_key_permissions` — verify the actual mode applied, on create and on load of a pre-existing loose file, incl. non-Unix behaviour). Also check the hosted/serve path's key handling (which key signs hosted actions, where it lives, what mode).

Acceptance: recorded verdict per surface (CLI create, CLI load-existing, hosted/serve) with the observed file mode or custody fact for each.

code.title: id: implement Notion importer slice 5: fidelity report + incremental re-import (design #6436)
code.body:
Implementation slice 5 of the Notion importer design for #6436, landed as `doc/2026-11-10_design_id6436.md` (PR #8416, amended PR #8558). Parent implementation issue: #6513. Depends on slices 2–4.

Scope (design §6.2, §6.4, §7; Implementation slicing item 5):

- Fidelity report generation (§6.4): persisted with the manifest; objects by outcome (clean / degraded / failed / skipped) with counts and per-item reasons for every non-clean item; every §2.5 degradation class with counts; externalised links and relations; missing resources; comments coverage; access-metadata observations; re-import conflicts. The report's invariant: every source object in the inventory is accounted for exactly once — a report that does not reconcile to the inventory is a failed import.
- Incremental re-import (§6.2): full inventory re-crawl (including re-enumeration of every database's data sources), manifest diff in exactly the categories new / changed / unchanged / missing-from-source, importing only new/changed objects. Changed = `last_edited_time` advanced OR content hash differs; database schema diffs are computed per data source, never per database. Source-side deletions are reported only (§6 invariant 3); a re-import that finds locally-edited content creates its revision alongside and names the conflict (§6 invariant 2) — the importer never overwrites, deletes, or tombstones to make the source win.
- Read-authority compliance check (§7): imported objects carry no importer-specific authority state and the import creates no grants of any kind — including for pages the source had published to the web. Notion sharing facts appear only as provenance claims and in the report's access section.
- Corpus completion and the §8 acceptance harness: the full decidable check list run over the completed corpus, including the failure-injection cases (mid-content kill + resume per §6.3, export-only degraded run).

Acceptance:

- Design §8 checks 1–8 pass against the corpus (each names its oracle in §8).
- A repeat import of an unchanged workspace reports 0 creates / 0 updates (check 3).
- No imported object is readable beyond the ruled resolution order, and the published-to-web fixture page has no grant created by the import (check 5).
- Closing this slice completes the #6513 acceptance criteria; #6513 closes on this slice's done check, with any live-workspace verification leg named separately (it is gated on the Drew-owned editions/evaluation-budget answers recorded in #6513).

code.title: id: implement Notion importer slice 4: comments + degradation completion + export reader (design #6436)
code.body:
Implementation slice 4 of the Notion importer design for #6436, landed as `doc/2026-11-10_design_id6436.md` (PR #8416, amended PR #8558). Parent implementation issue: #6513. Depends on slices 2–3.

Scope (design §1.3, §2.4, §2.5; Implementation slicing item 4):

- Comment claims (§2.4): discussion comments become comment claims on the note (block-anchored comments name the block identity), with author recorded as Notion user provenance (ID + display name), timestamp, and body blob; replies chain by manifest-recorded parent comment ID; resolved discussions carry the resolution as a recorded provenance fact. Comments the acquisition path cannot see are absent and counted per page — never silently partial within a page the importer claims to have covered.
- Degradation completion (§2.5): the full block table — toggle / callout / columns / simple table / equation structure preserved with presentation attributes dropped-and-counted per attribute; embeds degraded to URL + link reference; synced blocks imported at the source block's page and replaced by a typed reference at every referencing page; table of contents, breadcrumb, template button, Notion AI blocks and unknown/future block types preserved as verbatim source blobs with provenance claims.
- Export-bundle reader (hybrid mode, §1.3; #6513 scope step 5): parse a workspace export (Markdown+CSV flavour) and normalize it into the same pipeline as the API path; content matched to API inventory by UUID where the flavour carries it, otherwise by recorded title+path matching with every uncertain match named for the fidelity report. Export-only runs are the design's degraded mode: identity falls back to content-hash + path keys and the degradation is headlined, not hidden.

Acceptance:

- Design §8 check 7: every fixture comment the acquisition path could see exists as a claim on the expected note; every page it could not is listed in the comments-coverage accounting.
- Design §8 check 4: for every degradation class in §2.5's table present in the corpus, the counted total equals the corpus's known count.
- Export-only run over the same corpus asserts the degraded mode's weaker guarantees as such (§1.3, §8 failure-injection list).

code.title: id: implement Notion importer slice 3: databases — schema claims, relations, rollups (design #6436)
code.body:
Implementation slice 3 of the Notion importer design for #6436, landed as `doc/2026-11-10_design_id6436.md` (PR #8416, amended PR #8558). Parent implementation issue: #6513. Depends on slice 2 (page/block core + link rewriting + files).

Scope (design §2.2, §3; Implementation slicing item 3):

- Database notes: one note per database (its own content blocks via slice 2's core), with each data source's schema recorded as provenance claims on the database note, scoped by `data_source_id` — two sources' claims are never merged, even where property names collide.
- Row notes: one note per row page, a typed reference to the database note, and property values recorded as claims interpreted against the schema of the data source the row was read from.
- Relations as typed references with the design's canonical identity: a relation's reference type is keyed by (data source, property), never by parent database; a two-way (dual) relation's canonical type is the unordered pair of both sides' (data_source_id, property_id) joined via `dual_property.synced_property_id`, canonical direction = the side that sorts first; relation values resolve only against rows of the schema's target data source, and values naming rows outside the import set are recorded as provenance claims and counted externalised.
- Rollups and formulas as derived-value provenance claims: computed display value plus the verbatim definition and its inputs, never as silently-authoritative values.
- System properties (unique ID, created/last-edited time and by) as provenance claims; button / verification / Notion AI properties named in accounting, not imported as values.
- A data source that moved databases since the previous import: schema claims recorded on the new database note, prior claims superseded (kept in history), row membership references updated, row identity unchanged (§6.1).

Acceptance:

- Offline fixture tests over the multi-source fixture database (design §8 check 8): manifest records both `data_source_id`s under the one database note; the two sources' schema claims are disjoint (the colliding property name appears once per source with each source's type); every row's claims validate against its own source's schema and no row's against the other's; the relation defined in only one source produces typed references for rows of that source only, resolving to rows of its target data source.
- Design §8 check 2, relation subset: every corpus relation is either a typed reference between the expected notes or listed externalised with the expected reason.

code.title: Code rename: replace identifier-bound person-name identifiers with role terms
code.body:
# Code rename: replace identifier-bound person-name identifiers with role terms

## Why

The prose sweep in #13392 replaced person-name references in the books and living references with role terms ("the user's X", "needs user", "needs decision", "needs orchestrator", "needs operator"). A set of names could not be rewritten in prose because they are literal code identifiers and quoted runtime strings — the books must keep matching the shipped surface until the code itself is renamed. This issue covers that code side.

## Identifier-bound names (from the #13392 census)

- `drew-cli` — CLI identity name, and the bridge address `drew`
- "Needs-drew payload" label
- `needs_drew` — field / module / payload name
- `drew_decision` — reason class
- The quoted phrase `"awaiting drew"`
- Atlas requester kind `drew` — a stored enum value, distinct from `user` (weights in the census record: drew 1.0, user 1.0, agent 0.25, anonymous 0.1)
- Atlas `reference/mcp.md` verbatim MCP instruction strings that name these identifiers

## Warning: persisted values — alias / migration, never a blind swap

Several of these are stored / persisted values, not just source identifiers:

- The atlas requester kind `drew` is a stored enum in persisted data.
- `needs_drew`, `drew_decision`, and the payload label appear in serialized payloads and stored records.
- The bridge address `drew` and the `drew-cli` identity may appear in configuration, stored sessions, and external references.

Renaming therefore needs an alias / migration plan for each name: accept the old value on read, write the new value, and migrate or dual-read stored data until the old values are gone. A blind find-and-replace in source will break stored data, in-flight payloads, and any external caller still using the old names.

## Scope

- Inventory every occurrence of the names above in code, config, and serialized formats (the #13392 census counted ~2,400 non-markdown lines repo-wide dominated by these identifiers).
- Propose the replacement role terms per identifier, consistent with the prose sweep (user / operator / orchestrator as context fits).
- Land the rename with aliases / migrations for persisted values, with tests covering old-value reads.
- Only after this lands, update the books and living references that quote these identifiers to match the new surface (those quoted occurrences were deliberately left untouched by #13392).

## Out of scope

- Prose references — already handled by #13392.
- Dated historical records — history is not rewritten.

code.title: Rename sensitivity ladder identifiers in code to canonical public/internal/private/sensitive (aliases/migration, not a blind swap)
code.body:
# Rename the sensitivity ladder identifiers in code to the canonical ladder (public < internal < private < sensitive)

## Why

The sensitivity ladder's canonical names were corrected on 2026-11-23. The classes are:

**`public < internal < private < sensitive`**

The old names are retired. They map onto the canonical rungs in order:

| Retired name (code today) | Canonical name |
|---|---|
| `shareable` | `public` |
| `personal` | `internal` |
| `local-only` | `private` |
| `secret-bearing` | `sensitive` |

Note: the retired `local-only` never meant "stored on the local laptop"; it was a rung name only.

## Scope of this issue: the CODE rename (not the prose sweep)

A companion prose sweep (living docs + the atlas/fleet/id books) is being done separately by Lane OA11 and will link its PR here. This issue owns the identifier rename in code, which must NOT be done as a blind search-and-replace, per the persisted-value caveat below.

## Code-surface inventory (measured 2026-11-23, `git grep -iE 'shareable|local-only|secret-bearing'` on main)

- `pkgs/atlas-search` (excluding its book): 33 files, ~379 lines. Includes the Rust `Sensitivity` enum (`Shareable / Personal / LocalOnly / SecretBearing`), the `SENS_ORDER` ordering in atlas-core, serde spellings, the `--max-sensitivity` CLI surface, service per-identity ceiling caps, disclosure-context ceilings, and the Worker/MCP pinned ceiling strings.
- `pkgs/id` (excluding its book): ~19 files, ~51 lines. (The id book's `local-only` occurrences are the ordinary English "runs only locally / not deployed" sense, not the ladder — not part of this rename.)
- `pkgs/fleet` (excluding its book): ~13 files, ~62 lines, including the `fleet search` `--max-sensitivity` pass-through and `docs/verbs.md`.
- `pkgs/mcpx`: ~6 code files, ~7 lines. (The mcpx book has zero ladder occurrences; its docs' `shareable`/`local-only` hits are ordinary prose and an upstream MCP spec identifier — not part of this rename.)
- Elsewhere: `pkgs/note-submission` (src + tests), `pm-stack/aggregator` (`server.ts`, `views.ts`, `views.test.ts`), `pkgs/gh-fleet/default.nix`, `nixos/home/atlas-backup.sh`, `nixos/home/laptop-repo-keeper.test.sh`.

## Persisted-serde caveat — stored values need alias/migration handling, never a blind swap

The retired strings are not just identifiers; they are stored and exchanged values:

- Scheme-1.0 `sensitivity` column labels in Atlas staging databases, and the published `chunks` / `session_labels` sensitivity labels in the corpus databases (at the frozen census: 100,060 `personal`, 6,941 `local-only`, 638 `secret-bearing` chunk labels).
- Per-identity ceiling configuration (e.g. the service's named client caps) and user config carrying ceiling values.
- CLI values: `--max-sensitivity` accepted spellings and its `personal` default, on `atlas-search`, `fleet search`, and related verbs; segment-file sensitivity names accepted by `atlas-stage`.
- Wire/JSON values: search envelope fields such as `max_sensitivity` and per-hit `sensitivity`, and the MCP tool description strings that quote the ceiling verbatim.

A rename therefore needs a compatibility design before any swap: serde aliases (accept old, emit new) or an explicit data migration for stored labels, a dual-accept window for CLI/config values, and a decided cutover for emitted JSON. Renaming the Rust enum variants and their serde spellings in one step would make existing databases, configs, and scripts unreadable.

## Open question — one ladder or two (decision still owed; do not decide inside the rename PR)

The docs currently present the corpus tiers (`public` / `internal` / `secret`) and the four-rung ceiling ladder as "two namings, one ladder" (see the atlas book glossary), with the working correspondence `shareable -> public`, `personal + local-only -> internal`, `secret-bearing -> secret`. After this rename, the ceiling ladder (`public < internal < private < sensitive`) will share the names `public` and `internal` with the tier vocabulary. Whether the end state is one unified ladder or two distinct vocabularies that happen to share two rung names is a deliberate decision that is still owed by the design owner. This issue records the question; the rename must not silently settle it.

## Acceptance shape (for whoever implements)

- [ ] Compatibility design recorded (aliases vs migration, per surface above).
- [ ] Code identifiers, enum variants, and CLI spellings renamed with the compatibility layer in place.
- [ ] Stored-label migration or alias-read verified against a copy of a staging + publish database.
- [ ] Books/reference updated to the new literal spellings in the same change (they currently document the legacy spellings as the code's values).

code.title: PM platform on Cloudflare: what is left
code.body:
What is left for the PM platform to run from Cloudflare and the app alone, after the work of 2026-11-23. The laptop is one machine among however many there are; nothing below should need it, except where a thing is a machine's by its nature (its own units, its own sessions).

**In service today.** The app is served by Cloudflare and works with every machine away. Cloudflare reads the board, prompts, pull requests, ranked issues, the queue, roadmaps, bugs, intake and releases itself, and does these at once: ask, reply, close a prompt, comment, rank, move a task, merge, start a deploy, file a note, a bug or a change. The app works with no connection and sends what was done once, in order, when it is back. Machines says what each machine can do and what waits for one. Platform lists every Worker.

**Cloudflare does the core by itself**

- [ ] #13489 its own GitHub allowance, so the core does not stop when the fleet is busy (half done in #13570: unchanged lists cost nothing, and GitHub's time is kept to; its own identity is what is left)
- [ ] #13490 file, cancel and unblock a queue task with no machine
- [ ] #13491 questions, what needs you and sessions with no machine
- [ ] #13502 a message to an agent with no machine
- [ ] #13398 an older action held for a machine against a newer one the edge does itself
- [ ] #13831 the edge does what it holds for a machine itself, once it can

**The laptop as one machine among several**

- [ ] #13492 enrol a second machine under its own key; send each action to one that can do it
- [ ] #13833 the laptop's console stopped following main on 2026-11-23; a machine on other code than Cloudflare should be said on the Machines screen

**One platform**

- [ ] #13493 deploy the twelve hand-deployed Workers from Actions
- [ ] #13494 the edge checks each Worker is in service and which version it runs
- [ ] #13495 the hostname, its sign-in and its route applied from Actions, not from the laptop
- [ ] #13496 see and manage the stores (Turso) from the app
- [ ] #13503 fold the decision events and the queue's alert into the PM console

**The plan's pages**

- [ ] #13497 roadmap files for fleet and atlas (done in #13828); the platform makes roadmap changes itself (not started)

**Kept true**

- [x] #13498 type-check the console before it is deployed
- [x] #13499 the signed-in flows and the alarm, in the real Worker runtime
- [ ] #13500 the Android app with no connection, on a device in CI
- [ ] #13501 offline: what is left to harden

Design record: `doc/2026-11-23T06-50-00Z_architecture_pm_platform_cloudflare_core/`. The one-platform plan: `pm-stack/platform/README.md`.

code.title: Platform: fold the decision events and the queue's alert into the PM console
code.body:
**Today.** Three Workers hold state about the same thing, the fleet's work as the owner sees it: the PM console (the board, prompts, what is held), `decision-events` (each decision-set event, once), and `queue-transport-alert` (whether the queue's broker answers, every ten minutes). Each has its own Durable Object, its own deploy and its own way of telling the owner something: the console's notifications, a D1 table nobody reads at the edge, an alert of its own.

**What done looks like.**

- The queue's alert becomes one of the console's notifications: the console's own alarm does the probe, and the separate Worker and its queue are retired. One place decides what reaches the owner's phone.
- Decision events are kept where the console can read them, so open questions are read at the edge with no machine (see the issue on questions). Either the console takes the events itself, or it binds to `decision-events` as a service.
- `pm-stack/platform/workers.json` loses the rows that are retired, and the Platform screen with them.
- Nothing is merged before it is deployed from Actions with a way back (the issue on deploys), so that a merge that goes wrong can be undone.

Design record: `doc/2026-11-23T06-50-00Z_architecture_pm_platform_cloudflare_core/`.

code.title: Send a message to an agent from Cloudflare with no machine
code.body:
**Today.** `message.send` from the app is a machine's: it is relayed to the laptop, which runs the fleet binary to deliver it, and it is held while the laptop is away. The agents list on the Agents screen is the laptop's report too. Yet the messages themselves already pass through a Worker on the same account (`message-bridge`), and the fleet's registry of agents is in the store.

**What done looks like.**

- The edge delivers a message itself: through the message bridge (a service binding, once it is deployed from Actions) or by the write the fleet binary makes, with the fleet's rules for who may be addressed.
- The Agents screen reads who is registered and when each was last seen from the store, at the edge.
- With no machine reporting, a message sent from the app is delivered, and is not listed under "Waiting for a machine".

code.title: pm-console offline: what is left to harden
code.body:
What the offline work (#13287) leaves as it is, each on its own small.

- **The platform does not check how old an action is.** A merge, a deploy, a cancel, an unblock or a unit action older than ten minutes is kept back by the device until the owner confirms. A device with a wrong clock, or another client, is not held to that. The act route could refuse one of those kinds whose `at` is too old unless it says `sure`.
- **Copies on the device are not encrypted** beyond what the device does itself. What the app showed and what the owner did sit in the browser's cache and database in the clear. Signing out by hand clears the copies of what was read; it does not clear what was done and not yet sent (on purpose: it would be lost).
- **Background Sync is Chrome's.** In Safari and Firefox what is kept is sent when the app is next opened. A periodic try from an open page covers the case of the app left open in the background; nothing covers the app closed.
- **A screen never visited has no copy** until it is visited or "Keep a copy of every screen now" is pressed. Keeping them all in the background after sign-in, on Wi-Fi, would close that.
- **What is kept is kept per browser.** The same owner on two devices sees two lists. The platform's record of what was done is the shared one.

Design record: `doc/2026-11-23T06-50-00Z_architecture_pm_platform_cloudflare_core/`.

It was not checked on Android: a real phone with no signal, the app opened from its icon, the widget, Background Sync with the app swiped away.

**What done looks like.**

- Token expiry is shown, and a token close to running out raises a notification.
- A migration is run from the app by starting its workflow (as a deploy is started today), and the screen shows the last run.

code.title: Platform: the hostname, its sign-in and its route are applied from Actions, not from the laptop
code.body:
**Today.** `pm-stack/console/scripts/expose.py`, run on the laptop by a timer, is what points `pm.security.cab` at the Worker, keeps the Cloudflare Access application and its policy in place, and hands the Worker its two tokens. If the laptop is gone for good, none of that can be changed or repaired from anywhere else.

**What done looks like.**

- The route, the Access application and its policy, and the Worker's settings are described in the repository and applied by a workflow (Terraform under `infra/`, or the API calls `expose.py` makes, moved into the deploy), with the repository's own Cloudflare secret.
- The Worker's two tokens are set by that workflow from the repository's secret store, and rotated by running it. `expose.py --edge-direct` stops uploading them; the switch in the app turns the capability off without a machine.
- `expose.py` keeps only what is the laptop's own: the tunnel to itself.
- The Cloudflare screen in the app says where each of these was last applied from and when.

code.title: Platform: the edge checks each Worker is in service and which version it runs
code.body:
**Today.** Whether a Worker is in service is written in `pm-stack/platform/workers.json` by hand, from asking each address from outside on a given day (`checked`). The Platform screen says when that was. The edge does not check, because a Worker cannot ask another Worker on the same account by its public address (it is answered with error 1042) without the `global_fetch_strictly_public` setting, and that setting also changes how the console reaches the laptop through the tunnel.

**What done looks like.**

- Each Worker in service answers `GET /version` (or says its version in a health answer) with no sign-in: the commit it was deployed from.
- The edge asks each one on a schedule and keeps the answer: in service or not, the version, when it was asked. The Platform screen shows that in place of the hand-written state, and a Worker that stops answering raises a notification.
- How the edge reaches them is decided and tested first: service bindings to each (no public hop, and no setting to change), or the setting with a test in the real runtime that the relay to the laptop still works (`scripts/edge-smoke.ts`).

Design record: `doc/2026-11-23T06-50-00Z_architecture_pm_platform_cloudflare_core/`.

code.title: Platform: deploy the twelve hand-deployed Workers from Actions, each with a check and a way back
code.body:
**Today.** Fourteen Workers are in service. Two are deployed from Actions (the PM console, the pkarr door). Twelve were deployed by running `wrangler deploy` on a machine: nothing in the repository says which commit each runs, and none can be put back from the app. They are listed in `pm-stack/platform/workers.json` with `"deploy": "by hand"`, and More, Platform shows each as "Deployed by hand, from a machine".

**What done looks like, for each.** As `pm-stack/platform/README.md` sets out: a push to main that touches it uploads a version, puts it in service, asks it which version it is, and puts the previous one back if it does not answer as the new one; its secrets are named in the repository and set by the deploy; `workers.json` says `"deploy": "actions"` with its workflow, and the Platform screen shows its last deploy. The PM console's release (`pm-stack/console/edge/release.mjs`) is the pattern: make it a shared step, do not copy it twelve times.

Each one first needs its secrets and bindings written down (its README or wrangler file), and a rehearsal on a scratch name, before its real deploy is switched over.

- [ ] `message-bridge` (`pkgs/message-bridge/worker`, custom domain `bridge.security.cab`, a Durable Object)
- [ ] `decision-events` (`pm-stack/decision-events-worker`, D1 and a Durable Object)
- [ ] `queue-transport-alert` (`pkgs/queue-transport-alert/worker`, a queue, a Durable Object, a cron)
- [ ] `github-ci` (`pkgs/github-ci/worker`, the webhook secret, the store's token)
- [ ] `voice-line` (`pm-stack/voice-line-worker`, a Durable Object)
- [ ] `muse-agent-handoff` (`scripts/muse/handoff/worker`, a Durable Object)
- [ ] `desktop-commander` (`pkgs/desktop-commander/worker`)

code.title: Machines: enrol a second machine under its own key, send each action to one that can do it
code.body:
**Today.** A machine says what it is called and what it can do in each report, and More, Machines shows it (#13471). But only one machine can report: the edge holds one key, learned by asking the machine through the tunnel, and relays every action it does not do itself to that one address.

**What done looks like.**

- A second machine is enrolled from the app: it shows a code, the owner approves it on the Machines screen (as a phone is linked today), and the edge then takes reports under its key. A machine can be removed there too.
- The edge keeps each machine's sections apart and says which machine each came from. Where two report the same section, the screen says whose it is showing.
- An action that needs a machine goes to one that says it can do it. A machine with no address the edge can reach (no tunnel) takes its actions with the answer to its next report, as held actions are taken today.
- What is held is held for a machine that can do it, and Machines shows it under that machine.
- When no connected machine says it can do a kind, the edge answers at once that none can, and does not relay blind.
- The protocol change is in `pm-stack/console/src/edge-proto.ts`; reports from a machine older than the change still work.

Design record: `doc/2026-11-23T06-50-00Z_architecture_pm_platform_cloudflare_core/`.

code.title: Questions, what needs you, and sessions: readable and answerable with no machine
code.body:
**Today.** Four sections of the app are a machine's report: sessions, questions (and their count), what needs you (the census), and the dashboard's pages. With the laptop away they are as old as its last report, and an answer to a question is held until it is back. Machines (More, Machines) lists exactly these under "Only it reports".

**What done looks like.** For each, either the edge reads it from where it lives, or the screen says plainly that it is a machine's and why.

- **What needs you**: these are GitHub issues by label in the repositories the config names (`needsRepos`). The edge can read them with the token it has, like the owner's prompts. `need.comment` is already done at the edge.
- **Questions**: decision sets live with the aggregator on the laptop and their events already go to the `decision-events` Worker. Reading open questions and recording an answer at the edge needs that Worker (or its store) to be the place they are read from. See the one-platform plan (`pm-stack/platform/README.md`).
- **Sessions**: what each lane is doing is only known to the machine running it. Each machine reports its own; with more than one machine the screen shows them by machine.
- Tests with the machine away for each section the edge takes over.

Design record: `doc/2026-11-23T06-50-00Z_architecture_pm_platform_cloudflare_core/`.

code.title: Queue: file, cancel and unblock a task from Cloudflare with no machine
code.body:
**Today.** The edge files the issue of a prompt, a note or a bug itself, but the queue task that makes the fleet pick it up is a machine's: it is held (`prompt.enqueue`, `triage.enqueue`) until a machine reports and files it through the fleet binary. Cancelling and unblocking a task are a machine's too and are refused while none can be reached. So with the laptop away a prompt is filed and nobody works on it.

**Why it was left.** Filing a task is the fleet binary's: its keys, its de-duplication and its events are not something to copy into SQL at the edge.

**What done looks like.**

- A task can be filed, cancelled and unblocked with no machine reporting, by the same rules the fleet binary applies. The route the repository already points at is the fleet's hosted front door (`pkgs/fleet/hosted-worker`, its queue door; #12583 and the issues beside it), which is local-only today; when it is deployed the edge calls it. The alternative is the fleet's rules as a library both use.
- With no machine reporting, a prompt sent from the app has its queue task within a minute, and Machines, "Waiting for a machine" stays empty for it.
- `task.cancel` and `task.unblock` are done at the edge and say so on the Cloudflare screen.
- Tests in `pm-stack/console/test/edge.test.ts` for each, with the machine away.

Design record: `doc/2026-11-23T06-50-00Z_architecture_pm_platform_cloudflare_core/`.

code.title: pm-console edge: its own GitHub allowance, so the core does not stop when the fleet is busy
code.body:
**Today.** The edge reads pull requests, ranked issues and the owner's prompts from GitHub with the repository automation token, which is the fleet's token on the owner's account. GitHub's hourly allowance is per account. On 2026-11-23 at about 16:22Z the edge's read of pull requests failed with "API rate limit exceeded for user ID 11225574": the fleet had used the hour. The edge treats that as "one too many just now", hands the read to a machine for five minutes (whose token is the same account, so it fails too), and asks again. Nothing is lost, but the core is not readable until the hour turns.

**What done looks like.**

- The edge's reads and writes of GitHub do not draw on the allowance agents draw on. Two ways, not exclusive:
  1. Conditional requests. The edge keeps each list's `ETag` and sends `If-None-Match`; an unchanged list answers 304 and costs nothing against the allowance. This needs no new identity and can be done now in `ghApi` (`pm-stack/console/edge/src/direct.ts`), with the kept answer per address held in the Durable Object.
  2. An installation token of a GitHub App of its own, which has its own allowance. This is a new identity on the account and wants the owner's say-so before it is made.
- When the allowance is used up all the same, the app says so in those words on the screens it affects ("GitHub's hourly allowance for the account is used up; this is as of HH:MM"), not "could not be read".
- A test in `test/direct.test.ts` for the conditional read (200 then 304 returns the kept answer; a changed list replaces it), and one in `test/edge.test.ts` that a limited read shows the last good copy with its age.

Design record: `doc/2026-11-23T06-50-00Z_architecture_pm_platform_cloudflare_core/`.

code.title: pm-stack notifications Phase 2 step 4: cron narrowing to the daily DO canary (#8569)
code.body:
## Phase 2 step 4 — cron narrowing to the daily DO canary (of #8569)

Parent: #8569. Design of record: `doc/2026-11-17_design_pm8569_notifications_phase2.md` §5 step 4 + the parent design's §8. Steps 1–3 land first; step 1's deploy leg must be live (heartbeats flowing) before the page checks retire — the DO owns them only once it is actually receiving beats.

### Scope

- The page-health-push cron narrows the day this ships: its page checks retire (the pm-notify DO's alarm owns stack-silence detection) and it becomes a **daily canary only** — is the DO itself alive, and did it receive yesterday's heartbeats (read `GET /status` on the relay: `lastBeatAt`, `snapshotSeq`, `lastDelivery`).
- The schedule change updates `doc/fleet-schedule-registry.md` in the same pass (repo schedule rule): the registry row(s) for the page-health-push surface change to the daily-canary shape; no schedule is created or retired without its row moving with it.
- Separately reviewed under this issue (a recorded decision, not a silent default): whether any mirrored class beyond `stack.silent` ever cuts over to edge sending. The review's outcome is recorded on #8569 either way; a "yes" files its own implementation issue — it is not built here.

### Acceptance

- The cron's page checks no longer run; the daily canary runs and reports DO liveness + yesterday's heartbeat receipt.
- A dead DO (or a day with no heartbeats while the stack was up) makes the canary fail loudly through the existing cron reporting path.
- `doc/fleet-schedule-registry.md` matches the live schedule after the change.

### Out of scope

- The cutover build itself, if the review says yes (its own issue).

code.title: pm-stack notifications Phase 2 step 3: edge answer intake + heartbeat drain (#8569)
code.body:
## Phase 2 step 3 — edge answer intake (of #8569)

Parent: #8569. Design of record: `doc/2026-11-17_design_pm8569_notifications_phase2.md` §1 (heartbeat + answer drain), §2 (routes), §3 (answers while down). Steps 1 (relay skeleton + dead-man's switch) and 2 (event mirror) land first — the mirrored question state this step serves comes from step 2's mirror.

### Scope

- Edge: `GET /answer/:ledgerId` + `POST /api/needs-drew/:ledgerId/answer` on the pm-notify Worker, serving the question + full option list from DO state (parent design §5 answerable choices), authorized by the per-question answer token — the DO stores only the token's hash beside the mirrored question, expiring when the question is answered or withdrawn (design §4). Submitted answers are stored in the DO as pending, keyed by answer id: `{ledgerId, optionId | freeText, answeredAt, answerTokenHash}`.
- Drain: the heartbeat response carries the pending-answer count (the field exists since step 1, always 0 until this step); the aggregator pulls pending answers (GET + ack by answer id) in the same contact, so a crash mid-drain re-offers the answer instead of losing it. The Phase-1 catcher remains the single writer to the pending-questions ledger — the edge path changes transport, never the place of record (invariant 1).
- If the laptop is up, the Worker may also forward immediately through the existing tunnel ingress pattern (design §3 of the parent issue); the drain remains the correctness path.

### Acceptance (Drew's terms, #8569)

- Answer a needs-drew question from the push while the laptop is down → when the stack returns, the ledger shows it answered and the blocked task unblocks; nothing is lost or double-applied (answer ids dedupe the drain).
- An answer submitted twice (double-tap, retry) is applied exactly once.
- An expired/withdrawn question's answer page refuses the answer instead of storing it.

Tests name their oracles (repo testing doctrine) and run remotely per REMOTE BUILDS ONLY.

### Out of scope

- Cron narrowing (step 4); any change to the catcher's application of answers.

_Filed by lane felix from #8569's step-1 pass, 2026-11-23. Filed without a pilot packet: the shortlist is operator-managed, and chained packets for #8569's steps are cut by the queue operator (same recorded pattern as #13342)._

code.title: pm-stack notifications Phase 2 step 2: event mirror to the pm-notify DO (#8569)
code.body:
## Phase 2 step 2 — event mirror (of #8569)

Parent: #8569. Design of record: `doc/2026-11-17_design_pm8569_notifications_phase2.md` §1 (sync topology) + §5 step 2. Step 1 (relay skeleton + dead-man's switch: `pm-stack/notify-relay` Worker/DO + the aggregator's heartbeat/subscription-mirror client) landed first; this step builds on it.

### Scope

- Edge: add `POST /mirror/event` to the pm-notify Worker (shared-secret auth, same as the other laptop → edge POSTs). The DO appends each event to its mirror log, deduped on the envelope's `mirrorId` (duplicates ack as success), pruned to a rolling 30 days (design §2). The mirror log is a mirror, never the record — the throat's store stays authoritative (invariant 1).
- Laptop: the aggregator mirrors every push-worthy event — incident raised/escalated transitions, needs-drew raises, quota walls — at raise/transition time, one POST per event carrying the throat's existing event payload plus the mirror envelope `{mirrorId, objectRef, transition, raisedAt}`. Delivery obligation is retry-until-acked (the §1 shape); reuse the step-1 relay client's auth/secret plumbing.
- Dual-send discipline holds: the edge remains a **silent mirror** for these classes (no sends). This step proves the sync before any cutover is contemplated; whether any mirrored class beyond `stack.silent` ever cuts over to edge sending is separately reviewed (step 4's review, not this issue).

### Acceptance

- Mirror log in the DO matches the throat store across a soak window (the comparison method is part of the work: a read-back surface or a test harness against both stores).
- Dedupe verified by forced retries: replaying the same `mirrorId` (simulated lost acks) leaves exactly one log entry per event.
- A missed mirror POST (edge down at raise time) is retried until acked — no event in the throat store is absent from the mirror log after the edge returns.
- Tests name their oracles (repo testing doctrine) and run remotely per REMOTE BUILDS ONLY.

### Out of scope

- Any edge sending for mirrored classes; answer intake (step 3); cron narrowing (step 4).

code.title: impl(backups): mesh restore-verification rotation + watchdog surface (#1841)
code.body:
Parent: #9093 (backup mesh) · Program: #8983 · Design: `doc/2026-11-23T16-34-18Z_design_backup_mesh/note.md` (landed with the #9093 design PR).
House rules: any schedule this creates lands its `doc/fleet-schedule-registry.md` row in the same PR; secrets by name only (Bitwarden at runtime, repo-archive pattern); builds/tests run via remote dispatch, never on the laptop or sandbox.

## Scope
Backup-verified is not restore-verified. This issue owns the mesh's standing restore-verification rotation and its watchdog surface: every mesh leg is restore-verified on a schedule, and the #1841 laptop-backups watchdog reports mesh health (per-leg freshness + last restore verification per store) alongside the existing jobs. The per-leg issues (#13455, #13456, #13457, #13458, #13459, #13461, #13462) each carry their own first restore verification; this issue owns the *recurring* rotation after first light.

## Terms (from the design)
- Rotation: one leg's restore verification per week, cycling through all legs and all three stores (R2, laptop, Drive), so every store's copy of every leg is restore-proven at least quarterly.
- A failed verification is a watchdog failure that names the leg and the store — and files/updates an issue, never just a log line.
- Drill shape follows the #10300 cold-restore drill and the #8584 D1 restore drill: restore to an isolated scratch target only, production stores are never written by a drill, credentials by name only.
- The existing monthly cold-store drill (cold-store-drill.timer) is the model and stays; the mesh rotation is additive.

## Acceptance
- [ ] The watchdog reports mesh legs (freshness + completion evidence, same standard as the cold-store check added in PR #10988) and a stale or failed leg reads as a watchdog failure naming it — demonstrated with one deliberately stalled test leg.
- [ ] The first full rotation cycle completes: every leg × every store restore-verified once, results recorded on this issue.
- [ ] A deliberately corrupted scratch snapshot is caught by the verification (integrity/row-count mismatch named), proving the check is not a rubber stamp.
- [ ] Schedule registry rows updated in the implementation PR.

code.title: impl(backups): mesh leg — OpenCode session DB backup (gated on research #9094)
code.body:
Parent: #9093 (backup mesh) · Program: #8983 · Design: `doc/2026-11-23T16-34-18Z_design_backup_mesh/note.md` (landed with the #9093 design PR).
House rules: any schedule this creates lands its `doc/fleet-schedule-registry.md` row in the same PR; secrets by name only (Bitwarden at runtime, repo-archive pattern); builds/tests run via remote dispatch, never on the laptop or sandbox.

## Scope
The OpenCode session database joins the mesh. It is large on purpose (21.37 GB measured 2026-11-12, ~5.1 GB zstd) and has no scheduled off-laptop backup today (#10297, closed as the research tracker). Storage price is not the constraint; churn rate, restore time, and upload bandwidth are.

## Gate
This leg is **gated on research #9094** (OpenCode DB backup economics: measured churn, per-table growth model, costed comparison of full copy / zstd copy / restic deltas). Do not implement a scheme before #9094's comparison lands; the scheme choice is #9094's deliverable. When #9094 closes, this issue proceeds with the chosen scheme unmodified.

## Terms (from the design, whichever scheme #9094 picks)
- Targets: Google Drive + the laptop archive location (per the proto design §B); R2 joins only if #9094's costing says so.
- The DB is laptop-local state: it does NOT take a Turso home (size + churn break the appropriateness line, design §6).

## Acceptance
- [ ] #9094 closed with the scheme recorded; the chosen scheme implemented on a schedule.
- [ ] One full backup cycle completes; size/time recorded on this issue.
- [ ] **Restore verification:** the backup restored to a scratch path; the OpenCode DB integrity check passes and session row counts match the source manifest. Recorded on this issue.
- [ ] Schedule registry row updated in the implementation PR.

code.title: impl(backups): mesh coverage — embedding/shard stores restore without a re-embed pass
code.body:
Parent: #9093 (backup mesh) · Program: #8983 · Design: `doc/2026-11-23T16-34-18Z_design_backup_mesh/note.md` (landed with the #9093 design PR).
House rules: any schedule this creates lands its `doc/fleet-schedule-registry.md` row in the same PR; secrets by name only (Bitwarden at runtime, repo-archive pattern); builds/tests run via remote dispatch, never on the laptop or sandbox.

## Scope
The embedding stores ride the mesh: the Atlas vector tables / shard databases (the embedding corpora under the atlas-search shard layout) are snapshotted by the same Turso→R2 restic legs as their parent databases, and — the point of this issue — a restore is proven to rebuild search **without a re-embed pass**. Embeddings are the most expensive data in the fleet to recompute; a backup that restores rows but loses or invalidates the embedding store fails the mesh's purpose.

## Terms (from the design)
- No separate embedding backup system: shard DBs are class-B (or class-A where the design names them) members of the rotation like any other Turso DB. This issue owns the *verification* that they are in fact enumerated (the rotation enumerates from `turso db list`, so any shard DB living outside Turso is a named exception handled here).
- Any embedding data living outside a Turso DB (local shard files, hosted vector stores) is inventoried by name and given a leg (restic file backup into the mesh repos) or an exclusion with reason.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Inventory posted on this issue: every embedding/vector store, its home (Turso DB / local files / hosted), and its mesh coverage path.
- [ ] **Restore verification (the acceptance that matters):** one corpus restored from mesh snapshots to a scratch environment; a fixed probe query set returns the same top-k results (ids + order) as against the live store, with zero re-embedding performed. Recorded on this issue.
- [ ] Any store found uncovered gets its own follow-on issue filed from this one, linked here.

code.title: impl(backups): mesh leg — laptop-local DBs → Turso backup homes (inventory + appropriateness line)
code.body:
Parent: #9093 (backup mesh) · Program: #8983 · Design: `doc/2026-11-23T16-34-18Z_design_backup_mesh/note.md` (landed with the #9093 design PR).
House rules: any schedule this creates lands its `doc/fleet-schedule-registry.md` row in the same PR; secrets by name only (Bitwarden at runtime, repo-archive pattern); builds/tests run via remote dispatch, never on the laptop or sandbox.

## Scope
Laptop-local databases that hold real state and are not already covered by an existing leg land in the mesh via a Turso backup home, per the design's appropriateness line (§6): a local DB qualifies when it is SQL-shaped, modest in size, and has no other off-laptop copy. Candidates to disposition by name at implementation time: the pm-aggregator's local stores not covered by dashboard-backup, local atlas working DBs not covered by atlas-backup, and any SQLite state under the fleet tools' state dirs. Explicitly NOT this leg: the OpenCode session DB (own leg, gated on research #9094) and anything already covered by repo-archive / laptop-state / dashboard / atlas backups (no double coverage).

## Terms (from the design)
- Each qualifying DB gets a Turso home (`laptop-backup-<name>`); a scheduled export/import replaces the home's contents wholesale, weekly, staggered with the D1 leg.
- The inventory is the deliverable's first half: every laptop-local DB found is listed as qualifying, already-covered (naming the covering leg), or excluded-with-reason. An unlisted DB is a finding, not a silent skip.

## Acceptance
- [ ] The laptop-local DB inventory is posted on this issue with a per-DB disposition (qualifying / already-covered-by / excluded-because).
- [ ] Each qualifying DB's Turso home exists and receives its weekly import; one import record per DB posted.
- [ ] **Restore verification:** one qualifying DB restored from its Turso home to a scratch path and opened successfully (integrity check + row counts vs source manifest). Recorded on this issue.
- [ ] Schedule registry row updated in the implementation PR.

code.title: impl(backups): mesh leg — D1 exports → Turso backup home (fleet-queue-backup D1 first)
code.body:
Parent: #9093 (backup mesh) · Program: #8983 · Design: `doc/2026-11-23T16-34-18Z_design_backup_mesh/note.md` (landed with the #9093 design PR).
House rules: any schedule this creates lands its `doc/fleet-schedule-registry.md` row in the same PR; secrets by name only (Bitwarden at runtime, repo-archive pattern); builds/tests run via remote dispatch, never on the laptop or sandbox.

## Scope
The reverse-direction leg for Cloudflare D1: scheduled D1 exports land in a dedicated Turso database as their backup home, per the design's appropriateness line (§6) — D1 is SQL-shaped, small, and its native export is a SQL file, so a Turso home gives it PITR + the mesh's restic coverage for free. First tenant: the `fleet-queue-backup` D1 database created under #8584. The #8584 export timer (fleet-queue Turso → D1) is the opposite direction and is untouched by this leg; this leg protects the D1 side itself.

## Terms (from the design)
- Cadence: weekly export of each in-scope D1 database, imported into its own Turso home DB (`d1-backup-<name>`), replacing the prior import wholesale (the Turso home is a backup target, never a live read path).
- An export whose import fails leaves the previous import intact and is named in the run record.
- Out of scope by the appropriateness line: D1 databases that are themselves pure replicas of a Turso source (their source's mesh coverage is their backup) — each exclusion is recorded by name on this issue when the leg is implemented.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `fleet-queue-backup` D1 exported and imported into its Turso home on the weekly schedule; import record (row counts per table) posted on this issue.
- [ ] **Restore verification:** the D1 database is rebuilt from its Turso home into a scratch D1 (or local SQLite equivalent) and table row counts match the export. Recorded on this issue.
- [ ] The appropriateness line is applied explicitly: every D1 database in the account is listed on this issue as in-scope or excluded-with-reason.
- [ ] Schedule registry row updated in the implementation PR.

code.title: impl(backups): mesh replication — R2 → laptop and R2 → Google Drive restic copies
code.body:
Parent: #9093 (backup mesh) · Program: #8983 · Design: `doc/2026-11-23T16-34-18Z_design_backup_mesh/note.md` (landed with the #9093 design PR).
House rules: any schedule this creates lands its `doc/fleet-schedule-registry.md` row in the same PR; secrets by name only (Bitwarden at runtime, repo-archive pattern); builds/tests run via remote dispatch, never on the laptop or sandbox.

## Scope
The replication legs that make it a mesh rather than a single backup: `restic copy` of the `restic-turso-mesh` snapshots from R2 to (a) the laptop-local restic repository and (b) the Google Drive restic repository — the same three-backend shape repo-archive-backup and laptop-state-backup already run. After this leg, every store (R2, laptop, Drive) holds the full mesh snapshot set and any one of them can rebuild the others.

## Terms (from the design)
- Replication runs after each night's Turso→R2 cohort completes; a replication failure never blocks the next night's ingest leg, but is named in the run record and the watchdog.
- Retention is a property of the snapshot set, applied identically in all three repos (keep-daily 7 / keep-weekly 8 / keep-monthly 12); forget/prune runs in R2 first, then copies propagate the thinned set — a store must never prune independently.
- Drive bandwidth is the known constraint (the #10300 drill measured the Drive leg at ~8 KB/s for bulk byte download): replication to Drive is incremental restic copy (changed packs only), and the first-seed copy is a named, separately scheduled operation, not part of the nightly window.

## Acceptance
- [ ] All three repos list the same snapshot set for the mesh (listing diff recorded on this issue).
- [ ] **Rebuild verification:** with the R2 repo made unavailable to the test (credentials withheld), one mesh snapshot is restored using only the laptop repo, and one using only the Drive repo; row counts match the export manifest. Recorded on this issue.
- [ ] First-seed Drive copy measured (bytes, wall time) and recorded; nightly incremental copy time recorded for one week of runs.
- [ ] Watchdog: per-store mesh freshness visible to the #1841 laptop-backups watchdog, or the gap is filed as its own issue.
- [ ] Schedule registry rows updated in the implementation PR.

code.title: impl(backups): mesh leg — general Turso DBs → R2 restic deltas on the 14-day rotation
code.body:
Parent: #9093 (backup mesh) · Program: #8983 · Design: `doc/2026-11-23T16-34-18Z_design_backup_mesh/note.md` (landed with the #9093 design PR).
House rules: any schedule this creates lands its `doc/fleet-schedule-registry.md` row in the same PR; secrets by name only (Bitwarden at runtime, repo-archive pattern); builds/tests run via remote dispatch, never on the laptop or sandbox.

## Scope
The fleet-scale leg: extend the #13455 pattern to every remaining Turso database (class B — the ~39 general DBs beyond the platform set) so the whole Turso fleet rides the 14-day mesh cycle as restic deltas (stream-zstd) into the R2 `restic-turso-mesh` repository. The DB list is enumerated from `turso db list` at run time, never hard-coded, so new databases join the mesh automatically; per-user databases (#9083's tenancy design) join this same rotation when they arrive.

## Terms (from the design)
- Rotation: the class-B set is divided into 14 daily cohorts (2–3 DBs/day at today's count); each DB is snapshotted once per 14 days, cohort assignment stable by database name hash.
- A DB whose export fails stays in a retry list for the next night and is named in the run record — a cohort miss must never be silent.
- Retention in the R2 repo: keep-daily 7 / keep-weekly 8 / keep-monthly 12 (design §5), applied per DB via restic tags.
- Turso plan wall respected: exports are reads; the 24 GB storage wall and PITR are unaffected. Delete Protection is already ON fleet-wide (2026-11-17, #9093 step-1 record).

## Acceptance
- [ ] One full 14-day rotation completes with every class-B DB snapshotted at least once; the rotation record (per-DB snapshot ids + dates) is posted on this issue.
- [ ] Failure handling proven: a deliberately misnamed/removed DB in a test cohort surfaces in the run record and the watchdog, not as a silent skip.
- [ ] **Restore verification:** one snapshot from each of three different cohorts restored to scratch targets; per-table row counts match the export manifests. Recorded on this issue.
- [ ] Watchdog: cohort freshness (oldest unsnapshotted DB age) is visible to the #1841 laptop-backups watchdog, or the gap is filed as its own issue.

code.title: laptop build infra: shared sccache server stalls under multi-lane load (clients parked 7+ min on trivial crates)
code.body:
## Observation (2026-11-23, reference laptop)

Under multi-lane load (~20 lanes), the shared `sccache` server stopped turning around compile requests in usable time, fleet-wide:

- A `cargo bench --no-run` build for `pkgs/id` (Lane XZ, #13084) started 10 crates through sccache and then made **zero progress for 7+ minutes**: the `sccache rustc` client processes sat at 0.0% CPU in `Sl` state waiting on the server — including trivial crates (`cfg-if`, `unicode-ident`) that are certainly cache hits.
- Other lanes' sccache clients showed the same shape (e.g. a clippy lane's `sccache cc`/`rustc` clients parked since ~07:31 CST).
- The server process itself was alive (PID 264387, up 5h22m, ~10% CPU) with ~284 established client connections; stats at the time: 77,699 compile requests, 65,806 executed. Disk was not full (256 GiB free; broker pool 298.91/300 GiB).
- Bypassing the wrapper (`RUSTC_WRAPPER=` / `RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER=` empty) let the same build compile 456 crates in ~2 minutes under the same host load, and finish cleanly.

## Impact

Any lane building through the standard dev shell (which sets `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache`) can silently stall for many minutes with no error. The failure mode looks like a slow build, so it is easy to misread.

## Ask

Investigate the sccache server's behaviour under many concurrent clients (request queueing / concurrency limits / cache I/O), and consider a documented fallback (e.g. lanes may set `RUSTC_WRAPPER=` when the server is saturated) or server-side tuning. Filed from Lane XZ's #13084 run; the stall cost ~25 minutes including diagnosis and a slot re-queue.

code.title: Self-hosted Desktop Commander MCP endpoint: Worker front door, Access gate, laptop bridge
code.body:
# Self-hosted Desktop Commander MCP endpoint (Worker front door, Access-gated, laptop bridge)

Build a self-hosted replacement for the vendor's metered Remote Desktop Commander relay, following the fleet's existing Worker patterns (atlas-search Worker, id-mail publish/promote).

## Shape

- **Worker** `desktop-commander` in `pkgs/desktop-commander/worker/` (atlas-search worker layout: `wrangler.toml` + `cloudflare.config.ts` + `src/`): a transparent streamable-HTTP MCP proxy. `workers_dev` off — the only door is the Access-gated custom hostname.
- **Deploys**: Cloudflare version deployments with the `cf` binary (`cf workers versions create`), driven by GitHub Actions publish + promote workflows modeled on `id-mail-worker-publish.yml` / `id-mail-worker-promote.yml` (upload version with provenance artifact; promote the verified upload to 100%).
- **Public door**: `commander.security.cab` — Cloudflare Access app (self-hosted, 24h session) with (1) an Allow policy for the owner's Google identity via the existing Google IdP (client saved under #12417, wiring under #12412) and (2) a service-token policy for machine MCP clients that can send Access headers.
- **Bridge door**: `commander-link.security.cab` — Access app, service-token-only (the atlas-search pattern), token held by the Worker as version secrets. Ingress added to the existing sandbox-link tunnel -> `http://localhost:8931` on amd.
- **Laptop bridge**: the packaged Desktop Commander (`pkgs/desktop-commander`, stdio) wrapped by supergateway in streamable-HTTP mode on `127.0.0.1:8931`, run as a systemd user service; the service definition is added to the Nix home config in the same change so it survives rebuilds.
- **Secrets**: by name only, in fleet secrets / GitHub environment secrets; values never in the repo or logs. New names: `cloudflare.access.desktop-commander-client-id` / `-client-secret` (bridge door), a public-door client token pair, and a dedicated deploy token `cloudflare.api-token-desktop-commander-worker`.

## Acceptance

- `POST https://commander.security.cab/mcp` with the public-door service token completes an MCP `initialize` + `tools/list` against the real Desktop Commander on amd.
- The same URL without credentials is stopped by Access (login wall / 401).
- A publish run uploads a new Worker version without promoting it; a promote run moves exactly that version to 100%.
- mcpx on the laptop consumes the endpoint as a remote server (first verified client).
- The vendor device agent (`desktop-commander-remote.service`) is left running until this endpoint is verified, then stood down as a separate recorded step.

## Non-goals

- No use of the vendor's hosted relay or its pairing.
- No changes to the local stdio Desktop Commander wiring in mcpx (that path stays as-is).

code.title: id: event store — audit prune_behind_cut and range-sync advertisement against compacted residue
code.body:
## Context

The #3797 compaction change adds *residue* to the event store: a compacted event keeps its `hashes` and `applied` rows and gains a `compacted` row (ID + causal edges), while its `events`/`bodies`/`groups` rows are removed. Presence and applied verdicts are unchanged; only bytes are reclaimed.

Two older paths predate residue and do not know about it. Neither corrupts the store — `check_invariants` is residue-aware and the resolution counts residue as applied — but both deserve a deliberate decision:

## 1. `prune_behind_cut` (causal-cut removal for membership-removal flows)

`prune_behind_cut` removes events behind a causal cut *entirely* (including their `hashes` rows) and rewrites chain rows from the surviving **stored** events only. Run over a store that has compacted residue, it would:

- leave `compacted` rows behind for positions whose events it pruned (residue pointing at positions the cut meant to erase), and
- recompute a chain row whose applied prefix ends at a residue position from stored events only, dropping the prefix back to the last stored event — the chain row and the residue would disagree, and `check_invariants` would (correctly) refuse the store.

Decide: should a prune also drop the residue rows in its cut, and should its chain rewrite treat residue positions as it treats stored ones? Until decided, compaction and prune should not be composed over the same store without an explicit ruling.

## 2. Range-sync advertisement vs bytes

`sync_entries` advertises event IDs from the `hashes` index; `sync_bytes` returns `Ok(None)` for a compacted event (its bytes are gone). A peer asking for a compacted event's bytes gets a graceful "not held" rather than the bytes — durable, checkpoint, and proof traffic is unaffected (those classes never compact), and a compacted event is by construction an applied live-class event whose content the retention policy already declared reclaimable. Decide whether sync should advertise compacted IDs at all, or mark them in the advertisement so a peer does not spend requests on bytes the holder has reclaimed.

## Acceptance

A recorded decision for each path, and the code (plus tests) updated to match: prune either handles residue or refuses a store that has any; sync advertisement either excludes compacted IDs or marks them, with a compacted-store sync test.

Landed by PR #13400: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/13400

code.title: pm-console: order an older action held for a machine against a newer one the edge does itself
code.body:
What is done late is done in the order the owner did it, with one case left out.

**What holds today.** On the device a later action about the same thing (the same issue, task, reference or set of questions) waits behind an earlier one that has not been taken (`subject` in `pm-stack/console/public/outbox.js`). At the edge, an action that may be held goes behind an earlier one about the same thing that a machine has not taken yet, even when the machine can be reached again (`subjectOf` in `src/edge-proto.ts`, used in the act route of `edge/src/edge.ts`).

**What is left out.** An older action is held for a machine (it was relayed while the edge was not doing that kind itself, or was turned away), and then the edge does a newer one about the same thing itself. The machine does the older one when it is back, and for a kind where the last one wins (`issue.rank`) the older rank replaces the newer.

How to get there: with the laptop away and the edge's token turned away for writes, rank an issue (held for the laptop); press "Try again now" on the Cloudflare screen so the edge takes the kind back; rank the same issue again (done by the edge); bring the laptop back. The issue ends at the first rank.

**What done looks like.**

- When the edge does a kind itself and something older about the same thing is held for a machine and has never been handed to one, the edge does the older one itself first, under its name, and drops it from what is held; or, for a kind where the last one wins, drops the older one and records it as replaced by the newer.
- A held action that has already been handed to a machine (it was in an answer to a report and is not yet acknowledged) is not done by the edge: the machine may be doing it. The newer one waits behind it instead.
- A test in `test/edge.test.ts` for each of the three cases, and for an unrelated subject going straight through.

Files: `pm-stack/console/edge/src/edge.ts` (the act route, `keep`, the report handler that hands held actions out), `pm-stack/console/src/edge-proto.ts`.

Found while fixing review findings on #13287; recorded in the design record `doc/2026-11-23T06-50-00Z_architecture_pm_platform_cloudflare_core/`.
