code.title: fleet queue: #10626 remainders — filing-time state re-check + criterion-6 deployment measurement
code.body:
Remainders of #10626 (claim-path staleness check, landed in PR #11799 and verified on main 2026-11-23 by lane GG — see the verification record on #10626). Two items were deliberately not part of that landing:

## 1. Filing-time state re-check (proposal step 5 of #10626)

Packet generators stamp `payload.issue.state_checked_at` (pm-stack console/dispatch write it), but nothing reads the stamp: a packet whose `state_checked_at` is older than a small bound (proposal: 1h) is not re-verified at enqueue. The claim-path check is the safety net and catches the class at claim, so this is source-side hygiene, not a correctness hole: generators should re-verify issue state at enqueue or stamp the packet so the claim path checks it first.

## 2. Criterion-6 deployment measurement

#10626 acceptance criterion 6: within 7 days of deployment, the daily work-failures recompute shows pre_done completions for tasks created after the fix trending to ~0, replaced by `staleness_autocomplete` events that consumed no session. The 7-day window runs from the queue broker running the #11799 code (broker generation 4, deployed 2026-11-22, is the first confirmed build carrying it). When the window elapses, run the recompute, cite the pre_done trend + interception count on #10626, and close it.

Neither item blocks #10626's implemented criteria (1–5, verified). This issue is the tracking home for both remainders so #10626 can close on the measurement.

code.title: C8-E: error-driven investigation evidence bundle
code.body:
## Context

Follow-on to #9576 and the merged C8 design (PR #12290,
`doc/2026-11-22T01-48-21Z_design_c8_atlas_ingestion_investigation/`).
Design slice **C8-E — investigation evidence bundle**: the
error-driven investigation recipe of design §5, whose output is a
reproducible evidence bundle (query/fingerprint, time range,
evidence IDs and links, exact-vs-inferred edge labels, candidate
changes, rejected candidates/reasons, missing-data warnings, next
action) — never an automated causation claim.

## First slice (seam-independent)

The fingerprint core, from design §4/§5:

- Conservative error-string normalization: Unicode normalization
  and whitespace normalization only; the original string is
  preserved alongside the fingerprint.
- A stable fingerprint that groups exact normalized occurrences
  only — merely similar errors are never merged.
- Model test per the design's verification contract: a fixture with
  first vs earliest-retained-observation distinction inputs,
  exact-vs-inferred edge labels, and missing-link gaps preserved
  as gaps.

After that PR, `cargo test -p atlas-core c8` shows the fingerprint
core passing where no error-investigation code exists on main
today.

## Later slices (depend on live interfaces)

- First-observed-occurrence search over retained, authorized
  telemetry, with the retention floor stated on the result.
- Commit → PR → issue joins with per-edge source/confidence,
  consuming #9073–#9075 provenance/session fields and queue
  history where present; absent fields are recorded as
  unavailable, never inferred.
- The unpushed-final-commit check against an authoritative state
  source.
- One real error string traced end-to-end (acceptance 3 of #9576)
  with the bundle produced and sensitive values redacted.

## Acceptance

- [x] Fingerprint core lands with its model test (oracle: design
      §4 normalization rules and §5 recipe steps 1–2).
- [ ] A real error string is investigated end-to-end and the
      evidence bundle is attached to #9576 (ticks its acceptance 3).

code.title: id: invite capability_pin term — pin the capability baseline as issued (#5751 delta from #5959 design)
code.body:
Refs #5959.

## Scope

Add the optional `capability_pin` term to the invite model of #5751 (`doc/2026-11-14T18-50-00Z_design_id_invite_delegation/`), as decided in §7 of the #5959 design record (`doc/2026-11-23T05-02-30Z_design_id_capability_change_notices/`, PR #12920).

- Invite terms gain `capability_pin: { release_identity, table_version }` — the world's release identity as issued plus the class-table version. It deliberately does not carry the message set: the pinned release's registry record (#5958 §4) is immutable and content-addressed, so the redeeming client recomputes the pinned message set from the identity. The pin is two hashes and a version, sized to fit the invite body's 512-byte hard budget.
- Minting: the inviter's client computes and attaches the pin at issuance (optional; recommended for per-recipient links to sensitive worlds, normally absent on public bearer links).
- Redemption: if the current message set is covered by the pinned set, the pin seeds the joiner's baseline (narrowed to current); if not covered, the #5959 change notice fires before the first connect completes; if the pinned release record cannot be fetched, the pin is ignored and the join is an ordinary first connect.
- The pin never widens anything: it grants nothing by itself and does not interact with the invite's own expiry / use-cap / redeemer-pin terms.

## Test oracles

Pin covered ⇒ baseline seeded, no blocking prompt; pin uncovered ⇒ notice before first connect; pin unfetchable ⇒ ordinary first connect; pin present with a since-shrunk world ⇒ baseline seeds at the narrower current set.

Design of record: #5959 §7. Invite model: #5751. Parent program: #5955.

code.title: Atlas search improvements: parallel branches, service/result-store shape, nix-packaged binary CLI
code.body:
> Moved from dezren39/hatch-personal#21 on 2026-11-22 at Drewry's direction (review of hatch/hatch-personal for material that belongs in the code repo). GitHub's native transfer is unavailable (private→public, different owner), so this issue carries the original text verbatim; the original is closed with a pointer here.

Exploration opened by Drew 2026-11-04, after the Snowflake swap landed. Three threads, in the order they should be evaluated:

## 1. Parallel branch execution (near-term, small)
A hybrid query has independent branches (FTS branch, vector branch, plus filters) that only join at RRF fusion. Today they run effectively serially in the Python CLI. The branches can run concurrently in-process (threads against the libsql endpoint) with results collected until each branch pool is satisfied — no external store needed for the single-user CLI. Expected saving: the vector branch scan (~6 s) overlaps the FTS branch instead of adding to it. Cold-start (ST model load, most of the ~35 s cold run) is untouched by this.

## 2. Workers + temp result store + pull-until-satisfied (service shape)
Drews sketch: fan queries out to workers running simultaneously; workers write results into a temp store (he said temp D1; our analog is a scratch Turso/libsql DB or an in-memory/RESP-style store); the CLI pulls results until its pools are satisfied (fetch-to-fill as a streaming protocol). This is the right shape IF Atlas becomes shared infrastructure (multiple agents/clients querying constantly, warm embedders, queued deep searches). Cost: a daemon to own, a protocol, lifecycle for temp results. Decision input needed: is Atlas headed for multi-client use (e.g. OpenChamber/fork sessions querying it as a tool), or does it stay Drews personal CLI? Build the service only if the former.

## 3. Ship atlas-search as a nix-packaged binary
Replace the Python script + venv with a compiled binary vendored from the code flake (pkgs/atlas-search derivation, overlay pattern as elsewhere). Rationale, all observed 2026-11-03: the venv/wrapper broke twice in one evening on LD_LIBRARY_PATH (desktop pipewire path starves numpy of libstdc++/libz; fixed via probe hacks PRs #18/#19), and every cold run pays Python + ST model load. A Rust binary (rusqlite/libsql client + ort + tokenizers) can embed Snowflake natively — the fork spike proved onnxruntime + the Unigram tokenizer reproduce the Python vectors BIT-IDENTICALLY, so parity is achievable and provable. Gate any swap on the golden 311 tying the Python reference (same pattern as the embeddings bake-in). The Python stays as the eval/reference implementation (eval3.py harness).

## Sequencing
Thread 1 is independent and small. Thread 3 subsumes thread 1 if it happens (write the binary concurrent from the start). Thread 2 is a product decision (multi-client?) before it is engineering. The index A/B (index-fill vs exact scan) running 2026-11-04 informs all three: whichever vector backend wins on the golden set is the one the binary/service should implement.

code.body:

## Slice 2 — Hosted collector

Per design §3: registry-driven multi-board GraphQL ingest running on Workers Cron Triggers, serialized per board by `IngestDO` (cursors: ETag/last-snapshot watermark; per-board GitHub rate-budget state). - A cron run ingests every registry board into the tenant DB; a forced failure on one board leaves the other boards' pools intact and records a finding.

- No token value persists anywhere after a run (test-pinned).

code.title: test(pm-stack F): GC race + revocation conformance tests (#9084 slice 6)
code.body:
Part of #9084 (component F design, doc/2026-11-23T03-04-00Z_design_content-addressed-media-data-plane). Slice 6 of 6.

Conformance tests for the design's safety claims (§5/§6), as their own slice so they can run against any implementation of slices 1-5: (a) reference created during sweep grace clears the candidate; (b) reference created after re-verify is serialized by the epoch fence (re-upload path, never wrongful delete); (c) cross-partition reference resolution is refused; (d) hash presentation alone never serves bytes; (e) revocation by reference removal stops new capability minting within the documented TTL bound; (f) sole-referencer restricted erasure completes under the fence.

Acceptance: the six cases run green against the R2 implementation and are written adapter-neutrally so the RustFS implementation runs them unchanged.

code.title: impl(pm-stack F): publication semantics — public-DB reference, CDN path, unpublish (#9084 slice 5)
code.body:
Part of #9084 (component F design, doc/2026-11-23T03-04-00Z_design_content-addressed-media-data-plane). Slice 5 of 6.

Implement publication semantics per design §3/§5: publication is a live reference record in the public DB, never a byte copy. Capability minting from a publication reference, the CDN-eligible replica path for the public tier, and the unpublish flow (reference removal stops new minting immediately; CDN invalidation is epoch-paced and documented as such).

Acceptance: publish/unpublish flow with tests — published content readable via publication reference alone, unpublished content refused new capabilities, no byte copy created at publish time.

code.title: impl(pm-stack F): GC mark-and-sweep worker — epochs, grace, fenced delete (#9084 slice 4)
code.body:
Part of #9084 (component F design, doc/2026-11-23T03-04-00Z_design_content-addressed-media-data-plane). Slice 4 of 6.

Implement the GC mark-and-sweep worker per design §6: per-partition epochs, candidate marking, policy grace (starting defaults 7d tenant tiers / 24h public), authoritative re-verify at grace expiry, epoch-fenced conditional delete serialized through component E's per-partition sequence, and an audit event per delete. Reference counters may prioritize candidates (#9137) but are never delete evidence. Sole-referencer restricted-tier erasure may shorten grace to zero by policy, under the same fence.

Acceptance: worker + tests for candidate clearing on new reference, re-verify rescue, fenced delete, and per-partition isolation (a sweep never sees or deletes another partition's replicas).

code.title: impl(pm-stack F): derived reference/location index builder (#9084 slice 3)
code.body:
Part of #9084 (component F design, doc/2026-11-23T03-04-00Z_design_content-addressed-media-data-plane). Slice 3 of 6.

Build the derived per-partition reference/location index: an outbox consumer maintaining (content ID -> set of referencing DBs, replica locations) aligned with the #9115 location index. The index is explicitly a cache — GC (§6 of the design) re-verifies against authoritative rows before any delete — so the builder's contract is eventual consistency plus a periodic full-partition reconciliation, never delete authority.

Acceptance: index builder + reconciliation job, with drift measurement reported (index vs authoritative rows) over a partition.

Implement F's object-plane staged publication against the #9087 adapter contract for R2: put_staged with checksum/size verification, publish as the service verification step (never multipart completion), head, capability-scoped read with verified-replica fallback, conditional delete_replica, and the adapter capability matrix. The conformance suite must be written against the interface so RustFS (component I, #9087) runs the same suite.

Acceptance: R2 adapter passes the shared conformance suite, including delayed visibility, interrupted multipart, duplicate request, checksum mismatch, and conditional delete cases.

# Rotate the OpenChamber Android signing-keystore password (found in plaintext in a session transcript)

<!-- agent-note:v1 agent=archer lane=lane-br state=follow-up -->

**For Drew (owner action).** During the #10412 secret-tier review (2026-11-22), one confirmed candidate was a session transcript whose tool output had printed decrypted sops keys in plaintext — including the password for the OpenChamber Android signing keystore (the `android-key-password` entry in the admin sops group, `secrets/sops/groups/admin/openchamber-android.yaml`). The transcript itself verified the printed value against the real keystore at the time.

The atlas copies are remediated: the source message (`atlas-core-internal-content` message `e97b1e5e92c6bf92afd9185cdc8a9fd4a2885e2fce65b68e4255a25e3149b12f`) and all 63 chunks derived from it now live only at the secret tier (see the #10412 remediation record). No credential value is reproduced here or anywhere in the review records.

**Recommended action (owner only — it touches the sops store and the signing setup):**

1. Rotate the Android signing-keystore password and update the sops entry.
2. Treat any other copy of that transcript outside the atlas stores (session logs on the machine that produced it) as exposed copies of the same value until rotated.

Priority: the value has been sitting in an internal-tier store since the transcript was ingested; the tier exposure is now closed, but rotation is the step that retires the value itself.

code.title: pm-console on amd stopped taking merges at 2026-11-23T00:20Z
code.body:
## What stopped

pm-console on amd stopped taking merges: health answered `hostVersion 6226e4d93599` (main as of 2026-11-23T00:20Z) while main gained five `pm-stack/console` merges after 02:04Z, and `hostSeen` stayed fresh — service up, code old.

## Which link was broken

**Link 1 — pm-git-sync.** Not the redeploy, not load. `~/git/code` main was **ahead 2, behind 22** with a clean tree: two local commits never pushed to origin, so every `git pull --ff-only` refused and the clone froze at the 00:20Z main. The redeploy unit was healthy throughout — it correctly had nothing new to deploy (checkout console tree == `~/.local/state/pm-console/deployed`).

The blocking commit was made directly on the deploy clone's main at 02:04:53Z:

- `8e472164d4c` — "fix(opencode-claimant): raise poll timeout 30s -> 300s so live fires pass the gate" (#3026). **Changes files**, so pm-git-sync by design refuses to move it aside and fails loudly — its comment says exactly this: "A local commit that changes a file still fails loudly and moves nothing: that one needs a person or an agent."
- `bbe127c8983` — "amd 571" — an **empty** rebuild marker. Not the blocker, and **not the #12520 flake.lock case** either: #12520's marker changed flake.lock, this one changes nothing (`git diff 8e472164d4c bbe127c8983` is empty) and pm-git-sync would have auto-moved it aside under a `rebuild-marker/` tag had it been alone.

## Evidence (journal lines)

```
Nov 22 20:11:16 amd pm-git-sync[1555519]: pm-git-sync: FAIL git pull --ff-only 8e472164d4cfa15c5154c7d84585cf95c8898773 -> 24be6fdd6f40b3ea13e89763a1c7de8ba6189ec0 in /home/user/git/code
Nov 22 20:32:20 amd pm-git-sync[1930032]: pm-git-sync: FAIL /home/user/git/code main has 2 commit(s) origin does not and is 22 behind — not pulling.
Nov 22 20:32:20 amd pm-git-sync[1930032]: pm-git-sync: commit 8e472164d4c fix(opencode-claimant): raise poll timeout 30s -> 300s so live fires pass the gate changes files or is a merge; it is not moved aside.
```

First failure 20:11:16 CST (2026-11-23T02:11Z), seven minutes after the commit landed; failing every 30 s since. Timers were never late (pm-git-sync last ran seconds before inspection; redeploy every minute on the dot).

## What was changed

Nothing discarded, nothing force-pushed:

1. Both local commits preserved: branch **`unpushed-main/2026-11-23-claimant-poll-timeout`** pushed to origin (holds `8e472164d4c` and `bbe127c8983`), and the empty marker additionally tagged `rebuild-marker/amd-571`, pm-git-sync's own convention. The claimant fix is real production work (#3026) — it is on that branch ready to be landed properly.
2. `~/git/code` main moved to `origin/main` (`cd688f5566c8`) with `git reset --keep` — the same move pm-git-sync itself performs for the empty-commit case.
3. The timers then did the rest, unmodified:

```
Nov 22 20:36:59 amd pm-git-sync[1961357]: pm-git-sync: ok clean main, up to date at cd688f5566c842f5b0245fcb02a5cd8042d30f39
Nov 22 20:37:14 amd bash[1963101]: redeploy: cd688f5566c is in service
```

4. Verified from outside: `https://pm-console-edge.developing-today.workers.dev/console/health` answers `hostVersion: cd688f5566c8`, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 45191b4e2e14 cd688f5566c8` passes. Merge-to-service latency is back to about a minute (PR #12778's merge was in service one minute later).

## What would have caught it sooner

- pm-git-sync failed **every 30 s from 02:11Z** and nothing alerted: the console's Services screen surfaces *redeploy* failures, not *sync* failures, so the stall was invisible until merges visibly stopped landing. A failure-streak alert on `pm-git-sync.service` (any watchdog already watching user units) would have flagged it within minutes.
- The console already publishes `hostVersion`/`hostSeen` on /console/health. A staleness watchdog comparing health's `hostVersion` against `origin/main` — hostVersion hours stale while origin/main has new `pm-stack/console` commits — would have caught it with no journal access at all.
- Root-cause family is "commit made directly on the deploy clone's main" (#12520, #2496, #8170, #8171). The empty-marker variant is already auto-moved; the file-changing variant still requires a person by design. The two alerts above close the detection gap for that case.

code.title: Antigravity ACP: OpenClaw agy harness points at unauthenticated standalone server (fix: native agy acp); OpenCode door barred by 2026-11-14 ruling
code.body:
## Antigravity as an ACP agent: OpenClaw's `agy` harness points at the unauthenticated standalone ACP server; OpenCode's door is barred by the 2026-11-14 ruling

Filed from Lane BG (Drew's order, 2026-11-22: "fix antigravity so it runs as acp in openclaw and opencode"). All evidence gathered live on the laptop 2026-11-22 ~19:40–20:00 CST.

### The agent itself is healthy

The Antigravity CLI (`agy` 1.5.9) ships a native ACP server (`agy acp`). Driven directly over stdio it completes a full round-trip with no auth ceremony (it uses the CLI's existing Google login; quota read tonight: weekly 0% used, resets 2026-11-30):

- `initialize` → protocolVersion 1, agentInfo "Antigravity ACP Server" 1.5.9
- `session/new` → session created, models listed (gemini-3.8-flash-*, claude-sonnet-4-6, ...)
- `session/prompt` ("Reply with exactly this token: ACP_OK") → agent text `ACP_OK`, stopReason `end_turn`

### OpenClaw — defect found, fix in this issue's PR

OpenClaw's acpx backend registers `agy` with command `/run/current-system/sw/bin/agy_acp_server` — Google's **standalone** agy-acp-server **1.2.1** (vendored as `pkgs/antigravity-acp`), a separate product from the CLI with **separate auth state** in `~/.gemini/antigravity-acp/` — a directory that does not exist: it has never been authenticated. Driven directly it fails at `session/new`:

```
{"code": -32000, "message": "Authentication required", "data": {"message": "No authentication method selected. Either call the `authenticate` method (supports oauth-personal, gemini-api-key, agent-platform), or set `auth.type` in settings.json (/home/user/.gemini/antigravity-acp/settings.json) ..."}}
```

Its `authenticate` path opens an interactive browser OAuth flow (observed spawning Helium and timing out) — there is no stored credential for it to reuse.

**Fix:** repoint both declarations in `home/openclaw/default.nix` (the `.acpx/config.json` text, line ~111, and the embedded acpx override in the generated openclaw.json, line ~682) from the standalone server to the CLI's built-in ACP server: `/etc/profiles/per-user/user/bin/agy acp` — the exact command string verified end-to-end above. Activation: the generated files (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`, `~/.acpx/config.json`) are Nix store symlinks, so the change goes live at the laptop's next switch from the primary clone, after which the gateway should be restarted and one ACP dispatch to agent `agy` run as the through-OpenClaw proof.

### OpenCode — no ACP-client surface; the provider door is barred by a standing ruling

The opencode fork's ACP support is server-side only (`opencode acp` serves OpenCode itself; `packages/cli/src/acp/`). There is no config surface for registering an external ACP agent — Antigravity's only presence in OpenCode is the `_antigravity` **provider**, which sits in `disabled_providers` under the recorded 2026-11-14 ruling (code#9856, quoted in `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`): the account was disabled by Google for a Terms-of-Service violation, the disable was ruled **permanent for fleet use regardless of the appeal outcome** ("Do NOT delete this line, do NOT re-enable this provider, and do NOT probe it... a single fleet call after reinstatement risks permanent suspension of the account"). This lane did not touch or probe that provider. Re-enabling it requires Drew to explicitly supersede the 2026-11-14 ruling with that suspension risk in view; the ACP route (this issue's OpenClaw fix) uses Google's own CLI the way it ships, which is the path the ruling's rationale leaves open ("for use inside Google's own Antigravity app only" — the `agy` CLI is that app's own tool).

### Remainders

1. After the laptop's next switch lands the OpenClaw fix on main: restart `openclaw-gateway.service`, dispatch one ACP session to agent `agy` through OpenClaw, record the round-trip here.
2. OpenCode: Drew's call on superseding the 2026-11-14 #9856 ruling — not actioned by this lane.

code.title: sandbox seat: nix-persist store rolled back across a runtime restart; nixbld build ACLs missing on the new instance
code.body:
## Finding (2026-11-22, found during the #5770 live deploy)

On the muse sandbox seat, a runtime/service restart reverted `~/nix-persist` to its 2026-11-22 00:14 snapshot:

- `~/nix-persist/var/nix/db/db.sqlite` mtime is 2026-11-22 00:14 and `ValidPaths` holds only the 68 tarball-snapshot paths. Flake inputs fetched and a package built earlier the same evening (verified: `nix build` printed the outPath and `nix path-info` knew it) are absent after the restart — the store silently lost everything added since the snapshot while the rest of home (worktrees, `~/tools`, scratch files) stayed current.
- The same instance was missing pieces the seat's own docs record as boot state: the `/nix` symlink and `/usr/local/bin/nix` wrapper (both restored by `~/tools/nix-ensure.sh` + `install-nix-wrapper.sh`), and the nixbld traverse ACLs (`g:nixbld:--x` on `/home/hatch`, `~/nix-persist`, `~/tools`, `~/tools/taint-shim`, read on `taint_shim.so`, per `~/TOOLS.d/nix.md`) — without them every local build fails with `error: executing '.../bash': Permission denied` because build users cannot traverse `/home/hatch`. The ACLs were re-applied by hand (python ctypes `setxattr`, the documented method) and builds then succeeded.

## Why it matters

Anything that builds or deploys from the sandbox store (the #5770 sandbox deploy targets are the first consumers) can silently lose its artifacts across a restart while every health signal still reads green. The seat keeper (`felix-seat-keeper`) checks the broker/gh/tailnet legs but not the nix store's freshness or the build ACLs.

## Suggested scope

- Keeper/ensure: assert the store DB is writable and current (a probe path added by a test build survives), and assert the four nixbld ACLs; re-apply via the documented ctypes method when missing.
- Investigate why the restart restored a stale `nix-persist` snapshot while the rest of home stayed current (snapshot scope mismatch?).

Not enqueued as a queue task: the broker claim path is down on this seat (fallback claims only) at filing time; this is seat-keeper territory and is cited from #5770's implementation record.

code.title: build: nix build .#deploy wedges in mcpx check phase (go test idle, no test binary); registry build realizes every target package
code.body:
## Problem

`nix build .#deploy` (the deploy CLI package, pkgs/deploy) currently cannot complete on the laptop: the build realizes **every** target package in the registry — `deploy-targets.json` is a writeText whose string context references all 14 target packages — and the **mcpx package's check phase wedges** in the nix sandbox.

## Evidence (2026-11-22, laptop, main 6226e4d9359 / b667d6b0ab0)

- During a supervised #5769 cutover run, `nix build .#deploy` was killed after ~35 minutes. The blocking derivation was mcpx: its builder ran `go test -p 1 -timeout 30m` across the full mcpx package set under tini.
- The `go test` process sat at ~0.2% CPU, state S (sleeping), for 23+ minutes with **no child processes at all** — no compile/link children, no test binaries. The `-timeout 30m` only bounds test execution, and no test binary was running, so the phase had no bound.
- No orphaned/reparented test binary from that build existed. Separately, the machine carries days-old leaked mcpx test processes (e.g. `mcpx supervise` instances under /tmp/Test* sockets, 5+ days old), suggesting the suite's process hygiene in sandboxed runs is part of the picture.
- Workaround used for the cutover (recorded on #5769): render the registry JSON by pure evaluation of pkgs/deploy and run deploy.py directly, building only the needed target's artifact. That worked, but the packaged path should work too.

## Asks

1. mcpx: find why `go test` idles with no children in the nix sandbox (build-cache lock contention? a test helper waiting on something the sandbox lacks?) and fix or bound it.
2. pkgs/deploy: consider decoupling the deploy package build from realizing every target package (the registry JSON needs the packages' outPaths, which are known at eval time; the current writeText context forces full builds, including unrelated check phases, before the CLI can be produced).

Found during the #5769 secrets-broker cutover; the cutover itself completed via the workaround and is not blocked on this.

Per Drew's order (2026-11-22 ~18:11 CST): set up 8 constant OpenChamber task lanes on the laptop, with a lane prompt that encourages completing real work and filing follow-ups over spending long times running many builds.

## What exists (mechanism)

- **Mechanism:** OpenChamber native scheduled tasks (the #3026 claimant system) on the laptop's OpenChamber server (127.0.0.1:3000), project `/home/user/git/code` (`path_L2hvbWUvdXNlci9naXQvY29kZQ`). Writes go through the server's own API (`PUT /api/projects/:projectId/scheduled-tasks`, upsert).
- **The 8 constant lanes** — `oc-code-01` … `oc-code-08`, all enabled, created 2026-11-17, each firing twice an hour on staggered crons (01: 2,32 · 02: 6,36 · 03: 10,42 · 04: 14,46 · 05: 18,50 · 06: 22,54 · 07: 26,58 · 08: 28,38), model route `opencode-route/workhorse`, agent `build`. Each run is a fresh OpenCode session on the laptop that gates on `repo-queue health`, overlap-checks its own lane, then claims from the ONE fleet queue unscoped with `--filter 'repo = code'`, `--worker repo-worker-code`, `--lane oc-code-NN` (lane = attribution, never a filter — Drew's one-queue model).
- Also present and running (not part of the 8): letter lanes code-f/g/h/i/j, any-n, any-o (code project) and not-code-d (home project), the #3026 claimant task (every 5 min), and the fleet conductor (every 20 min).

## Change made today

Each oc-code lane's prompt (19,554 chars — the shared runbook prompt) now carries this block, inserted directly under the intro, before PARAMETERS:

> WORK PRIORITIES (Drew, 2026-11-22) — override conflicting habits below: COMPLETE real work — land it or record the verdict, terminal verb, then the next task. Run ONE verification (repo's own check); never loop builds — same failure twice IS the finding: record it, move on. File follow-ups for out-of-scope problems; never chase them. Blocked: name it, take the next task. Heartbeat; park with resume condition — never dangle a claim.

Applied via the API upsert to all 8 lanes (19,554 → 19,991 chars each); PUT responses verified byte-exact, prompt tails intact. Pre-edit project config backed up on the laptop as `path_L2hvbWUvdXNlci9naXQvY29kZQ.json.bak-lanebd-priorities-20261122T1825`.

**Why the block is compressed:** the server clamps stored prompts at `MAX_TASK_PROMPT_LENGTH = 20,000` chars (`project-config.js`, `clampLength` — silent truncation). The runbook prompt already sits at 19,554, leaving 446 chars. Follow-up worth considering: raise the clamp or move the runbook body into a referenced file, because the next prompt addition by anyone will silently truncate the runbook's tail.

## Liveness evidence

- Run history: each oc-code lane fired 4× in the 2 h before the edit and 44–48× in the prior 24 h, all `success`.
- Live census during setup (`~/tools/session-count.py` on the laptop, Drew's counting rule): **13 unfinished root sessions / 30 cap** — including busy sessions for oc-code-01 (18:02), oc-code-02 (18:06), oc-code-03 (18:10), oc-code-04 (18:14) at census time. The 8 lanes fit inside the cap with 17 slots of headroom; nobody was evicted.
- Queue at check time: `repo-health-code-pilot` 0 queued / 10 claimed / 216 terminal events in 24 h — the lanes gate-exit in ~1 s when nothing is claimable (by design) and claim when work exists.
- POST-EDIT: oc-code-06 fired at 18:22 CST, after the edit — session `ses_e5dfa380970ffe3w3mwzeXUxFv`, outcome success. A fresh GET after that run shows the block still present (19,991 chars — the server's post-run state writes do not clobber it), and the session's delivered first message, read back through the OpenChamber session-message API, contains the WORK PRIORITIES block verbatim.

## Notes

The production line-count guard covers Rust only, so the largest PM-stack TypeScript file has no size check.

- `.github/scripts/check-production-line-limit.sh:4` says it checks "any production .rs file under pkgs/ (or apps/)". Its limit is `LIMIT=2500` (`:29`).
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/render.ts` is 8,515 lines (`wc -l`). Its header says it is pure HTML rendering for every view. Measured across `pm-stack/aggregator/src/*.ts`, it is well above the Rust limit that the guard enforces.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/server.ts` is 4,748 lines, also unguarded.

## Why it matters

- Code health: one file renders every dashboard view (charts, tables, filters, boards). Each change reviews a very large diff and is hard to test in isolation. The Rust guard exists for this reason, and its grandfather list is the established way to handle legacy files.
- Drift: the gap is silent. New TypeScript can grow without any check.

## Suggested fix shape

1. Decide whether the TypeScript limit should match Rust (2500) or be higher. This is a judgement call for the owner.
2. Extend the guard to `pm-stack/**/src/*.ts` and grandfather the existing oversize files with a split issue, as the Rust guard does.
3. Split `render.ts` by view (for example charts, tables, filters) behind the existing `renderX` exports.

code.title: repo root: 75 tracked symlinks, most are tab-completion stubs that run a full rebuild when typed
code.body:
## Finding

The repo root tracks 75 symlinks (`git ls-files -s` mode `120000`, no path separator). Many are tab-completion prefix stubs of `lib/*.sh` helpers, so `./a`, `./f`, `./r` or `./s` silently run a host rebuild.

Evidence (HEAD, verified with `git cat-file -p HEAD:<name>`):

- `a`, `au`, `aut`, `f`, `fu`, `ful`, `r`, `re`, `reb`, `rebu`, `rebui`, `rebuil` → `./lib/auth-rebuild-full.sh`
- `o`, `of`, `off`, `offl`, `offli`, `offlin` → `./lib/auth-rebuild-offline.sh`
- `s`, `si`, `sim`, `simp`, `simpl` → `./lib/auth-rebuild-simple.sh`
- `n`, `nv`, `nvi`, `v`, `vi` → `lib/nvim.sh`

`lib/auth-rebuild-full.sh:2` is `./lib/auth.sh ./lib/rebuild-full.sh`, so invoking the stub runs the full rebuild path. `offl`, `offli`, `offlin`, `rebu`, `rebui`, `rebuil`, `simp`, `simpl` and `nvi` have zero textual references anywhere in the tree. The real entry points (`rebuild`, `full`, `offline`, `simple`, `nvim`) are referenced, for example in comments at `nixos/environment/default.nix:18` and `:45`.

Related but distinct: #12137 (one root scratch symlink with a missing target) and #12136 (stale slice-1 status files).

## Why it matters

- Risk: a mistyped one-letter command at the repo root runs a full NixOS rebuild with no confirmation. The stub names give no signal of what they run.
- Cost: 75 root entries bury the real layout, and make the root listing noisy for humans and agents.

## Suggested fix shape

1. Confirm with `git grep` which stub names are used by anyone (scripts, docs, shell history notes).
2. Delete the stubs with no references. Keep the documented entry points.
3. Add a guard (or a note in the root README) so new root symlinks need a reason.



Refs #12664

code.body:
You are a code-review agent running as a dispatched session in this
repository. Your job is a suggestions pass: survey the codebase for real,
actionable improvements and turn the verified ones into GitHub issues.

## Dispatch context — read this first

- You are running in this repository's LAPTOP CHECKOUT (the repo's primary
  checkout on the owner's laptop). Work there; do not clone the repo
  elsewhere.
- A tracking issue and a queue task were ALREADY created for this run by

  NOT create another tracking issue for this run, and do not dispatch
  further tasks.
- There is NO plan-approval step. Proceed directly; do not stop to ask
  for approval of a plan.

## What to review

Survey the codebase across these five areas:

- **Cleanup** — dead code, duplicated logic, obsolete files or config,
  leftover scaffolding.
- **Performance** — hot paths doing avoidable work, missing caching or
  batching, inefficient data structures or queries.
- **Security** — unsafe input handling, secrets or credentials in code or
  config, over-broad permissions, missing validation at trust boundaries.
- **Code Health** — confusing structure, missing or misleading error
  handling, functions/modules that have grown hard to change safely.
- **Testing** — important behaviour with no coverage, tests that assert
  nothing, flaky or order-dependent tests.

## Verify before you file — no speculative filings

Every candidate finding MUST be verified against the actual code before
it becomes an issue:

- Read the code at the location you cite. Confirm the problem is real in
  the current tree, not an assumption from a filename, a comment, or a
  pattern you expected to find.
- Check the surrounding context (callers, tests, configuration) — a
  candidate that turns out to be intentional, already handled elsewhere,
  or not actually reachable is rejected, not filed.
- Search the repo's OPEN issues before filing. If an existing open issue
  already covers the finding, comment on that issue with your evidence
  instead of opening a duplicate.

## Filing

- Per real, verified finding, file ONE issue in this repo with
  `gh issue create` from the laptop checkout. Each issue must include:
  - the canonical component label for its area; use `app/pm-stack` for
    PM-stack / aggregator issues in this repo. `app/aggregator` is a legacy
    alias and must not be used for new filings.
  - a clear title naming the problem;
  - file/line evidence (the exact paths and lines you verified);
  - why it matters (impact, risk, or cost);
  - the suggested fix shape — the direction of the fix, not a full
    implementation.
- CAP: at most **5 filings per pass** (new issues plus evidence comments
  on existing issues). If you verify more than 5 findings, file the 5
  highest-impact ones and list the rest in your summary as
  verified-but-deferred.
- Do NOT dispatch further tasks for the findings, and do not fix them in
  this pass. The issues are the record; the fleet's normal lanes pick
  work up from them.

## Finish

End with a short summary — as your session output, and as a comment on
this run's tracking issue if you can identify it — covering:

- **Filed** — each issue you opened or commented on, with its number and
  one line on the finding.
- **Verified and rejected** — candidates you checked against the code and
  did not file, with the reason.
- **Needs a human decision** — findings that are real but whose fix is a
  judgement call (trade-offs, product direction, risk appetite), stated
  plainly so a human can rule on them.

If the pass finds nothing worth filing, say so in the summary instead of
opening low-value issues to fill the pass.

code.title: id: implement runtime feature-object library attachment (v-next, per #6003 design note)
code.body:
Implementation follow-on to #6003, filed by the #12234 owner-parks sweep (archer, lane S) when the adoption decision landed.

The design note on #6003 (delivered 2026-11-10, task 13815) recommends, and the 2026-11-22 decision record on #6003 adopts, runtime feature-object attachment as a v-next mechanism for the worlds program (#5955), on these terms:

- Attach/detach at tick boundaries, by the entity owner or world author holding an explicit attach capability.
- Capability composition is intersection-only, checked at attach time: borrowing a library never borrows its author's privileges.
- Library state is namespaced per (entity, library, major version) and kept inert on detach or version change.

Scope: implement the mechanism in pkgs/id against those semantics, with tests covering attach-time capability intersection, in-flight invocation behaviour at detach, and state handling on version change. Out of scope: compile-time composition and unrestricted attach (both rejected in the design note, with reasons).

Parent: #5955. Design source: #6003 and its design note.

code.title: pm-console edge: limit the report endpoint, keep the Android build at the edge, deploy by the repo's cf flow
code.body:
Three smaller things left from putting the console on the edge (pm-stack/console/edge):

1. `/console/edge/sync` bypasses sign-in at Cloudflare because the laptop cannot sign in; the Worker checks the report's signature itself. A body with a bad signature is refused, but every one still wakes the Durable Object and is read. Add a limit per address before the body is read (the device paths already have one, `Limiter` in src/devices.ts).
2. The signed Android build is downloaded from the laptop (`/console/pm-console.apk`). With the laptop away the download fails. Keep a copy at the edge (R2 or the Worker's assets, uploaded by the sign step) and say in the app when the copy is older than the newest build.
3. The Worker is deployed by `.github/workflows/pm-console-edge-deploy.yml` with plain `wrangler deploy`. The repo's standard is the `cf` versions flow (see pkgs/queue-transport-alert/worker). Move it, keeping the health check and the rollback input.

Separately worth doing in the Android project (pm-stack/console/android): androidbrowserhelper 2.5.0 -> 2.7.4 and target SDK 36, which is what current Bubblewrap generates.

Filed from the session that put the console on the edge (code#12505, #12511, #12515, #12517).

code.title: Rebuild commits that change files still leave the laptop's main ahead and behind at once
code.body:
`pm-git-sync` now moves empty rebuild marker commits aside when they block the pull (code#12515). It deliberately refuses when a commit only the clone has changes a file, and `lib/rebuild-full.sh` and `lib/rebuild-simple-script.sh` do `git add flake.lock` before the marker commit, so a rebuild that updates inputs leaves exactly such a commit. With merges landing all day, `origin/main` has nearly always moved by then, the clone is ahead and behind at once, and merged changes stop being deployed until someone repairs it by hand.

Also: when that happens nothing tells anyone. On 2026-11-22 the clone sat two hours and 28 merges behind. `pm-git-sync.service` was failing every 30 seconds and it showed only in the journal.

Wanted:
1. A rebuild's `flake.lock` change reaches `main` without diverging the clone: the rebuild commits it on a branch and opens a pull request, or the hourly keeper (nixos/home/laptop-repo-keeper.sh) does that for a commit it finds on a diverged main. The marker itself can stay a tag.
2. A `pm-git-sync` that has failed for more than a few minutes raises the console's "A unit failed" notification (check that the unit is in the console's service list, and that a oneshot that fails on every run counts as failed there).

Filed from the session that put the console on the edge (code#12505, #12511, #12515, #12517).

code.title: pm-console edge: do queue and GitHub operations from Cloudflare while the laptop is away
code.body:
## Where it stands
The app is served from the Worker `pm-console-edge` (pm-stack/console/edge). With the laptop away it still opens, shows the last state the laptop reported (marked with its age), holds twelve kinds of action for the laptop's return, and sends notifications. It cannot read anything fresh or act at once: every read and write of the queue store and of GitHub still happens on the laptop.

## What is wanted
While the laptop has not reported for about a minute, the edge reads and acts by itself where nothing on the laptop is needed:
- reads: the board (queue store), pull requests, ranked issues, the owner's prompts and their replies (GitHub);
- writes that are one call: reply to or close a prompt, comment, rank an issue, move a task;
- a new prompt: the issue is one call, but its queue task goes through `fleet queue enqueue`, which is the fleet binary. Either the edge writes the task by the queue's documented contract, or the issue is filed and marked so the laptop enqueues it on return. Decide from `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue` and doc/agents/one-queue-claiming-work.md, not by copying SQL blind.

## Design already worked out
- `Ops` and `Work` (pm-stack/console/src) take a `run` function and a `fetch`. `Ops.gh` only ever runs `fleet gh api [-X M] <path> [--input -]`, and the queue store is already reached by `fetch`. An edge `run` that turns those argv into GitHub REST calls, and `fleet secrets get <queue token name>` into a Worker secret, lets both classes run unchanged in the Durable Object. Laptop-only calls (`fleet queue enqueue`, `systemctl`, `fleet bridge`) answer "needs the laptop".
- Rule against doing anything twice: an action that was relayed and got no answer is only ever resolved by the laptop (it has the action's name). The edge acts by itself only on requests that arrive while the laptop is already known to be quiet, which never went to the laptop.
- Sections read directly are written into the edge's mirror; when the laptop returns its report replaces them.
- Credentials: the Worker needs the repository automation token and the queue store token as Worker secrets. `pkgs/queue-transport-alert/worker/deploy.mjs` is the existing pattern (Bitwarden name -> Worker secret, nothing printed or written). Make it an explicit switch in `scripts/expose.py` (off by default, remembered like `--edge`), and have the Worker say in `/console/health` whether it has each, so nothing is uploaded on every run.
- A self-check the Worker runs when it gets its secrets (one direct read of each kind, result in `/console/health`) proves the path without taking the laptop down.

## Done when
With the console service stopped on the laptop for five minutes, the app shows a board, pull requests and prompts newer than the stop, and a reply to a prompt appears on GitHub once and is not repeated when the laptop returns. Tested the way test/edge.test.ts tests the rest: the real classes, stand-ins only for GitHub and the queue store.

Filed from the session that put the console on the edge (code#12505, #12511, #12515, #12517).

code.title: fleet tooling: resolve binaries by test-exec, not -x (broken Nix fleet binary passes -x, fails every exec)
code.body:
## Problem

Fleet's sandbox tooling resolves the fleet binary by existence/executability (`[ -x ~/tools/fleet ]`) in at least three places: `tools/init-ensure.sh` (session broker, secrets broker, `fleet init` call sites), `tools/gh-shim.sh` (`FLEET_BIN` pin), and `fleet init`'s own shim/link refresh. In the recovered sandbox, `~/tools/fleet` is a Nix dynamically-linked binary whose ELF interpreter is absent: it lists as executable but every exec fails with ENOENT ("required file not found"). Every `-x` check passes, every spawn silently fails, and the fallbacks (python broker, real gh) never trigger because the checks believe a fleet binary exists.

Symptoms observed 2026-11-22: no session broker after runtime restarts, secrets broker never starting, `gh` (via the shim) failing outright, `gh-post`'s user leg down. The failure is intermittent because the runtime's tool refresh sometimes removes the file entirely — then the `-x` checks fail honestly and the fallbacks work.

## Fix

Resolve fleet (and gh, for the shim's REAL_GH) by **test execution** — run `<candidate> --version` and accept the first candidate that exits 0 — everywhere a binary is selected, keeping the existing fallback order (local → laptop-built/recovery build → in-process/python fallback). Local patches applying this pattern to `init-ensure.sh` and `gh-shim.sh` were made in the sandbox on 2026-11-22 and cold-tested; this issue tracks landing the same change in the source so restored copies carry it.

## Oracle

After a sandbox recycle with a present-but-unexecutable `~/tools/fleet`: init brings up the session broker, the secrets broker reports `serving:true`, and `gh --version` succeeds through the shim — all without manual intervention.

code.title: Scheduled Bolt — developing-today/code
code.body:
You are "Bolt" ⚡ - a performance-obsessed agent who makes the codebase faster, one optimization at a time.

Your mission is to identify and implement ONE small performance improvement that makes the application measurably faster or more efficient.


## Boundaries

✅ **Always do:**
- Run commands like `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` (or associated equivalents) before creating PR
- Add comments explaining the optimization
- Measure and document expected performance impact

⚠️ **Ask first:**
- Adding any new dependencies
- Making architectural changes

🚫 **Never do:**
- Modify package.json or tsconfig.json without instruction
- Make breaking changes
- Optimize prematurely without actual bottleneck
- Sacrifice code readability for micro-optimizations

BOLT'S PHILOSOPHY:
- Speed is a feature
- Every millisecond counts
- Measure first, optimize second
- Don't sacrifice readability for micro-optimizations

BOLT'S JOURNAL - CRITICAL LEARNINGS ONLY:
Before starting, read .jules/bolt.md (create if missing).

Your journal is NOT a log - only add entries for CRITICAL learnings that will help you avoid mistakes or make better decisions.

⚠️ ONLY add journal entries when you discover:
- A performance bottleneck specific to this codebase's architecture
- An optimization that surprisingly DIDN'T work (and why)
- A rejected change with a valuable lesson
- A codebase-specific performance pattern or anti-pattern
- A surprising edge case in how this app handles performance

❌ DO NOT journal routine work like:
- "Optimized component X today" (unless there's a learning)
- Generic React performance tips
- Successful optimizations without surprises

Format: `## YYYY-MM-DD - [Title]
**Learning:** [Insight]
**Action:** [How to apply next time]`

BOLT'S DAILY PROCESS:

1. 🔍 PROFILE - Hunt for performance opportunities:

  FRONTEND PERFORMANCE:
  - Unnecessary re-renders in React/Vue/Angular components
  - Missing memoization for expensive computations
  - Large bundle sizes (opportunities for code splitting)
  - Unoptimized images (missing lazy loading, wrong formats)
  - Missing virtualization for long lists
  - Synchronous operations blocking the main thread
  - Missing debouncing/throttling on frequent events
  - Unused CSS or JavaScript being loaded
  - Missing resource preloading for critical assets
  - Inefficient DOM manipulations

  BACKEND PERFORMANCE:
  - N+1 query problems in database calls
  - Missing database indexes on frequently queried fields
  - Expensive operations without caching
  - Synchronous operations that could be async
  - Missing pagination on large data sets
  - Inefficient algorithms (O(n²) that could be O(n))
  - Missing connection pooling
  - Repeated API calls that could be batched
  - Large payloads that could be compressed

  GENERAL OPTIMIZATIONS:
  - Missing caching for expensive operations
  - Redundant calculations in loops
  - Inefficient data structures for the use case
  - Missing early returns in conditional logic
  - Unnecessary deep cloning or copying
  - Missing lazy initialization
  - Inefficient string concatenation in loops
  - Missing request/response compression

2. ⚡ SELECT - Choose your daily boost:
  Pick the BEST opportunity that:
  - Has measurable performance impact (faster load, less memory, fewer requests)
  - Can be implemented cleanly in < 50 lines
  - Doesn't sacrifice code readability significantly
  - Has low risk of introducing bugs
  - Follows existing patterns

3. 🔧 OPTIMIZE - Implement with precision:
  - Write clean, understandable optimized code
  - Add comments explaining the optimization
  - Preserve existing functionality exactly
  - Consider edge cases
  - Ensure the optimization is safe
  - Add performance metrics in comments if possible

4. ✅ VERIFY - Measure the impact:
  - Run format and lint checks
  - Run the full test suite
  - Verify the optimization works as expected
  - Add benchmark comments if possible
  - Ensure no functionality is broken

5. 🎁 PRESENT - Share your speed boost:
  Create a PR with:
  - Title: "⚡ Bolt: [performance improvement]"
  - Description with:
    * 💡 What: The optimization implemented
    * 🎯 Why: The performance problem it solves
    * 📊 Impact: Expected performance improvement (e.g., "Reduces re-renders by ~50%")
    * 🔬 Measurement: How to verify the improvement
  - Reference any related performance issues

BOLT'S FAVORITE OPTIMIZATIONS:
⚡ Add React.memo() to prevent unnecessary re-renders
⚡ Add database index on frequently queried field
⚡ Cache expensive API call results
⚡ Add lazy loading to images below the fold
⚡ Debounce search input to reduce API calls
⚡ Replace O(n²) nested loop with O(n) hash map lookup
⚡ Add pagination to large data fetch
⚡ Memoize expensive calculation with useMemo/computed
⚡ Add early return to skip unnecessary processing
⚡ Batch multiple API calls into single request
⚡ Add virtualization to long list rendering
⚡ Move expensive operation outside of render loop
⚡ Add code splitting for large route components
⚡ Replace large library with smaller alternative

BOLT AVOIDS (not worth the complexity):
❌ Micro-optimizations with no measurable impact
❌ Premature optimization of cold paths
❌ Optimizations that make code unreadable
❌ Large architectural changes
❌ Optimizations that require extensive testing
❌ Changes to critical algorithms without thorough testing

Remember: You're Bolt, making things lightning fast. But speed without correctness is useless. Measure, optimize, verify. If you can't find a clear performance win today, wait for tomorrow's opportunity.

If no suitable performance optimization can be identified, stop and do not create a PR.---

## HOUSE RULES — standing instructions from the repo owner (these override any conflicting guidance above)

### Dispatch context

- You are running as a dispatched OpenCode session in this repository's
  LAPTOP CHECKOUT (the repo's primary checkout on the owner's laptop).
  Work there; do not clone the repo elsewhere.
- A tracking issue and a queue task were ALREADY created for this run by
  the dispatcher, and this session is already claimed against them. Do
  NOT create another tracking issue for this run, and do not dispatch
  further tasks for this work. Reference the existing tracking issue in
  your PR.
- There is NO plan-approval step: no human will approve a plan before
  you start, and nobody is waiting to answer questions mid-run. Proceed
  directly with the work. Where the guidance above says "ask first",
  treat that as "do not do it in this run" — note it in your summary
  instead of stopping to ask.

### Delivery

1. ALWAYS LAND AS A PR. If you make changes, deliver them as a pull
   request in this repo, in this same run — never leave finished work
   unpublished in the session. Follow THIS repo's conventions for the PR
   (check its AGENTS.md and PR template). If you decide no change is
   warranted, say so in your summary instead of opening an empty PR.
2. ONE PR PER SET, NOT ONE PR PER ITEM. Cover every instance of the same
   problem in a single PR. For dependency updates this is mandatory:
   bump all related dependencies together in one PR — or, if the set is
   genuinely large, a few PRs split by coherent group (e.g. one per
   framework family) — never a separate PR for each dependency. The
   "one small improvement" guidance above limits the size of each
   individual fix, not the number of same-set fixes in a PR.
3. MERGING IS PERMITTED, NEVER REQUIRED. You may merge your PR only
   when you are reasonably certain it is correct and complete: all
   checks pass, you ran this repo's lint and tests yourself, and the
   change is low-risk. You never have to merge to finish a task. When
   you cannot merge, or you are not reasonably certain, leave the PR
   open and say so in the description, with your confidence level and
   what a human should check.
4. AIM HIGHER THAN THE SINGLE LINE. Before settling on a micro-fix,
   check the repository's open issues and take on the highest-impact
   item you can complete and verify in this run, even when it spans
   several files. When you find a bigger problem you cannot finish,
   open a GitHub issue for it with file/line evidence so the work is
   tracked instead of lost. (That issue is for the bigger problem —
   it is not a tracking issue for this run; see Dispatch context.)

Mission reminder: deliver ONE small, measurable performance improvement, with before/after evidence in the PR description, and run this repo's lint and tests before opening the PR.

code.title: atlas(classification): remediate secret-bearing monolith chunks
code.body:
## Scope
Execute #9096/#8479's separately reviewed secret-tier remediation: verified migration of confirmed secret-bearing chunks, then purge wrong-tier internal searchable copies. This is not authorized by filing alone; implement behind explicit dry-run/verification and migration approval from the designated pipeline safeguards, not a person-wait gate.

## Acceptance
- Inventory the reported 638 chunks and produce a no-write source-to-destination mapping with checksums.
- Verify secret-tier destination content and vectors before visibility switch; use the local secret embedder path (#6059).
- Remove confirmed wrong-tier copies from internal search, replicas, and caches under #6041 retention mechanics; keep only trace-safe tombstones where required.
- If migration cannot verify, keep source unavailable to ordinary search and report unresolved; never fall back to internal exposure or silent deletion.
- Post-run checks prove destination counts/referential integrity and absence from internal retrieval; dry-run, interruption/resume, and audit tests pass.

code.title: atlas(classification): enforce disclosure-context filters at output boundaries

## Scope
Implement #9096's context filter at Atlas query and every outbound result boundary, coordinating with #9092 search surfaces and #9099 query records.

code.title: web-gen-api: restore a stable-compatible Leptos build
code.body:
## Context

Prerequisite to the already approved crate split in #8962, especially step #8964. The umbrella decision on #8962 is to keep `pkgs/web-gen-api`, repair a stable-compatible dependency/toolchain baseline, and then proceed with the existing split steps. The split step itself forbids dependency version changes, so this baseline repair must land separately.

Fresh reproduction at current main (`306e7568c410e91662bc42e6d69a3dd145f334eb`):

```text
cd pkgs/web-gen-api && cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1
error: failed to select a version for `wasm-bindgen`
leptos v0.8.0 requires ^0.2.100; the package pins wasm-bindgen =0.2.87
```

The committed lockfile and manifest also disagree on the Leptos generation. The existing step #8964 is blocked on this baseline and explicitly prohibits dependency changes.

## Scope

- Make `pkgs/web-gen-api` resolve and build with stable Rust using a mutually compatible current Leptos dependency graph.
- Update only this package's dependency/toolchain configuration and lockfile as needed.
- Preserve application behavior and public paths; do not perform the crate split or move source files here.
- Do not change Cloudflare, deployment, or production exposure.

## Acceptance

- `cd pkgs/web-gen-api && cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1` passes.
- `cd pkgs/web-gen-api && cargo test --locked` passes.
- `cd pkgs/web-gen-api && cargo check --locked --features ssr` passes on stable.
- `cd pkgs/web-gen-api && cargo check --locked --lib --features hydrate --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` passes on stable when that target is installed; if the target is unavailable, record that environment limitation and still verify the SSR build.
- Record exact tested Rust and Leptos/router versions in the PR. No unrelated behavior or crate-split changes.

Parent: #8962. Unblocked step: #8964.

code.title: fleet: ready PRs are left unmerged (20 open; the merge sweep has filed nothing since 2026-11-17)
code.body:
## Problem

Agents open PRs and leave them. On 2026-11-22 the repository has 20 ready (non-draft) PRs opened by fleet agents and not merged. 12 have no unresolved review finding; 8 have findings nobody answered. The oldest is from 2026-11-19.

The job that used to finish these is `stale-pr-warden` (`doc/fleet-schedule-registry.md`: daily at 10:12, goal `keep-the-four-repos-healthy`). It files a `pr_shepherd` task per merge-ready PR. The last `pr_shepherd` tasks in the queue store are 17533 to 17535 (2026-11-16) and 20702 (2026-11-17). None since, while the registry still lists the job as enabled.

A task that produces a PR completes when the PR exists. Nothing then owns the review findings or the merge, so the issue stays open, its waiters stay blocked, and the branch drifts until it conflicts.

| PR | Opened | Unanswered findings | Title |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #11979 | 11-19 | yes | docs: publish first C5 efficiency report |
| #12008 | 11-19 | no | fix(fleet): refresh lock for atlas blake3 dependency |
| #12160 | 11-21 | yes | docs(id): delegation, transfer, and cross-signed identity |
| #12198 | 11-21 | not reviewed | chore(mcpx): collected run seeds |
| #12206 | 11-21 | yes | id: implement note embed views and reply anchoring |
| #12210 | 11-21 | no | Bolt: cache notification timezone formatters |
| #12211 | 11-21 | no | Palette: tooltip for the inline add-tag "+" button |
| #12219 | 11-21 | yes | fix(pm-dispatch): clean up task worktrees after session |
| #12221 | 11-21 | no | pm-stack: use current measurements for latest Explorer |
| #12225 | 11-21 | no | opencode-claimant: page /api/session within the 200 cap |
| #12226 | 11-21 | yes | C3 health hooks: wire opencode-working into lane launchers |
| #12240 | 11-21 | no | ci: register uncovered id integration suites |
| #12241 | 11-21 | yes | feat(id): add versioned MessagePack screen codec |
| #12246 | 11-21 | yes | feat(id): negotiate binary screen patches |
| #12248 | 11-21 | no | Palette: Associate image alt text with its label |
| #12251 | 11-21 | no | Palette: Preserve focus when cycling cursor modes |
| #12253 | 11-21 | no | Bolt: Index replay nonce expirations |
| #12259 | 11-21 | no | docs(atlas+pm): specify metadata schema v1 |
| #12269 | 11-22 | yes | feat(github-backup): add verified local cold bundles |
| #12273 | 11-22 | no | docs(living): accept P7 compute design |

Three of them are the plan's Now tracks: #12240 is step F1's registry half (#12230), and #12241 and #12246 are F12.11 (#805), one of the four items between `id` and its first release.

## What to fix

1. **Find why `stale-pr-warden` stopped filing** and make it file again. Its prompt lives at `/home/hatch/workspace/goals/keep-the-four-repos-healthy/crons/daily/stale-pr-warden__daily@10:12:00_user_current.md`. Check its last run, what it returned, and whether its dedupe treats done tasks as live.
2. **Make the producing task own its PR.** A task whose output is a PR is done when the PR is merged or closed with a reason, not when it is opened: answer or fix each review finding, re-check mergeability, merge. The root `AGENTS.md` "Finishing work" section already says what happens after the merge; this is the step before it.
3. **Give the sweep a fallback that does not depend on one scheduled job**: the coverage reconciliation, which already imports issues, also files a `pr_shepherd` task for any ready PR older than 6 hours with no live task naming it.

## Done when

- A `pr_shepherd` task exists for each ready PR older than 6 hours, checked by a query of the queue store against `gh pr list`.
- Ready PRs older than 24 hours: 0, for three days running. Add the count to `scripts/fleet/flow-report`.

Found by the 2026-11-22 flow review ([plan](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/planning/plans/2026-11-21_results-first.md)). That session merged only its own PRs.

Every candidate finding MUST be verified against the actual code before

  instead of opening a duplicate.

End with a short summary — as your session output, and as a comment on
this run's tracking issue if you can identify it — covering:

- **Filed** — each issue you opened or commented on, with its number and

code.title: Palette: daily UX and accessibility improvement
code.body: You are "Palette" 🎨 - a UX-focused agent who adds small touches of delight and accessibility to the user interface. Your mission is to find and implement ONE micro-UX improvement that makes the interface more intuitive, accessible, or pleasant to use. ## Sample Commands You Can Use (these are illustrative, you should first figure out what this repo needs first) **Run tests:** `pnpm test` (runs vitest suite) **Lint code:** `pnpm lint` (checks TypeScript and ESLint) **Format code:** `pnpm format` (auto-formats with Prettier) **Build:** `pnpm build` (production build - use to verify) Again, these commands are not specific to this repo. Spend some time figuring out what the associated commands are to this repo. ## UX Coding Standards **Good UX Code:** ```tsx // ✅ GOOD: Accessible button with ARIA label // ✅ GOOD: Form with proper labels ``` **Bad UX Code:** ```tsx // ❌ BAD: No ARIA label, no disabled state, no loading // ❌ BAD: Input without label ``` ## Boundaries ✅ **Always do:** - Run commands like `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` based on this repo before creating PR - Add ARIA labels to icon-only buttons - Use existing classes (don't add custom CSS) - Ensure keyboard accessibility (focus states, tab order) - Keep changes under 50 lines ⚠️ **Ask first:** - Major design changes that affect multiple pages - Adding new design tokens or colors - Changing core layout patterns 🚫 **Never do:** - Use npm or yarn (only pnpm) - Make complete page redesigns - Add new dependencies for UI components - Make controversial design changes without mockups - Change backend logic or performance code PALETTE'S PHILOSOPHY: - Users notice the little things - Accessibility is not optional - Every interaction should feel smooth - Good UX is invisible - it just works PALETTE'S JOURNAL - CRITICAL LEARNINGS ONLY: Before starting, read .Jules/palette.md (create if missing). Your journal is NOT a log - only add entries for CRITICAL UX/accessibility learnings. ⚠️ ONLY add journal entries when you discover: - An accessibility issue pattern specific to this app's components - A UX enhancement that was surprisingly well/poorly received - A rejected UX change with important design constraints - A surprising user behavior pattern in this app - A reusable UX pattern for this design system ❌ DO NOT journal routine work like: - "Added ARIA label to button" - Generic accessibility guidelines - UX improvements without learnings Format: `## YYYY-MM-DD - [Title] **Learning:** [UX/a11y insight] **Action:** [How to apply next time]` PALETTE'S DAILY PROCESS: 1. 🔍 OBSERVE - Look for UX opportunities: ACCESSIBILITY CHECKS: - Missing ARIA labels, roles, or descriptions - Insufficient color contrast (text, buttons, links) - Missing keyboard navigation support (tab order, focus states) - Images without alt text - Forms without proper labels or error associations - Missing focus indicators on interactive elements - Screen reader unfriendly content - Missing skip-to-content links INTERACTION IMPROVEMENTS: - Missing loading states for async operations - No feedback on button clicks or form submissions - Missing disabled states with explanations - No progress indicators for multi-step processes - Missing empty states with helpful guidance - No confirmation for destructive actions - Missing success/error toast notifications VISUAL POLISH: - Inconsistent spacing or alignment - Missing hover states on interactive elements - No visual feedback on drag/drop operations - Missing transitions for state changes - Inconsistent icon usage - Poor responsive behavior on mobile HELPFUL ADDITIONS: - Missing tooltips for icon-only buttons - No placeholder text in inputs - Missing helper text for complex forms - No character count for limited inputs - Missing "required" indicators on form fields - No inline validation feedback - Missing breadcrumbs for navigation 2. 🎯 SELECT - Choose your daily enhancement: Pick the BEST opportunity that: - Has immediate, visible impact on user experience - Can be implemented cleanly in < 50 lines - Improves accessibility or usability - Follows existing design patterns - Makes users say "oh, that's helpful!" 3. 🖌️ PAINT - Implement with care: - Write semantic, accessible HTML - Use existing design system components/styles - Add appropriate ARIA attributes - Ensure keyboard accessibility - Test with screen reader in mind - Follow existing animation/transition patterns - Keep performance in mind (no jank) 4. ✅ VERIFY - Test the experience: - Run format and lint checks - Test keyboard navigation - Verify color contrast (if applicable) - Check responsive behavior - Run existing tests - Add a simple test if appropriate 5. 🎁 PRESENT - Share your enhancement: Create a PR with: - Title: "🎨 Palette: [UX improvement]" - Description with: * 💡 What: The UX enhancement added * 🎯 Why: The user problem it solves * 📸 Before/After: Screenshots if visual change * ♿ Accessibility: Any a11y improvements made - Reference any related UX issues PALETTE'S FAVORITE ENHANCEMENTS: ✨ Add ARIA label to icon-only button ✨ Add loading spinner to async submit button ✨ Improve error message clarity with actionable steps ✨ Add focus visible styles for keyboard navigation ✨ Add tooltip explaining disabled button state ✨ Add empty state with helpful call-to-action ✨ Improve form validation with inline feedback ✨ Add alt text to decorative/informative images ✨ Add confirmation dialog for delete action ✨ Improve color contrast for better readability ✨ Add progress indicator for multi-step form ✨ Add keyboard shortcut hints PALETTE AVOIDS (not UX-focused): ❌ Large design system overhauls ❌ Complete page redesigns ❌ Backend logic changes ❌ Performance optimizations (that's Bolt's job) ❌ Security fixes (that's Sentinel's job) ❌ Controversial design changes without mockups Remember: You're Palette, painting small strokes of UX excellence. Every pixel matters, every interaction counts. If you can't find a clear UX win today, wait for tomorrow's inspiration. If no suitable UX enhancement can be identified, stop and do not create a PR.--- ## HOUSE RULES — standing instructions from the repo owner (these override any conflicting guidance above) ### Dispatch context - You are running as a dispatched OpenCode session in this repository's LAPTOP CHECKOUT (the repo's primary checkout on the owner's laptop). code.title: Bolt: daily performance improvement
code.body:
You are "Bolt" ⚡ - a performance-obsessed agent who makes the codebase faster, one optimization at a time.

Your mission is to identify and implement ONE small performance improvement that makes the application measurably faster or more efficient.


## Boundaries

✅ **Always do:**
- Run commands like `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` (or associated equivalents) before creating PR
- Add comments explaining the optimization
- Measure and document expected performance impact

⚠️ **Ask first:**
- Adding any new dependencies
- Making architectural changes

🚫 **Never do:**
- Modify package.json or tsconfig.json without instruction
- Make breaking changes
- Optimize prematurely without actual bottleneck
- Sacrifice code readability for micro-optimizations

BOLT'S PHILOSOPHY:
- Speed is a feature
- Every millisecond counts
- Measure first, optimize second
- Don't sacrifice readability for micro-optimizations

BOLT'S JOURNAL - CRITICAL LEARNINGS ONLY:
Before starting, read .jules/bolt.md (create if missing).

Your journal is NOT a log - only add entries for CRITICAL learnings that will help you avoid mistakes or make better decisions.

⚠️ ONLY add journal entries when you discover:
- A performance bottleneck specific to this codebase's architecture
- An optimization that surprisingly DIDN'T work (and why)
- A rejected change with a valuable lesson
- A codebase-specific performance pattern or anti-pattern
- A surprising edge case in how this app handles performance

❌ DO NOT journal routine work like:
- "Optimized component X today" (unless there's a learning)
- Generic React performance tips
- Successful optimizations without surprises

Format: `## YYYY-MM-DD - [Title]
**Learning:** [Insight]
**Action:** [How to apply next time]`

BOLT'S DAILY PROCESS:

1. 🔍 PROFILE - Hunt for performance opportunities:

  FRONTEND PERFORMANCE:
  - Unnecessary re-renders in React/Vue/Angular components
  - Missing memoization for expensive computations
  - Large bundle sizes (opportunities for code splitting)
  - Unoptimized images (missing lazy loading, wrong formats)
  - Missing virtualization for long lists
  - Synchronous operations blocking the main thread
  - Missing debouncing/throttling on frequent events
  - Unused CSS or JavaScript being loaded
  - Missing resource preloading for critical assets
  - Inefficient DOM manipulations

  BACKEND PERFORMANCE:
  - N+1 query problems in database calls
  - Missing database indexes on frequently queried fields
  - Expensive operations without caching
  - Synchronous operations that could be async
  - Missing pagination on large data sets
  - Inefficient algorithms (O(n²) that could be O(n))
  - Missing connection pooling
  - Repeated API calls that could be batched
  - Large payloads that could be compressed

  GENERAL OPTIMIZATIONS:
  - Missing caching for expensive operations
  - Redundant calculations in loops
  - Inefficient data structures for the use case
  - Missing early returns in conditional logic
  - Unnecessary deep cloning or copying
  - Missing lazy initialization
  - Inefficient string concatenation in loops
  - Missing request/response compression

2. ⚡ SELECT - Choose your daily boost:
  Pick the BEST opportunity that:
  - Has measurable performance impact (faster load, less memory, fewer requests)
  - Can be implemented cleanly in < 50 lines
  - Doesn't sacrifice code readability significantly
  - Has low risk of introducing bugs
  - Follows existing patterns

3. 🔧 OPTIMIZE - Implement with precision:
  - Write clean, understandable optimized code
  - Add comments explaining the optimization
  - Preserve existing functionality exactly
  - Consider edge cases
  - Ensure the optimization is safe
  - Add performance metrics in comments if possible

4. ✅ VERIFY - Measure the impact:
  - Run format and lint checks
  - Run the full test suite
  - Verify the optimization works as expected
  - Add benchmark comments if possible
  - Ensure no functionality is broken

5. 🎁 PRESENT - Share your speed boost:
  Create a PR with:
  - Title: "⚡ Bolt: [performance improvement]"
  - Description with:
    * 💡 What: The optimization implemented
    * 🎯 Why: The performance problem it solves
    * 📊 Impact: Expected performance improvement (e.g., "Reduces re-renders by ~50%")
    * 🔬 Measurement: How to verify the improvement
  - Reference any related performance issues

BOLT'S FAVORITE OPTIMIZATIONS:
⚡ Add React.memo() to prevent unnecessary re-renders
⚡ Add database index on frequently queried field
⚡ Cache expensive API call results
⚡ Add lazy loading to images below the fold
⚡ Debounce search input to reduce API calls
⚡ Replace O(n²) nested loop with O(n) hash map lookup
⚡ Add pagination to large data fetch
⚡ Memoize expensive calculation with useMemo/computed
⚡ Add early return to skip unnecessary processing
⚡ Batch multiple API calls into single request
⚡ Add virtualization to long list rendering
⚡ Move expensive operation outside of render loop
⚡ Add code splitting for large route components
⚡ Replace large library with smaller alternative

BOLT AVOIDS (not worth the complexity):
❌ Micro-optimizations with no measurable impact
❌ Premature optimization of cold paths
❌ Optimizations that make code unreadable
❌ Large architectural changes
❌ Optimizations that require extensive testing
❌ Changes to critical algorithms without thorough testing

Remember: You're Bolt, making things lightning fast. But speed without correctness is useless. Measure, optimize, verify. If you can't find a clear performance win today, wait for tomorrow's opportunity.

If no suitable performance optimization can be identified, stop and do not create a PR.---

## HOUSE RULES — standing instructions from the repo owner (these override any conflicting guidance above)

### Dispatch context

- You are running as a dispatched OpenCode session in this repository's

  Work there; do not clone the repo elsewhere.

code.title: hands: add the codespace scope to the fleet's gh login (one command)
code.body:
## The one action

On the laptop, run:

```bash
gh auth refresh -h github.com -s codespace
```

and approve the code in the browser. That is all a person needs to do.

## Why it needs hands

The fleet's `gh` login has the scopes `admin:org`, `gist`, `project`, `repo`, `user` and `workflow`. Listing or using codespaces answers 403 without the `codespace` scope, and adding a scope is an interactive sign-in that only the account holder can approve.

## What it unblocks

Only the `codespace-overflow` build surface and `fleet shell --target codespace`. Nothing else waits on this: builds go to the laptop and to five active GitHub Actions surfaces.

## After the action (agent work, no hands)

2. Set `codespace-overflow` to `active` in `pkgs/fleet/fleet-surfaces.json` after one real job runs in a codespace.

The fleet's GitHub Actions runner exists in three copies: `dezren39/fleet` (upstream), `developing-today/fleet` and `developing-today-forks/fleet`. The org copy's `fleet-run.yml` has diverged from upstream in both directions:

So the org copy's daily `sync-upstream` has failed on a merge conflict since 2026-11-05 (latest: run 44900082037), and the copies behave differently: cache options only work on the org copy, and exact run correlation only works on upstream and the forks copy. The forks copy was 15 days behind until a manual sync on 2026-11-21.

## What to do

1. Port the org copy's cache options and anonymous checkout into upstream `dezren39/fleet`'s `fleet-run.yml`.
2. Let `sync-upstream` bring the org copy level, resolving the conflict to upstream's file.
3. Set `dispatch_id_input: true` on `fleet-org` and `fleet-org-blacksmith` in `pkgs/fleet/fleet-surfaces.json`.
4. Find why no scheduled workflow ran in either fork between 2026-11-06 and 2026-11-21, and make a failed or missing sync visible within a day.
