code.title: www.security.cab HTTPS broken since 2026-11-01 - Porkbun uixie forwarding cert expired; the outside-in watch cannot see it
code.body:
Fleet downtime investigation, 2026-11-14 (Drew: "fix why website keep go down").

## What is broken

HTTPS to www.security.cab fails for every real browser: the TLS certificate served by Porkbun's forwarding host (uixie.porkbun.com) is EXPIRED.

Verified 2026-11-14 ~08:55Z from the laptop:
- openssl s_client -servername www.security.cab: subject CN=security.cab, issuer Let's Encrypt YR2, notBefore Aug 3 2026, **notAfter Nov 1 2026 23:59:18 GMT** - expired ~13 days ago. Verify return code 10 (certificate has expired). SANs: *.security.cab, security.cab.
- curl https://www.security.cab/ -> connection result 000 (cert verify failure) from both the sandbox and the laptop, direct to all three uixie IPs.
- Plain HTTP still works: 307 -> http://developing-today.com/ -> news.developing-today.com (200). So the redirect logic is fine; only HTTPS is dead.

## Why nobody caught it

The hourly Globalping watch reports www.security.cab HEALTHY (307) in every run - its HTTP measurement records the status code and does not fail on TLS validity. A cert that expired on Nov 1 has been invisible to the outside-in watch for 13 days. (The idea-engine traffic figures show security.cab still gets ~300k requests/week, mostly over HTTP or from cert-tolerant clients.)

## Account facts (Porkbun API, read-only, fleet keys by name)

- security.cab lives in the Porkbun account "developingtoday" (39 domains), status ACTIVE, autoRenew on, domain itself expires 2027-02-24.
- DNS (Porkbun-hosted): *.security.cab CNAME -> uixie.porkbun.com (the wildcard forwarding setup that the expired cert serves).
- ssl/retrieve via API: "The SSL certificate is not ready for this domain" - Porkbun has no current cert bundle for it.
- The API's /urlforward/* routes return Porkbun's web 404 (control test: /dns/retrieve works fine with the same keys) - cert re-issuance for this setup is NOT reachable through the API the fleet holds.

## Fix paths (needs Drew - see below)

1. Porkbun dashboard (developingtoday account): re-save or re-enable SSL on the security.cab wildcard forwarding so Let's Encrypt re-issues. ~2 minutes in the dashboard; no DNS change.
2. OR move www.security.cab's redirect behind Cloudflare (where Drew's other properties live) with a redirect rule and a Cloudflare-managed cert. This is a DNS change, so it is Drew's call per standing rules.

## Follow-up (fleet-side, separate fix)

The outside-in watch needs a TLS-validating check for security.cab (cert validity + days-to-expiry), because Globalping's status-code verdict structurally cannot see this failure class. Job-body change - needs Drew's yes like any cron change.

<!-- hands:v1 kind=interactive-login action="In the Porkbun dashboard (developingtoday account), re-save or re-enable SSL on the security.cab wildcard forwarding so Let's Encrypt re-issues, then confirm https://www.security.cab/ serves a valid cert." -->

code.title: pm-projector /health stalls >=90s under load - sentinel down alerts fire while the process never restarts
code.body:
Fleet downtime investigation, 2026-11-14 (Drew: "fix why website keep go down").

## Evidence

The PM stack-health sentinel (pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/stack-sentinel.ts) probes the projector at http://127.0.0.1:7801/health with a 10s timeout and declares down after 3 consecutive failed probes (PR #9053 damping, merged 2026-11-12). That config is verified correct in the running tree - the flapping is NOT a probe-config problem anymore.

Down-episode counts from ~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/notifications.jsonl (stack-health, service:projector, episode = one recovered transition):
- 2026-11-11: 46 episodes
- 2026-11-12: 60 episodes
- 2026-11-13: 17 episodes
- 2026-11-14: 5 episodes by 08:39Z (incl. 06:38Z and 07:37Z, each recovering in ~2-4 min)

Meanwhile the projector process itself never restarts: pm-projector.service has run as a single PID (2121) since 2026-11-13 19:29 CST, 578MB memory, ~6m39s CPU in 7h, no restarts in today's journal. So /health stops answering for >=90s windows while the process stays alive - an event-loop stall or a hung await inside the projector (its GitHub projection sync is the prime suspect: a long sync or an unbounded fetch with no timeout would block exactly like this), most frequent when the laptop is loaded (load1 observed 8.58 with ~60 fleet jobs).

User impact today is alert noise + stale board data (the aggregator serves the pages; service:aggregator recorded exactly 1 down in 3 days). But a health endpoint that stalls for minutes is also how a real projector death would hide, and this is the single largest source of stack-health alerts in the fleet.

## Acceptance

- Root cause of the /health stalls named with evidence (e.g. stall windows correlated with projection sync cycles in the projector's own logs).
- 7 consecutive days with zero stack-health 'sent' notifications for service:projector, OR every declared down backed by a journal-verified real failure.
- A regression guard: the stall mechanism (sync blocking the health path) covered by a test or by a heartbeat/watchdog that makes a stall self-evident in logs.

code.title: OpenCode: Whisper STT + TTS as routed pool models — failover, proxying, silence auto-trim
code.body:
Drew's order (2026-11-13, main chat): in addition to using Whisper directly from the Cloudflare models, add Whisper (speech-to-text) and TTS into the OpenCode config, supporting routing pools, auto failover, and proper proxying to the model — possibly a pool for both directions.

Scope:
- Transcription models (Whisper family) and speech models (MeloTTS family) become first-class routable models in the OpenCode config, addressable through route pools like text models are today.
- Pools for both directions: a speech-to-text pool and a text-to-speech pool; evaluate one combined speech pool covering both directions and pick the shape that keeps direction/capability gating clean.
- Auto failover across providers carrying these models (Cloudflare Workers AI first; any other provider in the catalog carrying the same models joins as another door), with the standing routing rules (a 100%-walled leg is not attempted; failure skips to the next leg inside the same request).
- Proper proxying to the model: audio payloads pass through the route layer intact, with per-provider format translation where providers differ (the capabilities supplement's per-provider input-variance rule applies to audio too).
- Automatic silence removal in the OpenCode path as well as the Cloudflare-direct path: audio is trimmed / voice-activity-detected before transcription so silence is not billed or transcribed; for TTS, generated-audio duration is what is billed, so nothing extra is synthesized.
- Capability declarations: audio-in / audio-out capabilities declared on the models and pools per the #9399 capabilities design (brief-capabilities-supplement sections 1-5), so a text-only request never routes to a speech pool and a speech request only lands on models that can serve it.

Sequencing: this is the config/pool layer; the #9399 design mill's capabilities work is the design authority where the two overlap — align, do not fork the design. The voice-line first step (companion issue) uses the Cloudflare-direct route and does not wait on this issue.

Acceptance: a transcription request and a speech request each served through a named pool in the running config, each demonstrably failing over to a second door when the first is made unavailable, with route attempts recorded the same way text attempts are.

code.title: Daily codebase innovation & maintenance
code.body:
Perform a comprehensive daily codebase review, innovation scan, and issue/PR maintenance pass across developing-today/code.

You are acting as an unrestricted principal architect and senior systems engineer. Do not hold back: generate bold ideas, surface hidden gaps, polish proposals, and solve immediate problems opportunistically.
Follow these directives and areas of focus:
### 1. COMPREHENSIVE REPOSITORY & ACTIVITY AUDIT - Inspect recent commits on `main` to understand the latest velocity and architectural direction. - Review open, recently closed, and merged issues and PRs (`gh issue list --state all --limit 50`, `gh pr list --state all --limit 30`). - Review each major package, tool, and subsystem in the repository:
  - **`pkgs/id`**: Distributed identity, cryptographic event log, p2panda synchronization, local event store, group encryption, discovery, and capability delegation.
  - **`pkgs/mcpx`**: Model Context Protocol daemon, multi-server multiplexing, protocol compliance, session leasing, JIT secret prompt vault, and Code Mode projection.
  - **`pkgs/fleet`**: The Rust multicall fleet tools and queue client — automated multi-agent coding workflows, issue triage, and parallel agent execution (the retired packages were removed by PR #5376; audit the fleet queue automation under `pkgs/fleet` and `.github/workflows`, the dispatch actions `.github/actions/pm-dispatch-start` and `.github/actions/pm-dispatch-task`, the scheduler `.github/workflows/pm-scheduled.yml` and its repo-specific scheduled callers, and the CI-breakage automation).
  - **NixOS System Infrastructure & Web Services**: Modules, cloud functions, background daemons, and system services.

### 2. UNRESTRICTED INNOVATION & NEW FEATURE GENERATION - You are NOT restricted by what currently exists. Brainstorm things that *should* exist, would be exceptionally useful, or incorporate frontier concepts:
  - Edge architectures using Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects, KV, and Queues.
  - Distributed SQLite / libSQL / Turso primitives for offline-first, syncable state.
  - Advanced autonomous coding loops, speculative tool execution, and local verification loops.
  - Cross-platform bridges, native desktop integrations, and performance optimizations.
- **Bias Toward Capture**: It is far better to create an issue to triage later than to let a valuable opportunity or insight pass.
### 3. ACTIVE ISSUE & PR MAINTENANCE - **Scope Variety**: Create single large architectural vision issues for strategic direction, or narrow, highly focused issues for targeted improvements. - **Issue Decomposition**: If an existing issue is too broad, ambiguous, or monolithic (including issues created by others), break it apart into a series of clear, modular, linked sub-issues with explicit dependencies. - **Deduplication & Consolidation**: Identify overlapping or duplicate proposals/issues and consolidate them into unified, high-quality reference issues. - **Comments & Spec Refinement**: Leave comments or edit existing issues/PRs to provide missing technical specifications, edge-case analysis, data schemas, or suggested test cases. - **Zero-Context Hand-off Standard**: Every issue you author must be self-contained, citing exact file paths, interfaces, architectural rationale, and verifiable acceptance criteria so a new agent with zero prior context can execute it.

### 4. OPPORTUNISTIC IMPLEMENTATION (QUICK-WIN PRS) - If you identify straightforward bugs, unhandled edge cases, missing test coverage, or clean opportunities to refactor code to prevent future merge conflicts:
  - You are actively encouraged to open small, focused Pull Requests implementing the fix or feature directly.
  - Ensure all added code follows repository standards, includes tests, and passes formatting/linting hooks (`treefmt`, `conform`).
  - Never introduce breaking regressions to existing stable flows.
  - **One PR per coherent set**: batch every instance of the same problem — and all related dependency updates — into a single PR, or a few PRs split by coherent group. Never one PR per item or per dependency.
  - **Prefer tracked, higher-impact work**: before inventing a new micro-fix, check the open issues and implement the highest-impact one you can complete and verify, even when it spans several files.
  - **Merging is permitted, never required**: merge your PR only when checks pass and you are reasonably certain it is correct and low-risk. Otherwise leave it open and state your confidence and what a human should check in the description.

---

code.title: C8 — Atlas ingestion of reports & pages + error-driven investigation boosts
code.body:
# C8 — Atlas ingestion of reports & pages + error-driven investigation boosts

Component of the reporting-architecture program (starter epic #9568).
Source: Drew's directive, Reports chat, 2026-11-13 09:11 CST.
Statements: S4.12, S4.24–S4.30.

## Scope

- **Ingestion.** All report data and pages (C6 pages, C7 rollups, incident
  pages, forecast records) ingest into Atlas **many times a day**, biased
  toward recency and toward datasets Drew named: reports on issues and
  major happenings — so an agent searching a problem learns about an
  incident from a day or two ago and gets the resource links (GitHub,
  database) to go deeper.
- **Link-rich embeddings.** Every link on a page becomes a metadata link
  to the related item; embeddings cross-link an item with the items it
  links (classifications link to the file that caused them), giving
  searches 1–2-step skips between related material.
- **Page metadata schema.** URL exploded into base name, path, file name,
  last path part, port, MIME/media type; is-HTML / is-video flags; page
  kind (report; page with comments + stream; live stream); graphs present
  + libraries used to generate them; the specific scripts (Python/JS) and
  libraries that generated dynamic content or static pictures; all linked
  GitHub issues.
- **Query-planner boosts.** For error-flavored queries (e.g. a new error
  message about a config property never added to the config), the planner
  boosts embeds sorted by recency from reports, issues/PRs with certain
  labels, and direct error-string matches anywhere.
- **Error-driven investigation.** Given an error line (e.g. from a
  found-bugs-and-errors page for ID): find the string's **first
  appearance** across all embedded logs and its event-log add time → time
  range → all issues touching the file that now carries the string →
  PRs/mentions/bug reports for the keywords → commits touching the string
  or its use sites, reviewed in full and associated commit → PR → issue.
  Joined per issue: queue attempts, models used, worktrees used; a check
  for a final commit never pushed; session transcripts read by session ID
  for recorded expectations ("this error may occur; if it does, do X").
- **Class fixes.** Related fixes for the same issue class (label families,
  "rhyming" fixes) assemble into a permanent class fix; class fix +
  investigation tooling combine into the architectural fix that makes the
  class impossible; residual occurrences become routine triage scripts or
  subtasks of a triage job (C2 drains them).

## Boundaries / collisions

- This is an **input to #9091 (Atlas v1)** — its ingestion, classification,
  and query threads (E/G) own the platform; C8 owns the reports/pages
  corpus contract and the investigation recipe. Coordinate, don't fork.
- Metadata/session joins depend on #9073/#9074/#9075 — consume their
  records; where a needed field doesn't exist, file it there.
- Classification is per-embed (Atlas doctrine from #9091/#9095): report
  pages carry mixed sensitivity (public-allowed surfaces are filtered at
  serve time regardless of searcher rights).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Merged design: corpus contract (kinds, cadence, metadata schema),
      cross-link model, planner-boost rules, investigation recipe.
- [ ] Report pages from C6/C7 searchable in Atlas within one ingestion
      cycle, with recency bias demonstrated.
- [ ] One real error string investigated end-to-end by the recipe, with
      the association chain (log → issue → commit → PR) produced.

code.title: C7 — Rollups, design pages, per-project spaces, reports timeline
code.body:
# C7 — Rollups, design pages, per-project spaces, reports timeline

Component of the reporting-architecture program (starter epic #9568).
Source: Drew's directive, Reports chat, 2026-11-13 09:11 CST.
Statements: S4.1–S4.11, S4.13–S4.23 (+ S3.17 timeline input).

## Scope

- **Activity rollups.** Daily (midnight–midnight CT), weekly (Mon–Mon CT),
  monthly, quarterly pages that answer **"What did we do today?"** in
  prose per project — what was worked on, what pivoted and why (issues
  named), and which permanent remediations resulted. Weekly adds: biggest
  items/issues/designs made, modified, or built out; next week's plan;
  queue-prioritization summary + custom report; links/spaces for planned
  items, issues, PRs. Dailies roll into the weekly backwards in time, with
  reach-back context (through Friday of the week before) including how
  past work was used and what issues it later caused.
- **Edit-window doctrine.** Soft windows: daily until early next morning
  (~2/5/8 am) for final details; weekly ~1–2 days; monthly ~3–7 days;
  quarterly ~a week. After a window, edits are restricted to quote blocks,
  end appends, top banners, event-log injections, and a
  post-finalization feedback section. Outcomes that land after a day
  closes are noted on the NEW day's page ("yesterday we also achieved…;
  this confirmed/disproved the hypothesis set up N days ago").
- **Snapshots.** At each period close, the current view is cloned into a
  dated, unpinned, never-updated library space (original name + date /
  week number / year+quarter).
- **Per-project spaces** (Fleet, PM stack, Atlas, ID): what exists; what
  we'd like to exist; what we're actually working on; what we've designed;
  inspiration and end state; open research items; links to reports and
  PM-stack design pages; links to other spaces.
- **Design pages.** One page per design (many/most/all, in priority
  order): subdesign trees with why each is needed (full epic / roadmap
  part / originating document); a status ladder per design — idea →
  planned → initial issue created → initial issue built out → fully
  designed → fully designed with implementation issues — and
  implementation rollups (e.g. 50 issues: 20 done, 10 in progress,
  5 blocked, 15 queued) rolling child → parent → roadmap/epic pages with
  summaries, reasons, statuses, and per-day/week update notes.
  Long-running items get a fresh page per month/quarter.
- **Reports timeline page.** Quarters unfold to months → weeks → days;
  overall activity reports are the first column (name as link, 1–3 big
  positives/negatives, folded detail, deeper unfold without
  click-through); domain weeklies (ID; fleet/queues/PM stack;
  Atlas/Turso/Cloudflare incl. LLM + tertiary cloud quotas) sit as
  columns/subitems beside the overall weekly; dated special reports
  (e.g. a queue overhaul) attach to their day; long designs appear as
  links with phase-milestone dates (created, phase starts/ends, pauses).
  Monthly/quarterly rollups add roadmap, features, struggles, process
  improvements, cost/capability changes, traffic patterns, surprises,
  learnings; the monthly ideas report covers largest designs started /
  fully designed / closed out, automation-suggested ideas, kernels and
  rejected ideas, passed-over alternatives, design-mill detail in prose,
  and visual storytelling (graphs, flow diagrams, wireframes, SVGs as UI
  work grows).
- **Permanence & discovery.** Pages render from PM-stack stored data
  (permanent records); a sitemap/tree + search over page names and text
  fields — discovery is not top-nav-only.

## Boundaries / collisions

- Renders the #9060 genealogy (#9070 read model, #9073/#9074 Metadata) —
  design pages display the hierarchy; they do not re-model it. Roadmap
  facts reconcile with roadmap-sync (Grist ↔ MD) rather than forking them.
- Mobile-first layout rules come from C6 and bind every page here.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Merged design: page kinds + templates, edit-window rules,
      snapshot mechanics, rollup counting rules (what counts as done /
      in-progress / blocked / queued).
- [ ] "What did we do today?" answered for one real day, generated from
      stored data, with a weekly rollup above it.
- [ ] One major design (a live mill program) rendered as a full design
      page with subdesign tree + implementation rollup.
- [ ] Timeline page live for the current quarter.

code.title: C6 — Report pages & spaces freshness: mobile-first, questions module, confirmable actions, incident pages
code.body:
# C6 — Report pages & spaces freshness: mobile-first, questions module, confirmable actions, incident pages

Component of the reporting-architecture program (starter epic #9568).
Source: Drew's directive, Reports chat, 2026-11-13 09:11 CST.
Statements: S3.1–S3.17 (+ S2.12 surfaces).

## Scope

- **Freshness contract:** every space and report is updated routinely by
  its owning task as data arrives; a space stale beyond its class budget
  is a defect with an exception path to Reports. (Known wound: spaces have
  been found days stale; the Fleet Reports Space job-status/pool-status
  display defect is an input, recorded on #9568.)
- **Data-blob architecture:** pages/spaces may render from a JSON data
  blob produced by hooks (C2/C3); the refresh job only swaps the data
  object or its file pointer — presentation and data evolve separately.
- **MOBILE-FIRST (hard requirement):** all spaces, reports, and PM-stack
  pages are designed for a phone first — relatively large font, narrow
  width. Desktop is an adaptation (two-column tiles, wider emphasis) or a
  separate/degraded view — never the design target.
- **Questions module everywhere:** the shared questions module embeds
  beside facts on quota and other pages. Confirmation-bubble actions with
  real effects, queueable from mobile: **queue an OpenAI / Anthropic /
  Fable reset when the matching weekly/monthly quota reaches 100%**;
  candidate standing rule — when all other queues are down and Claude
  reaches 100%, trigger a cloud reset immediately (**requires Drew's
  explicit ruling, recorded as an FDR per #9180, before automation**).
- **Error question sets:** on a page error — Should I try to fix it?
  Hotpatch the binary the service runs? Trigger a NixOS reset? Wait for
  downtime, then reset? Plus free feedback / comments / multi-selects.
  Answers spawn Muse tasks that do the work, update the page, and notify
  (push / category chat / main chat).
- **Custom report pages:** per-incident pages with their own graphs and a
  story (start, beginning, end), updated over time: progress; fix attempts
  ("trials and tribulations"); findings; recurrence-prevention issues;
  related previous incidents; final root cause; short/medium/long-term
  remediation. (Shape case: the Claude authentication outage.) Period and
  forecast pages: today's activity; predicted workhorse full-wall;
  predicted wall-until (data from C4); pool-availability/quota-change
  specials. Not every wall/reset earns a page — the design names the
  threshold.
- **Reports index:** all reports listed somewhere searchable (the
  question-sets list is the precedent), feeding C7's timeline and C8's
  ingestion.

## Boundaries / collisions

- Builds on the Fleet Reports Space + PM-stack pages; the questions module
  and decision machinery (pending-questions / decision-set processor) are
  generalized, not replaced by a second system.
- Reset actions ride the pool steward's existing audibles/reset machinery;
  this component owns the page surface and the ask, not a new actuator.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Merged design: freshness budgets per page class, blob schema,
      mobile-first layout rules, questions-module action contract,
      incident-page template.
- [ ] One quota page live with an embedded questions module and a
      confirmable reset action working from mobile.
- [ ] One real incident rendered as a full incident page (the Claude auth
      outage is the candidate).
- [ ] Reports index live and searchable.

code.title: C5 — Efficiency accounting + provider/model policy
code.body:
# C5 — Efficiency accounting + provider/model policy

Component of the reporting-architecture program (starter epic #9568).
Source: Drew's directive, Reports chat, 2026-11-13 09:11 CST.
Statements: S2.1, S2.2, S2.8–S2.11, S2.15–S2.18 (+ S3.16 genre).

## Scope

- **Efficiency accounting:** join quota/token consumption to output
  (merged PRs, completed tasks) per surface, pool, provider, and model.
  A period where quota usage fell but merged PRs fell further is
  documented as what it is — **worse efficiency** — with the distribution
  diagnosis (e.g. tokens shifted Muse → OpenCode while merges declined).
  This is a standing report genre, not a one-off.
- **Consistency / troughs:** recommendations to smooth consumption and
  reduce wall-troughs, with measured effect after adoption.
- **Routing-mode policy:** per provider, ordered vs round-robin vs
  weighted selection, decided against measured rate-limit behavior; the
  resulting config changes are proposed with evidence (pool steward
  executes config changes under its own rules; this component recommends).
- **Never-serve rules:** which providers must never serve which models
  (e.g. a multi-model provider used for Sonnet when it should only carry
  DeepSeek/GLM-class work), recorded as policy the composition review
  checks against.
- **Free-provider inventory:** free tiers and free-for-a-time models with
  **empirically tested context windows** (tested vs official record —
  usually smaller, sometimes larger — is a tracked field), reliability,
  and rate ceilings; wiring into small / speed / scout paths, and free
  decision-class models in front of workhorse where their context allows,
  **with reliable fall prevention**: on quota exhaustion or rate limit,
  work moves to the next model and takes the cache hit — it does not stop.
- **Plan & model recommendations:** another OpenCode plan, CommandCode
  full plan, GLM plan, and benchmarks of models that may outperform
  expectations — each as a costed recommendation Drew can act on.
- "Everything is perfect as is" is an allowed conclusion only with the
  measurements attached (Drew doubts it; so does the record).

## Boundaries / collisions

- Consumes pool-composition-review / pool-intelligence / pool-meta-reviewer
  outputs (Space streams); does not replace those jobs.
- Fall-prevention mechanics overlap #9196 (selection/dispatch) and the
  pool steward's flip machinery — this component sets policy; those own
  mechanism.

## Acceptance

- [ ] First efficiency report published with the join methodology stated
      and reproducible from stored data.
- [ ] Routing-mode + never-serve policy tables in a merged design, with
      the evidence for each row.
- [ ] Free-provider inventory live with tested context windows for every
      wired provider; at least one free path wired in front of a
      production path with fall prevention demonstrated.

code.title: C4 — Quota forecasting: exhaustion, downtime, and reset-duration predictions, tracked until accurate
code.body:
# C4 — Quota forecasting: exhaustion, downtime, and reset-duration predictions, tracked until accurate

Component of the reporting-architecture program (starter epic #9568).
Source: Drew's directive, Reports chat, 2026-11-13 09:11 CST.
Statements: S2.3–S2.7, S2.12 (alerts), S2.13, S2.14 (+ S3.15 page inputs).

## Scope

A prediction system, not a vibe:

- **What is predicted:** per-pool exhaustion times; arrival of new
  models/plans; **complete-downtime windows** (all pools walled at once);
  **reset durations** expressed as ranges in Drew's formats — "between X
  and Y hours from now", "2.5 to 3.7 days", "2 days 4 hours to up to 3
  days 16 hours", "likely runs out between tomorrow afternoon and Sunday
  2 am".
- **Recorded bases** (each prediction names its basis): trailing-30-day
  rates; rates used until the last reset; rates since a named config
  change; past-day vs trailing-30d comparison.
- **Adjustments:** day-type models — same time-of-day on other days, other
  Fridays, other weekends; spike-day modeling (a week running ~10% light
  predicts a ~+20% spike day, and the model says so explicitly).
- **Tracking & methodology:** every prediction is logged with its inputs
  and scored against the outcome; methodology updates are themselves
  logged; the loop runs until predictions are relatively accurate, and
  the accuracy record is a report (C6/C7 consume it).
- **Delivery:** push notifications with useful info; forecast pages
  (predicted workhorse full-wall; predicted wall-until) are C6 surfaces
  fed by this component's data.

## Boundaries / collisions

- Data substrate exists: the laptop quota gatherer (quota-current.json),
  the burn plan (plan-current.md, v46+), Turso quota records, and the
  Fleet Reports Space streams. This component adds the prediction +
  scoring layer; it does not build a second gatherer.
- Pool composition facts come from the pool review/steward jobs; routing
  recommendations are C5's.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Merged design: prediction record schema (basis, inputs, range,
      issued-at), scoring rules, methodology-change log format.
- [ ] Live predictions for every open pool, refreshed on gatherer ticks,
      with the first scored outcomes published.
- [ ] Downtime-window prediction demonstrated against a known wall
      (e.g. a Sunday-evening reopening set) with the error recorded.

code.title: C3 — Health hooks: failure-triggered checks that troubleshoot and report
code.body:
# C3 — Health hooks: failure-triggered checks that troubleshoot and report

Component of the reporting-architecture program (starter epic #9568).
Source: Drew's directive, Reports chat, 2026-11-13 09:11 CST.
Statements: S1.3.

## Scope

Checks like **"PM stack reachable"** and **"OpenCode working"** stop being
interval polls and become **hook scripts that fire on failure-to-connect**:

- On a failed connect (from any caller: PM stack surfaces, lane launches,
  aggregator ticks), the hook fires immediately, runs a bounded
  troubleshoot sequence (reachability, service state, auth/credential
  health, recent changes), and **reports what occurred** — a note to the
  queues/PM-health category chat, escalating to Reports when it is an
  exception and to the main chat when Drew is blocked.
- The hook records the incident into the PM-stack event store so C6 can
  render an incident page and C8 can ingest it (first-appearance data for
  error strings starts here).
- Recovery is also an event: the same hook reports the recovery (the
  watchdog's new-alert/recovery pattern, event-driven).

## Boundaries / collisions

- This is the successor to the **disabled** opencode-session-minder's
  detection role — hooks, not a revived cron (the Fleet CA coordinator's
  finding stands: no durable monitor covered sessions after 2026-11-08;
  this component closes that gap by trigger, not by schedule).
- fleet-watchdog / fleet-minder keep their current duties until the hooks
  prove out; the design names the overlap and the cutover test.
- Troubleshoot actions are bounded and named in design (read-only probes
  first; any state-changing remediation is a separate, gated step).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Merged design: trigger surface (who calls, what counts as
      failure-to-connect), probe sequence per check, report format,
      escalation rules.
- [ ] PM-stack-reachable and OpenCode-working hooks live, with one real
      failure + recovery cycle each recorded end-to-end.
- [ ] Incident records land in the event store in the shape C6/C8 consume.

code.title: C2 — Event pipeline: webhook/catchup queues, threshold hook drains, cron triage
code.body:
# C2 — Event pipeline: webhook/catchup queues, threshold hook drains, cron triage

Component of the reporting-architecture program (starter epic #9568).
Source: Drew's directive, Reports chat, 2026-11-13 09:11 CST.
Statements: S1.1, S1.2, S1.4, S1.5, S1.6 (+ S0.9 mechanism, S3.2/S3.12 inputs).

## Scope

Replace heavy repeated polling crons with events:

- Items of a kind arriving from the **GitHub org webhook** or **catchup
  scans** are (a) logged, (b) inserted into the appropriate databases, and
  (c) gathered into **dedicated per-kind queues** (new issues, open PRs,
  CI failures, mentions, …).
- **Muse hook scripts** check those queues and drain them on thresholds —
  default **≥10 new items OR oldest item ≥15 min** (per-kind tuning is a
  design question) — and on drain: triage new issues, review open PRs,
  ensure a queue task minds each item, and report current + projected
  quota (forecast data from C4).
- The **PM stack triggers Muse directly** to fill queue items (no
  polling intermediary).
- **Cron triage:** every existing heavy repeated job is classified
  keep-as-check / convert-to-hook / retire; every surviving cron is named
  with its reason. Candidates named in the directive: most of the current
  sweep/monitor fleet; checks whose failure is itself the event move to C3.
- Integration options across **OpenClaw, OpenChamber, OpenCode,
  Cloudflare Workers, and the PM stack** are evaluated and the chosen
  topology recorded (FDR per #9180).

## Boundaries / collisions

- Consumes #9196's dispatch/selection/lifecycle design — this is the
  trigger layer, not a second dispatcher. Assumes #9178's claim surface
  (claim-any / manual-only) for hook-spawned tasks.
- The orchestration pass and fleet-minder keep working until their hook
  replacements are proven; no big-bang cutover.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Event-kind inventory + per-kind queue + threshold table in a merged
      design.
- [ ] At least one kind (GitHub issues) draining end-to-end via hooks:
      webhook → DB + queue → threshold drain → tasks minded → report.
- [ ] Cron triage table covering every heavy repeated job, each with a
      named disposition; retirements executed only after replacements
      verified for one full cycle.

code.title: C1 — Chat operating model: category side chats, insert-only job writes
code.body:
# C1 — Chat operating model: category side chats, insert-only job writes

Component of the reporting-architecture program (starter epic #9568).
Source: Drew's directive, Reports chat, 2026-11-13 09:11 CST.
Statements: S0.1–S0.9 (inventory in the program design doc).

## Scope

One category side chat per job family. A job's agent executes, updates the
backend/repo itself, inserts its update into its category chat
**insert-only (it never reads the chat)**, and ends. Chats are write-sinks,
not state stores. Category map (from the intake audit):

- **Reports** — exceptions, errors, decisions (2026-11-07 ruling; unchanged)
- **Lanes** — all lane effort (Muse lanes + OpenChamber lane notes)
- **Designs, Issues & PRs** — all GitHub activity
- **Orchestration — queues, PM health & questions** (renamed orchestration
  chat; open question Q1) — queue state, PM-stack health, pending questions
- **Pools & Quota** (open question Q2: separate sink vs Space+Reports only)

Per-task notes lines in every rerouted job body literally name its sink.
Escalation paths: exceptions → Reports; high-urgency → main chat as well
(page-health-push is the precedent); jobs may message other tasks / the
orchestrator / enqueue queue items.

## Input

The intake audit (chat-by-chat inventory of ~180 chats, per-chat fate, and
the consolidated reroute list) ships in the program design PR under
`sources/` and is summarized on #9568. Highlights: 28 per-lane shift chats
retire into Lanes (Muse lane jobs already deliver there); ~15
GitHub-activity per-job chats merge into Designs, Issues & PRs; the
questions pair merges into the orchestration category; rebuilt jobs' origin
chats retire as reading surfaces (the Fleet Reports Space is the record);
OpenChamber conductor/babysitter/dispatcher + session-minder chats stay
retired.

## Boundaries

- **No rerouting ships before Drew approves the map.** This issue owns the
  implementation once approved: repo-copy-first job edits + cron.update +
  live read-back, per the standing cron-definition workflow.
- Open questions for Drew (defaults in the design doc): Q1 category-4 home;
  Q2 four vs five category chats; Q3 archive retired chats after one
  verified cycle; Q4 space-owner chats stay unpinned owners.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Drew-approved map recorded (as an FDR per #9180).
- [ ] Every live reporting job's body names exactly one category sink;
      deliveries verified live for one full cycle per job.
- [ ] Retired chats archived per the approved Q3 rule; pinned set = the
      category chats only.

code.title: Reporting architecture — event-driven reporting, quota forecasting, living report pages (design-mill starter)
code.body:
# Reporting architecture — event-driven reporting, quota forecasting, living report pages (design-mill starter)

**Directive:** Drew, Reports side chat, 2026-11-13 09:11 CST. **Urgency 400 (High).**
This epic is the starter issue for the reporting-architecture design mill:
statement inventory → proto design (merged, see the design doc under
`doc/2026-11-13T15-12-00Z_design_reporting-architecture-event-driven/`) →
summit elaboration → component designs → granular issues. The epic does
NOT close on the design pass.

## Program (five threads; thread 5 already routed away)

0. **Chat operating model** — one category side chat per job family; jobs
   execute, update the backend/repo themselves, insert their update into
   their category chat insert-only (never read it), and end. Category map:
   Reports (exceptions/decisions), Lanes (all lane effort), Designs, Issues
   & PRs (all GitHub activity), Orchestration — queues, PM health &
   questions, Pools & Quota (detail). The intake audit (chat-by-chat fates +
   reroute list) is filed as this program's input; **no rerouting ships
   before Drew approves the map.**
1. **Event-driven reporting** — Muse hooks + PM-stack triggers fill queue
   items directly; GitHub org webhook + catchup-scan items land logged in
   DBs AND in dedicated per-kind queues; hook drains fire at ≥10 new items
   or oldest item ≥15 min → triage issues, review PRs, ensure a task minds
   each, report quota current + projected. Heavy repeated crons retire;
   surviving crons are named with reasons. Health checks (PM stack
   reachable, OpenCode working) become failure-triggered hook scripts that
   troubleshoot and report immediately.
2. **Quota forecasting & efficiency** — exhaustion / downtime /
   reset-duration predictions as ranges on recorded bases (trailing-30d,
   rates-until-last-reset, since-config-change, past-day vs 30d) with
   day-type and spike-day adjustments; predictions logged, scored, and the
   methodology refined until relatively accurate. Efficiency accounting
   (quota vs merged PRs), routing-mode policy (ordered / round-robin /
   weighted per provider), never-serve rules, free-provider inventory with
   TESTED context windows, plan/model recommendations. Push notifications.
3. **Report pages & spaces freshness** — every space/report updated by its
   owning task as data arrives (staleness is a defect); spaces may run off
   a hook-produced JSON blob. **Mobile-first is a hard requirement** for
   all spaces, reports, and PM-stack pages. The shared questions module
   embeds beside facts; confirmation-bubble actions carry real effects
   (queue an OpenAI/Anthropic/Fable reset at 100%); error question sets
   spawn Muse tasks that update the page and notify. Custom incident
   report pages + period/predicted-wall pages; a searchable reports index.
4. **Rollups, design pages, Atlas** — daily (midnight–midnight CT) /
   weekly (Mon–Mon CT) / monthly / quarterly activity pages answering
   "what did we do today?", with soft edit windows then restricted edit
   forms; period snapshots cloned into dated frozen library spaces;
   per-project spaces (Fleet, PM stack, Atlas, ID); per-design pages with
   subdesign trees and implementation rollups (done / in-progress /
   blocked / queued) up to roadmap/epic pages; a reports timeline
   (quarter → month → week → day). Everything ingests into Atlas many
   times daily, recency-biased, with metadata links, cross-linked
   embeddings, rich page metadata, and query-planner boosts for
   error-driven investigation (first-appearance of an error string →
   issues/PRs/commits → queue attempts/models/worktrees → transcript
   expectations → rhyming/class fixes).
5. **Identity material — NOT this program.** Drew's kiosk / cross-signing
   elaboration was filed at intake as amendment comments on #9132
   (pointers #9121, #9127) of the federation/namespaces program #9106.

## Collisions (consume / extend, never duplicate)

#1184 (PM-stack coherence; at the 100-sub-issue cap → cross-linked, not
parented), #9196 (orchestration — dispatch/selection/lifecycle substrate),
#9060 + #9070/#9073/#9074/#9075 (hierarchy, genealogy, Metadata, session
state), #9091 (Atlas v1 — C8 is an input, not a parallel program), #9106
(identity amendment target), #9178 (queue claim surface this program
assumes), #9180 (this program's rulings get FDRs). The Fleet Reports Space
(17 streams) and page-health-push are existing surfaces, not competitors.

## Safety gates

Designs + issues only from the mill. No live job, cron, hook, or chat
delivery changes in the intake pass; chat rerouting ships only after Drew
approves the audit map; the standing cloud-reset rule (thread 3) requires
Drew's explicit ruling (proposed as an FDR per #9180) before any
automation acts on it.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Statement inventory re-verified at atomic coverage by the summit
      (zero unmapped).
- [ ] Component designs for C1–C8 merged under doc/, each answering its
      named open questions or batching them to Drew with defaults.
- [ ] Granular implementation issues filed under each component.
- [ ] Coverage audit + traceability matrix posted here.

code.title: pool flag: test Luna #medium as the workhorse-weighted rung — measured 50.7 t/s vs #high 32.3 t/s (1.57×) at equal reliability (99.7% n=4,584 vs 99.8% n=35,538), AA II 18.5 vs 21.4, same plan window
code.body:
**Pool-intelligence flag (hypothesis — earns a config change only via the controlled-test mechanism #1342 and the steward's PR path). Filed 2026-11-13, window 2026-11-12T14:12Z → 2026-11-13T14:12Z, laptop `route_attempt` read-only.**

Quantified trade, same door (`_openai.main`), same window:

- **Luna #medium: 99.7% success on n=4,584 at median 50.7 t/s**, first-token 1.43s. Halves: H1 45.7 t/s (n=499), H2 51.0 t/s (n=4,085).
- **Luna #high (the current workhorse-weighted rung): 99.8% on n=35,538 at median 32.3 t/s**, first-token 1.16s. Halves: H1 30.7, H2 36.0 t/s.
- Within-half speed ratio #medium/#high: **1.49× (H1), 1.42× (H2)** — the rung effect is not a time-of-window artifact.
- AA prior (2026-11-13 pull): the two rungs' AA speeds are near-equal (Medium 94.7 vs High 97.2 t/s), so AA predicts parity; our measured exchange rate is rung-shaped (conclusion 43). AA II: Medium 18.45 vs High 21.43 (−3.0). AA cost/task: $0.042 vs $0.073 — both plan-covered on the same OpenAI window, so plan cost is identical; the trade is throughput vs −3 AA II on workhorse-class tasks.

Hypothesis: for workhorse-weighted work (throughput-bound, not intelligence-bound), the #medium rung delivers ~1.5× the measured throughput at equal reliability for −3 AA II. Test: controlled A/B via #1342 on workhorse-class tasks before any seat change. Related: composition R20 owns the Luna seat's pace verdict; program #9399 (effort tiers per pool).

code.title: PM-stack prompt & chat surface: scoped prompt widgets + session interface (program)
code.body:
**Program starter (Drew, 2026-11-13 05:54 CT).** Full brief: `doc/2026-11-13T11-54-00Z_design_pm_stack_prompt_surface/brief.md` on main (PR #9535, merged `e30df92199`).

**What Drew wants:** prompt widgets on all appropriate PM-stack pages — scoped to a section, a page, the PM stack generically, generic agent access (chat + task delegation queued at a priority), and specialized task variants (reprioritization, detail gathering, comparing new options, integrating insights since last review). Targets: Claude or Muse per prompt/default; the OpenCode/OpenChamber pools with auto + low/medium/high; a decision-model variant that generates a question series for a decision API / LLM / hybrid with effort steering, default fallbacks, "not confident" answers, and speed-optimized answer generation at a provided context level; access to the advanced (conditional-clause) constraints; context generation via any model or queued task, shaped for the decision API; attachments/multimedia now, streaming audio later. Async (checkable ID, optional completion notification) and sync (block, or WebSocket until answered) modes. Plus a chat surface: review all messages, new session per message unless replying in context, open/close/archive/reply/cross-reference, notification count + push, defaults = Muse hook task immediately or a medium-high queue item on auto/workhorse, everything overridable.

**Cross-links:** the decision-question variant builds on the decision-model supplement in the pool/effort mill (code#9399); the async queue + ID pattern should reuse the fleet queue, not invent a second one.

**Sequencing for the owning task:** (1) design pass — placement map per PM-stack page + the prompt API contract (scopes, targets, modes) as a design doc in this folder + a summary comment here; (2) granular implementation issues per slice; (3) build the core slice first: the generic PM-stack prompt widget + section/page-scoped widgets on the main pages, target selector, async submission with checkable ID. Chat surface and decision variant are following slices, not the first build.

code.title: Nix cache as the content store: derivations + flakes per item (design program)
code.body:
**Program starter (Drew, 2026-11-13 05:42 CT).** Full brief: `doc/2026-11-13T11-42-00Z_design_nix_content_store/brief.md` on main (PR #9520, merged `31718d6bf1`). Drew flagged this as separate from the pool/effort mill (code#9399); it belongs to the Nix program.

**The question:** can our Nix cache be the content store directly — every file and file-set as a content-addressed derivation, a flake per item (sharded by CA prefix), date.increment versioning with fork lineage in the version, and constraint-based resolution (newest allowed version; documented divergence where pragmatic)?

**The gate is measurement:** benchmark before committing — space, per-derivation eval overhead, complex-flake behavior — across compiler × store-backend × resolver combinations (Nix, Lix, Tvix, Trust Nix, mixed pairings incl. hot-cache-over-long-term-store). Drew's rule: if it's a wash with no significant downside, keep it for the option value.

**The surface if it holds:** pruning to final artefacts per consumer kind; the full target matrix (static/dynamic, VM/container, deb/RPM/Arch/snap/Homebrew/Windows installer, embeddable libraries, roc+ID worlds, Wasm/WASI/browser and Cloudflare variants, Android APK, ratatui); an admin platform surface with retention config and usage statistics; trusted store sharing with ACLs; per-tenant derivation lists as complete backups.

EPIC GUARD: this issue holds work in itself; subtasks completing never closes it. Next action: a design pass (mill-style inventory + benchmark plan) when the Nix program's turn comes — not yet launched.

### REL-08 — Direct `work complete` CLI and human/JSON recovery output

**Tier:** recommended after state machine. **Goal:** add `fleet work complete` parser contract with explicit refs, `--wait/--verify`, idempotency and shared structured outcome. **Owns:** one shared #9206 CLI integration slice for `fleet/src/main.rs`, `fleet-registry/src/lib.rs`, golden help/output and command inventory; #9209 does not create duplicate writers. **Hard blockers:** #9206 Command/Result contract; REL-07; #9203 dispatch excluded. **First failing oracle:** `pmo_cli_complete_requires_explicit_remote_resource_allowlist` plus `pmo_cli_complete_reports_partial_receipt`; census shows proposed namespace absent at pin. **Done:** named tests must be listed in their owning integration target, then run that exact target; queue crate command tests service composition only. **Negative:** ambiguous repo, implicit close-all, timeout, unauthorized merge, changed digest. **Compatibility:** additive, preserve all source options and queue aliases. - `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/work/completion.rs`

Explicit read-only consumers (not writable ownership): none declared.

Use the existing Fleet queue/PM Stack/adapter owners named in the design; do not add a queue, database, scheduler, service, resolver, executable, GitHub client, or general creation-outbox producer. Shared CLI glue remains owned by the single CLI-13 registration slice. Do not edit #6533 or duplicate its live acceptance; consume #9028/#9073–#9076/#9079/#9081/#9178/#9179/#3424/#8575/#8579 as applicable, not as replacement work.

## Prerequisites and sequencing

Hard blockers named by the source slice, after granular-key normalization: REL-01, REL-02, REL-03, REL-04, REL-05, REL-06, HYD-06, AUTH-01
File-collision sequencing edges added by stable topological serialization: none.
Existing issue references retained as non-blocking runtime/evidence gates: none.
Domain-starter parent references are never emitted as hard native blockers. Source parents normalized to granular slices or runtime gates: #9207→HYD-06, #9208→AUTH-01, #9196→runtime gate.




Use only granular issue-key edges after all keys are resolved. Never make a whole domain starter a hard blocker when it creates a cycle. File collisions are hard sequencing edges. Parent integration adds native parent/blocker edges in a later pass after the command map, requirements IDs, and acyclic graph are verified.

## Starting failing test, oracle, and done check

- **First failing test:** `pmo_rel_completion_recovers_merge_after_lost_ack_without_webhook`
- **Oracle:** The source slice’s stated reference model, golden fixture, or invariant; compare expected and observed state explicitly. No mock-only claim of deployed/live behavior.
- **Done command:** `list exact test then run `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml -p fleet-queue --lib --features client,queue-broker pmo_rel_completion_recovers_merge_after_lost_ack_without_webhook`.`
- Tests must first be listed by exact name in the owning target (`-- --list`); assert the test exists before execution. A zero-test filter passing is not acceptance.

## Acceptance and negative cases

directly close local canonical item only after all required effect receipts; preserve partial effects.

Negative coverage: old lease expires but operation receipt permitted only scoped; no new stale worker mutations; partial issue close; async merge pending.

## Compatibility, migration, and runtime gates

- Preserve the current queue/status/identity/Project-writer/Fleet `gh` compatibility surfaces. Do not silently change existing spellings or normalize ratified `expedite=15` / `next-up=25`; those remain distinct from `do_now`.
- QTI remains unlocated/unverified; #9241 is the existing provenance-recovery issue. #3424/#8575/#8579/#8602 are candidates/constraints, not presumed equivalents. Any overlapping persisted field/schema change waits for the QTI crosswalk and named current owner.
- Runtime gates: implementation starts only after the document PR is merged, the exact curated requirement IDs are integrated, and this issue's granular prerequisite edges are resolved. Schema/migration, production rollout, telemetry, authenticated remote writes, deployed behavior, and live acceptance each require their own explicit evidence and approval. Normal triage does not inherit urgency 450/Do Now.
- Projection rows being rebuildable/disposable does not authorize deleting the PM PostgREST database or unrelated tables. Preserve unique human-authored `pmp_links`/link writes and all unrelated tables; follow the existing backup/restore requirements before any future migration or cleanup.
- Compatibility: `completing` additive transition approved by #9178/storage owner; rollback leaves inspectable recoverable state.
- Rollback: Disable only the new capability; preserve pending intents, artifacts, existing state, and remote effects. No broad reset, destructive cleanup, or deletion of history.

- Raw source refs: handoff `sources/01_handoff_pm_stack_fleet_orchestration.md`; charter `sources/02_charter_v1_1.md`; recovered original `sources/04_recovered_original_combined_design.md`; cited source section(s) in `sources/03_full_orchestration_proposal.md` as named by the component; exact occurrence citations are in the curated trace above when allocated.

- Existing external requirement refs not assigned a new curated ID: none.

### Original slice text (preserved)

### REL-07 — Completion prepare/partial/recovery state machine

**Tier:** crucial. **Goal:** explicit resource allowlist, policy effect set, `completing` recovery, no-webhook normal success. **Owns:** `src/work/completion.rs`, consuming `operations.rs`, `activity.rs`, `relations.rs`, `authority.rs`; no CLI glue. **Hard blockers:** REL-01–06; #9207 cursor/final-refresh contract; #9208 readiness/authority contract; #9196 active-task proof guard. **First failing oracle:** `pmo_rel_completion_recovers_merge_after_lost_ack_without_webhook` crashes after remote merge before local receipt; model must resume. **Done command:** list exact test then run `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml -p fleet-queue --lib --features client,queue-broker pmo_rel_completion_recovers_merge_after_lost_ack_without_webhook`. **Negative:** old lease expires but operation receipt permitted only scoped; no new stale worker mutations; partial issue close; async merge pending. **Acceptance:** directly close local canonical item only after all required effect receipts; preserve partial effects. **Migration:** `completing` additive transition approved by #9178/storage owner; rollback leaves inspectable recoverable state.

## Prerequisites and sequencing

Hard blockers named by the source slice, after granular-key normalization: REL-04, AUTH-02
File-collision sequencing edges added by stable topological serialization: none.
Existing issue references retained as non-blocking runtime/evidence gates: none.
Domain-starter parent references are never emitted as hard native blockers. Source parents normalized to granular slices or runtime gates: #9208→AUTH-02, #9208→AUTH-02.


Ordering note: AUTH-03 is a recommended rework-if-early review for REL-05, not a hard edge; keeping it hard would cycle with AUTH-03→REL-05.

Use only granular issue-key edges after all keys are resolved. Never make a whole domain starter a hard blocker when it creates a cycle. File collisions are hard sequencing edges. Parent integration adds native parent/blocker edges in a later pass after the command map, requirements IDs, and acyclic graph are verified.

## Starting failing test, oracle, and done check

- **First failing test:** `pmo_rel_stale_relay_ack_cannot_regress_operation`
- **Oracle:** The source slice’s stated reference model, golden fixture, or invariant; compare expected and observed state explicitly. No mock-only claim of deployed/live behavior.
- **Done command:** `verify test listed, then run `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml -p fleet-queue --lib --features client,queue-broker pmo_rel_stale_relay_ack_cannot_regress_operation`.`
- Tests must first be listed by exact name in the owning target (`-- --list`); assert the test exists before execution. A zero-test filter passing is not acceptance.

## Acceptance and negative cases

attach late effect to immutable op, reject stale local status update, verify remote before retry.

Negative coverage: old op sent then desired state reverses, rate-limit/transient handling, lease expires during HTTP.

## Compatibility, migration, and runtime gates

- Preserve the current queue/status/identity/Project-writer/Fleet `gh` compatibility surfaces. Do not silently change existing spellings or normalize ratified `expedite=15` / `next-up=25`; those remain distinct from `do_now`.
- QTI remains unlocated/unverified; #9241 is the existing provenance-recovery issue. #3424/#8575/#8579/#8602 are candidates/constraints, not presumed equivalents. Any overlapping persisted field/schema change waits for the QTI crosswalk and named current owner.
- Runtime gates: implementation starts only after the document PR is merged, the exact curated requirement IDs are integrated, and this issue's granular prerequisite edges are resolved. Schema/migration, production rollout, telemetry, authenticated remote writes, deployed behavior, and live acceptance each require their own explicit evidence and approval. Normal triage does not inherit urgency 450/Do Now.
- Projection rows being rebuildable/disposable does not authorize deleting the PM PostgREST database or unrelated tables. Preserve unique human-authored `pmp_links`/link writes and all unrelated tables; follow the existing backup/restore requirements before any future migration or cleanup.
- Compatibility: staged read/rollback preserves all in-flight rows. Retry budget follows provider policy, no invented cap.
- Rollback: Disable only the new capability; preserve pending intents, artifacts, existing state, and remote effects. No broad reset, destructive cleanup, or deletion of history.

**Tier:** crucial. **Goal:** prevent stale relay overwriting newer status; serialize same target; define pre-send supersede vs post-send unknown/reconcile. **Owns:** `src/work/operations.rs` relay model and current broker drain only after integration approval. **Hard blockers:** REL-04 durable operation contract and #9208 `AUTH-02` public-mirror authorization contract. #9208 AUTH-03/04 adapter policy consumes this relay contract; they are downstream/recommended integration edges, not hard blockers, avoiding a cycle. **First failing oracle:** `pmo_rel_stale_relay_ack_cannot_regress_operation` interleaves relay generation N ack after N+1 claim. **Done command:** verify test listed, then run `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml -p fleet-queue --lib --features client,queue-broker pmo_rel_stale_relay_ack_cannot_regress_operation`. **Negative:** old op sent then desired state reverses, rate-limit/transient handling, lease expires during HTTP. **Acceptance:** attach late effect to immutable op, reject stale local status update, verify remote before retry. **Migration:** staged read/rollback preserves all in-flight rows. Use the existing Fleet queue/PM Stack/adapter owners named in the design; do not add a queue, database, scheduler, service, resolver, executable, GitHub client, or general creation-outbox producer. Shared CLI glue remains owned by the single CLI-13 registration slice. Do not edit #6533 or duplicate its live acceptance; consume #9028/#9073–#9076/#9079/#9081/#9178/#9179/#3424/#8575/#8579 as applicable, not as replacement work.

## Prerequisites and sequencing

Hard blockers named by the source slice, after granular-key normalization: #9074
File-collision sequencing edges added by stable topological serialization: none.
Existing issue references retained as non-blocking runtime/evidence gates: none.
Domain-starter parent references are never emitted as hard native blockers. Source parents normalized to granular slices or runtime gates: none.

Source-local candidate aliases normalized for this packet: DST-ORDER-01 → PRI-03; PRI-CMP-01 → PRI-03; PRI-05 → PRI-05a, PRI-05b, PRI-05c, PRI-05d.


Use only granular issue-key edges after all keys are resolved. Never make a whole domain starter a hard blocker when it creates a cycle. File collisions are hard sequencing edges. Parent integration adds native parent/blocker edges in a later pass after the command map, requirements IDs, and acyclic graph are verified.

## Starting failing test, oracle, and done check

- **First failing test:** `pmo_peer_rank_rebalances_local_range; pmo_work_id_decimal_strings_order_numeric_not_lexical`
- **Oracle:** The source slice’s stated reference model, golden fixture, or invariant; compare expected and observed state explicitly. No mock-only claim of deployed/live behavior.
- **Done command:** `Verify `pmo_peer_rank_rebalances_local_range` and `pmo_work_id_decimal_strings_order_numeric_not_lexical` are listed; then run both exact fleet-queue filters. Comparator oracle asserts ID 9 sorts before 10 numerically for equal prior keys.`
- Tests must first be listed by exact name in the owning target (`-- --list`); assert the test exists before execution. A zero-test filter passing is not acceptance.

## Acceptance and negative cases

Required before/after peer ordering within equal effective urgency; exact integer rank and local deterministic rebalance in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/work/priority.rs`; comparator parity in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/turso_queue.rs`.

Negative coverage: stale input, duplicate/replay, ambiguous resource, unauthorized actor, partial remote effect, unknown version, and no false verified/completed result where applicable.

### Canonical work-ID tie order and selection-order digest

Wire work IDs are canonical unsigned decimal strings, but after authority IDs compare bytewise, work IDs compare by arbitrary-precision numeric value (digit-count then digits), not lexical string order or floating point. Golden tie fixture must place work ID `9` before `10`; canonical IDs are not coerced through JavaScript numbers. Opaque provider/session IDs remain opaque strings. The optional full `order_hash` uses `fleet.selection-order/v1` and the shared `ASCII(domain) || 0x00 || UTF8(JCS(order_object))` + SHA-256 `sha256:` lower-hex framing. Hash the complete eligible population in canonical comparator order—not a UI top-page—and include `owner_policy_ref` and all selection-policy/revision inputs. This fingerprint neither grants a claim nor proves a complete snapshot.

## Compatibility, migration, and runtime gates

- Preserve the current queue/status/identity/Project-writer/Fleet `gh` compatibility surfaces. Do not silently change existing spellings or normalize ratified `expedite=15` / `next-up=25`; those remain distinct from `do_now`.
- QTI remains unlocated/unverified; #9241 is the existing provenance-recovery issue. #3424/#8575/#8579/#8602 are candidates/constraints, not presumed equivalents. Any overlapping persisted field/schema change waits for the QTI crosswalk and named current owner.
- Runtime gates: implementation starts only after the document PR is merged, the exact curated requirement IDs are integrated, and this issue's granular prerequisite edges are resolved. Schema/migration, production rollout, telemetry, authenticated remote writes, deployed behavior, and live acceptance each require their own explicit evidence and approval. Normal triage does not inherit urgency 450/Do Now.
- Projection rows being rebuildable/disposable does not authorize deleting the PM PostgREST database or unrelated tables. Preserve unique human-authored `pmp_links`/link writes and all unrelated tables; follow the existing backup/restore requirements before any future migration or cleanup.
- Compatibility: Additive and reversible only after existing owner/schema review; retain prior data and behavior; no silent fallback or dual authority.
- Rollback: Disable only the new capability; preserve pending intents, artifacts, existing state, and remote effects. No broad reset, destructive cleanup, or deletion of history.

## Source trail

- Raw source refs: handoff `sources/01_handoff_pm_stack_fleet_orchestration.md`; charter `sources/02_charter_v1_1.md`; recovered original `sources/04_recovered_original_combined_design.md`; cited source section(s) in `sources/03_full_orchestration_proposal.md` as named by the component; exact occurrence citations are in the curated trace above when allocated.
- Design ref: `components/9199-distributed-priority.md`, slice `PRI-03` (proposal only).
- Prior-art/evidence receipts: `research/track-a-state-of-art.md`, `research/track-b-state-of-art.md`, `research/track-b-sources.json`; additional exact evidence anchors for this slice: architecture.md#identity-and-authority, architecture.md#digest-and-serialization-contract, research/canonical-json-evidence.md, contracts/digest-vectors.json.
- Parent-approved support mapping (validation/expansion support only, not a direct slice-key match): none.
- Existing external requirement refs not assigned a new curated ID: none.
- Command allocation: `flag.order, flag.priority-after, flag.priority-before, priority.move`. Full command inventory remains `census/commands.jsonl`; exact allocation source is `census/command-slice-map.jsonl` (215 rows, no wildcard). V1 baseline keys are not refiled as duplicate implementation issues.
- Shared architecture: `architecture.md`; FDR index: `decisions/README.md` (all FDR-PMO records remain proposed, not ratified).

---

### Original slice text (preserved)

| `PRI-03` / recommended | Required before/after peer ordering within equal effective urgency; exact integer rank and local deterministic rebalance in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/work/priority.rs`; comparator parity in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/turso_queue.rs`. | `PRI-CMP-01`; `DST-ORDER-01`; persistent rank writes gated on Queue Table Improvements/#9074 schema disposition | Same snapshot permutations yield same order; moves work within group; cross-group requires confirmation; stale neighbors/epoch conflict; rebalance bounded/atomic/audited. |

Before running each, issue verification must run its exact command with `-- --list` and assert the test is present; zero-test success is not acceptance. ## Prerequisites and sequencing

Hard blockers named by the source slice, after granular-key normalization: HYD-01, CEN-04, REL-03

Use only granular issue-key edges after all keys are resolved. Never make a whole domain starter a hard blocker when it creates a cycle. File collisions are hard sequencing edges. ## Starting failing test, oracle, and done check

- **First failing test:** `pmo_hyd_page_ingest_and_cursor_commit_atomically`
- **Oracle:** The source slice’s stated reference model, golden fixture, or invariant; compare expected and observed state explicitly. No mock-only claim of deployed/live behavior.
- **Done command:** `confirm exact filter listed, then run `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml -p fleet-queue --lib --features client,queue-broker pmo_hyd_page_ingest_and_cursor_commit_atomically`.`
- Tests must first be listed by exact name in the owning target (`-- --list`); assert the test exists before execution. A zero-test filter passing is not acceptance.

## Acceptance and negative cases

`Link` continuation; cap explicit truncation; idempotent repeated page; query/API version fingerprint.

Negative coverage: absent/malformed Link, duplicate/reordered entries, documented 250 commits/3000 files caps, object-store success + DB failure, cursor without events.

## Compatibility, migration, and runtime gates

- Preserve the current queue/status/identity/Project-writer/Fleet `gh` compatibility surfaces. Do not silently change existing spellings or normalize ratified `expedite=15` / `next-up=25`; those remain distinct from `do_now`.

- Runtime gates: implementation starts only after the document PR is merged, the exact curated requirement IDs are integrated, and this issue's granular prerequisite edges are resolved. verified matching task/session sends once; unbound shell sends never; unsupported adapter says unsupported; Slack delivered is not ack; retry after timeout reconciles. ## Compatibility, migration, and runtime gates

- Preserve the current queue/status/identity/Project-writer/Fleet `gh` compatibility surfaces. Do not silently change existing spellings or normalize ratified `expedite=15` / `next-up=25`; those remain distinct from `do_now`.

- Rollback: Disable only the new capability; preserve pending intents, artifacts, existing state, and remote effects. No broad reset, destructive cleanup, or deletion of history.

## Owned files and boundaries

- `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/work/relations.rs`

Explicit read-only consumers (not writable ownership): none declared.

Use the existing Fleet queue/PM Stack/adapter owners named in the design; do not add a queue, database, scheduler, service, resolver, executable, GitHub client, or general creation-outbox producer. Shared CLI glue remains owned by the single CLI-13 registration slice. Do not edit #6533 or duplicate its live acceptance; consume #9028/#9073–#9076/#9079/#9081/#9178/#9179/#3424/#8575/#8579 as applicable, not as replacement work.

## Prerequisites and sequencing

Hard blockers named by the source slice, after granular-key normalization: CLI-02, CEN-04
File-collision sequencing edges added by stable topological serialization: none.
Existing issue references retained as non-blocking runtime/evidence gates: none.
Domain-starter parent references are never emitted as hard native blockers. Source parents normalized to granular slices or runtime gates: #9206→CLI-02, #9206→CLI-02, #9198→CEN-04.




Use only granular issue-key edges after all keys are resolved. Never make a whole domain starter a hard blocker when it creates a cycle. File collisions are hard sequencing edges. Parent integration adds native parent/blocker edges in a later pass after the command map, requirements IDs, and acyclic graph are verified.

## Starting failing test, oracle, and done check

- **First failing test:** `pmo_dep_aliases_normalize_to_one_canonical_edge`
- **Oracle:** The source slice’s stated reference model, golden fixture, or invariant; compare expected and observed state explicitly. No mock-only claim of deployed/live behavior.
- **Done command:** ``cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml -p fleet-queue --lib --features client,queue-broker pmo_dep_` after checking exact test names with the same command plus `-- --list`.`
- Tests must first be listed by exact name in the owning target (`-- --list`); assert the test exists before execution. A zero-test filter passing is not acceptance.

## Acceptance and negative cases

`cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml -p fleet-queue --lib --features client,queue-broker pmo_dep_` after checking exact test names with the same command plus `-- --list`.

Negative coverage: same GH number across repos, inverse duplicate, unknown enum, shorthand under ambiguous authority, unresolved external target.

## Compatibility, migration, and runtime gates

- Preserve the current queue/status/identity/Project-writer/Fleet `gh` compatibility surfaces. Do not silently change existing spellings or normalize ratified `expedite=15` / `next-up=25`; those remain distinct from `do_now`.
- QTI remains unlocated/unverified; #9241 is the existing provenance-recovery issue. #3424/#8575/#8579/#8602 are candidates/constraints, not presumed equivalents. Any overlapping persisted field/schema change waits for the QTI crosswalk and named current owner.
- Runtime gates: implementation starts only after the document PR is merged, the exact curated requirement IDs are integrated, and this issue's granular prerequisite edges are resolved. Schema/migration, production rollout, telemetry, authenticated remote writes, deployed behavior, and live acceptance each require their own explicit evidence and approval. Normal triage does not inherit urgency 450/Do Now.
- Projection rows being rebuildable/disposable does not authorize deleting the PM PostgREST database or unrelated tables. Preserve unique human-authored `pmp_links`/link writes and all unrelated tables; follow the existing backup/restore requirements before any future migration or cleanup.
- Compatibility: no storage change; proposed version only.
- Rollback: Disable only the new capability; preserve pending intents, artifacts, existing state, and remote effects. No broad reset, destructive cleanup, or deletion of history.

## Source trail

- Raw source refs: handoff `sources/01_handoff_pm_stack_fleet_orchestration.md`; charter `sources/02_charter_v1_1.md`; recovered original `sources/04_recovered_original_combined_design.md`; cited source section(s) in `sources/03_full_orchestration_proposal.md` as named by the component; exact occurrence citations are in the curated trace above when allocated.
- Design ref: `components/9208-typed-dependencies-notes-journal-field-authority.md`, slice `DEP-02` (proposal only).
- Prior-art/evidence receipts: `research/track-a-state-of-art.md`, `research/track-b-state-of-art.md`, `research/track-b-sources.json`; additional exact evidence anchors for this slice: see the pinned census and component evidence links above.
- Parent-approved support mapping (validation/expansion support only, not a direct slice-key match): none.
- Existing external requirement refs not assigned a new curated ID: none.
- Command allocation: `dependency.add, dependency.blockers, dependency.graph, dependency.list, dependency.ready, dependency.remove, flag.blocked-by, flag.blocks, flag.depth, flag.hard`. Full command inventory remains `census/commands.jsonl`; exact allocation source is `census/command-slice-map.jsonl` (215 rows, no wildcard). V1 baseline keys are not refiled as duplicate implementation issues.
- Shared architecture: `architecture.md`; FDR index: `decisions/README.md` (all FDR-PMO records remain proposed, not ratified).

---

### Original slice text (preserved)

### DEP-02 — Typed edge model, canonical direction, and JSON/error contract

**Tier:** crucial. **Goal:** pure `relations.rs` types/validation for seven spellings, canonical target refs, hardness/status/provenance/certainty/revisions, before/after and shared error envelope. **Owns:** `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/work/relations.rs`; tests in same module. **Hard blockers:** granular #9206 shared `contracts.rs` identity/result schema (authority_id/work_id string pair, snake_case, decimal string versions), not whole #9206; #9198 storage identity. **First failing oracle:** add `pmo_dep_aliases_normalize_to_one_canonical_edge` and `pmo_dep_edge_wire_preserves_before_after`; confirm both listed and failing before implementation. **Done command:** `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml -p fleet-queue --lib --features client,queue-broker pmo_dep_` after checking exact test names with the same command plus `-- --list`. **Negative:** same GH number across repos, inverse duplicate, unknown enum, shorthand under ambiguous authority, unresolved external target. **Migration:** no storage change; proposed version only. **Docs:** update examples to shared snake_case contract.

- `CLI-08` → `DEP-02`: Dependency verbs/options are merged across DEP-02/DEP-03/DEP-04; readiness consumes the typed graph, no second graph. ## Prerequisites and sequencing

Hard blockers named by the source slice, after granular-key normalization: No inferred hard edge is added at preparation time; parent integration must resolve granular contracts before the native graph is applied.

Existing issue references retained as non-blocking runtime/evidence gates: none.
Domain-starter parent references are never emitted as hard native blockers. Source parents normalized to granular slices or runtime gates: none.




Use only granular issue-key edges after all keys are resolved. Never make a whole domain starter a hard blocker when it creates a cycle. File collisions are hard sequencing edges. Parent integration adds native parent/blocker edges in a later pass after the command map, requirements IDs, and acyclic graph are verified.

## Starting failing test, oracle, and done check

- **First failing test:** `work_park_requires_durable_checkpoint_before_release`
- **Oracle:** The source slice’s stated reference model, golden fixture, or invariant; compare expected and observed state explicitly. No mock-only claim of deployed/live behavior.
- **Done command:** ``cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml -p fleet-queue --lib --features client,queue-broker work_park_requires_durable_checkpoint_before_release` passes; every transition defines partial recovery and receipts separate delivery/ack/start. |`
- Tests must first be listed by exact name in the owning target (`-- --list`); assert the test exists before execution. A zero-test filter passing is not acceptance.

## Acceptance and negative cases

`cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml -p fleet-queue --lib --features client,queue-broker work_park_requires_durable_checkpoint_before_release` passes; every transition defines partial recovery and receipts separate delivery/ack/start. |

Negative coverage: stale input, duplicate/replay, ambiguous resource, unauthorized actor, partial remote effect, unknown version, and no false verified/completed result where applicable.

## Compatibility, migration, and runtime gates

- Preserve the current queue/status/identity/Project-writer/Fleet `gh` compatibility surfaces. Do not silently change existing spellings or normalize ratified `expedite=15` / `next-up=25`; those remain distinct from `do_now`.
- QTI remains unlocated/unverified; #9241 is the existing provenance-recovery issue. #3424/#8575/#8579/#8602 are candidates/constraints, not presumed equivalents. Any overlapping persisted field/schema change waits for the QTI crosswalk and named current owner.
- Runtime gates: implementation starts only after the document PR is merged, the exact curated requirement IDs are integrated, and this issue's granular prerequisite edges are resolved. Schema/migration, production rollout, telemetry, authenticated remote writes, deployed behavior, and live acceptance each require their own explicit evidence and approval. Normal triage does not inherit urgency 450/Do Now.
- Projection rows being rebuildable/disposable does not authorize deleting the PM PostgREST database or unrelated tables. Preserve unique human-authored `pmp_links`/link writes and all unrelated tables; follow the existing backup/restore requirements before any future migration or cleanup.
- Compatibility: Additive and reversible only after existing owner/schema review; retain prior data and behavior; no silent fallback or dual authority.
- Rollback: Disable only the new capability; preserve pending intents, artifacts, existing state, and remote effects. No broad reset, destructive cleanup, or deletion of history.
