code.title: ci: PR workflow runs cancelled en masse before finishing (PR #8858 runs, 2026-11-12); one mcpx run stuck queued
code.body:
## Problem

Pull-request workflow runs in this repo are being cancelled en masse before they can finish, so PR checks never reach a real pass/fail conclusion.

## Evidence (2026-11-12, PR #8858, head d42d6cb3c3)

- Original runs 43165830647 (fleet-search-parity-guard), 43165830657 (mcpx test), 43165830659 (scripts-test), 43165830668/43165830768 (mcpx docs), 43165830773 (proxy port fallbacks) all started 2026-11-12T06:06:39Z and were all CANCELLED at 06:24:15–06:24:18Z.
- Four runs were re-run at ~06:33Z; the re-runs were CANCELLED again at ~06:46Z after ~13m16s each. Every conclusion is CANCELLED, none is FAILURE.
- Run 43165830657 (mcpx test) is stuck in QUEUED state: its jobs were cancelled but its `mcpx-test ci-ok` job has been queued since 06:24Z; `gh run cancel` was requested at ~06:36Z and the run still showed `queued` minutes later, and `gh run rerun` refuses with "already running".

## Impact

- Lanes cannot satisfy a checks-green merge gate on any PR while this lasts; work either stalls in park loops or merges on local verification under the CI-runs-on-main doctrine.
- The stuck queued run also leaves a permanent pending check on affected PRs.

## Ask

Find what cancels these runs (concurrency group with cancel-in-progress, a fleet watchdog/cleanup job, runner-side cancellation, or GitHub-side), fix the canceller or the workflow config, and clear/repair stuck queued runs like 43165830657.

Found by lane any-a while working task 14521 / PR #8858.

code.title: Attribution: declarative auditd for signal syscalls on the laptop (follow-up to #8777)
code.body:
Follow-up to #8777 (the 2026-11-11T22:01:09Z SIGTERM that killed pm-aggregator and pm-dispatch in the same second, sender unidentified).

## Why

The laptop kernel supports auditing (CONFIG_AUDIT=y, CONFIG_AUDITSYSCALL=y) but no audit tooling is installed and no rules exist, so a signal sent by hand leaves no record anywhere: systemd logs the death, never the sender. The two pm units are covered meanwhile by the sigterm-witness wrapper (live via drop-ins; declarative in PR #8786), but every other process on the box is still unattributed.

## Ask

Enable auditd declaratively in the laptop's NixOS configuration, with rules that log signal-sending syscalls with the sender's identity, e.g.:

```
-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S kill -S tkill -S tgkill -k signal-attribution
```

so any future "who killed this process" question is answered by `ausearch -k signal-attribution` (auid, exe, pid, comm of the sender) instead of an investigation.

## Notes / constraints

- This needs root and a system activation — it cannot be hot-installed. Ride the coordinated switch or a maintenance window; do not hand-install packages outside the NixOS config.
- Signal syscalls are not a hot path on this box; expected log volume is low. Keep the rule set to kill-family syscalls only.
- The witness on the pm units stays: it is per-service, survives even if auditd is later dropped, and its log sits next to the service's state.

## Acceptance

From a marked shell, send SIGTERM to a throwaway process; show the audit record names the sender (auid/exe/pid). Note the verification on this issue.

code.title: Decisions page 'crash' 2026-11-11: pm-aggregator + pm-dispatch SIGTERM'd mid-session, no self-heal (Restart=on-failure treats SIGTERM as clean)
code.body:
## Symptom

2026-11-11 ~16:03 CST: Drew reported "the front end crashed when I was using it" about the decisions page (set `decisions-2026-11-11`, #8766) while working through it on his phone.

## Timeline (all verified on the laptop, 2026-11-11)

- 21:49–22:00Z — Drew lands 18 resolutions on the page (answers, defers incl. guided, request-infos with notes/comments). Store and fleet feed agree exactly: 18 landed, none lost, none corrupt.
- 22:00:46Z — his last landed resolution (router-edge-6649 #3, request-info with note).
- 22:01:09Z — **pm-aggregator and pm-dispatch are both SIGTERM'd in the same second** (systemd: `code=killed, signal=TERM` for both). Neither restarts. Both services share an identical ExecStart command line (`bun run src/server.ts`), so a single pattern-based kill takes both at once. The sender is not identifiable from the journal (no auditd on the laptop); pm-git-sync is exonerated (it was failing on its dirty-tree guard, which fires before it touches any service).
- 22:01:32Z — the stack sentinel notices the aggregator is down; nothing restarts it.
- ~22:03Z — Drew's next interaction hits the dead backend (public origin 502 / connection refused) — the "crash" he saw. The v2 page JS itself is not the cause: it rendered and submitted correctly for all 18 of his resolutions, its inline script parses cleanly against the live set, and all question text reaches the page only through `esc()`.

## Root cause

1. Both PM services received SIGTERM and died together.
2. Their units run `Restart=on-failure`, and systemd counts SIGTERM as a *clean* exit — so the self-heal never fired. A stop nobody issued through systemctl leaves the stack down indefinitely.

## Accounting for Drew's work

- Landed and safe (18/24): census-agent-sdks #1 (info), census-link-system #1 (info), census-quota-benchmark #1 (Keep deferred), census-close-batch #1+#2, review-loop-2025 #1+#2, host-eval-3039 #1, id-engine-5536 #1, bot-autoclose-7610 #1 (deferred), joplin-7676 #1 (deferred, lean approve, guided), opencode-autocheck-10 #1 (answered) + #2 (deferred, guided) + #3 (info), open-knowledge-6435 #1, router-edge-6649 #1+#2+#3 (info, with his notes).
- Still open (6): router-edge-6649 #4, #5, #6; watch-cadence-7013 #1; gpl-uploads-5984 #1; release-3792 #1.
- Anything Drew typed but never submitted after 22:00:46Z (most plausibly a draft note on router-edge #4, the next question he was on) lived only in the browser and is unrecoverable server-side. Everything he submitted is intact.

## Fix

- Services restarted 22:06Z; board + attention verified 200; decisions page re-verified with zero-effect probes (bad token 403) and the production store byte-identical.
- systemd drop-ins: `Restart=always` for pm-aggregator + pm-dispatch, so a raw SIGTERM self-heals in seconds. (Durable home for this policy is the home-manager source that generates these units — the drop-ins under `~/.config/systemd/user/*.service.d/` carry it until the source adopts it.)
- Decisions page draft persistence (this issue's PR): in-progress answers, comments, defer picks, info notes, and bulk selections are saved to localStorage as Drew types and restored on load; recorded questions' drafts prune automatically. A dead backend or a crashed tab can never again eat typed work.
- Regression tests: draft-script wiring + parse, and `esc()` script-breakout neutralization, in `test/decisions.test.ts`.

## Follow-ups

- Identify the SIGTERM sender if it recurs — with `Restart=always` a recurrence becomes a seconds-long blip with a fresh journal trail (start/stop timestamps) instead of an outage.
- pm-git-sync has been failing every ~35s all afternoon on untracked `.bak` files in the primary checkout (its dirt guard counts untracked backups as dirt) — deploy path fragility worth its own look; not this incident's cause.

Related: #8766 (the decisions feature).

code.title: needs-drew: close the alert incident when the question is answered
code.body:
**Symptom.** When a needs-drew question (code#8568) is answered, its alert incident stays `open` forever. The aggregator has no close path for `needs-drew:<ledgerId>` incidents: the answer endpoint records the answer, the candidate disappears (no re-push), but the incident row is never closed, so the board accumulates answered questions as open incidents.

**Evidence.** The #8568 live proof run, 2026-11-11: question `proof-8568-needs-drew` raised 07:44:12Z, push sent 07:44:12.982Z, answer recorded 07:44:35Z (`optionId: seen, via: api`), task 14917 unblocked + cancelled — the incident was still `open` minutes later and was closed by hand through the aggregator's own Supabase client (`status='closed', closed_at=now()`; verified in `/api/alerts.json`).

**Scope.** In the aggregator's answer path (where `recordAnswer` succeeds for a needs-drew question), close the open incident for key `needs-drew:<ledgerId>` — the store already has `AlertsStore.closeOpenIncidentByKey` (built for stack-health "up" events in #8568). Same treatment when a raised question's task is cancelled without an answer, if a clean signal for that exists; otherwise answer-close alone is the fix.

**Acceptance.** Raise a test needs-drew question, answer it, and read back the incident as `closed` in `/api/alerts.json` with no manual store write. No change to push behavior (answered questions already stop re-pushing).

Refs: #8568 (Phase 1), design `pm-stack-notifications-design-2026-11-11.md` §5/§8.

code.title: Fleet unification slice 7: label de-mirroring and the final reconciliation
code.body:
Parent design: #8575 (one door, one home per fact — fleet tool state unification). Slice 7 of 7 — the closing slice; it lands after slices 1–6. Approved by Drew 2026-11-11: implement in full.

## Work

1. **Label de-mirroring:** stop writing queue-state mirror labels (the queue/claimed-style labels that copy database state onto GitHub). Labels change only at durable transitions: triaged, done, blocked on the user, and the standing hard-stop labels. Remove the mirroring writes from every producer, lane runbook, and helper.
2. **Final reconciliation:** one pass over the broker-era parked/blocked backlog reconciling database rows against GitHub state, using slice 1's classification: coordination rows expire or re-queue; durable facts get written to their GitHub home; divergences are listed on this issue, not silently resolved.
3. **Retire the backlog:** when the pass completes, the standing broker-to-label reconciliation backlog is closed out and the recurring reconciliation work is deleted — there is nothing left to reconcile, because there is one home per fact.

## Acceptance

- No code path in the fleet writes a queue-state mirror label (verified by search plus a week of label-change audit on a sample of worked issues).
- The reconciliation pass reports counts: rows expired, facts moved to GitHub, divergences found and their dispositions.
- The reconciliation backlog items are closed with a link to this issue's final report.

   - R2 bundles: scheduled git bundles of each repo stored in R2.

## Acceptance

code.title: Fleet unification slice 5: local coordination replica for database-down resilience
code.body:
Parent design: #8575 (one door, one home per fact — fleet tool state unification). Slice 5 of 7. Approved by Drew 2026-11-11: implement in full.

## Work

Database-down resilience for coordination:

1. Run a Turso embedded replica of the coordination tables on the laptop, so claims, leases, and heartbeats continue against the local copy when the cloud database or the broker path is unreachable.
2. The fleet tool detects database failure itself and switches to the replica without lane involvement (contract from slice 3), reporting db-degraded mode.
3. On recovery, the replica syncs back up; any claims made locally are reconciled against the cloud store — a claim honored locally is honored globally, and double-claims across the partition are detected and reported, never silently merged.
4. Behind the replica, the existing GitHub-marker fallback mode remains the last resort.

## Acceptance

- A drill: database made unreachable mid-shift; lanes keep claiming and working against the replica; on restoration, sync completes with zero lost claims and any partition double-claims surfaced in a report.
- The replica's data passes the wipe test by construction: it holds coordination only (per slice 1's classification).

code.title: Fleet unification slice 3: fleet verb contract v2 — routes and degraded modes in the tool
code.body:
Parent design: #8575 (one door, one home per fact — fleet tool state unification). Slice 3 of 7. Approved by Drew 2026-11-11: implement in full.

## Work

Fleet verb contract v2: every fleet queue verb declares, in the tool itself, its route order and its degraded behavior for each failure leg — GitHub write failure, GitHub read failure, database failure. The verb reports the mode it actually operated in (normal, gh-write-degraded, gh-read-degraded, db-degraded) on every call. The tool also caches a significant working set of issues from the database mirror (slice 2) so lanes spend almost no GitHub reads.

Per Drew's ruling on #8575: never stop working. No verb refuses to operate because a leg is degraded or a mirror is stale; it degrades, says so, and continues.

Lane instruction bodies then shrink to calling the verbs: all fallback improvisation comes out of the lane runbooks.

## Acceptance

- A mode line on every verb's output, machine-readable, naming the route used.
- A drill per leg: with GitHub writes blocked, claims and work proceed and outcomes buffer; with GitHub reads blocked, lanes run off the mirror and cache; with the database blocked, slice 5's replica path engages.
- Lane runbooks updated in the same change to remove local fallback logic.

Refs #12538 (tracking dispatch). Refs #12756 (mode-line slice PR for the acceptance remainder).

code.title: Design: one door, one home per fact — the fleet tool owns every route and every fallback
code.body:
# Design: one door, one home per fact — the fleet tool owns every route and every fallback

Direction from Drew (2026-11-11): the fleet tool is used for most interactions; it must handle all known and future edge cases and fallback itself. There must be a written plan for each failure scenario: GitHub write failure, GitHub read failure, and database failure.

## Problem

The queue grew two durable stores for the same facts: the broker database (task outcomes, parked/blocked state, attempt history) and GitHub (issues, labels, PRs). Keeping them in sync is a permanent tax, and its failures are the fleet's top infra problem: lane registrations dropped mid-shift (unknown lane_id verdicts), claims evaporating or stamped with the wrong lane, parked handoffs re-served immediately, and a standing broker-to-label reconciliation backlog. The broker concept itself is not the flaw — a database is the right tool for coordination. The flaw is that the database also holds durable truth that GitHub holds too.

## Principle: one home per fact, tested by the wipe test

- Coordination (claims, leases, heartbeats, checkpoints, merge-order lists) lives in the database. It is ephemeral by design: wiping the database tonight may lose only in-flight leases; lanes re-claim in the morning.
- Durable truth (what a task is, whether it is done) lives on GitHub: the issue, its labels at durable transitions only, the outcome agent note, the close. About three writes per task.
- Labels stop mirroring claim state. The queue/claimed-style labels were the database copied onto GitHub — that mirroring is the sync traffic. Labels change only at durable moments: triaged, done, blocked on the user.
- Every field in the database must pass the wipe test: if wiping it would lose what was decided or done, it does not belong there.

## The fleet tool is the only door

Lanes never call GitHub or the database directly. Every fleet verb routes per current health, names the mode it is operating in, and carries its degraded behavior as part of the verb contract — a lane never improvises a fallback mid-shift. New edge cases get absorbed into the tool, not into lane instructions.

## Pieces

1. GitHub mirror in the database: the DB keeps a cached copy of most GitHub details (issues, labels, PR state, latest notes), fed by a GitHub webhook to a Cloudflare Worker that writes the DB. The webhook-to-Worker-to-Turso sink pattern is already live for CI events (#5693); this extends it. A slow backfill sweep repairs missed webhooks. The cache is a read model, rebuildable from GitHub at any time — never a second truth.
2. Tool-side caching: the fleet tool caches a significant number of issues from the DB, so a shift's working set (a few hundred issues) is local-fast and spends almost no GitHub reads.
3. Always-fresh local clone: a fetcher keeps the laptop clones updated at all times, so branching off current main never needs the network.
4. Local stack discipline: finished work stacks — each branch based on the previous branch's tip, with the intended merge order recorded in the database. Worth having even when GitHub is healthy: it makes ordering explicit instead of twenty lanes racing off the same main.

## Scenario plans

- GitHub writes fail (outage or rate limit): work continues. Lanes keep claiming from the database, keep working known items, and stack branches locally. Merge intents and outcome notes queue in the database (the outbox pattern, moved server-side) and replay on recovery, walking the stack bottom-up: push, open, merge, rebase the next branch onto the new main. The lane that wrote a change owns its conflicts at replay.
- GitHub reads fail: lanes run off the database copy. The tool surfaces mirror staleness (time of last webhook received) on every read. Discovery of brand-new items pauses; everything already mirrored keeps moving.
- Database fails: the laptop holds a local replica of the coordination tables (Turso embedded replica), so claiming continues on the laptop alone. Behind that, the existing GitHub-marker fallback mode is the last resort. On recovery the replica syncs up and the GitHub mirror backfills.
- Backups: Turso gets a scheduled export into D1 (same SQLite family, restorable; doubles as the analytics copy). The repos get a mirror push to a second home plus bundles in R2. Open question: whether Cloudflare repo hosting is the right second home for the repos — evaluate before committing.

## Non-goals

- No better reconciler between two durable stores. That is the sync burden with extra steps.
- No lane-instruction fallback logic. Fallback lives in the tool.

## Implementation slices (to be broken out as child issues)

1. Wipe-test audit of the current queue schema: classify every table/field as coordination (stays) or truth (moves to GitHub / becomes derived cache).
2. GitHub mirror: extend the #5693 webhook Worker to issues/PRs/comments/labels into the DB, plus the backfill sweep and a staleness readout.
3. Fleet verb contract v2: every verb declares its route order and degraded behavior per scenario; lanes' instructions shrink to calling the verbs.
4. Merge-intent queue and stack replay: local stacking, recorded merge order, bottom-up replay with conflict ownership.
5. Local coordination replica on the laptop and the DB-down drill.
6. Backups: Turso-to-D1 scheduled export with a restore drill; repo mirror plus R2 bundles; evaluate Cloudflare repo hosting as the second home.
7. Label de-mirroring: stop writing queue-state labels; one final reconciliation pass over the parked backlog, then the reconciliation backlog itself is retired.

code.title: pm-stack Phase 3: consolidation — merge aggregator, quota gatherer, fleet-feed collector and projector into one pm-core service (dispatch stays separate)
code.body:
## Phase 3 — consolidation: the glued-together tools become one core service

Design: `pm-stack-notifications-design-2026-11-11.md` (goal keep-the-four-repos-healthy, files/). Siblings: #8568 (Phase 1, producers), #8569 (Phase 2, edge relay). Context: #5082 (board dies with empty replies while siblings struggle), the pending pm-projector socket-activation work.

### What recon established

The "five tools" are already ONE Bun/TypeScript monorepo (`pm-stack/` in this repo) deployed as separate laptop processes from one checkout:

| Process today | Reality |
|---|---|
| pm-aggregator (:4870) | `bun run aggregator/src/server.ts` — board, quota views, attention, alert throat + push engine |
| quota-gatherer (timer) | `bun run aggregator/scripts/gather-quota.ts` — a script in the aggregator package, writes `quota-current.json` |
| fleet-feed-collector (timer) | `bun run aggregator/scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts` — same package, writes `fleet-feed.json` |
| pm-projector (:7801) | `bun run projector/src/index.ts` — GitHub webhook intake + reconcile; disposable projection DB; aggregator reads it over HTTP (`PM_PROJECTOR_URL`) |
| pm-dispatch (:4879) | separate Bun app, public via tunnel (`dispatch.security.cab`), holds session-launch authority |

State passes between them as files in `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/` and one HTTP hop — which is how the board 503s when a sibling is unhealthy, and why every deploy/restart story is five stories.

### The merged shape

- **pm-core** (one process): the aggregator server with the gatherer and feed collector folded in as in-process schedulers (same code, no file-polling handoff — freshness becomes in-memory, the JSON files remain as audit/debug artifacts written by the process, not read by it), the notification engine (already in-process), and the projector as a module: its webhook listener keeps its own port (public intake is a different trust surface) but runs in the same process, and the board reads projections in-process instead of over HTTP. The pending projector socket-activation work is absorbed into the core's listener story instead of being solved a second time.
- **pm-dispatch stays separate**: public ingress + session-launch authority is a different security posture, and it was just rebuilt under the item-5 work.
- **Kaneo + the Cloudflare Tunnel stay as they are** (upstream container; ingress).

Net: 5 laptop processes in the pm family → 2 (pm-core, pm-dispatch), one restart story, one deploy story.

### Acceptance (Drew's terms)

- One service restart moves board + quota + feed + projections together; there is no sibling process left whose bad day makes /board return 503.
- `systemctl --user` shows pm-core + pm-dispatch (+ tunnel) as the whole pm family; the two timer units are gone, replaced by in-process schedules with the same cadences (quota ~15 min ticks, feed ~5 min).
- Killing the projection module's GitHub intake degrades board link data visibly (provenance chips say so) — it does not take the board down.
- All pre-existing machine surfaces keep their shapes: /api/board.json, /api/quota.json, /api/attention.json, /api/alerts.json, /api/needs-drew.json byte-compatible for current consumers (fleet minder, steward, globalping watch).

code.title: id: implement program update channels + update flow into worlds (from #6293)
code.body:
# Implement: program update channels + update flow into worlds

Implementation next step from the Phase-14 Program ecosystem v2 step #6293 (gallery & updates); design of record: `doc/2026-11-11T05-24-00Z_design_id_program_ecosystem_v2/` (Program ecosystem — v2 design: gallery & updates), refining core decision D4 from `doc/2026-11-10T21-24-00Z_design_id_program_ecosystem/`. The registry side of v2 is issue #8281; this issue is the update machinery the v1 design explicitly deferred ("v1 records the policy field but builds no channel machinery — that is v2", v1 record §3).

## Scope
- Channel machinery behind the install record's policy field (v1 record §3 step 5): a channel is one author's version line for one program name — the (author key, name) pair of the D1 identity. `pinned` (the default) never changes without a fresh install decision; `tracking` opts an install into update discovery for exactly that line. A fork is a different line: lineage is history, not a channel (v1 record §4) — no install ever tracks a parent or a fork.
- Update discovery: a newer bundle for the tracked line, arriving by any path — a registry (#8281), pkarr, a self-hosted registry, or a local file — is an update candidate. Discovery is pull-based, at world-owner action; no background auto-fetch for any policy.
- Update application: the candidate runs the v1 import verification pipeline first (hash, F12.17 signature, F12.7 ABI fit, provenance check). Then the D4 envelope decides: an update that keeps the ABI descriptor, widens no required capabilities, and migrates state under the F12.9 (#1066) rules may apply under a tracking policy the owner chose; anything outside that envelope requires explicit world-owner approval, presented with the from→to identities, the author's changelog (signed manifest data; its absence is shown as "no changelog provided", never filled in), the ABI/capability delta, and the migration outcome. Rollback per F12.9 is part of the same act, and a failed update leaves the prior install untouched. Quotas re-check at apply time (F12.10, #1067).
- A bundle whose (author key, name) differs from the installed line is not an update — it is a new install through the ordinary v1 path.

## Dependencies
- Issue #8280 (signed bundle format + sideload import) — the import pipeline and install record this builds on.
- F12.9 upgrade/migration/rollback (#1066, spec landed), F12.7 ABI (#1064, spec landed).
- Registry-fed discovery rides issue #8281; file/registry-free discovery must not wait for it.

## Acceptance
- A tracking install discovers and applies an in-envelope update end to end; the install record after the act names the new D1 identity and preserves the policy.
- An out-of-envelope update (ABI widened, capabilities widened, or migration failure) does not apply without explicit owner approval; the refusal names the envelope term it breached.
- A pinned install is never modified by update discovery — discovery reports availability only.
- A failed or refused update leaves the previously installed version running, and rollback restores it byte-identically (F12.9 oracle).
- The same update offered via a local file and via a registry produces identical outcomes (path-independence oracle).

code.title: Atlas boundary remediation: secret-bearing rows still live in the production monolith and a local replica (#6021 wave 1)
code.body:
# Atlas boundary remediation: secret-bearing rows still live in the production monolith and a local replica (from #6021 wave 1)

Filed from the #6021 wave-1 revalidation scan (2026-11-11, queue task 10513; counts/classes/locations only — no content reproduced).

## Finding

The tier boundary inside the sharded corpus is clean: across all 29 internal Atlas DBs (107,001 chunks + 70,987 content-store messages), the number of rows labeled `secret-bearing` is **0**, and the secret tier holds exactly its labeled set (atlas-core-secret-main-01: 638/638 chunks secret-bearing; atlas-core-secret-content: 564 messages, all in secret-bearing sessions).

But the standing rule — secret material exists ONLY in the 2 secret DBs — does not hold outside the shard set:

1. **Production libSQL monolith (`atlas`, the shards' `source_db`):** 107,639 chunks, of which **638 are labeled `secret-bearing`** (100,060 personal + 6,941 local-only + 638 secret-bearing) — the full secret set, co-resident with the whole internal corpus in one database.
2. **Local replica `~/atlas/turso-atlas/data/atlas-publish-v2-2026-10-31.db` (laptop):** a full monolith copy carrying the same **638 secret-bearing chunks / 90 secret-bearing sessions**.
3. **Pre-tiering local snapshots** (`~/atlas/atlas-2026-10-26.db`, eval snapshots, staged-laptop DBs, sandbox archive copy): full/partial corpus copies from before the sensitivity column existed; labels are not carried in-file, so secret-bearing presence cannot be label-verified — treat as unclassified copies of a corpus that contained the secret set.

## Remediation decision needed

Pick and implement one, under parent #6018 (relate to the classification manifest work, #5410):

- **(a) Purge:** delete the secret-bearing rows from the monolith (post-restore it is a source of record, not a serving tier) and delete/replace the local replicas; shards remain the only live corpus. Requires an ingestion story for how new secret-class content reaches the secret shards without landing in the monolith first (see staging path #5669).
- **(b) Reclassify:** formally declare the monolith (and any retained replica) secret-tier storage, with access controls and handling to match, and amend the standing rule so the boundary statement is true as written.

Until one lands, the #6021 boundary statement must be reported as: boundary holds inside the shard set; does not hold for the monolith or local replicas.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Decision (a) or (b) recorded with rationale, linked from #6021 and #6018.
- [ ] Implemented and re-verified with the wave-1 scan method (counts/labels only): either monolith + replicas show 0 secret-bearing rows, or the rule text + controls match the reclassification.

## Problem

When the OpenClaw gateway dies, nothing off-box notices: the 2026-11-04 gateway death was silent for ~24h because the heartbeat dies with the gateway (issue #6167 §5). Any watch must NOT live inside OpenClaw itself.

## Scope (from #6167 §5, filed by queue task 14521)

Parent: #5030; related: #5203 (measurement), #1084 (fabric), #1090 (recovery), #1092 (workloads).

## Goal
Implement the egress operating controls proposed in #5030 and PR #8399 once the design and WAN fabric are reviewed. #5203 owns counters, provider meters, reports and alerts; this issue owns enforcement, not a duplicate dashboard.

## Scope and acceptance
- Declaratively configure and document a recoverable admission/shaping mechanism at the actual WAN or transfer scheduler, using separately measured ingress and egress rates; validate the provisional rolling-window target against link tests.
- Test holds of optional bulk at the approved monthly budget thresholds, earlier provider hard-wall safety margins including lag and in-flight work, and 95% pause of deferrable jobs; stale/missing metrics must not imply safe admission.
- Preserve health, security, control-plane, interactive recovery, and the sole recoverable backup; document explicit operator override and idempotent pause/resume. No automatic destructive deletion or unrestricted paid overage.
- Exercise fiber loss, candidate 100 Mbps fallback and return to primary using a representative test topology, verifying the degradation order and restore viability. Do not assume an alternate is provisioned.
- Record runnable tests and actual enforcement points; work with #1084, #1090 and #1092 to avoid conflicting network/recovery policy. No purchases or production rollout without approvals.

Dependencies: #5030 design review, #1084 WAN design, and #5203 authoritative metrics. Plan-specific quotas and live usage remain unknown until verified.

code.title: Scheduled Suggestions — developing-today/code
code.body:
You are a code-review agent running as a dispatched session in this
repository. Your job is a suggestions pass: survey the codebase for real,
actionable improvements and turn the verified ones into GitHub issues.

## Dispatch context — read this first

- You are running in this repository's LAPTOP CHECKOUT (the repo's primary
  checkout on the owner's laptop). Work there; do not clone the repo
  elsewhere.
- A tracking issue and a queue task were ALREADY created for this run by
  the dispatcher, and this session is already claimed against them. Do
  NOT create another tracking issue for this run, and do not dispatch
  further tasks.
- There is NO plan-approval step. Proceed directly; do not stop to ask
  for approval of a plan.

## What to review

Survey the codebase across these five areas:

- **Cleanup** — dead code, duplicated logic, obsolete files or config,
  leftover scaffolding.
- **Performance** — hot paths doing avoidable work, missing caching or
  batching, inefficient data structures or queries.
- **Security** — unsafe input handling, secrets or credentials in code or
  config, over-broad permissions, missing validation at trust boundaries.
- **Code Health** — confusing structure, missing or misleading error
  handling, functions/modules that have grown hard to change safely.
- **Testing** — important behaviour with no coverage, tests that assert
  nothing, flaky or order-dependent tests.

## Verify before you file — no speculative filings

Every candidate finding MUST be verified against the actual code before
it becomes an issue:

- Read the code at the location you cite. Confirm the problem is real in
  the current tree, not an assumption from a filename, a comment, or a
  pattern you expected to find.
- Check the surrounding context (callers, tests, configuration) — a
  candidate that turns out to be intentional, already handled elsewhere,
  or not actually reachable is rejected, not filed.
- Search the repo's OPEN issues before filing. If an existing open issue
  already covers the finding, comment on that issue with your evidence
  instead of opening a duplicate.

## Filing

- Per real, verified finding, file ONE issue in this repo with
  `gh issue create` from the laptop checkout. Each issue must include:
  - the canonical component label for its area; use `app/pm-stack` for
    PM-stack / aggregator issues in this repo. `app/aggregator` is a legacy
    alias and must not be used for new filings.
  - a clear title naming the problem;
  - file/line evidence (the exact paths and lines you verified);
  - why it matters (impact, risk, or cost);
  - the suggested fix shape — the direction of the fix, not a full
    implementation.
- CAP: at most **5 filings per pass** (new issues plus evidence comments
  on existing issues). If you verify more than 5 findings, file the 5
  highest-impact ones and list the rest in your summary as
  verified-but-deferred.
- Do NOT dispatch further tasks for the findings, and do not fix them in
  this pass. The issues are the record; the fleet's normal lanes pick
  work up from them.

## Finish

End with a short summary — as your session output, and as a comment on
this run's tracking issue if you can identify it — covering:

- **Filed** — each issue you opened or commented on, with its number and
  one line on the finding.
- **Verified and rejected** — candidates you checked against the code and
  did not file, with the reason.
- **Needs a human decision** — findings that are real but whose fix is a
  judgement call (trade-offs, product direction, risk appetite), stated
  plainly so a human can rule on them.

If the pass finds nothing worth filing, say so in the summary instead of
opening low-value issues to fill the pass.

---

code.title: id(phase-14) v2 step 4: owner review tooling (#6301)
code.body:
Step 4 of the v2 agents-as-citizens breakdown (#6301; outline §2.5, §6).

**Scope:** owner review as a working surface rendered from the audit log (which remains the record of truth): a per-agent review view for a world (role, quota state, recent actions and refusals per agent); a one-shot approval queue — an above-ceiling refusal can be offered to the owner as a single-action request, approval executes exactly that action under the owner's authority, audited as such, and never edits the role; refusal digests that surface repeated same-shape refusals as a pattern pointing at the role edit that fixes them. Standing approvals for an action class are NOT in scope unless Drew rules otherwise (open question 3 on #6301).

**Acceptance:**
- Review view renders per-agent role/quota/actions/refusals from the audit log alone.
- One-shot approval executes the one refused action, is audited as owner-authority, and leaves the role definition untouched (verified by test).
- A repeated-refusal pattern produces a digest naming the role edit that would fix it.

Blocked by v2 step 1 (role configuration) and step 3 (per-agent quota ledger). Parent: #6301 · core topic #6280.

code.title: id(phase-14) v2 step 3: per-agent quota ledger (#6301)
code.body:
Step 3 of the v2 agents-as-citizens breakdown (#6301; outline §2.3, §6).

**Scope:** per-(agent, world) quota ledgers on the policy point, replacing v1's per-session budget without changing the bridge or audit shapes. Budgets are granted with the role, replenish on the role's cadence, and persist across sessions — rejoining never resets a budget. Exhaustion parks the agent visibly, naming the replenishment time. The ledger event shape stays the one F12.10 (#1067) consumes, per v1 §9.3, so the ledger can become an account in the world's quota system when it lands. Owners can read spend per agent and per role.

**Acceptance:**
- Quota survives leave/rejoin cycles unchanged; charging is per action as in v1.
- Park event names the role's replenishment time; owner spend views exist per agent and per role.
- Event-shape compatibility with F12.10 is demonstrated against the #1067 design's consumed shape.

Blocked by v2 step 1 (role configuration) and v1 spike step #7916 (policy point). Parent: #6301 · plan of record #6312 · core topic #6280.

code.title: id(phase-14) v2 step 2: multi-agent sessions under distinct roles (#6301)
code.body:
Step 2 of the v2 agents-as-citizens breakdown (#6301; outline §2.2, §2.4, §6).

**Scope:** several agents holding concurrent sessions in one world under distinct roles. Policy-point checks keyed by (agent, role); agent presence/visibility under the same frame rules as any shell; per-role concurrency caps with audited join refusals; the co-presence invariants — no agent-to-agent delegation or authority transfer, and no agent channel outside world state/chat (collaboration semantics on world state are v3 #6302, out of scope here).

**Acceptance:**
- Two+ agents with different roles act in one world concurrently, each held to its own ceiling; one agent's refusal never affects another's session.
- Concurrency cap refusal is audited with its reason.
- Tests prove no sequence of agent actions widens another agent's ceiling (the no-inter-agent-delegation invariant).

Blocked by v2 step 1 (role configuration) and v1 spike steps #7914 (MCP bridge) and #7916 (policy point). Parent: #6301 · core topic #6280.

code.title: id(phase-14) v2 step 1: role configuration — roles as first-class world config (#6301)
code.body:
Step 1 of the v2 agents-as-citizens breakdown (#6301; outline: `doc/2026-11-10_design_id6301_agents_as_citizens_v2_outline.md` §2.1, §6).

**Scope:** role definitions as first-class, versioned world configuration — the definition shape (capability ceiling, quota class, delegation-lifetime bounds, review policy), starter roles shipped as ordinary editable definitions (observer, participant, archivist-class editor), and the grant/list/revoke operations with their audit event shapes. A role edit is a versioned world-config change; a changed ceiling applies at the next frame check, not the next join.

**Acceptance:**
- Role definition shape + versioning recorded in the v2 design (outline decisions 1–2) and implemented in world configuration.
- Grant, list and revoke operations exist; every grant/revoke/role-edit is an audited world event.
- Starter roles are plain definitions a world can copy and edit — no privileged tier.
- Conformance: an agent whose role's ceiling is lowered mid-session is refused the newly out-of-ceiling action on its next frame.

Extends v1 (#6300) surfaces: role binding at join (v1 §4.1/§5) and the policy point (#7916). Parent: #6301 · core topic #6280 · principles #1240.

code.body:
# Implement: template-world snapshot export/import

Implementation next step from the Phase-14 Program ecosystem core topic #6278; design of record: `doc/2026-11-10T21-24-00Z_design_id_program_ecosystem/` (Program ecosystem — share, fork, gallery: first-pass research + design), decision D5.

## Scope
- Template export: snapshot a world into a template bundle — world state, installed programs (as bundle references by identity + content hash, never silently re-hosted binaries the exporter does not hold), and role definitions.
- Strip rules, explicit and recorded in the template manifest: member lists, credentials/secrets, per-user data, and grants are stripped by default; anything retained is named in the manifest. A template never carries another user's identity material.
- Template import: instantiate a new world from a template — fresh world identity, roles recreated empty, programs installed from their bundles with the standard verification path, state imported as the starting state.
- Local-first: export/import are file operations; no server required. Publishing a template through a gallery reuses the registry object family (separate issue).

## Acceptance
- Round-trip: export world W → import creates W' with the same programs (hash-verified), same role definitions (empty of members), and the template-scoped state; W' has a distinct world identity.
- Manifest accurately lists everything stripped and everything retained (verified against a fixture world containing members, grants, and per-user data — none of which appear in W').

code.body:
# Implement: gallery registry protocol + reference registry service

Implementation next step from the Phase-14 Program ecosystem core topic #6278; design of record: `doc/2026-11-10T21-24-00Z_design_id_program_ecosystem/` (Program ecosystem — share, fork, gallery: first-pass research + design), decision D6.

## Scope
- The gallery registry protocol: publish / unpublish / list / fetch operations over program-bundle records (identity, version, content hash, signature, lineage — the bundle format issue from #6278 carries the object), in the same protocol family as world discovery (T2) with a different object type, transported over iroh per the #1240 principles.
- Three publishing paths, one protocol: (1) publish to a big hosted registry, (2) publish on pkarr, (3) self-host a registry. A client must be able to read any of them identically; our hosted registry is a public backstop, never a requirement.
- Reference registry service: an operator-runnable registry (small-server scale) storing bundle records + bundles, enforcing only the operator's own admission policy (signature validity is protocol; admission is policy).
- Out of scope: public-gallery curation/moderation UX (v3 #6294 design), ranking, payments.

## Acceptance
- A bundle published to a self-hosted reference registry is listable and fetchable by a second host over iroh, and installs via the sideload-equivalent verification path.
- The same record published via pkarr resolves and verifies identically.
- Registry runs standalone (no dependency on the hosted instance) at small scale.

code.body:
# Home-resolution contract: disposition the `os.homedir()` surface against #5762

Follow-up from the Phase 4 closing inventory audit (issue #5763, design issue #5762, contract in `files/designs/code-home-resolution-contract.md`, goal workspace keep-the-four-repos-healthy).

## Why this is filed separately

The Phase 4 audit (#5763) fixed the same-shape sites in-phase (invented substitute directories: root anchoring, CWD fallback, literal `~`, hardcoded `/home/user`). The `os.homedir()` surface is a genuinely different shape:

- Node's `os.homedir()` on POSIX returns `$HOME` when set, and otherwise the **passwd entry** for the process uid. It never invents a path — but passwd resolution is exactly the fallback the #5762 contract **declined as the default** ("another silent substitution"), so these sites do not conform either.
- The sites are concentrated in a different deploy unit (pm-stack aggregator/dispatch/exporters — long-running operator services whose config modules resolve `homedir()` once at module load) plus the bin/ proxy family. Converting them is a per-unit helper + test sweep of its own, not an audit fix.

## Inventory (origin/main 7dc4aefa23, from the #5763 audit)

bin/: opencode-route-proxy.mjs:73,77,80 (config/runtime-config/db path defaults; env overrides exist), opencode-acp-adapter.mjs:148, proxy-relay.mjs:56 (after an XDG_STATE_HOME override), proxy-supervise.mjs:71,72,372,399, check-opencode-go-seating.mjs:73, record.mjs:61.
Plugin: .opencode/plugin/mcpx/daemon.ts:293 and pkgs/mcpx/plugin/opencode/mcpx/daemon.ts:293 (`env.HOME ?? homedir()` — note the empty-string case: `??` does not catch `""`).
pm-stack: aggregator/scripts/*.ts (append-usage-snapshots, backfill-usage-snapshots, collect-fleet-feed, collect-github-billing, gather-quota, confirm-charges-surfaced, produce-charge-candidates, record-claude-launch), aggregator/src/config.ts (9 sites), aggregator/src/meta-renewal.ts, aggregator/src/secrets.ts, dispatch/src/config.ts:116, cloudflare-export, meta-exporter, supabase-export, opencode-usage-export, opencode-claimant/install.mjs:30.

## Acceptance

- Each site dispositioned against the contract: conform (with the reason a passwd-resolved home is authoritative for that surface, recorded per the design's exception rule), or converted to a non-empty-HOME named-error helper for its deploy unit, with the probe matrix as tests (unset and empty both named errors; set = unchanged paths).
- No site left unexamined; closing inventory commented back on #5762.

code.title: Provider self-renewal audit 2026-11-09 — every door checked against Drew's rule (all providers renew themselves)
code.body:
# Provider self-renewal audit — 2026-11-09

Drew's rule (2026-11-09 20:42 CST): **all the providers renew themselves.** Every OAuth/token credential must refresh itself automatically; a provider dying on an expired token because renewal was missing, mis-targeted, or unprovisioned is a defect. Tonight produced three instances of that defect class — openai.main (sync wrote to the wrong door; fixed, fork PR #2237), _claude (credential blanked Nov 7; restored by hand), _antigravity (client secret never provisioned; fixed, PRs #8098/#8099). This audit checks **every** door against the rule so the class is closed, not just tonight's three instances.

Method (all reads 2026-11-10 ~02:45–03:00Z, laptop, generation 551, fork build ff9858a = deployed HEAD): live config pair `opencode.jsonc` (17 providers), credential store (24 rows, metadata only — no values read), deployed source (`packages/core/src/credential/codex-sync.ts`, `packages/core/src/integration.ts` resolve path, `packages/ai/src/providers/*-auth.ts`, `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/{openai,opencode}.ts`), CLI credential files (timestamps/lengths only), route_attempt serving evidence (last 24h), quota gatherer records.

## How renewal works in this fork (the two paths)

- **In-provider refresh:** `Integration.connection.resolve` refreshes any stored OAuth credential within 5 min of expiry, when its method implements `refresh` — **unless** the credential is stamped `externalRefresh`, in which case an external owner is the sole refresher (by design, to avoid rotating a shared refresh-token lineage twice).
- **External-owner sync:** CodexSync runs every 1 min, copies `~/.codex/auth.json` into the stored credential **whose account ID matches the file's account** (selectTarget), and stamps it `externalRefresh`. One account's tokens are never written into another account's credential.

## Per-provider table

| Provider | Auth | Credential lives | Renewal mechanism (as configured) | Classification | Evidence | Next expiry |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| openai.main | OAuth (ChatGPT) | credential row `cred_oKXp448…` | CodexSync from Muse file (account-ID match), externalRefresh | **SELF-RENEWS (proven)** | Deliberate stale-write rewritten by the sync within one tick 2026-11-10T01:26:44Z; row access length == CLI file's | 2026-11-19T02:49:10Z (CLI refreshes the lineage) |
| openai.alternate | OAuth (ChatGPT, Student) | credential row `cred_17514e9…` | In-provider refresh at resolve (openai plugin implements refresh for both methods). Deliberately NOT CodexSync's target — different account than the CLI file | **SELF-RENEWS (proven)** | Row refresh-write 2026-11-04T22:05:48Z (expiry +10d exactly) during continuous service; 2,175 successful attempts in the last 24h on that lineage; no externalRefresh stamp | 2026-11-14T22:05:48Z (auto-refreshes at resolve) |
| opencode-go.popesdrew | OAuth (Console) | credential row `cred_1a1bd3e0…` (base `opencode` row is the same lineage, same expiry) | In-provider refresh at resolve (opencode plugin implements refresh, writes back the rotated pair) | **SELF-RENEWS-UNPROVEN** | Mechanism in deployed source; row untouched since creation 2026-11-04 — no refresh event has occurred yet. Acceptance check: row `time_updated` advances on first resolve at/after ~2026-12-03T17:37Z with no human step | 2026-12-03T17:42:29Z |
| opencode-go.drewrypope | API key | credential row | — | **NO-RENEWAL-NEEDED** | 3,296 successes / 24h | — |
| opencode-go.developing-today-0 | API key | credential row | — | **NO-RENEWAL-NEEDED** | 3,539 successes / 24h | — |

Acceptance check: file mtime/expiresAt advance past the access expiry with no human or CLI step. Tracked on #6120 gap 4 (comment posted) | access 2026-11-10T10:28:53Z; refresh token to 2026-12-07T05:57:08Z |

No re-mint event observed, and the account credential carries no recorded expiry — the meta-renewal watcher validates it every tick (status valid, lastGood 2026-11-10T02:30Z). | google (OAuth row `cred_12e4e76…`) | OAuth | credential row | Door disabled in config; access token expired 2026-10-12, refresh token still held | **DORMANT** — not serving; no live defect. If the door is ever re-enabled, first resolve must be watched: the row has been expired for a month | Row untouched since 2026-10-12 | access expired 2026-10-12T05:10:53Z |
| github-copilot | OAuth | credential row + auth.json | Door disabled in config | **DORMANT** — not serving | Last success 2026-10-24 (legacy id) | none recorded |
| opencode (base row) | OAuth | credential row | Disabled integration; same token lineage and expiry as opencode-go.popesdrew | **DORMANT duplicate** of the popesdrew door row | Identical expiry to the second (2026-12-03T17:42:29Z) | 2026-12-03T17:42:29Z |

## Findings

1. **Zero CANNOT-RENEW defects among live doors.** After tonight's three fixes, every serving door either self-renews, holds a static key, or has a configured renewal that has not yet had its first natural test.
2. **Three SELF-RENEWS-UNPROVEN doors, each with a dated acceptance check:** opencode-go.popesdrew (first refresh due at the 2026-12-03 expiry approach), _claude (first rotation due at the 2026-11-10T10:28:53Z access expiry — today), _muse (re-mint unobserved; account-token expiry uninstrumented, watched by the meta-renewal validator). If any acceptance check fails, it becomes a CANNOT-RENEW defect on sight.
3. **Hygiene observations (not renewal defects):** (a) the legacy `claude-code` credential row holds stub-length tokens from 2026-10-05 and the legacy provider id drew 9 auth-failing attempts in 24h (last 2026-11-10T00:14Z, pre-restore) — the live _claude door never reads this row; recommend deleting the stub row and retiring the legacy id. (b) The dormant `google` OAuth row (above). (c) The base `opencode` row duplicates the popesdrew lineage.
4. **Quota-side browser sessions are a separate surface**, already owned by #6120 (OpenDesign keeper landed; Meta portal re-capture requirement sits on #6079; ClinePass dashboard adapter dormant by design). This audit covers serving credentials; #6120 covers the monitoring reads. Cross-linked, not duplicated.

## Acceptance for closing this audit

- [ ] _claude: file rotation observed past 2026-11-10T10:28:53Z with no human/CLI step (or a defect filed the same day).

code.title: Scheduled Suggestions — developing-today/code
code.body:
You are a code-review agent running as a dispatched session in this
repository. Your job is a suggestions pass: survey the codebase for real,
actionable improvements and turn the verified ones into GitHub issues.

## Dispatch context — read this first

- You are running in this repository's LAPTOP CHECKOUT (the repo's primary
  checkout on the owner's laptop). Work there; do not clone the repo
  elsewhere.
- A tracking issue and a queue task were ALREADY created for this run by
  the dispatcher, and this session is already claimed against them. Do
  NOT create another tracking issue for this run, and do not dispatch
  further tasks.
- There is NO plan-approval step. Proceed directly; do not stop to ask
  for approval of a plan.

## What to review

Survey the codebase across these five areas:

- **Cleanup** — dead code, duplicated logic, obsolete files or config,
  leftover scaffolding.
- **Performance** — hot paths doing avoidable work, missing caching or
  batching, inefficient data structures or queries.
- **Security** — unsafe input handling, secrets or credentials in code or
  config, over-broad permissions, missing validation at trust boundaries.
- **Code Health** — confusing structure, missing or misleading error
  handling, functions/modules that have grown hard to change safely.
- **Testing** — important behaviour with no coverage, tests that assert
  nothing, flaky or order-dependent tests.

## Verify before you file — no speculative filings

Every candidate finding MUST be verified against the actual code before
it becomes an issue:

- Read the code at the location you cite. Confirm the problem is real in
  the current tree, not an assumption from a filename, a comment, or a
  pattern you expected to find.
- Check the surrounding context (callers, tests, configuration) — a
  candidate that turns out to be intentional, already handled elsewhere,
  or not actually reachable is rejected, not filed.
- Search the repo's OPEN issues before filing. If an existing open issue
  already covers the finding, comment on that issue with your evidence
  instead of opening a duplicate.

## Filing

- Per real, verified finding, file ONE issue in this repo with
  `gh issue create` from the laptop checkout. Each issue must include:
  - the canonical component label for its area; use `app/pm-stack` for
    PM-stack / aggregator issues in this repo. `app/aggregator` is a legacy
    alias and must not be used for new filings.
  - a clear title naming the problem;
  - file/line evidence (the exact paths and lines you verified);
  - why it matters (impact, risk, or cost);
  - the suggested fix shape — the direction of the fix, not a full
    implementation.
- CAP: at most **5 filings per pass** (new issues plus evidence comments
  on existing issues). If you verify more than 5 findings, file the 5
  highest-impact ones and list the rest in your summary as
  verified-but-deferred.
- Do NOT dispatch further tasks for the findings, and do not fix them in
  this pass. The issues are the record; the fleet's normal lanes pick
  work up from them.

## Finish

End with a short summary — as your session output, and as a comment on
this run's tracking issue if you can identify it — covering:

- **Filed** — each issue you opened or commented on, with its number and
  one line on the finding.
- **Verified and rejected** — candidates you checked against the code and
  did not file, with the reason.
- **Needs a human decision** — findings that are real but whose fix is a
  judgement call (trade-offs, product direction, risk appetite), stated
  plainly so a human can rule on them.

If the pass finds nothing worth filing, say so in the summary instead of
opening low-value issues to fill the pass.

code.title: ci(id): planted-bug-check.sh (the membership/voiding mutation proof from #1395) runs nowhere — no workflow, no flake check, not in check-all, not in the test-suite registry
code.body:
## Evidence

`pkgs/id/tests/planted-bug-check.sh` is the mutation proof for the membership / voiding layer (plan P2.3/P2.8, #1395): it requires the unmutated baseline green, then plants `voiding-authority` (inverted resolver-filter verdict in `Membership::is_effective`) and `frontier-mapping` (inverted mapping test in `CausalIndex::combine`) and requires the voiding/frontier suites to FAIL on each. A suite that passes with the bug planted proves nothing — this script is what proves the suites can fail.

It runs nowhere:

- No workflow invokes it: `grep -rn "planted" .github/workflows/` is empty; `pkgs/id/flake.nix` has zero `planted`/`mutation` mentions, so it is neither a PR-matrix check (`id-pr-checks.txt` unlisted), nor part of the nightly full flake check, nor covered by the `check-id-pr-checks.sh` drift guard (which only guards flake checks).
- `pkgs/id/check-all` never calls it (no `planted`/`mutation` mention) — the laptop gate doesn't run it either.
- `.github/test-suite-registry.json` has no entry for it, so the #6185 coverage contract never flags it.
- Only references repo-wide: the manual `just planted-bug-check` recipe (`pkgs/id/justfile:233-234`) and `pkgs/id/tests/README.md` ("Run it on demand").

Verified on origin/main `c2283a57` in a clean worktree: both patches `git apply --check` clean; the suites it drives (`voiding_scenarios`, `voiding_properties`, `membership_properties`, `membership_scenarios`, `id-core` frontier/membership lib tests) are the pinned suites that run in `test-shard-*` — it is specifically the mutation proof that has no venue. Full script run inside `nix develop ./pkgs/id` on that tree — green:

```
== baseline: all suites must pass unmutated ==
baseline green
== mutation: voiding-authority ==
caught: voiding-authority makes the suites fail, as required
== mutation: frontier-mapping ==
caught: frontier-mapping makes the suites fail, as required
planted-bug-check: OK — baseline green, all planted bugs caught
```

So the script works; it simply has no venue to run in.

Recency: the mutated files move under active development — `membership/layer.rs` touched 2026-11-06 (#4998), plus treefmt/perf/refusal changes 11-04/11-03/11-02. The proof rots exactly while its targets change.

## Why it matters

Without a venue, a future change can silently weaken the voiding/frontier suites (e.g. dropping the catching assertion) and CI stays green while the suites lose their fault-detection power — the Script's own plant history notes two `Engine::void` mutations already survived these suites once (#7071 family). The script exists precisely to catch that; unwired, it can't. Same fixed-before class as #6084/#6344/#7681 (suites that run nowhere).

## Suggested fix shape

Add a flake check (or a `pm-stack-tests`-style explicit CI step) running `bash tests/planted-bug-check.sh`, list it in `id-pr-checks.txt` or the nightly tier with the heavy-suite exclusion rationale documented, and record the venue in `.github/test-suite-registry.json`. Note it needs a clean tree for the two mutated files and runs the suites 3x — nightly may fit better than the PR matrix; that scoping is a triage call.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `planted-bug-check.sh` runs in CI (PR or nightly tier, documented) and fails the job on SURVIVED-mutation or red baseline.
- [ ] The drift guard (`check-id-pr-checks.sh`) or the registry covers it, so removing the venue fails loudly.
- [ ] `.github/test-suite-registry.json` records its venue.

COMPREHENSIVE REPOSITORY & ACTIVITY AUDIT - Inspect recent commits on `main` to understand the latest velocity and architectural direction. - Review open, recently closed, and merged issues and PRs (`gh issue list --state all --limit 50`, `gh pr list --state all --limit 30`). - Review each major package, tool, and subsystem in the repository:
  - **`pkgs/id`**: Distributed identity, cryptographic event log, p2panda synchronization, local event store, group encryption, discovery, and capability delegation.
  - **`pkgs/mcpx`**: Model Context Protocol daemon, multi-server multiplexing, protocol compliance, session leasing, JIT secret prompt vault, and Code Mode projection.
  - **`pkgs/fleet`**: The Rust multicall fleet tools and queue client — automated multi-agent coding workflows, issue triage, and parallel agent execution (the retired Jules packages were removed by PR #5376; audit the fleet queue automation under `pkgs/fleet` and `.github/workflows`, the dispatch actions `.github/actions/pm-dispatch-start` and `.github/actions/pm-dispatch-task`, the scheduler `.github/workflows/pm-scheduled.yml` and its repo-specific scheduled callers, and the CI-breakage automation).
  - **NixOS System Infrastructure & Web Services**: Modules, cloud functions, background daemons, and system services.

### 2. UNRESTRICTED INNOVATION & NEW FEATURE GENERATION - You are NOT restricted by what currently exists. Brainstorm things that *should* exist, would be exceptionally useful, or incorporate frontier concepts:
  - Edge architectures using Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects, KV, and Queues.
  - Distributed SQLite / libSQL / Turso primitives for offline-first, syncable state.
  - Advanced autonomous coding loops, speculative tool execution, and local verification loops.
  - Cross-platform bridges, native desktop integrations, and performance optimizations.
- **Bias Toward Capture**: It is far better to create an issue to triage later than to let a valuable opportunity or insight pass.
### 3. ACTIVE ISSUE & PR MAINTENANCE - **Scope Variety**: Create single large architectural vision issues for strategic direction, or narrow, highly focused issues for targeted improvements. - **Issue Decomposition**: If an existing issue is too broad, ambiguous, or monolithic (including issues created by others), break it apart into a series of clear, modular, linked sub-issues with explicit dependencies. - **Deduplication & Consolidation**: Identify overlapping or duplicate proposals/issues and consolidate them into unified, high-quality reference issues. - **Comments & Spec Refinement**: Leave comments or edit existing issues/PRs to provide missing technical specifications, edge-case analysis, data schemas, or suggested test cases. - **Zero-Context Hand-off Standard**: Every issue you author must be self-contained, citing exact file paths, interfaces, architectural rationale, and verifiable acceptance criteria so a new agent with zero prior context can execute it.

### 4. OPPORTUNISTIC IMPLEMENTATION (QUICK-WIN PRS) - If you identify straightforward bugs, unhandled edge cases, missing test coverage, or clean opportunities to refactor code to prevent future merge conflicts:
  - You are actively encouraged to open small, focused Pull Requests implementing the fix or feature directly.
  - Ensure all added code follows repository standards, includes tests, and passes formatting/linting hooks (`treefmt`, `conform`).
  - Never introduce breaking regressions to existing stable flows.
  - **One PR per coherent set**: batch every instance of the same problem — and all related dependency updates — into a single PR, or a few PRs split by coherent group. Never one PR per item or per dependency.
  - **Prefer tracked, higher-impact work**: before inventing a new micro-fix, check the open issues and implement the highest-impact one you can complete and verify, even when it spans several files.
  - **Merging is permitted, never required**: merge your PR only when checks pass and you are reasonably certain it is correct and low-risk. Otherwise leave it open and state your confidence and what a human should check in the description.

code.title: mcpx github failover: daemon call-path wiring + live activation (follow-on to #7948)

code.title: id: implement: native Android client v1 — slices from the #5780 design
code.body:
## Summary

Implementation home for the native Android client whose design landed in
[`doc/2026-11-08T22-06-00Z_design_id_android_client/2026-11-08T22-06-00Z_design_id_android_client.md`](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/doc/2026-11-08T22-06-00Z_design_id_android_client/2026-11-08T22-06-00Z_design_id_android_client.md)
(design for #5780). The design decides the product shape; this issue owns the
implementation slices so the decisions do not sit unowned.

The design's decisions in one line: a **thick, local-first Android client** with a
Kotlin/Jetpack Compose shell around a Rust client-only core, Ed25519 identity in
hardware-backed storage where a real-device spike proves it, a local journal synced
through the existing ID seams, remote-drive as one mode using the shared shell
contract, the phone as a two-gate capability provider, and honest presence with no
guaranteed background wake.

## Slices

Each slice is independently openable as its own issue when work starts; a slice is
done only when its check passes.

1. **Client-only Rust facade + Android target.** Extract a dedicated client facade
   (`id-client`) along #3447's crate seams; prove `wasmtime`, web/Axum, SSH, and
   serve/listener code are absent from the Android dependency graph; build
   arm64-v8a and run one authenticated client session. *Blocked by #3447.*
2. **Identity and enrollment spike.** Test direct Ed25519 Keystore/StrongBox support
   and the encrypted-key-envelope fallback on representative API levels/devices;
   specify backup exclusions, biometric invalidation, key zeroization, and the #5684
   recovery handoff. *Recovery semantics stay owned by #5684.*
3. **Local journal and reconnect sync.** Persist and reopen a local world, sync
   through the existing event-sync seams, inject interruption and storage-full
   cases, and prove no remote event is shown committed before authority accepts it.
   No new merge algorithm without a failing trace.
4. **Kotlin shell and contract conformance.** Portable screen/text client, lifecycle
   cancellation, versioned session transport, and the shared shell-contract corpus
   run against Android. Native-only surfaces stay behind typed adapters.
5. **Remote-drive integration from #1831.** After the input-event contract slice
   lands, implement Android gesture mapping and explicit-refusal UX; replay
   tap/long-press/drag/scroll and cover unsupported multi-touch. *Blocked by #1831's
   contract slice.*
6. **Phone provider v1.** Pick a minimal user-mediated capability set; implement the
   ID-grant ∩ Android-permission two-gate check, revoke/suspend behavior, and
   foreground-only actuation. AppFunctions may be a projection, never authority.
7. **Lifecycle, presence, and release channels.** Verify WorkManager and session
   expiry on real devices; ship signed sideload updates and Play-track updates from
   one signing lineage, or record the explicit channel migration decision. No push
   service without a separate approved decision.

## Out of scope

- Re-doing the #1831 PoC or the #5931 field survey.
- Hosting a world from the phone in v1 (client-only boundary, #790).
- Any central push/rendezvous service, FCM, or always-on presence promise.
- Inventing recovery semantics; #5684 owns them.

## Acceptance

- The seven slices above are either tracked as their own issues or completed, and
  every design invariant in §10 of the design record has a test that checks it.
- The shipped app connects to a test world, reopens its local journal, and passes
  the shared shell-contract corpus before provider surfaces are added.

code.title: id: implement the note→board sharing model (decision on #5830)
code.body:
## Summary

Implementation follow-on for the note→board sharing model decision recorded on issue #5830 (decision record: https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5830#issuecomment-6719439492), under parent design issue #5677 and programme epic #2056. Filed so the recorded decision has a named implementation next action; implementation timing is a separate decision, per issue #5830's filing note.

## Scope (from the decision record's invariants)

1. Board posts store a note **reference** (object id, home server, pinned version id + content hash, sharer attribution) — never note content as the post's own content.
2. Embed rendering offers both views — live head (default) and as-posted pinned — with a "changed since posted" indicator whenever they differ; a poster/board may pin the default view.
3. Reply anchoring: anchors name a note version + passage selector (section id + text-range/quote-hash) and resolve as exact / relocated / orphaned against newer versions; orphaned replies display against the pinned view and are never silently re-pointed or deleted.
4. Reference edges (`post —embeds→ note`, `reply —anchors→ note-version/passage`, `post —discusses→ note`) live in ID's native graph; backlinks are a query over the same edge store; jump-through works both ways with human/CLI/API/agent parity.
5. Cross-server: resolution is grant-checked against a selective sharing grant and hash-verified; board-side caches are render-only, version-labelled, and honour visibility revocation on refresh; backlink registration is announce-and-ack with retry, and a failed announcement never blocks posting.
6. Share/reply/anchor events are attributed and land in the objects' changelogs; sharing grants no edit rights and creates no fork.

## Out of scope

Anything parent issue #5677 reserves to its other decomposition designs (graph navigation API surface, multiplayer sessions, approval flow mechanics, personalized ranking) and the takedown/erasure reconciliation named in #5677's non-goals.

## Acceptance

- An end-to-end slice: share a note into a board, reply anchored to a passage, edit the note, and observe the live/pinned views, the anchor state transition, and the backlink from the note — locally, and in a two-server setup exercising grant-checked fetch and announce-and-ack backlink registration.

## Acceptance criteria

- An end-to-end slice works: share a note into a board, reply anchored to a passage, edit the note, and observe the live/pinned views, the anchor state transition (exact / relocated / orphaned), and the backlink — as the decision record's invariants require.
- Board posts store a note reference (object id, home server, pinned version id + content hash, sharer attribution) — never note content as the post's own content.
- Orphaned replies display against the pinned view and are never silently re-pointed or deleted.
- Cross-server resolution is grant-checked and hash-verified; board-side caches are render-only, version-labelled, and honour visibility revocation on refresh; a failed backlink announcement never blocks posting.
- Sharing grants no edit rights and creates no fork; share/reply/anchor events are attributed in the objects' changelogs.

code.title: id: spill v2 phase 3 — multi-world spill admission control and fairness budgets (#5787)
code.body:
## Summary

Implement spill v2 phase 3 from the #5787 design (`doc/2026-11-08_design_id5787.md`, §4): multi-world spill on one host — admission control and resource fairness between spilled worlds.

## Scope

- Per-world budgets on a spill host: turn CPU time, concurrent in-flight turns, append submission rate, replay bandwidth. A world over budget is throttled at its own executor; heat alone never revokes a lease.
- Control-traffic priority: renewal submissions and replay catch-up for other worlds schedule ahead of a hot world's mutation submissions, so one world's flood cannot false-expire a neighbour.
- Grant-time admission control: the DO's selection policy treats a host at its holder budget as ineligible; an unplaceable spill waits as pending intent instead of over-committing the host.

## Trigger / gating

**Do not start until trigger T3 fires:** the first host holding (or asked to hold) more than one spilled world, or a #5685 fairness case is run against a spill host. Design: #5787. Composes with: #5685. Depends on: #3805.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The design §7 two-worlds-one-floods case passes: the flooding world is throttled at its budget while the other world's renewal and append latency stay in bound.
- [ ] #5685 fairness-attack cases applicable to a spill host are run and recorded on this issue.

code.title: id: spill v2 phase 2 — read replicas with position-watermark staleness contract (#5787)
code.body:
## Summary

Implement spill v2 phase 2 from the #5787 design (`doc/2026-11-08_design_id5787.md`, §3): read replicas for a spilled world with an explicit staleness contract.

## Scope

- Replica read service over the authoritative journal stream: every read response carries the journal position it was served at (the replica's replay watermark).
- Bounded service: a replica beyond the configured lag bound refuses with retryable `replica-behind` instead of serving silently old state.
- Read-your-writes / monotonic reads: a client presenting its last acknowledged position is served only at a watermark ≥ that position (bounded wait or redirect to holder/DO).
- Presence rules: replicas may serve and originate only explicitly ephemeral, TTL'd, unjournaled presence data; session traffic that mutates goes to the holder and the append gate, always; no replica acknowledgment before the gate's durable receipt.

## Trigger / gating

**Do not start until trigger T2 fires:** the first production spill, or read load on a spilled world measurably served stale / refused at the holder. Design: #5787. Depends on: #3805, and on F1's pool/replica join (the phase-1 follow-on filed with the #5787 design).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Watermark, staleness-bound, and read-your-writes behaviours covered by deterministic tests, including the design §7 "replica serves during failover" case.
- [ ] No code path lets a replica acknowledge a mutation or promote presence data to durable state.

code.title: id: spill v2 phase 1 — pool roster, reader-then-holder eligibility, automatic lease failover (#5787)
code.body:
## Summary

Implement spill v2 phase 1 from the #5787 design (`doc/2026-11-08_design_id5787.md`, §1–§2): the spill pool and automatic holder failover for the #2819 lease protocol.

## Scope

- Grantor-side pool roster and per-grant eligibility (authenticated, reachable, caught up within the bound).
- Reader-then-holder join: a node becomes grant-eligible only after serving as a read replica within the catch-up bound across the design's observation window.
- Deterministic selection policy (caught-up first, healthy/least-loaded, stickiness, identity tie-break) and minimum-tenure flap protection.
- Automatic failover sequence: fence (expiry or journaled revoke) → select → grant at epoch+1 → replay barrier → resume; DO self-grant when no successor is eligible.
- `holder-lost` retryable result for commands in flight during failover; command-level dedupe posture unchanged from v1.
- Owns the #5787 Q2 evidence duty: measure failover detection/grant/replay times (extending the #3805 failure walkthroughs) before any proposal to change the 30s/10s term/renewal defaults.

## Trigger / gating

**Do not start until trigger T1 fires:** v1 phases #3804 and #3805 have landed (journaled lease entries, epoch fencing, both handoffs proven). Design: #5787. Depends on: #3805.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Failover oracle cases from the design §7 pass deterministically (holder death with/without eligible successor, reconnect of a fenced holder, failover vs handback race, grant storm).
- [ ] No grant is ever issued before the predecessor epoch is fenced; epochs stay a single per-world monotonic chain.
