code.title: mcpx testing: extended platforms -- which artifacts ship static; alpine, scratch, distroless, flatpak, Fedora, Windows tiers
code.body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#136 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #97

## Summary

The notes list a wish-list of further environments (alpine-slim, `FROM scratch`, distroless, flatpak, fedora-kde, silverblue/kinoite, ubuntu, windows-11) and justify it with "basically everything should work because static binary". This issue checks that claim. mcpx itself **can** be a static binary; what stands in the way is elsewhere:
1. **The shipped artifacts are not static -- by choice, not by necessity.** The default nix package is built with the nixpkgs cgo default and installed behind a C wrapper with nix-store paths baked in; #182's `Containerfile` keeps `ARG CGO_ENABLED=1` deliberately. A `CGO_ENABLED=0` build is fully static and works (verified in #182, `docs/container.md` §4). Which artifacts *should* be static is a policy decision (decision 1 below), not a feasibility question.
2. **`exec` needs a JS runtime**, which no minimal image has -- and bun, deno and git are dynamically linked distribution binaries, so a static `mcpx` beside them does not make an image static.
3. **mcpx does not compile for Windows today.**

It then assigns each environment a tier, says what it needs (a copied binary or an installer, and any extra config), and says which runner provides it.

## Original notes

> - testing
>   - a general goal is to ensure all features have one or more integration tests
>     - for both binary && app entrypoint (consider binary a superset)
>       - all tests should pass for nix flake & container
>         - ideally would like if worked:
>           - alpine-slim/FROM scratch/distroless/flatpak
>           - fedora-kde,silverblue/kinoite,ubuntu
>           - windows-11
>         - basically everything should work because static binary
>           - non-vanilla may need extra config
>           - installers make assumptions and require permissions

## Current state: is the binary static? (checked on main d0b7e01; #182's measurements added at 05c78b2)

| Fact | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| nix builds with **`CGO_ENABLED=1`** | `buildGoModule` uses `CGO_ENABLED = args.env.CGO_ENABLED or go.CGO_ENABLED` (nixpkgs `c7def04`, `pkgs/build-support/go/module.nix:225`). Go 1.26's default is `1` except on wasi/ppc64-BE (`pkgs/development/compilers/go/1.26.nix:81-90`). `package.nix` sets nothing. Confirmed on the installed darwin build: `go version -m <store>/bin/.mcpx-wrapped` prints `CGO_ENABLED=1` and `otool -L` lists `libSystem`, `libresolv`, `CoreFoundation`, `Security` |
| **Under cgo** (the default nix build), Linux `net` (DNS resolver) and `os/user` link libc dynamically | mcpx imports `net` (daemon, runner) and `os/user` (`internal/logging/trace.go:9`). So the *default* nix Linux binary is dynamically linked against nix's glibc, with a `/nix/store/...` ELF interpreter, and will not start on a system without that store path. Not checked on Linux in this issue: `file result/bin/.mcpx-wrapped` on x86_64-linux is the one-line check. This is a property of the build flags, not of mcpx: see the next row |
| **With `CGO_ENABLED=0`, mcpx is fully static and works** | #182 built it both ways through the Containerfile's `ARG CGO_ENABLED` (linux/arm64): `ldd` reports "not a dynamic executable"; `--version`, `ls`, `call` and a bun `exec` all work; the size is the same to ~100 bytes (14,811,298 vs 14,811,401). `os/user` and `net` fall back to their pure-Go implementations; nothing else in mcpx needs cgo (`docs/container.md` §4, `Containerfile:22-39`). The only `os/user` call is `user.Current()` for the trace record's user fields, and its error is tolerated (`internal/logging/trace.go:143-146`) |
| The installed `bin/mcpx` is a **C wrapper** | `makeBinaryWrapper` (`package.nix` `postInstall`): a 50 KB Mach-O on darwin that execs `.mcpx-wrapped` with `PATH` suffixed by nix-store `git deno bun node`. Copying `result/bin/mcpx` into another image copies a wrapper pointing at paths that do not exist there |
| Pure-Go SQLite | `modernc.org/sqlite`, chosen to avoid a C toolchain (`package.nix` comment). This is **not** the obstacle |
| `meta.platforms = lib.platforms.unix` | `package.nix`. Windows is not a nix target |
| **Windows does not compile** (by reading; one-line check: `GOOS=windows go build ./cmd/mcpx`) | `syscall.SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}` and `syscall.Kill(-pid, ...)` in `internal/runner/runner.go:413-432` and `internal/mcpclient/stdio.go:69,202-207`, and `Setsid` in `internal/cli/client.go:312`, have no build tags. None of these exist in Go's Windows `syscall`. Only the TTY code is split (`internal/cli/tty_unix.go`/`tty_other.go`) |

The claim, corrected: a **`CGO_ENABLED=0`** build (or `-tags netgo,osusergo`) of the **unwrapped** binary is static on Linux -- verified, not assumed (#182) -- so the non-`exec` surfaces should run anywhere with a Linux kernel. That covers `ls`, `call`, `serve`, the daemon, `/v1`, `/mcp`, and `api --spec`. **`exec`/`run` do not**, because they spawn deno, bun or node. The static-binary argument covers the daemon and CLI surfaces only. Nothing in mcpx "prevents" a static build; the open question is which shipped artifacts should be static, below.

## The runtime caveat (`exec`)

| Runtime | glibc | musl (alpine) | static / scratch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| deno | single binary, links glibc | **no musl build**. `denoland/deno:alpine` copies glibc from `gcr.io/distroless/cc` and patchelfs deno to use it (https://github.com/denoland/deno_docker/blob/main/alpine.dockerfile; upstream answer in denoland/deno_docker#428) | needs glibc: `distroless/cc` is the smallest working base |
| bun | yes | musl builds are published (`bun-linux-x64-musl`). Version floor to verify | no |
| node | yes | official `node:*-alpine` images | no |

So "FROM scratch/distroless-static" means **non-exec surfaces only**, unless a runtime is added, which then makes the image `distroless/cc` or larger. #182 confirmed the same from the other side: in its debian image bun and git are dynamically linked distribution binaries, so a static `mcpx` beside them "saves nothing at all" until everything in the image is static or `exec` is dropped (`docs/container.md` §4).

## Environments, tiered

| Environment | What works | Delivery | Extra config ("non-vanilla") | CI | Tier |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ubuntu (host) | everything | nix or copied static binary + runtimes | none | `ubuntu-latest` hosted | **1** |
| nix flake / flake image (#134) | everything | nix | none | `ubuntu-latest` | **1** |
| macOS (host) | everything | nix | none | `macos-latest` hosted | 2 |
| debian-slim / ubuntu container | everything | copied static binary + runtimes | none | `container:` on ubuntu | 2 |
| ↳ #182's `pkgs/mcpx/Containerfile` (exists) | everything, with **bun** only (`MCPX_SCRIPT_RUNTIME=bun`) | builds mcpx in a Go stage (`CGO_ENABLED=1` by default, glibc-linked) rather than copying a static one; git + ca-certificates; 413 MB | none | nothing builds or runs it yet (#134 `container-user`) | 2 |
| distroless/cc | everything with deno only | copied static binary + deno | `script.runtime=deno` | `container:` | 2 |
| alpine-slim | non-exec. exec with node or bun (musl) or with deno + glibc shim | copied static binary + `apk add nodejs` | `script.runtime=node`; no socket for node (it uses TCP, #35) | `container:` | 2 |
| `FROM scratch` / distroless-static | **non-exec only** | copied static binary; needs `/tmp` and a writable state dir, plus CA certs for the registry. No `/etc/passwd` is harmless: `user.Current()` fails and the trace record just omits the user (`internal/logging/trace.go:143`) | `daemon.inline` maybe (no init to reap; `daemon.inline`'s description names that container as a use case, `registry.go:377-388`); `MCPX_STATE_DIR` | `container:` | 2 |
| fedora (kde) | everything | copied binary, or an rpm later | none. KDE is irrelevant to a CLI except the TUI's terminal (Konsole) | `container: fedora:latest` | 3 |
| silverblue / kinoite | everything, **inside a toolbox**. On the host: `/usr` is read-only, so copy to `~/.local/bin` (works) or layer an rpm with `rpm-ostree install` (needs a reboot and root) | copied binary to `~/.local/bin` | none, if runtimes come from toolbox or homebrew | not simulable by a container (ostree host). A `fedora-toolbox` image covers the toolbox case. The real host needs a VM, **self-hosted** | 3 |
| flatpak | awkward fit: flatpak packages desktop apps, and mcpx is a CLI plus daemon that spawns host tools (MCP servers, runtimes) | a flatpak manifest | sandbox: the socket must live in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/app/<id>/` or be exposed with `--filesystem=xdg-run/mcpx`; host MCP servers only via `flatpak-spawn --host` (needs `--talk-name=org.freedesktop.Flatpak`, which effectively disables the sandbox) | `flatpak-builder` on ubuntu | 3 |
| windows-11 | **nothing until it compiles** | copied `.exe`, or an installer (winget/scoop) | see below | `windows-latest` hosted | 3, then 2 once it compiles |

"installers make assumptions and require permissions": the tier 1-2 set needs **no installer**. It uses nix, or a copied binary into `~/.local/bin` or the image. Installers appear only for:
- rpm-ostree layering (root, reboot);
- flatpak (a portal/permission model);
- Windows (winget/scoop: per-user vs machine-wide, SmartScreen, Defender scans of a new unsigned `.exe`).

Recommendation: ship and test "copy the static binary" as the universal path, and treat each installer as its own tier 3 target with its own issue when one is wanted.

### Windows, in detail

- **Build:** split `runner.go`, `stdio.go`, `client.go` process handling into `_unix.go`/`_windows.go`. Windows has no process groups in the POSIX sense. The equivalent is a Job Object (`CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` + `JobObject` with `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`), and `Setsid` detach becomes `DETACHED_PROCESS`. This is not a build-tag exercise: process-group kill is how mcpx stops an MCP server and everything it spawned, and without a Job Object a Windows mcpx leaks children -- the failure `scripts/stress.sh` exists to catch (from #163). `internal/pool/pool.go:736` also checks liveness with `syscall.Signal(0)`, meaningless on Windows.
- **Sockets:** AF_UNIX exists on Windows 10 1803+ and Windows 11 (https://devblogs.microsoft.com/commandline/af_unix-comes-to-windows/), and Go supports `net.Listen("unix", ...)` there. Whether deno's and bun's unix-socket clients work on Windows is **unverified**. Node already uses TCP (#35), so a TCP-only mode (`daemon.port` + `MCPX_ENDPOINT`) is the fallback.
- **Paths:** `XDG_*` fallbacks become `%LOCALAPPDATA%`. The `maxSocketPath` logic (`internal/daemon/paths.go:96` at 05c78b2) differs on Windows (sun_path is 108 there too, but paths are longer and use backslashes). `os.Getuid()` in `privateRuntimeDir` (`paths.go:148`) returns -1 on Windows.
- **Signals:** `signal.NotifyContext(..., SIGINT, SIGTERM)` (`cmd/mcpx/main.go:53`). SIGTERM is never delivered on Windows. The HTTP shutdown route will not help as written: `handleShutdown` stops the daemon by sending SIGTERM **to its own process** (`internal/daemon/server.go:774-780`), and on Windows `os.Process.Signal` supports only `os.Kill`. Shutdown has to become a context cancel.
- **e2e:** `e2e_test.go:590` uses `syscall.Signal(0)` for liveness, `:2704` and `:2717` (added by #182) use `syscall.Kill(pid, 0)`, and `exec_test.go:107-108` uses `syscall.Stat_t`. All need build tags.

### GitHub-hosted vs self-hosted

Hosted: `ubuntu-latest`/`ubuntu-24.04-arm`, `macos-latest`, `windows-latest`. `container:` and `services:` run only on Linux runners (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-where-your-workflow-runs/running-jobs-in-a-container). So every distro and minimal image above is a Linux `container:` job. Silverblue/kinoite on a real ostree host, and a real KDE session, need a VM or a self-hosted runner. Flatpak can be built and run headless on ubuntu.

## Approaches

### Decision 1 -- which artifacts are static (policy)

What `CGO_ENABLED=0` costs, for users rather than for images: pure-Go `os/user` parses `/etc/passwd` instead of asking NSS (LDAP/sssd users lose only the user name in trace records, since `trace.go:143` tolerates the error), and the pure-Go resolver stops honouring `nsswitch.conf` and the host resolver's configuration (on Linux; this is the whole trade-off. On macOS `CGO_ENABLED=0` changes nothing: since Go 1.20 `net` and `os/user` there call the system resolver and user database without cgo, https://go.dev/doc/go1.20#cgo). It matters for hostnames mcpx resolves itself: `daemon.endpoint`, HTTP MCP servers, the registry. Inside a container neither matters.

- **A -- flip the default nix package to `CGO_ENABLED=0` on Linux.** One artifact, static everywhere. But it changes DNS and user lookup for every nix user on a Linux desktop to fix a problem only containers and tarballs have, and the installed `bin/mcpx` is still a wrapper with nix-store paths, so the nix package does not become copyable anyway. Not recommended.
- **B -- static only through the container build arg** (`docker build --build-arg CGO_ENABLED=0`, already wired in #182). No new package, nothing changes for nix users. But there is no static artifact outside an image -- nothing for #158's release tarball, and nothing for the tier-2 images below to copy except by rebuilding in each Dockerfile.
- **C -- keep the default nix package as it is; add a Linux `mcpx-static` output (recommended).** `env.CGO_ENABLED = 0`, no wrapper, Linux only (darwin cannot be fully static and keeps the system resolver). It is the artifact every container entry copies and #158 ships in a tarball, with a test that `go version -m` reports `CGO_ENABLED=0` and `file` reports "statically linked". The Containerfile's default (`ARG CGO_ENABLED=1`) is the GIT architect's to set; C does not depend on it. Recommended because it gives the static artifact to the places that need it without changing name resolution for anyone who installed the ordinary package.

### Decision 2 -- how far to go

#### A -- attempt the whole list as tier 1 (least recommended)
Every entry gates merges. CI time would exceed any budget (#95), Windows fails until a port is done, and silverblue needs self-hosted infrastructure. The first red flatpak job would train everyone to ignore CI.

#### B -- containers only
Add the Linux `container:` entries (alpine, distroless, scratch, fedora, ubuntu) as tier 2 nightly. Declare flatpak, silverblue and Windows out of scope. This is cheap and covers most real deployments. It drops a user-stated wish (windows-11) without a plan.

#### C -- tiers, with a static build first (recommended)
1. **Ship the static artifact** chosen in decision 1 (C: a Linux `mcpx-static` output, `env.CGO_ENABLED = 0`, no wrapper) with its test (`go version -m` reports `CGO_ENABLED=0`, `file` reports "statically linked"). #182 already showed the build works; this makes it a product. It is the artifact every container entry copies.
2. **Tier 1** (gates merges): ubuntu host, nix. Already in #134.
3. **Tier 2** (nightly): macOS, debian-slim (including #182's Containerfile), distroless/cc, alpine, scratch. Each runs the #134 labels its surface supports. For example, scratch runs everything except tests labelled `needsRuntime`, so the label system from #134 and #137 gains `needsRuntime:<deno|bun|node|any>` -- and `needsGit` for the `repo`/`worktree` scopes, unless the GIT architect's native git resolution removes that dependency (from #161). Where an image lacks what a test needs, prefer asserting mcpx's own refusal over skipping: `no JavaScript runtime found` is a feature, a crash is a bug, and only a run that expects the failure can tell them apart (from #161).
4. **Tier 3** (best-effort or manual, on release): fedora, toolbox, flatpak, silverblue VM, and Windows. The Windows port is its own design issue (process groups, detach, socket vs TCP). It becomes tier 2 once `GOOS=windows go build` passes, and a cheap `go vet`-level cross-compile check can go into tier 1 right away to stop it getting worse.

Recommended because it turns an unverified claim into a checked property, orders the work by users reached per unit of effort, and keeps every wish-list item on a path, not dropped.

Make the tiers mean something with entry and exit rules (from #163): tier 1 admits a platform where a bug has been found or an artifact that ships; tier 2 admits a plausible user environment that runs unattended and passes its surface; a tier-2 leg with no finding for two months is demoted; each tier-3 item gets one paragraph *now* saying what it would cost and what it would prove, so "ideally would like if worked" becomes a decision someone can revisit rather than a list re-argued every quarter. #163 also argued macOS belongs in tier 1, not 2: #35 is the only cross-OS bug on record, and a parallel leg costs queue time, not wall clock. Decide against #95's budget (#140).

## Open questions

- ~~Is `CGO_ENABLED=0` acceptable for the default Linux nix package too, or only for a `-static` variant?~~ Now decision 1 above (recommended: a `-static` variant; feasibility was settled by #182).
- What is bun's first release with musl builds, and does the pinned bun (1.3.11) have one? Does bun's unix-socket `fetch` work on musl?
- Is a Windows port wanted at all, or is WSL2 (which is ubuntu, tier 1) the supported Windows story? If WSL2 is the answer, "windows-11" becomes a doc page plus a WSL2 smoke job.
- Flatpak: is there a real user for it, given the sandbox fights the whole design (spawning host processes)? Proposal: tier 3 "documented as unsupported" unless a user appears.
- Should the static image default to `daemon.inline=true`, since there is no init to reap children?
- `meta.platforms = lib.platforms.unix`: narrow it to `linux ++ darwin` to match what is tested, or keep the BSD claim as an aspiration (from #163)?
- Who triages a nightly failure? A nightly nobody reads is worse than none; #99 should name the owner (from #163).
- `macos-latest` is arm64, so a macOS leg is also a second architecture; `ubuntu-24.04-arm` is the Linux arm64 leg (#134).

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** XL as a whole (static build and tier-2 containers: M; Windows port: L; silverblue/flatpak: M each, self-hosted) · **Impact** med (tier 2), low-med (tier 3)
**Depends on / related**: #134 (container image and #182's Containerfile, labels, matrix entries), #137 (which real servers each image must carry), #133 (binary override to test a copied binary), #158 (the release tarball ships the static artifact), #95 (tiers map to PR/nightly/release workflows), #49, #35 (the Linux/macOS split that motivates cross-OS runs), #99.

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

## Acceptance criteria

- The extended-platforms question is answered with evidence: which artifacts ship static, and the alpine/scratch/container legs specified in the body run or are explicitly deferred with reasons recorded on this issue.
- The work described in the Summary/Scope above is delivered via a branch + PR (no direct push to main); verification runs in GitHub Actions CI, not on the sandbox.
- Evidence (CI links, timings, or probe output as applicable) is recorded on this issue before it is closed.

code.title: mcpx testing: CI workflow skeleton -- init, matrix, final job; triggers, concurrency, caching, checkout
code.body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#135 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #95

## Summary

Replace the single serial `mcpx.yml` job with one test workflow shaped **init -> matrix -> final (budget + required check)**, triggered on every push to `main` and on non-draft PRs, with superseded PR runs cancelled, every download cached, and a checkout no bigger than it needs to be. This issue decides the skeleton; the shard list (#139), the budget job (#140), the formatter/linter legs (#141), `format.yaml` (#142) and the first measured iteration (#143) plug into it. The seed is minted by the init job but designed in #93; environment legs from #97 join the same matrix.

## Original notes

> - testing
>   - importantly, as we add more testing agents should not run every single test basically ever. below documents a rough idea of a ci job design/policy, the main priority is being short as possible.
>   - make a comprehensive github action ci.yaml workflow (or test.yaml) that is as fast as possible,

The long bullet below is quoted here for its caching / shallow-clone / no-teardown / job-start clauses (its sharding and budget clauses are owned by #139 and #140):

> - testing
>   - make a comprehensive github action ci.yaml workflow (or test.yaml) that is as fast as possible,
>     - repeat this process whenever testing exceeds some time budget. make setup faster, rebalance alpha splits, split groups of tests on the longest shard. maybe flag that never tears down because just killing the box after. anything downloaded should be cached, shallow clone a partial path to mcpx dir, if there's unexplainable job start delays, try to keep all job times balanced, 10 ultrafast ones can give you quick signals but may put pressure on runner infra and cause the longest jobs to last a little longer. all that matters is how long the longest jobs take. job runners have 2 or 4 cores, consider if theres lengthy tests which are '1' test but re-exec N times 'in parallel': they will only run 1-3 at a time and so 30 cases _could_ take up to 10 tests worth of time even in parallel and may need to be examined. we're using go so im not too worried about time budget but its best to get this early. main focus is strong tests as each step of the lifecycle.

> - testing
>   - make a comprehensive github action ci.yaml workflow (or test.yaml) that is as fast as possible,
>     - automatically runs for every commit to main and on commit/open/undraft to a non-draft pr

## Current state

Measured on d0b7e01; re-checked at 05c78b2 after #182, which landed this issue's one-line cache fix (marked below). `.github/workflows/mcpx.yml` is the only mcpx workflow: one `ubuntu-latest` job, checkout `fetch-depth: 0`, `nix-installer-action@main`, `setup-go`, `setup-deno`, `setup-bun`, `setup-node` 24, `go test ./... -count=1`, a vendorHash repair step for `renovate/*` and `dependabot/*` branches that commits and `git push`es with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, then `nix build .#packages.x86_64-linux.mcpx`.

Step timings, run [36673523537](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/actions/runs/36673523537) (push to main, 3m57s wall, job 3m53s; full log at `issues/testing/ci-log-36673523537.txt`; step times from `gh api .../runs/36673523537/jobs`):

| Step | Time | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| queue (job `created_at` -> `started_at`) | 2 s | 2-3 s in 9 of the last 10 runs; **37 s** in run 36663358199 |
| Set up job (download 6 actions) | 3.4 s | |
| checkout, `fetch-depth: 0` | 2.4 s | repo is small: 930 tracked files, 4.4 MiB pack |
| nix-installer | 8.3 s | installer tarball is a cache hit; "FlakeHub is disabled because the workflow is misconfigured" (no `id-token: write`) |
| setup-go | 10.9 s | Go 1.26.7 is not in the image: download + **7.3 s "Adding to the cache"**. Then `##[warning]Restore cache failed: Dependencies file is not found in /home/runner/work/nix/nix. Supported file pattern: go.mod` -- the Go module/build cache never worked before #182, because `go.sum` is at `pkgs/mcpx/go.sum` and no `cache-dependency-path` was set; the post step confirmed "Primary key was not generated". **Fixed in #182** (`cache-dependency-path: pkgs/mcpx/go.sum`, `mcpx.yml:50`): the key is now generated and saved (`setup-go-Linux-x64-ubuntu24-go-1.26.7-77c3e85d…`). |
| setup-deno / setup-bun / setup-node | 2.5 / 1.7 / 3.4 s | installs **deno 2.9.7, bun 1.4.2, node 24.21.0** -- whatever is latest. The Nix wrapper pins `bun-bin` 1.3.14; a dev machine here has deno 2.9.6 / bun 1.3.11. Three different Buns. |
| `go test ./... -count=1` | 134.8 s | ~3 s module download, ~31 s compile (first `ok` at 05:29:07.8), then `internal/e2e` **100.7 s**; `internal/tui` 8.6 s and every other package overlap with e2e |
| vendorHash repair | 0 s | skipped (not a bot branch) |
| `nix build` | 59.6 s | ~8 s eval, 185 paths / 417.7 MiB fetched from cache.nixos.org, go-modules FOD ~5 s, `buildPhase` 24.1 s, `checkPhase` 16.5 s (the 18 unit packages again) |
| post steps | 2.0 s | nix-installer 1.2 s, checkout 0.2 s, setup-go 0.1 s, the rest ~0 |
| "Complete job" -> job completed | ~3 s | the runner's "Cleaning up orphan processes" |

The last 20 runs: 3m24s-4m30s; the last 10: 3m57s-4m30s. Setup is ~33 s, and the ~31 s of Go compile inside the test step is what a warm cache should remove.

After #182 (run [36693030957](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/actions/runs/36693030957), push to main at 05c78b2, 4m09s wall): setup 22 s (setup-go 8 s), `go test` **148 s** (~39 s of module download + compile before the first `ok`; `internal/e2e` 108.9 s for 209 tests), `nix build` 70 s (`buildPhase` 28.7 s, `checkPhase` 18.5 s), post steps ~5 s of which setup-go's cache **save** is 3 s. setup-go logged `Cache is not found` in this run and in both PR runs around it (36692557266, 36693225089): the first main run with a new key misses by construction, and the PR runs started before main had saved. **No warm-cache run exists yet**; the next push to main is the first, and #143 records the number.

Trigger gaps today:
- `pull_request` has no `types:`, so it runs on the defaults `opened`, `synchronize`, `reopened` ([events docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#pull_request)): **drafts run, and undrafting does not trigger a run**.
- `push` to main filters on `pkgs/mcpx/**` only, while the PR filter also has `flake.nix` and `flake.lock`. A `flake.lock` bump pushed straight to main (or merged from a PR that did not touch mcpx) **never builds mcpx on main**.
- No `concurrency:` group, so a force-pushed PR runs every superseded commit to completion.
- `main` has no branch protection and no rulesets (`gh api repos/dezren39/nix/branches/main/protection` -> 404, `.../rulesets` -> `[]`), so nothing is a required check yet. The repo is **public**, so `ubuntu-latest` is 4 vCPU / 16 GB and minutes are free ([runner reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners)).
- The vendorHash push-back uses `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Per the [trigger docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/trigger-a-workflow), a `GITHUB_TOKEN` update to a PR now creates the `synchronize` run in an **approval-required** state -- a human must click "Approve workflows to run" before the repaired commit is tested. #49 notes the repair has never run on a real Renovate PR.

## Decisions

### 1. File and workflow name

- **A -- `ci.yaml`.** In a repo that hosts ~15 packages (#49), a workflow called `ci` claims to be the repo's CI; the next package to add tests either piles into it or collides with the name. Not recommended.
- **B -- `test.yaml`** as in the notes. Same scoping problem, and `.yaml` breaks the `.yml` convention both existing workflows (`mcpx.yml`, `opencode.yml`) use.
- **C -- `.github/workflows/mcpx-test.yml`, `name: mcpx-test` (recommended).** Scoped like `mcpx.yml`, and the `name:` is what `format.yaml`'s `workflow_run: workflows: [mcpx-test]` keys on (#142). If mcpx ever moves to its own repo (package.nix already says `homepage = "https://github.com/dezren39/mcpx"`, which does not exist yet), rename to `test.yml` then.

### 2. Job graph

```
init ──┬─> unit                         (all packages except internal/e2e)
       ├─> e2e (shard 1..N)             (matrix from init output; #139)
       ├─> fmt / lint-go / lint-other   (#141)
       ├─> plugin                       (bun test; #141)
       ├─> nix                          (nix build + vendorHash repair on bot branches)
       ├─> docs-examples                (reserved slot, see below)
       └─> env legs                     (#97: macOS, nix-built binary, container, ...)
all ───> ci-ok                          (if: always(); required check + budget report, #140)
```

`init` does only what must happen once: decide relevance (decision 4), mint and export the seed (#93), compute the shard matrix as JSON (`strategy.matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.init.outputs.matrix) }}`), and optionally build the binaries (decision 7). Everything it does sits on the critical path, so it must stay small.

Honest cost: an init hop adds one job start (queue 2-3 s + set up ~3 s + checkout ~2 s + whatever it builds) before any test starts. If the seed could be derived identically in every leg (from `github.run_id` / `github.run_attempt`, evaluated in #122) and the shard list were computed inside each leg from a committed/cached timing file, `init` could be dropped and the matrix made static. #121 currently recommends **minting** a UUIDv7 per run, which has to happen exactly once -- so `init` stays, and the skeleton should budget for it rather than assume it is free.

### 3. Triggers

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      budget_seconds: { type: number, default: 0 }   # 0 = use the hardcoded default; #140
jobs:
  init:
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || !github.event.pull_request.draft
```

- "Undraft" is the `ready_for_review` type; it must be listed explicitly because it is not a default.
- Do **not** add `converted_to_draft`: it would run the suite on the one transition that means "stop looking at this" (from #165).
- Put the draft `if:` on `init` only: every other job `needs: init`, so a skipped `init` skips the run.
- A skipped job reports as passing to a required check. That is harmless for drafts (they cannot merge), and `ready_for_review` produces a fresh run whose result supersedes it.
- "every commit to main" means **every push**: a push of five commits tests the head only. That is standard and correct -- testing each intermediate commit would need a loop over `before..after`, and with squash merges a push is one commit anyway. Say so rather than build it.

### 4. Path filters vs always-run

- **A -- workflow-level `paths:` filters (today) plus a required check.** A PR that does not touch the paths never starts the workflow, so its required check sits at "Expected -- waiting for status" forever and the PR cannot merge. This is the well-known stuck-PR trap. GitHub's documented workaround is a second, same-named workflow that does nothing and always passes (a skip shim) -- it works, but it is one more file to keep in step with the real one (from #165). Also the current push filter is already inconsistent with the PR filter (see above).
- **B -- no filters at all.** Every PR in this monorepo (nix config, casks, other packages) runs the whole mcpx suite. Free on a public repo, but it spends the account's 20 concurrent standard-runner jobs ([limits](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits)) on irrelevant work and slows unrelated PRs.
- **C -- always trigger; decide relevance in `init`; one aggregator is the required check (recommended).** `init` diffs the PR (`git diff --name-only ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}...HEAD`, or `dorny/paths-filter`) against `pkgs/mcpx/**`, `flake.nix`, `flake.lock`, `.github/workflows/mcpx-*.yml`, and outputs `mcpx: true|false`; test jobs have `if: needs.init.outputs.mcpx == 'true'`. Pushes to main always run everything. The final `ci-ok` job (`needs:` every job, `if: always()`) fails if any needed job failed or was cancelled and passes if they succeeded or were skipped; **it is the only required check**. This also solves a problem sharding creates: matrix leg names (`e2e (3)`) change every time shards are rebalanced, and a required check keyed on a leg name breaks on every rebalance.

### 5. Concurrency

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: mcpx-test-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
```

PR runs share a group per PR and cancel the superseded one. Non-PR runs get a unique group (`run_id`), so a main run is **never** cancelled or queued behind another main run -- every main commit keeps a result (keying main on `github.sha` would make a `workflow_dispatch` of the same SHA queue behind the push run). `format.yaml` must ignore `cancelled` conclusions (#142).

### 6. What happens to `mcpx.yml`

- **A -- keep `mcpx.yml` unchanged and add the new workflow.** Unit tests would then run three times per PR (new unit job, old `go test`, and `checkPhase`), and the old serial job would stay the longest job.
- **B -- keep `mcpx.yml` as the Nix + vendorHash workflow only**, deleting its `go test` step. Minimal diff; Renovate keeps working. But it is a second workflow with its own path filters, so it inherits the stuck-required-check problem and cannot report to the one `ci-ok`. A variant from #165: move `nix build` into the test workflow as a matrix cell and shrink `mcpx.yml` to the repair alone (renamed, e.g. `vendor-hash.yml`, bot branches only, the only workflow holding `contents: write` and `fetch-depth: 0`). Same permission outcome as C, at the cost of a second workflow whose result `ci-ok` cannot see.
- **C -- fold it in as the `nix` job of `mcpx-test` (recommended).** Same steps minus `go test`; `permissions: contents: write` at **job** level on this job only (every other job `contents: read`, `persist-credentials: false`). It runs in parallel with the test legs, so its ~60 s is off the critical path until the e2e shards get shorter than it -- which #143 predicts will happen at 3 shards. Shape it as a reusable job so #49's every-package build can share it rather than fork it.

Keep the repair step's semantics exactly (bot branches only; a human's dependency change fails). The header comment (`mcpx.yml:3-11`) records why the build and the repair are load-bearing -- without them a Renovate Go bump "merged silently and was only found by the next person to rebuild" -- so neither may be lost in the move. The approval-required behaviour above is a reason for #49 to move the push-back to a GitHub App token; not in scope here.

**The duplicate unit run in `checkPhase` (from #168).** `package.nix:72-82` runs `doCheck` with a hand-written list of 18 packages inside `nix build`: 16.55 s on run 36673523537, 18.5 s on run 36693030957 at 05c78b2, all of it re-running tests `go test ./...` passed a minute earlier in the same job. Do not delete it (`doCheck = false`): the Nix sandbox is a genuinely different environment -- no network, no `$HOME`, state and cache forced under `$TMPDIR` (`package.nix:75`) -- and no network is exactly the property that would have caught #65 before CI did. Instead stop paying for it *in series*: once `nix` is its own job running beside the e2e shards (C above), its tests cost no wall clock, and the CI `unit` job can either drop the overlapping packages or keep ~15 s of redundancy on a job that is not the critical path. Separately, the list has drifted: `internal/opencode` has no test files, and 12 packages with tests are never run in the sandbox (`api`, `artifacts`, `cli`, `diagnose`, `elicit`, `events`, `execsvc`, `mcpauth`, `mcpclient`, `recipes`, `runner`, `tasks`; still true at 05c78b2). Replace the list with `go list ./...` minus `internal/e2e` (and anything that needs a runtime), or guard it with a test that every package with tests is listed. Coordinate the edit with #178, which also changes `package.nix`.

### 7. Caching everything that is downloaded

| What | Today | Proposed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Go modules + build cache | ~~broken (no `cache-dependency-path`)~~ **fixed in #182** (`mcpx.yml:50`); every run, PRs included, now saves | Keep `cache-dependency-path: pkgs/mcpx/go.sum` in every Go job. Still open: on PRs use `actions/cache/restore` only -- today each PR run saves its own branch-scoped copy (36692557266 and 36693225089 both did), and those evict main's under the 10 GB repo limit; save on main only. Expected to remove most of the ~31-39 s compile per job -- measure the first warm run in #143. |
| Go toolchain | downloaded + 7.3 s copied into hostedtoolcache every run | Either accept it (it is per job, so it multiplies by the shard count), cache it, or take Go from the flake (below). |
| Deno | `cache: false` | `cache: true` (caches `DENO_DIR`); matters once plugin/docs tests import anything. Pin the version (see below). |
| Bun / Node | no deps to cache | pin versions; nothing else. |
| Nix store | 417.7 MiB from cache.nixos.org each run; no binary cache | The free Magic Nix Cache ended 2025-02-01 ([Determinate blog](https://determinate.systems/blog/magic-nix-cache-free-tier-eol/)). Current options: `nix-community/cache-nix-action` (free, store in the GH Actions cache, counts against 10 GB), `DeterminateSystems/flakehub-cache-action` (FlakeHub Cache is paid, free for OSS on request; it also has a `use-gha-cache` input -- whether that works free today is unverified), Cachix (5 GB free for OSS). Honest: a store cache saves the fetch and the go-modules FOD, but **a PR that changes mcpx always re-runs `buildPhase` + `checkPhase` (~40 s)**; caching helps unchanged derivations (bun-bin, re-runs, #49's other packages) far more than it helps mcpx. |
| mcpx / fakemcp / askmcp binaries | built by `testsupport` once per test binary via `go build` in a subprocess (`internal/testsupport/build.go`) | See below. |

**Versions (local == CI).** Three different Buns (above) is exactly the #35 class of bug. #134 records the same drift. Two ways out: pin every `setup-*` action's version to the flake's (deno/bun/node from `flake.lock`) and let Renovate bump both; or run the test jobs inside the flake dev shell #134 proposes (`nix develop .#mcpx -c go test ...`) so Go, Deno, Bun, Node and the linters all come from `flake.lock`. The dev shell costs the Nix install (8.3 s) plus a substitution per job, and needs a store cache to be competitive; the `setup-*` route costs ~18 s per job today. Measure both in #143 rather than argue it here; #141 makes the same call for the linters.

**Shared binaries.** Options, least to most recommended:
- A -- keep building per test binary (today). With a warm `GOCACHE`, `go build ./cmd/mcpx` in each shard is likely a few seconds; zero new moving parts.
- B -- `init` builds `mcpx`, `fakemcp`, `askmcp` once and uploads an artifact; each shard downloads it. Costs an upload (~2-5 s) on the critical path in `init` and a download per shard, and needs `testsupport` to accept a prebuilt path: the mcpx binary override #133 designs (`MCPX_TEST_BINARY` or a `-mcpx.binary` test flag, name open there) plus the matching fakemcp/askmcp override #134 asks for.
- C -- B plus `go test -c ./internal/e2e` in `init`, so shards run `./e2e.test -test.run '<regex>'` and need no Go toolchain at all (drops setup-go, ~11 s, from every shard). The same env override lets #97 run the e2e suite against the **Nix-built** binary and the container binary, which is the real reason to do it. Recommended once #143 shows per-shard Go setup is significant.

### 8. Sparse, shallow checkout

The repo is small (930 files; full-history checkout 2.4 s). A sparse, depth-1 checkout saves about one to two seconds per job -- worth it because it is two lines, not because it is big:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v7
  with:
    fetch-depth: 1
    sparse-checkout: pkgs/mcpx      # cone mode also materialises root files: flake.nix, flake.lock
    persist-credentials: false
```

Caveats:
- **Not for the `nix` job.** The flake evaluates `./pkgs/bun-bin/package.nix` for mcpx (`flake.nix:276,385`) and copies the flake source from the git tree; whether a sparse working tree evaluates is unverified. Use depth 1, full tree.
- `fetch-depth: 0` in `mcpx.yml` is not needed for the vendorHash push: committing on a depth-1 checkout of the branch head and pushing a fast-forward works. Verify on the first bot PR.
- `init`'s relevance diff needs the base commit: fetch it explicitly (`git fetch --depth=1 origin ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}`) rather than deepening the whole clone.

### 9. "Never tears down"

Post steps cost **2.0 s** in total (nix-installer 1.2 s is most of it). There is no generic switch to skip a `uses:` action's post step, and 2 s of 4 min is not worth a custom flag. What is worth doing:
- restore-only caches on PRs (decision 7) -- a cache *save* on a miss is the one post step that can take tens of seconds;
- nothing else at the infra level.

**Do not skip test-level teardown.** The e2e `t.Cleanup` is the code that keeps #52 fixed: since #182 it runs `mcpx stop --all` (which reads the `daemon-<key>.json` info files) and logs its error instead of discarding it (`internal/e2e/e2e_test.go:71-85`), and `newEnv` sets `MCPX_AUTOSTART_IDLE_EXIT=60s` as the backstop (`:68`, `:92`). Skipping the cleanup in CI would hide a regression of exactly that. Note the opposite problem: the runner's "Cleaning up orphan processes" at job end silently kills anything that leaked, so CI can never see a leak on its own. The e2e job should count surviving `mcpx daemon` processes after `go test` and warn -- a regression check for #182's fix (policy in #99).

### 10. Seed (consume, not design)

`init` exposes `outputs.seed` (design in #93 / #121, collection in #122); every leg sets it in `env:` under the name #121 picks. Two consequences for this workflow: the seed and the shard list must be printed in each leg's job summary so a failure is reproducible locally with one command (#99), and if #93 uses `go test -shuffle=<seed>`, test result caching is off for that invocation (`-shuffle` is not in the cacheable flag list, `go help test`).

### 11. `-count=1` and the Go test cache

`go help test`: a result is reused only when the test binary and "cacheable" flags match, and "tests that open files within the package's module or that consult environment variables only match future runs in which the files and environment variables are unchanged." The cache cannot see what a subprocess does.

- `internal/e2e` imports only `internal/api` and `internal/testsupport`. It builds `cmd/mcpx` and `fakemcp` with `go build` in a subprocess. So a cached e2e pass would **survive a change to `cmd/mcpx`, `internal/daemon` or anything else the binary contains** -- a stale green. e2e must keep `-count=1`. A prebuilt binary path passed by env var does not help: the path string is tracked, the file (outside the module) is not.
- The same applies to `internal/pool` (builds fakemcp through `testsupport`) and `internal/config/scope_test.go` (`exec.Command`).
- Pure unit packages could use a restored `GOCACHE` and skip unchanged packages. Today all units except `tui` (8.6 s) finish in under 2 s, so the saving is small. Recommendation: keep `-count=1` everywhere now, and revisit only if the unit job ever becomes the longest job.

### 12. Reserved: docs-as-tests job

#91 decides that every runnable code block in the book is extracted and run against the built binary, and generated references (`mcpx man`, the OpenAPI from `mcpx api`, the settings table) are regenerated and diffed. The docs tree owns the book, the extraction format and the runner; this workflow only reserves a `docs-examples` leg that `needs: init`, consumes the same binary as the e2e shards (decision 7), receives the seed, and reports to `ci-ok`. Until the docs tree lands its runner, the leg does not exist; the skeleton should just not make it hard to add (matrix legs come from `init`'s JSON, so adding it is one entry).

## Open questions

1. Seed without `init`: will #93's seed be derivable in every leg (removing the init hop), or must it be minted once?
2. Does a sparse-checkout working tree evaluate `.#packages.x86_64-linux.mcpx`? (Try once; if not, the `nix` job stays full-tree.)
3. Dev shell vs `setup-*` for toolchains: which is faster per job once a Nix store cache exists? (#143 measures.)
4. Nix store cache: `cache-nix-action` (free, eats the 10 GB Actions cache that Go also uses) vs FlakeHub Cache OSS account vs Cachix? Shared with #49.
5. Should `ci-ok` become a required check on `main` now (main is unprotected today)? Required checks are what make stuck-PR design matter; if the user never merges red, it can wait.
6. `GITHUB_TOKEN` push-back now yields approval-required runs: acceptable for Renovate, or does #49 move to an App token?
7. How do #97's environment legs compose with the shards: N shards x M environments (the cell count explodes), or one full shard set on `ubuntu-latest` plus one smoke shard per other environment? #97/#134 decide; this workflow only has to be able to express either (from #165).
8. An empty matrix from `init` (a PR that touches nothing relevant) skips every dependent job; confirm `ci-ok`'s `always()` reads that as a pass, not a neutral (from #165).
9. `workflow_call`, so #142's `format.yaml` and #49's package builds reuse the setup block instead of copying it? It constrains `init`'s outputs (from #165).
10. Record `nproc` and the resolved runner image in `init` and pin `ubuntu-latest` (today it resolves to `ubuntu-24.04`): an image change silently invalidates the timing file #139 balances on. A hand-rolled Nix store cache also needs per-cell keys with a shared restore prefix, or matrix cells race to save one key (from #168).

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M · **Impact** high · **Depends on / related**: #95 (tracker), #139, #140, #141, #142, #143; #93 / #121 / #122 (seed minted in `init`, format, collection), #97 / #134 (environment legs join this matrix; shared dev shell), #133 (binary override), #130 (race/shuffle/repeat PR job and nightly run join this workflow), #99 (agent run policy -- CI is where "every test" runs so agents do not), #49 (Nix job, vendorHash repair, every-package CI), #178 (also edits `package.nix`; the `checkPhase` list change should land with or after it), #52 (closed, fixed in #182 -- the cache line and the teardown/orphan-count notes above reflect it), #35 (Linux/macOS drift; tool version pinning).

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

## Acceptance criteria

- The CI workflow skeleton (init, matrix, final job; triggers and concurrency as specified) exists, runs in GitHub Actions, and is green.
- The work described in the Summary/Scope above is delivered via a branch + PR (no direct push to main); verification runs in GitHub Actions CI, not on the sandbox.
- Evidence (CI links, timings, or probe output as applicable) is recorded on this issue before it is closed.

code.title: mcpx testing: environments -- nix flake, container, local, remote -- as CI matrix entries
code.body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#134 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #97

## Summary

Define the environments the integration suite must pass in: **nix flake**, **container**, **local**, and **remote**. For each, say what it needs, which tests it runs, and how it becomes a CI matrix entry. The CI tree (#95) owns the matrix and budget; this issue defines the entries. It also covers two proposals:
- test in a container. When this was written no image existed; #182 has since added `pkgs/mcpx/Containerfile`, but no CI job builds it and no test runs in it;
- label the small set of tests that cannot coexist with a user's own daemon. #138 makes every other test independent of that daemon.

The extended OS and distro list (alpine, scratch, distroless, flatpak, Fedora, Windows) is #136. The real-software subset is #137.

## Original notes

> - testing
>   - a general goal is to ensure all features have one or more integration tests
>     - for both binary && app entrypoint (consider binary a superset)
>       - all tests should pass for nix flake & container
>         - all local also but may need impractical setup
>           - very few shouldn't work if user has own real daemon running
>         - all non-cli should pass for remote

## Current state (written on d0b7e01; re-checked at 05c78b2)

| Environment | Today | Runs e2e? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| nix `nix build` | `package.nix` `checkPhase` runs 18 unit packages with `MCPX_STATE_DIR`/`MCPX_CACHE_DIR` under `$TMPDIR`. Its comment says "the end-to-end ones spawn JavaScript runtimes and bind unix sockets and do not" | **no** |
| nix `nix flake check` | `flake.nix:426-470` `checks` = `formatting`, `tidy`, plus darwin-only `sidepulse*`. **No mcpx check**, so `nix flake check` neither builds nor tests mcpx. There is no mcpx devShell (`flake.nix:526`) | **no** |
| container | **`pkgs/mcpx/Containerfile` exists since #182** (with `.dockerignore` and `docs/container.md`): three stages pinned by tag and digest -- `golang:1.26-bookworm` build, bun copied from `oven/bun:1-debian`, `debian:bookworm-slim` runtime -- plus `git` and `ca-certificates`, `ENV MCPX_SCRIPT_RUNTIME=bun` (**bun only**; `Containerfile:80`), a non-root user, `ARG CGO_ENABLED=1` threaded into the build (`:39-41`), 413 MB (108 MB base, 105 MB git with perl, 79 MB bun, 15 MB mcpx; `docs/container.md` §5). Deliberately not done (§6): **no CI job builds it, no test runs in it**, no scratch/distroless variant, not wired into `package.nix`. Its versions are a second set beside the flake's, and they already move separately: Renovate #184 bumps the Go image to 1.27 while `go.mod`/nixpkgs stay on 1.26, and that PR is green because nothing builds the file. There is still no `dockerTools` image in the flake | no |
| local (dev machine) | `go test ./...`. Needs Go, git, deno, bun, node, and **python3** (`seedElicitation`, `internal/e2e/e2e_test.go:2367-2381` at 05c78b2, shells out to `python3` for sqlite3). A missing runtime **skips** (`runtime_test.go:17-18,49-50`, `e2e_test.go:2481-2482`), which is silently green: the lesson of #35 | yes. The daemon leak (#52) is fixed in #182 (60 s idle exit, `stop --all`); the inherited environment is not (#138) |
| CI (`mcpx.yml`) | ubuntu-latest, `go test ./... -count=1` on the host with `setup-deno` **`v2.x`**, `setup-bun` **latest**, node **24**. These are *not* the versions `package.nix` wraps, so CI tests runtimes users of the nix package never get | yes |
| remote | Settings exist: `daemon.address` (default `127.0.0.1`, `internal/settings/registry.go:365`), `daemon.port` (`:343`), `daemon.endpoint` = `MCPX_DAEMON_ENDPOINT` (`:350`, "mcpx will not try to start that one"). The daemon's TCP listener is `internal/daemon/server.go:213`. The only e2e use is the **refusal** path, `TestANamedEndpointIsNotSilentlyReplacedByALocalDaemon` (`e2e_test.go:2399`). Nothing tests a *successful* remote run | refusal only |

## Approaches -- the container

### A -- `FROM nixos/nix`, run `nix build` inside (least recommended)
It reproduces the flake exactly, but it is slow (the nix store is populated per build), large, and tests a build environment rather than a runtime environment. It says nothing about "does mcpx run in a normal container".

### B -- a hand-written `Containerfile` on a distro base (debian-slim or ubuntu), with the distro's deno/bun/node
This is what non-nix users expect to read and extend, and it is in substance what #182 shipped (`debian:bookworm-slim`, bun from its own pinned image, Go from a pinned `golang` image). Its problem as the *test* environment: runtime versions now come from two places, the flake and the Containerfile's pinned images, and they drift -- already visible in #184. "the supported mcp version is the one in the flake/containerfile" (the note is quoted in #137) then has two answers. And the shipped image carries one runtime, so a test run inside it covers only bun's path to the daemon.

### C -- the image built from the flake, with a thin Containerfile for users (recommended)
- **CI image:** `pkgs.dockerTools.buildLayeredImage` (or nix2container), with contents `mcpx` plus exactly the `deno`, `bun-bin`, `nodejs` and `git` that `package.nix` wraps, plus `cacert` and a `/tmp`. One version set, defined once in the flake. It is exposed as `packages.x86_64-linux.mcpx-image`, so #49's "build every package" covers it.
- **Test image** = CI image + the precompiled test binaries: `go test -c -o e2e.test ./internal/e2e`, plus `fakemcp`/`askmcp` built on the host, with #133's binary override pointing at the image's `mcpx`. The image then needs **no Go toolchain**. Today it would, because `testsupport` runs `go build` at test time (`internal/testsupport/build.go:33,62`). So a `-fakemcp.binary` override is needed next to the mcpx one.
- **User `Containerfile`** = the one #182 added (`pkgs/mcpx/Containerfile`: debian-slim, bun only, git; it *builds* mcpx in a Go stage rather than copying a static one, with `CGO_ENABLED=1` by default and `0` one build-arg away -- verified static and working in #182, policy in #136; `docs/container.md` §4 explains why scratch/distroless saves nothing while bun and git are dynamic). What C adds to it: a CI job that builds it on every change to it (today none does, which is why #184 is green unbuilt), and a check that compares its pinned versions to the flake's and fails on drift. This is tier 2 (#136). The GIT architect owns the file and `docs/container.md` and is changing them now; this issue asks only for the job and the drift check, not for a different image.

Recommended because the flake stays the single source of versions, the image is a nix package that existing CI already knows how to build, and the test image tests the artifact rather than a rebuild.

The **test** image needs three runtimes because `exec` can only run on a host that has a JS runtime, and deno and bun reach the daemon over the unix socket, node over TCP (#35). So each test-image run must exercise all three, and it must set a `required runtimes` variable that turns the runtime skips into failures (see "Local" below). #182's user image ships one runtime on purpose (bun, the smallest; `docs/container.md` §2); a run inside it sets `MCPX_TEST_REQUIRE=bun` and covers that path only.

## Nix flake

- **`nix build`:** keep `checkPhase` unit-only. The sandbox has no network and no `$HOME`, and moving e2e in would double the build's 60 s.
- **Assert the installed output, not just build it** (from #161). `mcpx.yml` builds `result/bin/mcpx` and discards it. A few lines against it, under five seconds, cover what no other leg can: the `makeBinaryWrapper` PATH suffix works under `env -i` (`git`, `deno`, `bun`, `node` all resolve), and `mcpx doctor` passes. The man page, completion and `--version` assertions on the same output are #178's; run them in this leg rather than a second one. This is the cheapest entry in this issue and can land first.
- **`nix flake check`:** add `checks.<linux>.mcpx-e2e`, a `runCommand` with `nativeBuildInputs = [ mcpx deno bun nodejs git python3 ]` that runs the precompiled `e2e.test` against `${mcpx}/bin/mcpx`, so the **wrapped** binary is under test. Whether e2e passes in the nix sandbox is unverified; the `package.nix` comment implies nobody tried. Unix sockets under `$TMPDIR` are allowed in the Linux sandbox, but `deno` needs a writable `DENO_DIR` and must not fetch anything. That is the first thing to find out, and if it fails, the answer is a list of tests to mark `needs-network` or `needs-home`.
- A **devShell** `mcpx` providing go, gopls, deno, bun, node, git, python3 and golangci-lint at the flake's versions. This is the "impractical setup" made practical for local runs.

## Local

"may need impractical setup". Three steps make it practical:
1. `nix develop .#mcpx` (above) for anyone with nix.
2. A preflight in `TestMain` that prints what is missing (runtime, python3, git) once, not one skip per test.
3. `MCPX_TEST_REQUIRE=deno,bun,node,python3` (name to be decided). When it is set, a missing dependency **fails** instead of skipping. CI and container runs always set it; laptops do not. This closes the #35 gap, where "a test that skips a runtime it cannot find silently covers less" (the `mcpx.yml` comment).

### "very few shouldn't work if user has own real daemon running"

Two separate things:
- **Most tests must never touch the user's daemon.** Today they can. `newEnv` builds the child environment from `os.Environ()` (`e2e_test.go:52`), so an inherited `MCPX_DAEMON_ENDPOINT` points tests at it; the opencode plugin injects exactly that into every shell (`plugin/opencode/mcpx-session.ts:696-701`). #182 bounded leaked daemons to 60 s but did not change this. Fix: #138.
- **A few legitimately can't coexist**, because they test the *default* paths: default `XDG_STATE_HOME`/`~/.local/state/mcpx` resolution, the shared private runtime dir fallback (`internal/daemon/paths.go:115-148` at 05c78b2), `mcpx daemons` scanning, and the plugin's ladder against the real runtime dir.
- **A third option for "safe on a laptop" (from #162): run modes.** `MCPX_DAEMON_AUTOSTART=false MCPX_DAEMON_INLINE=true` runs the daemon in-process for one command on a private socket and leaves nothing behind (`internal/e2e/e2e_test.go` has two inline tests, `:2416` and `:2432`). A harness setting with three values -- `inline` (the default for a local developer/agent run: cannot collide, cannot leak, cannot test daemon lifetime), `spawn` (today's behaviour; the gating CI leg) and `remote` (below) -- with each test declaring `requiresDaemonLifetime` / `requiresLocalFilesystem`, makes the local run safe by construction rather than by discipline. It reuses existing settings only. It is the same per-test "needs" mechanism as the remote C below; build one scheme.

Labelling approaches:
- **A -- test-name prefix** (`TestHostDaemon...`). It is greppable and selectable with `-run`/`-skip`, but nothing enforces it. A new default-path test that forgets the prefix breaks on a dev machine and nobody knows why.
- **B -- build tag `hostdaemon`.** Excluded unless `-tags hostdaemon` is given, so nothing is forgotten at runtime. But a tagged file compiles only in a separate invocation, which adds one more `go test` to the matrix and hides compile errors in the default build.
- **C -- detection plus skip, with a name convention for the inventory (recommended).** A helper `testsupport.RequireNoUserDaemon(t)` resolves the user's default paths with the *real* environment, pings any socket there, and `t.Skip`s with the socket path if something answers. In CI nothing answers, so the tests run; on a dev machine they skip with a reason, not a mysterious failure. The helper is the label: the #132 inventory lists every test that calls it. Keep the set as small as possible, and treat every addition as a design smell to justify in review (#99).

## Remote

"all non-cli should pass for remote". Here non-cli means `/v1`, MCP at `/mcp`, and the generated client over TCP. The CLI tests stay local because they drive a local process.

What "non-cli" covers, by command (from #162): pure-local commands (`man`, `completion`, `help`, `init`, `config`) have nothing to be remote about; daemon-backed commands with no local path (`ls`, `call`, `status`, `settings`, `servers`, `search`, `prompts`, `resources`, `tasks`, ...) must pass; commands that name a local path (`mcpx run ./file.ts`, `exec --export`) must be **refused clearly** -- `docs/exec.md:64-73` already says a remote run sends the script's text and refuses `--export` with `--remote`; local-machine management (`daemons`, `stop`, `restart`) needs a decided answer. And one mechanism is easy to miss: the generated client picks its transport per runtime (`internal/codegen/emit.go:263-300`: deno and bun over the unix socket, anything else over TCP to `ENDPOINT`), so against a remote daemon **every runtime takes the TCP path** -- a remote leg covers node's transport under deno and bun, which nothing else does.

What breaks today if the suite is pointed at a remote daemon:
- tests read `e.dir/state/...` directly (the log DB, sockets, `seedElicitation`);
- `restart`/`stop` take the shared daemon away from every other test;
- per-test config files do not reach another host;
- two tests adding server `demo` collide.

### A -- run the whole e2e package with `MCPX_DAEMON_ENDPOINT` set (least recommended)
It needs one line of CI. Most tests would fail for the reasons above, and the failures would say nothing about remote support.

### B -- a separate hand-written remote suite
It is clean, but it duplicates the `/v1` and MCP assertions, and the two copies drift.

### C -- the same tests, tagged by need, and a remote runner (recommended)
- Each `/v1`/MCP test declares its needs through the harness: `localFS`, `ownsDaemon` (restart/stop), `perTestConfig`.
- The remote runner selects the tests with none of those needs.
- Per-test servers are added over `POST /v1/servers` with a per-test name suffix and removed in cleanup. This is a good reason for `/v1` tests to prefer live add over config files anyway.
- The daemon runs in a service container (GitHub Actions `services:`, Linux only) from the test image above, with `daemon.address=0.0.0.0`, a fixed `daemon.port`, and the scriptable `fakemcp` (#133) baked in.
- `TestExecOnTheDaemonRunsWhereTheDaemonIs` (`internal/e2e/exec_test.go:330`) becomes the canonical remote exec test.

Recommended because it tests the real claim with the real assertions, and makes "is this test remote-safe" something the harness knows rather than something a list claims.

## Matrix entries (for #95)

| Entry | Runner | Needs | Runs | Tier (#136) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `unit` | ubuntu-latest | Go | `go test` on non-e2e packages | 1 |
| `e2e-host-linux` | ubuntu-latest | Go + runtimes at **flake** versions (from the devShell, not `setup-*@latest`) + python3; `MCPX_TEST_REQUIRE` set | e2e, binary suite | 1 |
| `e2e-inproc` | ubuntu-latest | same | e2e, in-process suite (#133) | 1, once it exists |
| `nix-build` | ubuntu-latest | nix | `nix build .#mcpx` (unit `checkPhase`), then the installed-output assertions above (wrapper under `env -i`, `doctor`, #178's man/completion/version) | 1 (build exists; assertions new) |
| `nix-flake-check` | ubuntu-latest | nix | `checks.mcpx-e2e` against the wrapped binary | 1 if under budget, else 2 |
| `container` | ubuntu-latest, `container:` = test image | image from `packages.mcpx-image` | e2e binary suite inside | 2 |
| `container-user` | ubuntu-latest | `docker build -f pkgs/mcpx/Containerfile` (#182's image) | build on every change to the file (#184 is green unbuilt today); then `--version`, `ls` and one bun `exec` inside, `MCPX_TEST_REQUIRE=bun`; version-drift check against the flake | 1 for the build (it is a shipped file), 2 for the run |
| `e2e-no-deno` | ubuntu-latest | bun and node only on PATH | the real bun and node e2e paths with no Deno anywhere on `PATH` -- what a user without Deno gets from `script.runtime=auto`, which no nix-wrapped run can show (the wrapper suffixes Deno). #100's own `auto` test uses stub runtimes on `PATH` and runs in any leg; this leg is the end-to-end counterpart. **#100 owns the runtime question (#181 collision 11)** | 1 once #100 lands |
| `e2e-host-linux-arm64` | ubuntu-24.04-arm | as linux | e2e binary suite; a second *architecture* rather than a second OS (see the comment from #161 below) | 2 (open) |
| `remote` | ubuntu-latest + `services:` daemon | test image as the service | remote-safe `/v1` + MCP subset | 2 |
| `e2e-host-macos` | macos-latest | as linux | e2e binary suite (#35 was a macOS/Linux split) | 2 |
| `plugin` | ubuntu-latest | bun | `bun test plugin/opencode/mcpx/daemon.test.ts` (#132) | 1 |

`container:` and `services:` need a Linux runner on GitHub-hosted runners: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-where-your-workflow-runs/running-jobs-in-a-container.

## Open questions

- Does e2e pass in the nix Linux sandbox at all? Check deno's cache dir, the absence of `$HOME`, and the 104/108-byte socket path under `$TMPDIR`. This is the cheapest experiment in the tree.
- Should the host CI job take runtimes from the flake devShell (consistent with the package) or from `setup-*` (fast cached downloads)? Pinning `setup-deno` to the flake's exact version is a middle path, with a drift check.
- Remote: add `remote-safe` as an explicit opt-in per test, or derive it from declared needs? Opt-in is safer at first.
- Where does the test image live (ghcr.io?), or is it only built per run with `nix build` and `docker load`?
- A new e2e test that randomises must take the run seed (#93) in every environment. The seed must be passed into containers and service containers too.
- Remote: which side owns the config? `MCPX_CONFIG` is read by the daemon, so a remote daemon has a config the client cannot see; does the harness push servers over `POST /v1/servers` (C above) only, or also start the daemon with a per-run config (from #162)?
- Remote: is loopback TCP (`daemon.address=127.0.0.1`, fixed `daemon.port`) enough for the gating leg, with a real second host (a service container) nightly? Loopback is a different transport, not a different host (from #162).
- Container versions: should the Containerfile's pinned images be bumped together with `flake.lock` (one Renovate group), or read their versions from the flake? #184 is the first drift.
- **Likely to change under the GIT architect's in-flight work:** `docs/container.md` §3/§5 keep `git` in the image (105 MB with perl) because the `repo`/`worktree` scopes shell out to it. GIT is replacing that with native resolution in `internal/config/scope.go`; if it lands, `git` can leave the image and the `needs git` labels here and in #136 may disappear. Re-check this issue when that PR merges.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** L (devShell and `MCPX_TEST_REQUIRE`: S; flake image and `checks.mcpx-e2e`: M; remote runner: M-L) · **Impact** high
**Depends on / related**: #133 (binary and fakemcp overrides, scriptable fake), #138 (isolation first), #136 (tiers, extended OSes, static policy), #137 (the pinned version set), #95 (owns the matrix), #49 (build every flake package, including the image), #100 (owns #181 collision 11: the `auto` runtime test; the no-Deno leg is a row here), #178 (man/completion/version assertions on the nix output), #52 (closed, fixed in #182), #35, #65, #93 (seed), #99 (when agents run which entry).

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

## Acceptance criteria

- The environments matrix (nix flake, container, local, remote) is implemented as specified in the body and each leg's CI result is recorded.
- The work described in the Summary/Scope above is delivered via a branch + PR (no direct push to main); verification runs in GitHub Actions CI, not on the sandbox.
- Evidence (CI links, timings, or probe output as applicable) is recorded on this issue before it is closed.

code.title: mcpx docs: a custom subdomain for the site (DNS, CNAME, HTTPS)
code.body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#119 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #90

## Summary

Give the docs site its own hostname, e.g. `mcpx.drewrypope.com`: create the DNS record, set the custom domain on the repository's Pages, confirm the domain is verified against takeover, then enforce HTTPS. This is mostly clicks and one DNS record. The only real choice is subdomain vs. a path under `www.drewrypope.com` vs. a new domain.

## Original notes

> - documentation
>   - make a book using whatever is the most common and simple modern choice
>     - github static setup. separately, assign a subdomain

("github static setup" is #118.)

## Current state (checked 2026-09-30 with `dig`, `curl` and `gh api`)

| Name | Resolves to | Serves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `drewrypope.com` (apex) | Porkbun forwarding IPs `207.207.210.x` | a 307 redirect to `http://www.drewrypope.com/`, done by Porkbun rather than GitHub |
| `www.drewrypope.com` | CNAME `dezren39.github.io` | the user site `dezren39/dezren39.github.io` (branch-published, HTTPS enforced) |
| `mcpx.drewrypope.com`, `docs.drewrypope.com`, any random name | CNAME `uixie.porkbun.com` | Porkbun parking. This looks like a **wildcard** `*.drewrypope.com` record |
| `_github-pages-challenge-dezren39.drewrypope.com` | TXT present | the GitHub Pages domain-verification record for the `dezren39` account |

- **DNS is hosted at Porkbun** (NS `*.ns.porkbun.com`). This answers the question of who hosts the DNS.
- A domain verified for the account covers its immediate subdomains ([GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/configuring-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site/verifying-your-custom-domain-for-github-pages)). If `drewrypope.com` shows as verified under Settings > Pages, then `mcpx.drewrypope.com` is already protected from takeover. Confirm in the UI, because the TXT record is only evidence of verification.
- **The wildcard.** GitHub warns against wildcard DNS records because of takeover risk. That warning is about wildcards pointed at GitHub Pages; this one points at Porkbun parking. An explicit `mcpx` CNAME takes precedence over the wildcard for that name, so the wildcard does not block this issue. Whether to keep it is a separate call (security deferred).
- `dezren39/nix` has no Pages site yet (#118). Until it has a custom domain, a project site from it would be served at `https://www.drewrypope.com/nix/`, because it inherits the user site's domain.

## Steps (assuming Approach C and the Actions deploy from #118)

1. **Add the custom domain on the repository first**: Settings > Pages > Custom domain, or `gh api repos/dezren39/nix/pages -X PUT -f cname=mcpx.drewrypope.com`. GitHub asks for the domain to be added on GitHub **before** creating the DNS record, so that nobody else can claim it in between ([GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/configuring-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site/managing-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site)).
2. **At Porkbun**, create `CNAME mcpx -> dezren39.github.io.`. It must be the user domain: not `dezren39.github.io/nix`, and not the `*.pages.github.io` name shown in repository settings.
3. **Verify the record** with `dig mcpx.drewrypope.com +nostats +nocomments +nocmd`, which should show the CNAME chain ending at GitHub Pages. Propagation can take up to 24 hours.
4. **Wait for the certificate**, then tick **Enforce HTTPS**. The option can take up to 24 hours to appear.
5. **No `CNAME` file.** With a custom GitHub Actions workflow, "no `CNAME` file is created, and any existing `CNAME` file is ignored and is not required" (same GitHub page, step 4). Do not add one. It would do nothing, and it would mislead the next reader. It only matters if #118 chooses Approach A (branch deploy).
6. **Base URL.** Build the site for `https://mcpx.drewrypope.com/` with root `/`, not `/nix/`: #118's `baseUrl` argument, or mdBook's `site-url`.
7. **Check the old path.** GitHub normally redirects `www.drewrypope.com/nix/` to the new domain once one is set. Verify this after the switch; do not rely on it.

## Approaches: which hostname

### Approach A (least recommended): no custom domain, serve at `www.drewrypope.com/nix/`

- It costs nothing: no DNS change at all.
- But the URL names the config monorepo, not the product, and it breaks the day the docs move (a separate repository, a rename).
- The `/nix/` base path gets baked into every link and asset, and printed install one-liners (`curl <url> | sh`, #158) would carry it forever.

### Approach B (middle): a new dedicated domain, e.g. `mcpx.dev` or `getmcpx.com`

- It gives the best name for a product and the best short URL for `curl -fsSL <domain>/install.sh | sh`. It also survives any change of owner or repository.
- Costs: a registration fee every year, a second DNS zone, a separate domain verification, and the domain has to be renewed forever or it becomes a takeover target.
- It is worth it only if mcpx becomes a public product with users outside this machine. It can be added later: the domain setting on the repository is one field, and the old subdomain can redirect.

### Approach C (recommended): `mcpx.drewrypope.com`

- One CNAME in a zone that is already managed.
- The domain appears already verified for the account, so no new takeover surface.
- HTTPS comes free from GitHub Pages.
- It is independent of the repository name, so the docs can later move to another repository by moving one repository setting.
- It is exactly what the notes ask for ("assign a subdomain").

## Open questions

1. The name: `mcpx.drewrypope.com` or `docs.mcpx...`, or something else?
2. Does the short install URL for `curl <short> | sh` live on this host (e.g. `https://mcpx.drewrypope.com/install.sh`, served by Pages as a static file), or somewhere shorter? It is tied to the release channels in #158.
3. Keep or remove the Porkbun wildcard `*.drewrypope.com` record?
4. Should the apex keep forwarding to `www` via Porkbun, or move to GitHub's own apex-to-www redirect (A/AAAA records on the apex)? This is unrelated to mcpx and can be left alone.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** S (one DNS record, one repository setting, a wait for the certificate) · **Impact** med (stable public URL; every printed link and the install one-liner depend on it) · **Depends on / related**: #118 (the site must exist first), #158 (short install URL), #155

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.
