code.title: mcpx: resolve a script's import graph statically and prepare missing dependencies
code.body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#104 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #175

**Cache: deferred to #187** (#181 collision 12). #187 owns the cache mechanism
(layout, keys, eviction, leases); this issue owns what it puts in it — the
resolved import graph and the prepared environment. The cache text in stages 1
and 3 below stays as input to #187.

## Summary

When a script imports something that is not present, mcpx should be able to
work out what it needs and make it available — without an LLM in the loop, and
without executing the script. The static import graph of an ES module program
is fully determinable; the exceptions are enumerable and small. This issue
covers computing that graph, deciding what to do with the unresolved edges, and
the cross-directory case where an imported file belongs to a different project
with its own manifest and lockfile.

## Original notes

> - non-ai auto-import dynamic if a script imports something that isnt avaialble
>   - because of typescript and esm the entire import tree can be determined without executing anythign right?
>   - if i import a file in another dir that has its own package.json/lock can it auto-import, prepare dependencies to be available whereever needed

## Current state

- mcpx does not look at imports at all. `runner.Run` writes files and spawns a
  process; an unresolved import is a runtime error from deno/bun/node.
- `script.typecheck` (`off|on|strict`, default off) is the nearest thing: `deno
  check` resolves and checks the whole module graph without executing it, which
  is why its own description says "Resolves and checks every import without
  executing anything". It *fails* on an unresolved import rather than fixing it,
  and it only works under Deno (`internal/preflight/preflight.go:204-213`).
- `internal/diagnose` already parses a script statically to find tool calls
  before it runs; it is the existing precedent for "read the source, decide
  something, report deterministically". #79 notes its limits honestly:
  `tools[ns][name]` and dispatch on `search()` results are undecidable in
  general.
- Named scripts resolve across a search path (`internal/cli/scripts.go`), so a
  script *can* live somewhere other than the caller's directory today — which is
  precisely the situation where a relative import into another project arises.

### Is the import tree fully determinable? Mostly yes.

| construct | statically known? | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `import x from "./a.ts"` | yes | literal specifier, resolvable without executing |
| `export … from "…"` | yes | same |
| `import type` | yes, and erasable | matters: a type-only edge needs no runtime package |
| `import("./" + name)` | **no** | computed specifier; undecidable in general |
| `import("./a.ts")` (literal) | yes | a literal dynamic import is still a literal |
| `require("x")` in CJS | usually | literal in practice, but `require(v)` is the same hole |
| `npm:` / `jsr:` / `https:` | yes as an edge | but traversing *into* it needs a fetch |
| conditional exports / `imports` map | yes given the manifest | resolution depends on the manifest, so the manifest is part of the input |

`deno info --json <entry>` already emits exactly this graph. Verified here: it
returns `{version, roots, modules:[{kind:"esm", dependencies:[{specifier, code:
{specifier, span:{…}}}]}]}` with resolved file URLs and source spans, and it
lists npm packages separately. That is a usable, already-installed,
no-new-dependency implementation of the whole analysis — including for scripts
that will be *run* by bun or node, since the graph is a property of the source,
not of the runtime. The caveats are deno's stricter resolution rules
(extensionless relative imports fail; `--sloppy-imports` relaxes it) and that a
`deno info` over uncached remote/npm specifiers touches the network.

So the answer to the user's question is: **yes for everything except computed
dynamic `import()` and computed `require()`**, and those two can be detected and
reported ("this script has a dynamic import mcpx cannot resolve; declare it with
`--package` or it will fail at runtime") rather than silently mishandled.

### The cross-directory manifest case

Node and bun resolve `node_modules` by walking up from the **importing file**,
not from the entry point or the process cwd. So a script in `/a` importing
`/b/helper.ts`, where `/b` has its own `package.json` and `node_modules`,
already works on those two runtimes with no help from mcpx — `helper.ts`'s own
bare imports resolve against `/b/node_modules`. What does *not* happen is
installation: if `/b/node_modules` is absent, nothing creates it. Deno is
different again: resolution follows `deno.json`/import maps, and a second
project's `package.json` is only consulted if deno is pointed at it.

So "prepare dependencies to be available wherever needed" is a real gap on all
three, and it is specifically an *install/materialise* gap rather than a
*resolution* gap.

## Approaches

### Approach A — least recommended: catch the failure and retry

Run the script; when it dies with a module-not-found, parse the runtime's error
message for the specifier, install it, run again.

Why not: three different error formats that change between versions, and the
parse is a guess. Worse, the retry re-executes a script that already ran to the
point of failure — every side effect before the bad import happens twice, and
scripts here call MCP tools that write files, drive browsers and post to APIs.
"Run it twice" is not a safe primitive in a system whose whole purpose is
side-effecting tool calls. It also cannot see a failure behind a conditional
import that did not execute this time.

### Approach B — middle: a resolve-check gate before the run

Extend the preflight: compute the graph with `deno info --json`, diff it against
what is available, and either fail with a precise list of missing specifiers or
— under a `--auto-install` flag — install them and proceed.

Cheap, deterministic, no double execution, and it reuses the existing
`preflight.Report` shape (problems and warnings, all reported in one pass —
`TestEveryBadPathIsReportedInOnePass`). The output is immediately better than
what exists: a list of every missing import with a source span, instead of the
first one at runtime.

Its limits: it resolves but does not *prepare* — it has nowhere to put what it
installs that is not somebody's project directory — and it does nothing about a
second project's manifest.

### Approach C — recommended: static graph → resolved dependency set → prepared environment, keyed by hash

One pipeline with three named stages, each independently disableable, reusing
the resolved dependency set from the npm/dependency-configuration sibling issue:

1. **Graph.** `deno info --json` on the launcher (the launcher, not the script —
   the launcher is what actually runs, which is already the rule
   `runner.Run` applies for typechecking). Produces resolved edges, unresolved
   edges, npm/jsr specifiers, and a list of computed dynamic imports it cannot
   decide. Cacheable by the hash of the entry file plus its transitive mtimes
   (#187 argues for content hashes instead: mtimes are not stable across
   checkouts).
2. **Resolve.** Unresolved bare specifiers become entries in the dependency set,
   pinned by: an explicit `--package` if given, else the version in the nearest
   manifest that declares it, else the latest — and *latest is announced, not
   assumed silently*, because `docs/story.md:1672` already commits to pinned npm
   versions. Every *file* edge that crosses into a directory with its own
   `package.json`/`deno.json` contributes that manifest as a **sub-set**, kept
   distinct rather than flattened.
3. **Prepare.** Materialise per runtime into a content-addressed directory (an
   entry in #187's cache) keyed by the hash of the resolved set, exactly as the exec workdir is keyed by the
   hash of the generated client. Same set, same directory, warm cache; different
   set, no collision. For node/bun this is a `node_modules` (or a symlink farm);
   for deno an import map or `npm:` rewrite; for a cross-directory sub-set, a
   `node_modules` beside *that* file so the runtime's own upward walk finds it,
   which keeps node and bun semantics intact instead of merging two projects'
   dependency trees into one and getting version conflicts mcpx would then have
   to arbitrate.

Policy settings, in the one registry so they reach every surface:

| setting | values | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `script.imports` | `off\|report\|prepare` | `report` | how far the pipeline runs |
| `script.importsOnMissing` | `fail\|warn\|install` | `fail` | the missing-specifier policy |
| `script.importsOnDynamic` | `warn\|fail\|ignore` | `warn` | what to do about a computed `import()` |
| `script.importsCrossProject` | `isolate\|merge\|ignore` | `isolate` | how a second manifest is handled |
| `script.importsNetwork` | `off\|on` | `on` | whether resolution may fetch |

Naming (changed in the 2026-09-30 pass, same rule as #100's `script.check`):
these were `script.imports.onMissing` and so on. A nested config file cannot
hold `script.imports` as both a value and an object, and no declared setting
path is both a leaf and a branch (`internal/settings/file.go:18-24` flattens
nested objects), so the policy knobs are flat camelCase siblings.

Why this is the right one:

- It never executes the script to learn about it, which is the whole point of
  "non-ai auto-import dynamic".
- `report` as the default is honest and free: the user gets a precise list
  before anything starts, and opts into `prepare` when they want mcpx touching
  package state. An exec path that silently installs packages by default would
  be a surprising thing for a daemon to do on someone's behalf.
- Keying the prepared environment by content hash is the same fix the runner
  already applied twice (exec workdir per catalogue, launcher per content) after
  being burned by shared mutable directories. Applying it a third time is
  cheaper than discovering the same bug in `node_modules`.
- `isolate` for cross-project preserves the runtime's native resolution rather
  than replacing it. Merging two dependency trees means mcpx owns version
  conflict resolution, which is a package manager's job and not a small one.

Two smaller things that fall out and are worth doing regardless:

- The graph does **not** answer #79's point 3 (corrected 2026-09-30; an earlier
  version said it did). Namespaces reach a script as bare identifiers bound by the
  prelude (`buildPrelude`, `internal/cli/commands.go:1041-1044`) or through
  `tools[ns]`, not as imports, so they are not in the import graph. Only a named
  import from the client (`import { fff } from "./mcpx-client.ts"`) shows up.
  The diagnose scanner is the tool for namespaces; see #79 point 3.
- An unresolved import currently fails only when the runtime loads the module,
  after mcpx's own preflight and, on a fully cold cache, after every server was
  started to read schemas (`internal/cli/commands.go:1023-1039`).
  `runner.Run`'s comment says typechecking is deliberately placed "before a
  single server starts" for this reason; the graph stage belongs at the same
  point.

## Open questions

- Is `deno info` acceptable as the graph oracle for runs on bun and node?
  It makes deno a hard dependency of import analysis even when it is not the
  runtime. The alternative — a TypeScript/`es-module-lexer` resolver in Go — is a
  real implementation, and `docs/dependencies.md` sets a high bar for new
  dependencies.
- `deno info` over uncached npm/remote specifiers hits the network. Does
  `script.imports.network = off` degrade to "report the edge, do not traverse
  it", or refuse?
- Type-only imports (`import type`) contribute a checking dependency and no
  runtime one. Does `prepare` install them? It must for `report` under
  `script.check` to be meaningful.
- How is the prepared directory invalidated when a lockfile in a cross-project
  directory changes? Hashing the lockfile is easy; noticing it changed mid-run
  is not. (Keying is this issue's; leases that stop a prune removing an entry a
  run is using are #187's.)
- Does `prepare` ever write into the user's own project directory (the
  cross-project `node_modules` case), or always into mcpx-owned storage with a
  symlink? Writing into someone else's repo is the kind of thing that must be
  opt-in and loud.
- What does a remote exec do? It has no file graph — the script arrives as
  text — so only its top-level bare specifiers are analysable. Probably: resolve
  what is visible, and require the rest to arrive in `ExecOptions.deps`.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** L · **Impact** high — it is the difference between "scripts may use
libraries if you set the project up first" and "scripts may use libraries".

**Depends on / related**: #103 (supplies the dependency-set concept this
pipeline fills in), #187 (owns the cache mechanism, #181 collision 12), #100
(`script.check` and the preflight stage this sits beside; the naming rule
above), #79 (preflight scanner limits, cold-cache exec, typecheck cost), #78
(cache correctness), #40 (closed, fixed in #57 — ExecOptions), and siblings
#105 (Python parity) and #101 (comparison doc).

code.title: mcpx: how the JavaScript runtime is chosen, what each does with TypeScript, and an automatic validate/compile step
code.body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#100 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #175

**Owns #181 collision 1** (`script.typecheck` rename vs #79's default flip) and **collision 11** (`auto` resolution); see
"Owned decisions" below.

## Summary

Three questions in one: how a user picks the JavaScript runtime, what each of
deno/bun/node actually does with the TypeScript it is handed (they differ, and
node differs from itself depending on one flag mcpx does not pass), and whether
mcpx should validate/transpile a script automatically before running it.

The short answer to the first, which should also be the first line of the docs:

```
mcpx run x.ts --runtime deno        # flag (also spelled --script-runtime)
MCPX_SCRIPT_RUNTIME=bun mcpx exec …  # env var
{"script": {"runtime": "node"}}      # config key script.runtime
POST /v1/exec {"options":{"runtime":"deno"}}   # wire, and the same field on MCP mcpx_exec
mcpx set script.runtime deno         # /v1/settings, MCP settings tool
```

Values: `auto | deno | bun | node`, default `auto`.

## Original notes

> - how do i set the js runtime?
>   - you had mentioned node alongside bun etc, would a user run javascript there? typescript would fall over? 
>   - what is or can be automatically stitched together or compiled to js or doesnt need to can run ts direct?
>   - if node would fall over, could existing ts be compiled for a js project?
>   - is there a way to support .dt js type files? at least for validation etc?
>   - handle validate/import/compile automatically when possible then provide config to disable/skip/run-but-keep-going-on-error/etc.

## Current state

- `script.runtime` is one registry entry (`internal/settings/registry.go:176`):
  `KindEnum`, default `auto`, enum `auto|deno|bun|node`, `FlagAliases:
  ["runtime"]`, scope client, offered only on `run` and `exec`. The registry
  gives it the flag, the `MCPX_SCRIPT_RUNTIME` env var, the config key,
  `/v1/settings` and the MCP settings tool for free.
- `ExecOptions.runtime` carries it over the wire (`docs/exec.md`), and the
  daemon seeds its default from the same setting
  (`internal/daemon/routes_exec.go:173`).
- `runner.Detect` (`internal/runner/runner.go:72`) honours an explicit preference
  and otherwise takes the first of `deno`, `bun`, `node` found on `PATH`. The
  Nix wrapper suffixes all three onto `PATH` (`package.nix:96-103`,
  `docs/dependencies.md`), so on a packaged install `auto` always means deno.
  The container (#182) ships only bun and sets `MCPX_SCRIPT_RUNTIME=bun`
  (`Containerfile:73-80`), so `auto` never runs there either. No test asserts
  what `auto` picks; the only caller in a test is `execsvc_test.go:42`, which
  just needs *a* runtime.
- Per-runtime argv, verbatim from `Detect`:
  - deno: `run --quiet --no-check <perms…> script`
  - bun: `run script`
  - node: `--no-warnings --experimental-strip-types script` (`runner.go:100`;
    #108, in flight, replaces the flag)
- `script.typecheck` (`off|on|strict`, default `off`,
  `internal/settings/registry.go:244`) runs `deno check`, and
  `preflight.TypeCheck` reports "type checking is only available under Deno"
  for the other two rather than pretending
  (`internal/preflight/preflight.go:198-213`). That report is a non-fatal
  problem, so under bun or node every run with the check on prints it to
  stderr (`runner.go:333-340`).
- `script.typecheck` is **not** an `ExecOptions` field (`internal/execsvc/execsvc.go:101-124`).
  `/v1/exec` applies the daemon's own value (`execsvc.go:336`,
  `internal/daemon/routes_exec.go:176`), and `mcpx run --remote --typecheck on`
  hands off to the daemon (`internal/cli/commands.go:556-559`) before
  `--typecheck` is read (`:748`), so a remote run accepts the flag and drops it.
  Whatever replaces it has to travel on `ExecOptions`.
- `diagnose.preflight` (default on, `internal/defaults/defaults.json:84`) already
  stops a run on an unknown tool in a configured namespace before any side
  effect (`internal/cli/consumer.go:517-535`). It is deliberately silent about
  an unconfigured namespace (`internal/diagnose/diagnose.go:278-282`), and that
  gap is the one `--typecheck` closes (#66).
- Named scripts already resolve `.ts`, `.mts`, `.js`, `.mjs`
  (`ScriptExtensions`, `internal/cli/scripts.go`), with
  `plumbing.allowTsJsOverlap` for a directory holding both. So JavaScript
  scripts are already runnable; nothing *validates* them.

### What each runtime does with `.ts` (verified here, versions from the box)

deno 2.9.6 (TypeScript 6.0.3) · bun 1.3.11 · node v24.20.0.

| input | deno | bun | node (as mcpx invokes it) | node `--experimental-transform-types` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| plain type annotations | runs | runs | runs | runs |
| `enum E { A }` | runs | runs | **fails** | runs |
| `namespace N { export const v = 1 }` | runs | runs | **fails** | runs |
| legacy decorators | runs | runs | fails | **fails** |
| `import {a} from "./lib"` (no extension) | **fails** (wants `.ts` or `--sloppy-imports`) | runs | **fails** | fails |
| `import {a} from "./lib.ts"` | runs | runs | runs | runs |
| type *checking* | `deno check` | none | none | none |

Two facts worth pulling out of that table:

1. **node already strips types with no flag at all** in v24 — `node plain.ts`
   works. `--experimental-strip-types` is now a no-op default (`--no-strip-types`
   turns it off). What mcpx does *not* pass is `--experimental-transform-types`,
   and that single omission is the entire difference between "enum fails" and
   "enum works" on node. This is a one-line change in `Detect` and is the
   cheapest item in this theme; #108 (in flight) carries it.
2. **The extension rules are opposite.** deno refuses extensionless relative
   imports; node refuses `.ts`-less *and* ESM-extensionless ones; bun accepts
   both. A script written against bun is the one most likely to break when the
   runtime changes. mcpx's own generated launcher imports `./mcpx-client.ts`
   with the extension, which is the form all three accept — that was already the
   right call.

So: "would a user run JavaScript on node?" — yes, and `.js`/`.mjs` scripts
already resolve. "Would TypeScript fall over?" — only on non-erasable syntax
(`enum`, value `namespace`, parameter properties, legacy decorators), and
mostly not after passing `--experimental-transform-types`. Decorators remain
node's hard edge.

### Can TS be compiled for a JS project?

Yes, three ways, none currently wired up:

| tool | command | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| deno | `deno bundle -o out.js entry.ts` (present in 2.9, `--platform browser\|deno`, `--packages bundle\|external`) | no extra dependency; mcpx already requires deno for typecheck |
| bun | `bun build --target=node --outfile out.js` | fast, needs bun present |
| tsc | `tsc --declaration --allowJs --checkJs` | the only one that also emits `.d.ts`; **not installed here** (`which tsc` → not found) so it would be an `npx`/`bunx` dependency |

`deno compile` additionally produces a self-contained binary from a script,
which is a plausible later answer to "baked into binary" (see the dependency
issue).

### `.d.ts` for `.js` scripts

The user wrote ".dt"; the thing meant is `.d.ts`, and it already works without
any new machinery:

- mcpx already writes `mcpx-globals.d.ts` beside the client and the built-in
  launcher carries `/// <reference path="./mcpx-globals.d.ts" />`
  (`runner.GlobalsFileName`, `writeLauncher`). That is exactly the mechanism
  being asked for, applied so far only to the ambient globals.
- A `.js` script gets checked today by adding `// @ts-check` and JSDoc types.
  Verified: `deno check c.js` on a `// @ts-check` file with
  `/** @param {number} n */ … n.toUpperCase()` reports the type error and exits
  non-zero. Without the comment it is silent — Deno needs either `// @ts-check`
  per file or `compilerOptions.checkJs` in a `deno.json`.
- The generated client is `.ts`. For a `.js` script to be checked against it,
  mcpx would need to emit `mcpx-client.js` + `mcpx-client.d.ts` alongside, or
  rely on the runtime resolving `./mcpx-client.ts` from JS (deno and bun do;
  node does not from a `.js` file under plain strip-types).

## Approaches

The design choice is the last sub-bullet: what mcpx does automatically before
running a script, and how it is configured. The runtime-selection answer above
is documentation, not a choice, and the `--experimental-transform-types` fix is
a bug fix rather than a design.

### Approach A — least recommended: transpile everything to JS first

mcpx runs a bundler (`deno bundle` / `bun build`) over the launcher and hands
plain JavaScript to whichever runtime is selected, so all three behave
identically and node's syntax gaps vanish.

Why not: it destroys the thing the current design is built around. `runner.go`'s
header comment is explicit that a local file on disk exists so the *runtime's
own module cache* does the work and a run costs tens of milliseconds instead of
~10s. A bundle step is a cache mcpx now owns, invalidates and gets wrong; it
breaks stack traces and source positions in the error messages agents read; it
forces a decision on `npm:`/`jsr:`/`https:` specifiers that the runtimes resolve
for free; and it makes the bundler a hard dependency of running any script at
all. It also cannot fix decorators without a full TypeScript compiler.

### Approach B — middle: widen the existing typecheck setting into a validation policy

Keep `script.typecheck` as the single knob but give it more values and make it
runtime-aware: `off | on | strict | auto`, where `auto` means "check if the
selected runtime can" and stays silent otherwise. Add an error policy —
`script.onTypeError = fail | warn | run` — so "run-but-keep-going-on-error" is
expressible, which today it is not: `preflight.TypeCheck` returns and `runner.Run`
aborts on `rep.Err()`.

This covers most of the ask with a small diff and no new subsystem. What it
does not cover: it cannot check anything under bun or node (Deno-only, stated
in code), so the policy silently degrades on two of the three runtimes; and it
says nothing about `.js`+`.d.ts`, or about compiling.

Worth pairing with #79's proposal to default `script.typecheck` to `on` for
`run` — that measurement work (≈80 ms repeat, ≈400 ms new program) is the
evidence that a default-on check is affordable.

### Approach C — recommended: a declared preflight *pipeline* with per-stage policy

Name the stages that can run before a script does, make each one independently
configurable, and let each one declare what it does when the selected runtime
cannot perform it. This is what the last sub-bullet asks for, and it is the
shape mcpx already uses elsewhere (`internal/preflight` returns a `Report` with
problems and warnings; the launcher already has five named phases because "a
launcher that is half-configurable invites forking it" — same argument).

Proposed settings, all in the one registry so they arrive on CLI, env, config,
`/v1/settings` and MCP at once:

| setting | values | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `script.check` | `off\|syntax\|types\|strict` | `syntax` | how hard to look before running |
| `script.checkOnError` | `fail\|warn\|run` | `fail` | the "keep going on error" knob |
| `script.checkOnUnsupported` | `skip\|warn\|switch` | `warn` | what to do when the runtime cannot check — `switch` borrows deno purely as a checker while still *running* on the configured runtime |
| `script.compile` | `off\|auto\|always` | `off` | emit JS before running; `auto` only when the selected runtime would choke (node + non-erasable syntax) |
| `script.checkJs` | bool | `true` | pass `checkJs` so `.js` scripts with `// @ts-check` and `.d.ts` neighbours are validated |

Naming (changed in the 2026-09-30 pass): these were `script.check.onError` and
`script.check.onUnsupported`. A nested config file cannot hold `script.check`
as both a value and an object (`{"script":{"check":"types"}}` vs
`{"script":{"check":{"onError":"warn"}}}`); no declared setting path is both a
leaf and a branch today, and `settings.ApplyFile` flattens nested
objects (`internal/settings/file.go:18-24`). `script.onError` also already
exists as a launcher phase (`registry.go:230`), so a second `onError` under
`script.` invites confusion. Flat camelCase (`script.captureConsole`,
`plumbing.allowTsJsOverlap`) is the house style.

Three properties that make this better than B:

- **`onUnsupported: switch` is the real fix for bun/node validation.** deno is
  already a required-ish dependency (the Nix wrapper ships it; `--typecheck` is
  meaningless without it). Using `deno check` as a *checker* for a script that
  will be *run* by bun is legitimate — it is the same module graph — and turns
  "type checking is only available under Deno" from a limitation into an
  implementation detail. The one caveat to verify: deno's stricter
  extensionless-import rule means a bun-idiomatic script may fail the check for
  a reason that would not have failed the run, so `--sloppy-imports` (or
  reporting that class of diagnostic as a warning) is part of the work.
- **`compile: auto` is narrow enough to be safe.** It fires only in the case
  that actually breaks — node meeting non-erasable syntax — and only after
  `--experimental-transform-types` has failed to be enough. Everywhere else the
  module cache keeps doing its job, so Approach A's cost is not paid by the 95%
  of runs that do not need it.
- **`syntax` as the default is nearly free and catches the real failure.** The
  scanner in `internal/diagnose` already parses a script statically to find tool
  calls; the same parse can report a `enum`/decorator that the selected runtime
  will reject, before anything starts, with a message that names the runtime and
  suggests `--runtime deno`. That is a better error than node's stack trace and
  costs no subprocess.

Also in this issue, cheap and independent:

- pass `--experimental-transform-types` in `Detect` for node (one line, removes
  two of the four node failure modes). Carried by #108 (in flight under #177);
  not repeated here.
- drop the now-default `--experimental-strip-types`, or keep it with a comment
  naming the node version it stopped being needed at (also #108).
- when `Detect` falls back through `auto`, say which runtime was chosen. The
  machine-readable run envelope already carries `runtime`
  (`internal/cli/commands.go:956`); text output and the structured log say
  nothing, and `MCPX_RUNTIME` is visible only to the script.

## Owned decisions (#181 collisions 1 and 11)

### The `script.typecheck` → `script.check` rename (collision 1)

**Owns #181 collision 1:** alias-vs-replace is decided here, once, and #79's
default change lands on top of it as a change to `script.check`'s default,
not beside it. Facts that constrain it, at 05c78b2:

- An unknown key in a config file is reported, not fatal
  (`internal/settings/file.go:32-58`). An unread `MCPX_*` variable is simply
  ignored. `--typecheck` is a hand-written flag (`internal/cli/commands.go:465`),
  not a registry alias.
- The registry has `FlagAliases` and `EnvAliases` (`internal/settings/schema.go:146-154`)
  but no config-path alias, no value mapping, and one `Default` per setting
  (`schema.go:133-137`), so no per-command default either.

**A — replace.** Delete `script.typecheck`, add `script.check`. Least code, and
the worst outcome: `{"script":{"typecheck":"on"}}` becomes an unknown-key
warning and checking silently stops, `MCPX_SCRIPT_TYPECHECK` is silently
ignored, and `--typecheck` either breaks scripts that pass it or stays and
does nothing — #74's bug class (closed, fixed in #75). If #79 flips a default in
the same release, anyone who set the old key is broken twice.

**B — keep both.** Add `script.check` beside `script.typecheck` with a
precedence rule. Nothing breaks, but two settings mean one thing, can disagree
(`typecheck: on`, `check: syntax`), and both appear on every surface the
registry generates, permanently.

**C — recommended: `script.check` is the setting; `script.typecheck` is a
declared alias with a value map.** `off→off`, `on→types`, `strict→strict`, in
all three spellings: the config key, `MCPX_SCRIPT_TYPECHECK`, and `--typecheck`.
A use of the old spelling is reported once, the way unknown keys already are;
giving both at the same layer is the existing same-layer conflict
(`internal/settings/value.go` `Apply`). This needs one registry addition —
`PathAliases` with an optional value map — which is a registry capability, not
a special case, and `daemon.inline` (#79 point 2) is the next setting that will
want it. The new setting is an `ExecOptions` field from the start, closing the
remote-drop above. #79 then changes `script.check`'s default (and only that),
in the same release as the alias, with one note in `docs/configuration.md`.

### `auto` resolution (collision 11)

**Owns #181 collision 11.** The collision as first recorded is partly outdated:
the e2e suite already runs its runtime tests under each runtime explicitly
(`internal/e2e/runtime_test.go:14,46`, `internal/e2e/e2e_test.go:2478`), and CI
installs deno, bun and node (`.github/workflows/mcpx.yml:55-61`), so node is
exercised. What remains:

- `auto` itself. On a nix install the wrapper's `PATH` suffix makes it deno every
  time; in the container it is pinned to bun. The bun and node fall-through
  branches of `Detect` are never taken by a packaged install and are asserted by
  nothing. **This issue owns the test:** `runner.Detect("auto", nil)` with a
  `PATH` holding only a stub `deno`, only `bun`, only `node`, and none — four
  cases, stub executables in a temp dir, no real runtime needed.
- Non-erasable TypeScript under node: #108 (in flight).
- A CI leg with no deno on `PATH` at all goes through #134's matrix, not here.

No real choice for the test; the open question below about "first on PATH" vs
"first that can run this script" is the only design decision in `auto`.

## Open questions

- Should `auto` stay "first on PATH" or become "first on PATH that can run this
  script"? The latter is more useful and less predictable; a script that
  silently ran on a different runtime than yesterday is its own bug class.
- Does `script.check` replace `script.typecheck` or alias it? Answered above
  under "Owned decisions" (recommended: alias with a value map); it is this
  issue's to decide, before #79 changes the default.
- For `.js` + `.d.ts`: emit `mcpx-client.js`/`.d.ts` beside the `.ts` client, or
  require `.js` scripts to import the `.ts` one (fine on deno/bun, not on node)?
- Is `tsc` ever acceptable as a dependency, given `docs/dependencies.md`'s
  standard for adding one? `deno bundle` avoids it for compiling but not for
  emitting `.d.ts`.
- Does a compiled artifact belong in the content-addressed exec workdir
  (`WorkRoot`, one directory per catalogue hash) or in its own cache keyed by
  script hash + runtime? If its own cache, it is a tenant of #187's mechanism
  (#181 collision 12), not a fourth design.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M (S for the node flag fix and the docs; M for the check pipeline; L if
`compile` lands too) · **Impact** high — it is the first question a user asks and
the answer is currently only in source comments.

**Depends on / related**: #79 (typecheck default and measured costs; lands on
this issue's collision-1 decision), #108 (the node flag, in flight), #134 (the
CI leg without deno), #187 (cache mechanism, if `compile` caches), #74 (closed,
fixed in #75 — flags accepted and ignored), #66 (merged: `--typecheck` works),
#40 (closed, fixed in #57 — ExecOptions, where `runtime` crosses the wire), and
siblings #101 (comparison doc), #103 (dependency configuration), #104
(automatic imports), #105 (Python parity), #106 (shebang dispatch), #107 (flake
execution environments).

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

code.title: mcpx testing: integration tests for every feature, across environments
code.body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#97 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #91

## Purpose

The notes' goal: **"a general goal is to ensure all features have one or more integration tests"**, proved through the real product -- **"the mcp servers can be specialized mocks but the app entrypoint or binary is used"** -- and then proved again in every environment mcpx claims to run in.

Where it starts. The binary half of this is already good: `internal/e2e/e2e_test.go:35` `newEnv` builds the real binary once per test binary (`internal/testsupport/build.go`) and drives it against a fake MCP server (`internal/testsupport/fakemcp/main.go`, plus `askmcp` for elicitation), isolated by `MCPX_STATE_DIR`, `MCPX_CACHE_DIR`, `MCPX_CONFIG` and `MCPX_REGISTRY_URL`, with a 60 s `MCPX_AUTOSTART_IDLE_EXIT` and a `stop --all` cleanup since #182. 199 tests did this at d0b7e01; 209 at 05c78b2. So the notes' "for both binary && app entrypoint" is really one path that exists and one that does not: `cmd/mcpx/main.go:56` builds `&cli.App{...}` and dispatches inside `main()`, and there is no in-process entrypoint any test uses.

Three things this tracker had to correct in the notes, because the premises were not true when it was written (the first two are updated for #182):

- **There was no Containerfile when this was written; #182 added one.** `pkgs/mcpx/Containerfile` (with `docs/container.md`): `debian:bookworm-slim`, bun only, git, `ARG CGO_ENABLED=1`, pinned by tag and digest, 413 MB. **No CI job builds it and no test runs in it**, and there is still no `dockerTools` image in the flake. So "all tests should pass for nix flake & container" now has an artifact to point at but nothing that tests it, and "the supported mcp version is the one in the flake/containerfile" now has two version sources that already drift (Renovate #184 bumps the Containerfile's Go image on its own). #134 owns testing it; #137 owns the version pin.
- **"basically everything should work because static binary" is true of what mcpx can be and false of what ships.** mcpx *can* be static: `os/user` and `net` pull libc only under cgo, and #182 verified a `CGO_ENABLED=0` build is fully static and works (`ldd`: "not a dynamic executable"; `--version`, `ls`, `call`, `exec` pass). But the default nix package is built with nixpkgs' cgo default and `postInstall` wraps it to pin `git`, `deno`, `bun-bin` and `nodejs` onto `PATH`, and the Containerfile keeps `CGO_ENABLED=1` deliberately -- so the shipped artifacts are not static, by choice. And even a static `mcpx` cannot run `mcpx exec` without a JavaScript runtime, which (like git) is a dynamically linked distribution binary, so a `FROM scratch` image with `exec` needs those closures inside it. #136 owns the policy (which artifacts are static; the NSS/DNS trade-off). When checking the nix output, `file result/bin/mcpx` inspects the `makeBinaryWrapper` C launcher; look at `result/bin/.mcpx-wrapped`.
- **mcpx does not compile for `GOOS=windows`.** `syscall.SysProcAttr{Setpgid}`, `Setsid` and `syscall.Kill` appear unguarded across `internal/runner`, `internal/mcpclient` and `internal/cli`; only the tty files have a build-tag split, and `package.nix` agrees -- `meta.platforms = lib.platforms.unix`. Windows is a port, not a matrix leg, and #136 files it as one.

And one hazard that is a live bug rather than a design question, still open at 05c78b2: **`newEnv` does `append(os.Environ(), ...)`** (`e2e_test.go:52`), and `socketPath` returns `$MCPX_SOCKET` verbatim before any state-dir logic (`internal/daemon/paths.go:103-105`). A developer with `MCPX_SOCKET` or `MCPX_DAEMON_ENDPOINT` exported -- exactly the developer who has their own daemon running, which is the case the notes call out -- points the whole suite at it. That is #138, and it is the cheapest issue in this tracker.

What this tracker does **not** own: the CI job graph the environment legs become entries in (#95, #135/#139), the seed (#93), and the policy about which of these an agent runs locally (#99).

## Children

- [ ] #132 mcpx testing: inventory every feature against its integration tests, and guard that each has one
- [ ] #133 mcpx testing: an in-process app entrypoint beside the binary suite, and a scriptable mock MCP server
- [ ] #134 mcpx testing: environments -- nix flake, container, local, remote -- as CI matrix entries
- [ ] #136 mcpx testing: extended platforms -- which artifacts ship static; alpine, scratch, distroless, flatpak, Fedora, Windows tiers
- [ ] #137 mcpx testing: a labelled real-software subset, pinned by the flake, run nightly
- [ ] #138 mcpx testing: e2e inherits the caller's environment -- build it from an allowlist so tests never reach the user's daemon

## Proposed order

1. **#138** first, out of dependency order, because it is S-M, it is a correctness hole in every e2e run started from a shell that has `MCPX_*` set, and every environment leg added later inherits the bug if it is not fixed first. An allowlist-built environment is also the mechanism the "user has a real daemon running" subset needs. #182 already did its idle-exit step (and closed #52); the allowlist itself is what remains, and it is now also the last precondition for `t.Parallel` in e2e (#139).
2. **#132** -- inventory what exists against what is claimed, and make the coverage goal enforce itself. "Every feature has a test" is a slogan until something fails when it stops being true; the generalisation of `TestEveryDeclaredRouteAnswersOverTheSocket` (`internal/e2e/v1ops_test.go:287`) is what makes it a fact.
3. **#133** -- the in-process entrypoint, as a second driver running the same test bodies rather than a second copy of the tests. That is what makes "consider binary a superset" an executable claim instead of an assertion.
4. **#134** -- the environments the notes treat as required: nix flake, container, local, remote. A user-facing image now exists (#182); the bulk of the work is a flake-built test image and the legs that run in it. Its cheapest entries -- assertions on the installed nix output, and a CI build of #182's Containerfile -- can land earlier.
5. **#137** -- the real-software subset, opt-in by construction. It must be opt-in rather than opt-out: #65 is the recorded case of a test reaching the real internet and failing only in CI.
6. **#136** -- the wishlist. The notes frame these as "ideally would like if worked", not as requirements, and this issue tiers them accordingly.

## Children -- ease and impact

| # | Title | Kind | Ease | Impact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #132 | inventory features against tests, guard that each has one | design + review | M (review S; ledger and guard M; closing gaps is separate) | **high** |
| #133 | in-process entrypoint + scriptable mock MCP server | design | L (stage 1 M; env threading L; scriptable fake M) | **high** |
| #134 | nix flake, container, local, remote as matrix entries | design | L (devShell S; flake image and `checks.mcpx-e2e` M; remote runner M-L) | **high** |
| #136 | extended platforms; which artifacts ship static (feasibility verified in #182) | design + research | XL overall (static build + tier-2 containers M; Windows port L; flatpak/silverblue M each) | med (tier 2), low-med (tier 3) |
| #137 | labelled real-software subset, pinned, nightly | design | M (tag, helper, reference servers M; packaging S-M) | med-high -- the only proof mcpx works with anything but its own fakes |
| #138 | e2e inherits the caller's environment -- allowlist it | bug + implement | S-M | **high** -- a correctness hole in every affected run |

## Warnings carried by this tracker

- **A leg that skips is a green leg that tested nothing.** `internal/e2e/runtime_test.go` skips when a runtime is absent, so a runner without bun is silently green. This has to be fixed **before** any OS matrix is added, or the matrix is decorative.
- **There is no single "supported mcp version".** `internal/mcpserver` advertises a list of protocol versions and `internal/mcpclient` pins one; `GET /v1/protocol` already reports both directions. The pin is a golden-file diff on an existing route propagated outward into packaging, not a number typed into a Containerfile. #137 has the detail.
- **Every extra environment leg fights #95's time budget directly.** #136's tiering (gating / nightly / aspiration-with-no-CI) exists precisely so the wishlist does not quietly become the critical path.
- **Hidden interpreter dependency:** parts of the e2e suite and `scripts/stress.sh` shell out to `python3`, which `package.nix` does not declare. A minimal container image will find this the hard way.
- **Flatpak is a poor fit and should be argued, not assumed.** It is desktop GUI packaging; mcpx spawns arbitrary host processes and hands out unix sockets, so it would need `--filesystem=host --share=network --talk-name=org.freedesktop.Flatpak`, at which point the sandbox provides nothing the container image does not. Silverblue/Kinoite likewise are an *install* story, not a different runtime -- which is the notes' own "installers make assumptions and require permissions" bullet.

## Related

#91 (parent), #95 (#134/#136's legs are entries in its matrix; #135, #139, #140), #93 (generators aim at the features #132 inventories), #99 (#127 decides which of these an agent runs locally; #129 owns guards generally), #100 (owns #181 collision 11; its no-Deno leg is a #134 matrix row), #178 (assertions on the nix output's man page, completions, version), #158 (release artifacts; the static tarball), #52 (closed, fixed in #182), #88, #65, #35, #76, #79, #78, #47, #48, #49, #102, #106.

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

## Acceptance criteria
- Integration tests cover every mcpx feature named in this issue across the environments it lists, run in CI, and are enumerated in a matrix linked from this issue.
- A feature without integration coverage is either added to the matrix with a test or explicitly excluded with a reason recorded here.

code.title: mcpx: the backlog build-out — every theme, in one order, with the disagreements between them (super tracker)
code.body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#181 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

The whole mcpx backlog in one place: seven category trackers, 111 open issues, what is already done, a proposed
order, and the collisions between themes, each with an owner.

Every open issue in the milestone `mcpx: backlog build-out` descends from this one through native sub-issue links.
The only deliberate exception is #11 (Renovate's dependency dashboard), which the bot owns.

> **Revised 2026-09-30 (issues pass, at `05c78b2`).** Every open issue was re-checked against current `main`. What
> changed here: a **Done** section; #52, the CI cache line and "no Containerfile" moved to it (all #182); the
> static-binary evidence corrected (a `CGO_ENABLED=0` build is fully static -- nothing in mcpx blocks it); every
> collision given an owner, three of them new design issues (#185, #186, #187); two new bugs from the pass under #177
> (#192, #193); the grid and order re-rated from the leaves' own footers; the graph's wrong edges removed (#6 does not
> block #81's bus, #78 does not block #88, #88 does not block #87). Issues other architects were changing while this
> pass ran are marked *in flight*.

---

## Categories

| Category | Tracker | Open issues | Scope in one line |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Testing | **#91** → #93 #95 #97 #99 | 28 | Fuzzing with one seed per run, integration tests per feature, a sharded CI with a time budget, and the policy for what an agent runs. |
| Documentation | **#89** (under #91) → #90 #92 #94 #96 #98 | 26 | The book: a 30-second layer, a manual, a compendium; a site that deploys; reference pages generated from the binary so they cannot drift. |
| Runtimes, languages, dependencies | **#175** | 9 | What runs a script, in what language, with which packages -- runtime selection, the dependency chain, import resolution, one cache mechanism, Python, shebangs, flake refs. |
| The AI layer and search | **#176** | 10 | Where a model comes from, and what would use one -- search, repair, hooks, admin-by-intent, composed tool sets, connectors -- plus the shared matcher and the settings ceiling they need. |
| Extensibility | **#173** | 6 | A plugin is an MCP server; hooks over the event bus; anything as a tool source; embedding mcpx. |
| Surfaces | **#174** | 5 | Reaching the daemon over ssh and the browser, and keeping what you reached -- socket discovery, lifetimes, ssh, a web frontend. |
| A promise and a behaviour that disagree | **#177** | 16 | The bug class where something declared does not do what it says, and the guard-test pattern that closes it. 15 children, most of them found since the build-out began — nine of the fifteen were filed during this pass. |
| Pre-existing, no tracker | -- | 10 | #5 #6 #7 #47 #48 #49 #76 #77 #78 #79 -- each a dependency of something above, placed in the order below. |

**111 open issues in the milestone**, 17 of them trackers (this one included). Verified at the end of the
2026-09-30 pass by walking `repos/dezren39/nix/issues/<n>/parent` for every open issue: **all 110 below this
one reach it, and the walk has exactly two roots — this issue and #11.** No chain is orphaned and none
cycles.

## Children

Six category trackers, and the pre-existing issues that predate the build-out and have no tracker of their own because
each is a dependency of several parts of it.

- [ ] #91 design a comprehensive docs and testing strategy -- the joint root; #89 (the book) hangs under it
- [ ] #173 extensibility -- plugins, hooks, tool sources, embedding
- [ ] #174 surfaces -- ssh, a web frontend, lifetimes, socket discovery
- [ ] #175 runtimes, languages and dependencies
- [ ] #176 the AI layer and search
- [ ] #177 a promise and a behaviour that disagree -- the bug class, and the guard-test pattern
- [x] #5 `paths.config` should govern the rest of the config chain -- phase 3; dead on all three channels today (#159 item 19)
- [ ] #6 event store -- phase 3 for its **gap contract** (S, which #81 and #193 need); the store itself is phase 6
- [ ] #7 launcher placeholders -- fill-in, self-contained
- [ ] #47 port the opencode plugin to opencode v2 -- phase 6
- [ ] #48 a harness-free plugin core -- phase 6, related to #80/#82
- [ ] #49 CI: build every flake package -- phase 1
- [x] #52 the e2e suite leaks daemons -- **closed, fixed in #182**
- [ ] #76 CLI commands for the operations only /v1 and MCP have -- phase 3, **hard-blocks #113**; *in flight*
- [ ] #77 protocol follow-ups -- phase 6, related to #112; *in flight*
- [ ] #78 daemon state and cache correctness -- phase 6; its `MCPX_SOCKET` item moved to #88 (collision 8)
- [ ] #79 faster CLI and exec, typecheck default -- phase 3, **lands on #100's rename decision** (collision 1)

---

## Done

What this backlog asked for that has already landed. Closed issues stay attached to their trackers as checked items.

| Done | By | What it settled |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #52 -- the e2e suite leaked daemons for four hours | **#182** | Cleanup calls `stop --all`, which finds daemons through their info files, not a recomputed socket path; every test env sets `MCPX_AUTOSTART_IDLE_EXIT=60s` (`internal/e2e/e2e_test.go:68-83`). The test was falsified by reverting the fix. **No longer blocks sharding.** |
| #135's one-line cache fix (`cache-dependency-path`) | **#182** | `.github/workflows/mcpx.yml:50`. The key now saves; no warm run has been observed yet -- the first push to `main` after #182 was the one that saved it. The rest of #135 is open. |
| "There is no Containerfile" (#134, #158, #97) | **#182** | `pkgs/mcpx/Containerfile`, `docs/container.md`: pinned by tag and digest, debian-slim, ships bun, 413 MB. Not built or tested by CI yet (#134). |
| Whether mcpx *can* be a static binary (#136) | **#182** | Yes: `CGO_ENABLED=0` gives a fully static, working linux ELF. #136 is now the policy decision about which *shipped* artifacts should be. |
| The settings registry declared settings nothing read | **#171** | `consumed_test.go`'s three guards; 24 settings wired, dead ones removed; `logging` no longer declared; push capabilities gated per connection. It also let `registry.pageSize` through -- collision 15. |
| #74 -- exec flags accepted and ignored | **#75** | Five flags now work for inline snippets, with a guard table that asserts an observable outcome. Local path only -- the remote path is #192. |
| `--typecheck` works (`deno check`) · upstream completion (`/v1/complete` forwards `completion/complete`, `internal/api/ops.go:256`) | **#66** · **#61** | Making the check the default is #79 on #100's decision (collision 1). Anything calling `/v1/complete` local-only is stale. |
| #40 artifacts / ExecOptions · #41 diagnostics, recipes, intent · #44 the plugin without the binary | **#57** · **#58** · **#53** | Closed before the build-out began. The plugin reaches the daemon over the socket and spawns `mcpx` only as its last fallback. |
| #160-#170 duplicate testing issues | this pass | Closed earlier "until reconciled"; their remaining unique content was carried into the survivors (#132-#143), each listed in a comment. |

*In flight at the time of this revision* (other architects, merging now): #76, #77, #102, #108, #116, #172, #178,
#179, #180, #183 and #153; decision records for collisions 2, 3 and 10. When they land, this section gains rows.

---

## Ease vs impact

Ratings are the leaves' own footers, and each category tracker's table agrees with its leaves. Four quadrants.
*Quick wins* pay immediately and cost hours to days. *Big bets* are what the project is for and cost weeks.
*Fill-ins* are cheap and change nothing structural. *Thankless* is expensive work with a narrow beneficiary -- do it
when someone asks by name.

### Quick wins -- do these first

| Issue | Ease | Impact | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **#108** *(in flight)* | S | high | One flag. `--runtime node` restricts the language it claims to enable. |
| **#116** *(in flight)* | S | med-high | `diagnose.CallError` is written, tested, and called by nothing. |
| **#192** | S (B) / M (C) | med-high | A remote exec accepts and drops most exec flags -- including `--env` and inline `--export`, whose wire fields already exist. #74's class on the path #75 did not cover. |
| **#138** | S-M | high | e2e still appends `os.Environ()` (`e2e_test.go:52`), so a developer's `MCPX_*` leaks in. The last precondition for `t.Parallel`. |
| **#129**'s settings-effect guard | M | high | Collision 15: a setting must be able to change behaviour, not merely be read. Before or with #172. |
| **#193** | S / M | med | `/v1/events` replay drops past 256 events with no `gap`, though reconnection is documented as lossless. |
| **#102** *(in flight)* · **#178** *(in flight)* · **#179** *(in flight)* · **#180** *(in flight)* · **#183** *(in flight)* | S each | med / low-med | The rest of #177's small promise/behaviour fixes. |
| **#189** · **#196** · **#188** · **#190** · **#191** | S · S · S · M · S | high · high · med · med · low-med | Found by the merging architects while this pass ran, all under #177: the plugin's `DaemonClient.call` sends field names `/v1/call` does not read (#189); `PoolID` hashes headers in map order (#188); a wrong-case cwd keys a second daemon (#190), and so does any cwd under `$HOME`, which lists the user config twice (#196, PR #197 open); a log line misnames the scope (#191). Likely fixed in those architects' PRs -- check before starting. |
| **#88** | S → M | med | Resolve the socket through the info file; owns `MCPX_SOCKET` precedence (collision 8). #182's `stop --all` already works this way. |
| **#101** | S (B) / M (C) | med | `docs/runtimes.md` -- still does not exist. Its probe suite can run in the existing CI job. |
| **#143** | M | high | First real CI iteration with a recorded baseline (at `05c78b2`: test step 148 s, e2e 108.9 s, nix build 70 s). |
| **#141** | M | med | Formatters and linters in the matrix; the plugin's 21 `bun test` tests have never run in CI. |
| **#117** | S | high | Pick the site generator; the recommendation is already made. Everything in #90 waits on it. |

### Big bets -- the work the project is for

| Issue | Ease | Impact | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **#175** | L-XL | high | #100 M, #103 L, #104 L, #105 XL (slice 1 M), #106 M/L, #107 L, #187 M. "mcpx runs your code", currently one runtime deep. |
| **#176** | L-XL | high | #109 M, #110 L, #111 L, #113 L, #114 L. Where a model comes from, and what uses one. |
| **#173** | L-XL | high | #83 up to XL; #80 and #81 M/L. The plugin contract every future integration hangs off. |
| **#97** | XL | high | Integration tests for every feature across environments. Without it every other bet is unverifiable. |
| **#93** | L | high | One seed per run, a seed store, bug-shape generators -- the notes' "hack job of antithesis/tigerbeetle". |
| **#89** / **#98** | XL | high / med | The book. The compendium is open-ended by design. |
| **#158** | L | high | Release workflow and artifacts. Gates the download link and install commands on the home page. |
| **#177** | M overall | high | Fourteen children, individually S-M; the value is in doing the set and guarding the frame afterwards. |
| **#6** (the store) | M-L | med | The durable event store. Its gap contract (S) is split out and comes first. |

### Fill-ins -- cheap, safe, do them when blocked on something else

| Issue | Ease | Impact | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #119 | S | med | Subdomain + CNAME, after #118 creates the Pages site. |
| #149 | S (gallery M) | med-high | The FAQ, in the notes' own voice. |
| #153 *(in flight)* | M | med | Comparisons and the project's history; COMPARE is writing `docs/compare/` now. |
| #126 | S | low now, med long-term | Research only -- deterministic execution as an aspiration. |
| #131 | S | high | A contributor test page agents load. |
| #150 | M | med | Release markers and `<details>` section history. |
| #7 | M | med | Launcher placeholders. Self-contained. |
| #5 | S-M | med | `paths.config` -- currently dead on config, env and flag alike. |
| #78 | S | low-med | Daemon state and cache correctness; none of its items was touched by #69/#70/#73. |
| #11 | S | low | Renovate's dashboard. Outside the milestone; the bot maintains it. |

### Gating design objects -- small, and three issues each wait on them

Easy to misfile: by ease they look like fill-ins; by consequence they are phase-3 design. Each came out of a
collision nobody owned. Do them **before** their consumers.

| Issue | Ease | Impact | Waited on by | Why it gates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **#186** one near-miss matcher | S | med | #109, #111, #7 | Two implementations already exist and disagree; a third arrives the moment #109 or #111 starts. |
| **#185** `ClampedBy` | M | med (high once a dial ships) | #111, #112, #113 | A daemon-set ceiling a caller may lower but not raise -- a settings capability, not a repair feature. |
| **#187** one cache mechanism | M | med-high | #103, #104, #107, #78 | Cheap now, a migration after the first of the three ships its own cache. The prior art is already in the tree: #69/#70/#73 gave exec content-addressed workdirs, sized for scripts rather than `node_modules` trees or Nix closures. |

### Thankless -- real work, narrow beneficiary. Wait to be asked.

| Issue | Ease | Impact | Why it waits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #84 (C ABI, WASM halves) | L each | med overall, low until a caller names itself | The Go package API half is not thankless; the ABI and WASM halves are. |
| #105 slice 2 (the Python runner) | L | high if wanted | The notes do ask for it ("support python wherever and however typescript is used 1:1"), so it is not unwanted -- but slice 1 (a typed Python client, M) should prove demand before the runner. Slice 1 is a big-bet item, not thankless. |
| #136 (Windows tier) | L | low | Zero `//go:build windows` files. A port, not a matrix leg -- recommendation 3. |
| #136 (flatpak tier) | M | very low | Drop, do not schedule -- recommendation 2. |
| #156 (beyond copy-as-command) | M (XL hosted) | med | #156 recommends a copy-as-command example (S) and an in-browser simulation (M), never a hosted daemon; WASM is not the plan. |
| #152 | L | med | Migrating the existing design docs into the compendium. |
| #82 | L | med-high, **or near zero** | High if plugins land, near zero without them. Strictly after #80. |
| #86 (embedded UI slice) | M-L | med | Serving a directory is S. An embedded frontend is where a second toolchain sneaks in. |

---

## Proposed order

Seven phases. The reasoning is in each header; hard dependencies are in the graph below. *In flight* means another
architect is merging it now -- do not start it, check it.

### Phase 0 -- the one-line wins

**~~#135's cache line~~ (done, #182) · #108 *(in flight)* · #116 *(in flight)* · #192 (B) · #186**

The cache line and #52 are done. What remains here costs hours: #108 and #116 are already being merged; #192's B half
is filling two `execsvc.Options` fields the CLI never sets; #186 unifies two disagreeing matchers before a third is
written.

### Phase 1 -- make the suite trustworthy before making it bigger

**#138 → #143 → #49 → #141**, with **#127 + #131** (the agent test policy) alongside

#52 no longer blocks anything. The remaining isolation hole is #138 -- e2e appends the caller's whole environment --
and it is also the last precondition for `t.Parallel` in #139. Then **#143 records a baseline**, because #139 shards by
measured time and #140 budgets against it. The baseline at `05c78b2` (run 36693030957): setup 22 s, test step 148 s of
which `internal/e2e` is 108.9 s across 209 tests, `nix build` 70 s of which `checkPhase` is 18.5 s.

### Phase 2 -- close the promise/behaviour class while it is small

**#129's settings-effect guard (before or with #172) → #177's children · #128 · the rest of #129**

Most of #177's fourteen children are small and several are *in flight* (#102, #108, #116, #172, #178, #179, #180,
#183). The one ordering constraint that matters: **#129's guard that a setting can change behaviour must land before
or with #172**, which is about to declare 44 more `MCPX_*` variables into a registry whose guard only proves a
setting is *read* (collision 15). #192 and #193 are this pass's additions and are not in flight.

### Phase 3 -- the design objects other issues extend

**#100 · #103 · #187 · #110 (decide) · #83 slice 1 → #83 slice 2 → #80 · #76 *(in flight)* · #6's gap contract · #5 · #185**

Each of these is extended by several other issues, so getting it wrong is expensive and getting it late is worse.

- **#100 before #79** (collision 1): #100 recommends keeping `script.typecheck` as an alias of `script.check` with a
  value map; #79's default flip lands on that decision.
- **#187 before #104 and #107 ship a cache** (collision 12).
- **#110: decide now, build later.** Sampling is deprecated (recommendation 5), so where a model comes from is a
  prerequisite decision for #111-#114; #176 builds it fifth.
- **#83 slice 2 before #80** -- a fourth `mcpserver.Extra` list is how this ends with four half-integrated surfaces.
  (The previous revision put #80 beside slice 1; #173's own order is slice 1 → slice 2 → #80.)
- **#76 hard-blocks #113** -- the intent router's vocabulary is the ops table.
- **#6's gap contract (S) before #81** -- #81 needs gap semantics (collision 13), not the durable store. The bus
  already exists (`internal/events/events.go`). The previous revision said "#6 blocks #81"; only the contract does.
- **#185 before any autonomy dial ships** in #111, #112 or #113 (collision 5).

### Phase 4 -- release and packaging

**#134 → #136 → #178 *(in flight)* → #158**

A Containerfile exists now, but nothing builds or tests it (#134), and Renovate is already bumping it to Go 1.27 while
`go.mod` says 1.26.7 (#184) -- a drift nothing catches. #136 is now a **policy** decision (which shipped artifacts are
static; recommended: add a Linux `mcpx-static` output, keep the default nix package as is -- but open PR #194
flips the default instead, which would settle it as option A). The version is hard-coded
in **four** places (`package.nix:19`, `:61`, `cmd/mcpx/main.go:18`, `Containerfile:40`) and the man page stamps
`time.Now()` (#178). **#158 blocks #155's download link and install commands**; #157 can ship before it with an honest
status column.

### Phase 5 -- the site, then the pages

**#117 → #118 → #119 · #144 → #145 → #146 → #147 #148 #149 · #157 · #120 · #155 → #156**

Put **#144/#145 before the manual pages** so they are generated from the binary rather than hand-copied (#96, and the
lesson of #159). #119 needs the Pages site #118 creates, so it follows rather than runs alongside.

### Phase 6 -- the big bets, in dependency order

- **#175**: #104 → #106 → #105 (slice 1 may start earlier) → #107 → #101 finalised
- **#176**: #109 alongside #111 → the autonomy-dial record + #185 → #114 alongside #115 → build #110 → #112 → #113
- **#173**: #81 slice 1 → #81 slice 2 → #82 → #84's rest
- **#174**: #87 alongside #85 docs and #86 slice 1 → #85 `ssh://` and #86's embedded frontend
- **#93** and **#97** alongside, now that phase 1 made the suite trustworthy; #6's store; #47, #48; #77 *(in flight)*

Every child in #176 has a deterministic lower half that ships without a model and a model-backed upper half that does
not, and in every case the deterministic half carries more value. Do all the lower halves first.

### Phase 7 -- the compendium and the long tail

**#150 · #152 → #151 · #153 *(in flight)* · #154 · #126 · #84's ABI/WASM halves · #105 slice 2**

Open-ended by design. #150 and #152 come first (#98's own order); #151 needs #150 and #158.

## The evidence behind the dependencies asserted here

Checked by hand on `8001f23` when this tracker was written and re-checked on `05c78b2` in the 2026-09-30
issues pass. Each item names the leaf that owns it, where the detail lives.

- **Fixed since (see Done):** the Go cache never restored (#182 added `cache-dependency-path`); #52's
  leaked daemons blocked sharding (#182); there was no Containerfile (#182). **Still true:** CI is one job
  running `go test ./... -count=1`, and `internal/e2e` is 108.9 s of its 148 s test step, so e2e is the
  thing worth sharding; the other half of isolation -- e2e inheriting the caller's environment -- is #138.
- **Corrected: nothing in mcpx blocks a static binary.** The previous revision said `os/user` and `net`
  "pull libc on a default toolchain". They pull libc only **under cgo**; with `CGO_ENABLED=0` Go uses
  pure-Go implementations, and #182 verified a 21 MB, fully static, working linux ELF. The **shipped**
  artifacts are not static *by choice*: `package.nix` sets no `CGO_ENABLED` and wraps the binary with a

## Standing recommendations — where I would pick differently from the notes

The notes are the source of truth for *what* to build. These six are places where I would build it
differently. Every one is quoted verbatim in the leaf that owns it and argued there too; this
section exists so the disagreements are visible from the root rather than buried five issues deep.

### 1. `sudo $(curl <short> | sh)` is not a system-wide install — it is a root code-execution primitive

The notes propose, for the home page:

> - per-user `curl <short> | sh` [copy-button]
>   - ~system-wide `sudo $(curl <short> | sh)` [copy-button]

`$(...)` is command substitution. The shell runs `curl <short> | sh` **first, as the unprivileged
user** — so the installer never sees root and either fails or installs per-user anyway. Then the
shell takes that command's **stdout**, word-splits it, and hands the result to `sudo` as a command
line. If the script prints `Installed mcpx to ~/.local/bin`, `sudo` tries to execute a program
called `Installed`. If anything can influence what the script prints — a mirror, a proxy, a
compromised CDN edge, a stray `set -x` — it controls a root command line directly. This is strictly
worse than the thing it is trying to be.

**Use `curl -fsSL <short> | sudo sh`.** Better still, do what rustup and Deno do: one unprivileged
`curl | sh`, and let the script ask for elevation only for the step that needs it, so the user can
read the prompt and see what is being elevated. Owned by #155 (copy buttons) and #157 (install
page); the script itself is #158.

### 2. Flatpak is a poor fit and should be dropped from the wishlist, not merely deprioritised

The notes list it twice:

> - bash/nix/agent-prompt
>   - (pwsh/rpm/flatpack/pkg/docker/justThePlugin)

> - alpine-slim/FROM scratch/distroless/flatpak

Flatpak packages sandboxed desktop applications; host access is mediated by portals. mcpx is a CLI
plus a background daemon that must (a) bind a unix socket at a host path that *other* processes —
opencode, agents, `mcpx` itself — open by name, (b) spawn `deno`/`bun`/`node` subprocesses, (c) read
the user's whole config chain, and (d) execute arbitrary user scripts against arbitrary paths.
Supporting that under Flatpak means `--filesystem=host --share=network --device=all --talk-name=*`,
at which point the sandbox is off and what remains is a tarball with extra indirection and a worse
`$PATH`. Flathub is also not a distribution channel for CLI-only software.

**The channels that actually fit** are a tarball plus an install script, Nix (already works),
Homebrew, and an OCI image. Owned by #136 and #158. I would put the saved effort into the OCI
image, which the notes also ask for. A first `Containerfile` landed in #182 (bun, debian-slim,
413 MB); what it still lacks is a CI job, tests, and a release channel (#134, #158).

### 3. Windows is a port, not a matrix leg

> - windows-11

There are **zero** `//go:build windows` files and zero `_windows.go` files in the tree. The daemon
binds unix sockets (`internal/daemon/server.go`, `internal/cli/client.go`,
`internal/daemon/routes_resolve.go`), resolves paths through an XDG chain, detaches itself to
outlive its parent with `--idle-exit`, and dispatches shebangs. Windows has AF_UNIX, but the
detachment model, the service model, the path chain, signal handling and shebang execution each need
a deliberate implementation. That is a port with a design issue in front of it; a `windows-latest`
line in `runs-on` would fail on the first test and tell you nothing you do not already know.

**Tier it as "port, unscheduled".** If anyone wants it, the first deliverable is a design issue
naming the five boundaries and choosing named pipes vs AF_UNIX. Owned by #136.

### 4. Alphabetical sharding is the wrong partition once timings exist — but the timings come first

The notes anticipate this themselves, which makes it a refinement rather than a contradiction:

> at some point start splitting logical units by like, e.g. maybe a-f/g-s/t-z, balance number of letters by time.

Letter ranges are an arbitrary partition with no relationship to runtime, and the only way to
rebalance one is to move a boundary — which moves many tests at once and usually overshoots.
`go test -json` emits an `Elapsed` per test for free. With that, greedy bin-packing (LPT: sort
descending, assign each test to the currently-shortest shard) is the standard makespan
approximation and is provably within 4/3 − 1/(3m) of optimal, versus no bound at all for letters.

**Measure first, shard second, and never shard alphabetically once you have numbers.** The notes'
own warning about the pathological case is exactly right and is the one thing LPT cannot fix:

> consider if theres lengthy tests which are '1' test but re-exec N times 'in parallel': they will only run 1-3 at a time and so 30 cases _could_ take up to 10 tests worth of time even in parallel and may need to be examined.

A test larger than the target shard size is indivisible to *any* scheduler. That one has to be split
at the source. Owned by #139, with #143 producing the measurements.

### 5. Sampling is deprecated, which inverts what `docs/consumer.md` recommends

MCP revision **2026-07-28** deprecates Sampling, Roots and Logging under **SEP-2577**. The spec names
the migration for sampling explicitly: *integrate directly with LLM provider APIs*. Deprecation is
annotation-only with a twelve-month floor, so nothing breaks before 2027-07-28 — but "new
implementations SHOULD NOT adopt it" is the spec's own wording.

mcpx already speaks 2026-07-28 and already implements the MRTR `inputRequired` round trip that
replaced the held-open stream. But `docs/consumer.md:156-170` still frames sampling as *the* path for
`prompt.sample`, and mcpx declares `roots` to every upstream server (`docs/protocol.md:271`; code at
`internal/mcpclient/modern.go:52`) — deprecated by the same SEP. It also declares `sampling` whenever an
elicitation handler is installed (`modern.go:54-56`), which the daemon always installs, so in practice
every upstream server is told it may sample.

**A configured provider is no longer the ambitious option; it is the spec's own suggested
migration.** That inverts the framing in `docs/consumer.md` and makes #110 a prerequisite rather than
an enhancement -- in the sense of *decide now, build later*: #176 builds it fifth. The two consequences
this section said nobody owned now have one: #110 carries the `roots` and `sampling` declarations and the
`docs/consumer.md` sentence that must change with its decision.

### 6. Prefer settings over endpoints — restated, because it is the rule most easily lost at scale

This held. The leaves propose settings and conventions where the notes proposed endpoints: #87
replaces a renew-endpoint-per-resource with touch-on-read; #112 replaces four prompt endpoints with
one declared hook list; #86 adds `http.ui` settings rather than a second build system. The place it
is most at risk now is **#113**, where "administration by intent" could easily become a dozen
`/v1/admin/*` routes. It should not: the ops table already generates routes, MCP tools and OpenAPI
from one declaration, so the correct move is to *declare more operations*, not to hand-write more
endpoints — and `internal/api/parity_test.go` already enforces that.
