code.title: mcpx docs: level 1 -- the 30-second layer: home, overview, quick start, install (tracker)
code.body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#92 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #89

## Purpose

Level 1: the thirty-second look. Home page, overview, quick start, install -- simple enough that a reader skimming
while doing three other things learns what mcpx is and how to get it before closing the tab.

## Original notes

> - documentation
>   - make a book using whatever is the most common and simple modern choice
>     - 3 main things, not book sections jsut like levels of detail-
>       - the 30 seconds look at home page click the overview page, click the quick start page, ctrl+w should be simple enough that even this person skimming while doing 3 different things will accidentally learn

(Lines 9-48 are quoted in the children.)

## Children

- [ ] #158 mcpx: release.yaml, release artifacts and the install channels the docs will promise
- [ ] #157 mcpx docs: overview, quick start, install page and 'now what'
- [ ] #155 mcpx docs: the home page -- pitch, intro, video, example, install copy buttons, rotating agent prompt
- [ ] #156 mcpx docs: a runnable, editable example on the home page (WASM vs hosted daemon vs local)

## Proposed order

1. #158 is the critical path for the whole docs tree: there is no tag, no release, no install script and no
   published image today (a `pkgs/mcpx/Containerfile` exists since #182 and builds locally, but nothing builds or
   pushes it), and the version is hard-coded in four places (`package.nix:19`, `:61`, `cmd/mcpx/main.go:18`,
   `Containerfile:40`). Without it the home page has no download link and no `curl | sh`, and the compendium has
   no version to stamp. Settle "monorepo vs its own repo" first (it decides
   tag names, `go install`, and the short URL).
2. #157 overview / quick start / install, with an honest status column per channel. It can be written before
   #158 finishes (nix works today; the rest are "not started" or "partly"), and its status column is then
   regenerated from what each release publishes.
3. #155 the home page, once #117 has chosen the generator and #158 exists.
4. #156 last, staged: copy-as-`mcpx exec` plus an in-browser run against a fake daemon now; local-daemon mode later;
   never a hosted public daemon.

## Ease and impact

| # | Title | Kind | Ease | Impact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #158 | release.yaml, artifacts, install channels | design, enhancement | L (parts S-XL) | high |
| #157 | overview, quick start, install, now what | docs | M | high |
| #155 | home page | design | M | high |
| #156 | runnable editable example | research, design | S / M (XL if hosted) | med |

## Warnings

- The system-wide form in the notes, `sudo $(curl <short> | sh)`, runs the installer unprivileged and executes its
  *output* as root. #155 replaces it with `curl -fsSL <short> | sh -s -- --system`, where the script escalates only to
  copy the binary, with `curl -fsSL <short> | sudo sh` as the plain fallback; #157's install page shows the same two
  forms and #158 designs `--system`.
- `mcpx init` currently writes a config whose `mode` key is ignored (#159); the quick start must not use it until fixed.
- Windows does not compile today (unguarded `Setpgid`/`Setsid`/`syscall.Kill`), so pwsh/`install.ps1` is blocked on a
  port (#158); platform tests belong to #136.
- A bare release binary has no JavaScript runtime; the nix wrapper supplies deno, bun and node, and the container
  image ships bun only. Install docs must say so.
- "justThePlugin" is real because the plugin needs no mcpx binary on its machine (#53): it finds a daemon over the
  socket or `endpoint`, and spawns `mcpx --json status` only as a last-resort fallback. It still needs a daemon
  running somewhere, which the install page must say.

## Related

#117, #120 (bot home page carries the install prompt), #44 (closed, fixed in #53: plugin without the binary =
"justThePlugin"), #48, #79 (typecheck default affects quick start), #86 (daemon-served web UI), #102, #134 (container
image), #136 (platform coverage, static-build policy).

## Ease · Impact · Related

See the table above; related issues listed above.

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

code.title: mcpx: design a comprehensive docs and testing strategy
code.body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#91 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #181

## Summary

One strategy for how mcpx is **tested** and **documented**, decided once, so that the test suite, the CI that runs it, the policies agents follow, and the book that explains mcpx all pull the same way. This is a joint design issue: it sits at the top of both the testing tree (sub-trackers below) and the documentation tree (its top tracker is #89).

The testing half has one stated priority from the notes -- **CI as short as possible** -- and one stated focus -- **strong tests at each step of the lifecycle**. Everything below serves those two.

## Original notes

> make an issue to design a comprehensive docs/testing strategy:

> - testing

>   - importantly, as we add more testing agents should not run every single test basically ever. below documents a rough idea of a ci job design/policy, the main priority is being short as possible.

>   - a general goal is to ensure all features have one or more integration tests

(Every other `- testing` bullet is quoted verbatim in the leaf issue that owns it; see the sub-trackers. The `- documentation` bullets are owned by the documentation tracker.)

## Current state (written at d0b7e01; re-checked at 05c78b2, after #171 and #182)

| Fact | Where |
| --- | --- |
| 735 `func Test*` across 64 files; 209 of them in `internal/e2e` (719 / 61 / 199 at d0b7e01) | `rg -c '^func Test' --glob '*_test.go'` |
| **No** `Fuzz*`, `Benchmark*`, property tests, `math/rand`, or `t.Parallel()` anywhere | same `rg` |
| e2e drives the real binary (`testsupport.MCPXBinary`, built once per test binary) against a fake MCP server (`internal/testsupport/fakemcp`), isolated by `MCPX_STATE_DIR`/`MCPX_CACHE_DIR`/`MCPX_CONFIG`/`MCPX_REGISTRY_URL`/`MCPX_AUTOSTART_IDLE_EXIT` | `internal/e2e/e2e_test.go:35-92`, `internal/testsupport/build.go` |
| One CI job, `.github/workflows/mcpx.yml`: ~22 s setup, **148 s** `go test ./... -count=1`, **70 s** `nix build` (at d0b7e01: ~32 s, 135 s, 60 s) | run 36693030957 (05c78b2); run 36673523537 (d0b7e01) |
| Per-package: `internal/e2e` **108.9 s**, `internal/tui` 8.6 s, every other package < 2 s (e2e was 100.7 s at d0b7e01) | same runs, `--log` |
| `nix build` re-runs 18 unit packages in `checkPhase`, so unit tests run twice per CI run | `pkgs/mcpx/package.nix:72-82` |
| No formatter or linter runs on mcpx in CI; `plugin/opencode/mcpx/daemon.test.ts` is never run by CI | `.github/workflows/` has `mcpx.yml`, `opencode.yml` only |
| About 25 guard tests already exist as a pattern (listed in #129), among them `TestEveryExecFlagChangesSomething` (`e2e_test.go:2877`; covers 4 of 23 exec flags), `TestEveryDeclaredRouteAnswersOverTheSocket` (`v1ops_test.go:287`; asserts only "not 404/5xx") and `TestNoPackageRedeclaresADefault` (`defaults/guard_test.go:92`). The "declared but never read" audit and guard landed in #171 (`internal/settings/consumed_test.go`). Its inverse is #172 (in flight). The #171 guard proves a setting is *read*, not that reading it matters: `registry.pageSize` passed it (#179). #129 owns the stronger guard (#181 collision 15) | #129, #171, #172, #179 |
| ~~The e2e suite leaks daemons (#52), so "just run everything" is actively harmful on a dev machine today.~~ **Fixed in #182:** cleanup runs `stop --all` through the `daemon-<key>.json` info files, and `newEnv` sets `MCPX_AUTOSTART_IDLE_EXIT=60s` (`e2e_test.go:68,79,92`). `TestEnvCleanupStopsTheDaemonItStarted` (`:2630`) guards it and was falsified by reverting the fix. "Just run everything" is now a cost problem (~110 s of serial e2e), not a leak. `testsupport` still leaves its temp dirs behind (`build.go:27,57`) | #182, #127, #129 |
| The e2e harness passes the caller's whole environment (`os.Environ()`, `e2e_test.go:52`) to the binary, and the opencode plugin exports `MCPX_DAEMON_ENDPOINT` into every shell (`plugin/opencode/mcpx-session.ts:701`), so e2e run from opencode can reach the user's real daemon and real `HOME`/XDG config (from reading the code; unchanged by #182) | #138 |
| ~~The Go cache in CI has never restored (`cache-dependency-path` isn't set), which costs about 31 s of compiling per run~~ **Fixed in #182:** `cache-dependency-path: pkgs/mcpx/go.sum` (`mcpx.yml:50`). The rest of #135's caching design (nix store cache, the `checkPhase` double run, sparse checkout) is still open | #135, #143 |
| A static binary is **not** blocked by the code. With `CGO_ENABLED=0` Go uses its pure-Go `os/user` and `net`, and the result is a fully static, working linux binary (verified in #182: a 21 MB linux/arm64 "statically linked" ELF; `--build-arg CGO_ENABLED=0` on the Containerfile runs `--version`, `ls`, `call` and `exec`). The *shipped* artifacts are not static **by choice**: the nix package uses the nixpkgs cgo default and wraps a PATH suffix (`package.nix:96`), and the Containerfile leaves `ARG CGO_ENABLED=1` (`Containerfile:39`). What is open is policy, and only on Linux: pure-Go `os/user` reads `/etc/passwd`, not NSS/LDAP, and the pure-Go resolver bypasses NSS modules. On macOS `CGO_ENABLED=0` changes nothing (since Go 1.20 `net` and `os/user` there do not use cgo in either mode). `exec` also needs a JS runtime anyway. mcpx does not compile for Windows (`Setpgid`/`Setsid`/`syscall.Kill` with no build tags, e.g. `internal/runner/runner.go:413,428`, `internal/mcpclient/stdio.go:69,202`, `internal/cli/client.go:312`) | #136, #134 |
| A Containerfile exists (#182): `pkgs/mcpx/Containerfile` (3 stages pinned by tag and digest, `debian:bookworm-slim` runtime, ships bun with `MCPX_SCRIPT_RUNTIME=bun`, 413 MB), `.dockerignore`, `docs/container.md`. There is no CI job and there are no container tests | #134, #136 |

History that motivates the strategy -- each of these was found by accident, not by design:

- a flaky test surfaced only on the lead's **third** full-suite run (matches PR #46, "One run in three panicked"); the race fixed in PR #61 shows up about 1 run in 5, and only under `-race`, which CI doesn't use;
- a registry test reached the internet and failed only in CI (#65);
- two tests passed on macOS and failed on Linux (#35);
- flags accepted and silently ignored (#74, fixed in #75, now guarded by `TestEveryExecFlagChangesSomething`, whose own first assertion passed either way until the table's without-flag half caught it);
- e2e daemons leaking for four hours (#52, fixed in #182);
- a brand-new guard (#171's `consumed_test.go`) passing a setting that no ordinary caller can make matter (`registry.pageSize`, #179): proof that a guard has to be falsified too (#181 collision 15, owned by #129).

## Strategy (the layers, and who owns each)

| Layer | What it proves | Tree |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit | a package does what it says | policies |
| Property / fuzz, **one seed per run** | a function holds for inputs nobody thought of; every escaped bug becomes a generator for its shape | fuzz & seeds |
| Guard (meta) tests | a whole *class* of bug cannot recur (every flag, every route, every default, every declared field) | policies |
| Integration (binary and app entrypoint, mock MCP servers) | every feature works end to end | integration & environments |
| Real-software subset | the pinned real MCP servers still work | integration & environments |
| Environment matrix | nix, container, local, remote, other OSes | integration & environments |
| CI | all of the above, sharded to a time budget, plus formatters and linters | CI |
| Docs-as-tests | code blocks and generated references in the book are executed/diffed in CI, so docs cannot drift | joint (decided here, built by docs + CI trees) |

## Approaches

### A -- keep bolting on (least recommended)
Keep the single `mcpx.yml` job, add fuzz tests and docs ad hoc as features land. Cheapest today. Risks: CI time grows linearly with every e2e test (already ~110 s serial at 05c78b2), randomness enters without a seed discipline so failures are unreproducible, docs examples drift from the binary, and each accidental discovery above stays accidental. Every future bug costs a human noticing it.

### B -- testing first, docs later
Build the testing trees (seeds, CI sharding, integration matrix, policies) now and write the book afterwards against a stable suite. Sound, and the order most projects take. The cost is that the book's examples become a second, untested copy of behaviour, and the two efforts pick incompatible conventions (where examples live, which binary builds them, what "supported environment" means).

### C -- one lifecycle strategy, docs as a test surface (recommended)
Make the decisions that both halves depend on here, once, then let the trees proceed in parallel:
1. **Seed discipline first** (fuzz tree): every source of randomness in any test derives from one run seed. This must land before anyone adds a random test, or the first flaky fuzz failure is unreproducible.
2. **CI skeleton second** (CI tree): a test workflow with an init job (which also mints the seed), a matrix, and a budget job. Formatters/linters join the matrix. Existing `mcpx.yml` keeps only the vendorHash repair and nix build.
3. **Policies in parallel** (policies tree): what agents run locally, one test per bug, guard tests per bug class, flake handling.
4. **Integration coverage and environments** (integration tree), which lean on 1 and 2.
5. **Docs as a test surface** (joint): every runnable code block in the book is extracted and run by CI against the built binary, and generated references (`mcpx man`, OpenAPI from `mcpx api`, the settings table) are regenerated and diffed. The docs tree owns the book; the CI tree owns the job that runs its examples.

Recommended because it makes the one irreversible choice (how random inputs are generated) before any data exists, and because docs that execute are the cheapest integration tests mcpx will ever get.

## Tree

| Tracker | Leaves | First step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #93 fuzzing and property tests with one seed per run | #121 #123 #124 #125 #122 #126 | #121 seed format and derivation |
| #95 fast, sharded CI with a time budget, linters and auto-format | #135 #143 #140 #139 #141 #142 | #143 first iteration (3 e2e shards, baseline; its Go-cache line already landed in #182) |
| #97 integration tests for every feature, across environments | #138 (bug) #132 #133 #134 #137 #136 | #138 build the e2e environment from an allowlist |
| #99 policies for agents | #127 #131 #128 #129 #130 | #127 + #131 which tests an agent runs, and the contributor page |
| #89 documentation: the book -- overview, manual and compendium (XL / high) | #90 #92 #94 #96 #98 | #117 choose the generator; #158 is the critical path for the install story |

- [ ] #93 mcpx testing: fuzzing and property tests with one seed per run
- [ ] #95 mcpx testing: a fast, sharded CI with a time budget, linters and auto-format
- [ ] #97 mcpx testing: integration tests for every feature, across environments
- [ ] #99 mcpx testing: policies for agents -- what to run, a test per bug, guards per bug class
- [ ] #89 mcpx docs: the book -- overview, manual and compendium (tracker)

### Proposed order across trees
0. **Done (#182, 05c78b2):** #52's leak (info-file `stop --all` cleanup, a 60 s idle exit in `newEnv`, a leak test falsified by reverting the fix); the CI Go-cache line (`mcpx.yml:50`); a Containerfile (`pkgs/mcpx/Containerfile`, no CI job yet). Before that, #171 landed the "declared but never read" settings guard.
1. **Now, cheap, no dependencies:** #138 (a correctness hole), #127 + #131 (stop agents running the full suite), #143 (roughly halves CI wall time; its cache line is already in), and **#129's settings effect guard** (#181 collision 15), which must land before or with #172 (in flight) rather than wait for step 4.
2. **The one irreversible decision:** #121 seed format, then #123 engine and #124 generator versioning. No randomised test lands before #121.
3. **CI shape:** #135, #140, #139, #141, #142.
4. **Policies that need the seed and CI:** #128, the rest of #129, #130.
5. **Integration and environments:** #132, #133, #134, #137, then #136.
6. **Research, any time:** #126 and #122.

> Reconciled: two issue-writing sessions ran against this tree at once. The later pass duplicated the #97 and #95 branches. Its duplicates are closed, and their surviving issues are the leaves listed above: #132-#138 under #97, and #135 and #139-#143 under #95. The two genuinely new findings were moved across as comments on #134 and #141, and in the 2026-09-30 issues pass every remaining unique fact, argument and open question from #160-#170 was carried into its survivor's body (each closed duplicate has a comment listing what moved where). The 23 leaves listed above are the tree.

### Ease / impact
| Tracker | Ease | Impact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #93 | L | high |
| #95 | L | high |
| #97 | XL | high |
| #99 | M | high |

## Open questions

- Where does the contributor/agent test policy live? `pkgs/mcpx/AGENTS.md` today is **user-facing** (how an agent *uses* mcpx; 109 lines, no mention of tests), and anything added there is loaded into every consuming agent's context. A separate `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `docs/testing.md` referenced from a short AGENTS.md line is likely better -- decided in the policies tree (#131 recommends `docs/testing.md` plus a short nested `pkgs/mcpx/internal/AGENTS.md`, which opencode attaches only when an agent reads mcpx source).
- Should `mcpx.yml` be renamed/split into `test.yaml` + `build.yaml`, or keep its name (branch protection rules and Renovate references point at job names)?
- Is the docs-as-tests job part of the main test matrix (blocks merges) or a separate workflow (warns only) at first?
- #49 (CI for every flake package) overlaps the CI tree: one workflow design or two?

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** XL (as a tree; this issue itself is S once the children are settled) · **Impact** high
**Related**: #181 (parent), #49, #52 (closed, fixed in #182), #78, #79, #47, #48, #35, #65, #74, #75; #171 (merged: the "declared but never read" settings audit and guard), #172 (its inverse, in flight), #179 (the setting #171's guard passed; #181 collision 15, owned by #129); #89 (documentation top tracker).

code.title: mcpx: the AI layer and search -- where a model comes from, and everything that would use one (tracker)
code.body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#176 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #181

## Purpose

Everything in mcpx that would use a model, plus the search that should not.
Nine issues: better tool search, a provider layer mcpx owns, a graded
check/refuse/repair ladder, lifecycle hooks on exec, administration by intent,
composed tool views and generated tool sets, and the servers-and-feedback loop —
plus two small design issues split out because three of the others were each
about to build the same thing: one near-miss matcher (#186) and one settings
ceiling (#185).
The finding that shapes the whole tracker is that **every one of these has a
deterministic lower half that ships without a model and a model-backed upper
half that does not** — and in every case the deterministic half is the larger
share of the value. Tags and word-splitting beat embeddings on a catalogue of a
few hundred short identifiers; a schema-change diagnostic beats a model
rewording it; `toolViews.from` answers the tailscale request outright; `/v1/stats`
already measures the thing "this server is slow, host it locally" is about. So
the order is: build every deterministic half first, then #110, then the model
halves. #110 is not first despite being the dependency, because nothing above it
is blocked on it until the deterministic work is done. Its *decision* is another
matter: choosing Approach C (a thin `Provider` interface) and correcting
`docs/consumer.md`'s "should not be built" sentence is cheap and can be taken
early, which is why #181 places #110 in its design phase.

## Children

- [ ] #186 mcpx: one definition of 'close' -- a shared near-miss matcher for search, diagnostics and launcher placeholders — first: S and deterministic; #109's typo tolerance and #111's rung 1 both call it, and the two matchers already shipped disagree on transpositions.
- [ ] #109 mcpx: better tool search — tags, word-splitting, typo tolerance, synonyms, and what 'natural language' would actually cost — second, beside #111: entirely deterministic, `--explain` and tags are S, typo tolerance calls #186.
- [ ] #111 mcpx: checking, refusing and repairing a request — a graded ladder from deterministic diagnostics to rewrite-and-run — second, beside #109: `call` frames, the frame-order rule and rung 1 are S and need no model; rung 0 is #116 (in flight, not a child); it carries the one autonomy-dial vocabulary #112 and #113 adopt.
- [ ] #185 mcpx settings: a ceiling the daemon sets and a caller may lower but not raise (ClampedBy) — third, with the dial decision: must be designed before any dial ships in #111, #112 or #113.
- [ ] #114 mcpx: tool views and composed tool sets — rename/pin/hide, cross-server namespaces, script-backed tools, and generators that emit declarations — fourth: `toolViews.from`/`pin`/`hide` is S–M and unblocks the concrete tailscale request; script-backed tools make recipes first-class with no model at all, on #83's tool-source rules.
- [ ] #115 mcpx: Dropbox/Drive/Outlook/Tailscale, and a feedback loop built from evidence mcpx already collects — fourth, beside #114: richer registry metadata and the four adapter declarations are S (its registry-dedup item is struck — mcpx never had duplicates, #179), and the doctor recommendation is built purely from `/v1/stats` data that already flows.
- [ ] #110 mcpx: where the model comes from — a provider layer mcpx owns, model profiles, and life after MCP Sampling's deprecation — fifth to build (decide early): the gate every model-backed rung above waits on, and the answer to Sampling being deprecated in MCP 2026-07-28.
- [ ] #112 mcpx: lifecycle hooks on exec — prePrompt/postPrompt/onError as one declared list, script or prompt, with a declared effect — sixth: much of its deterministic half already ships as `script.*` launcher phases; per-call hooks follow the hook vocabulary (#81's decision record) and #111's frame rule; prompt hooks need #110.
- [ ] #113 mcpx: administration by intent — finish the operation surface, then route a sentence to a declared operation — last: hard-blocked on #76 (in flight); the router's entire vocabulary is the ops table, and its model is #110's.

## #181 collisions that touch this tracker

| Row | Collision | Owner | Here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | four hook vocabularies | #81 (#173), via a decision record SURFACES is writing under `pkgs/mcpx/docs/decisions/` (in flight) | #112 adopts it; its phase names are input |
| 3 | three autonomy dials | **#111**, via a decision record SURFACES is writing under `pkgs/mcpx/docs/decisions/` (in flight) | #112's `effect` and #113's `prompt.mode: plan` adopt it |
| 4 | namespacing and collision rules | #83 (#173) | #114's views, virtual namespaces and script-backed tools build on it |
| 5 | `ClampedBy` | **#185** | #111, #112, #113 consume it |
| 6 | the near-miss matcher | **#186** | #109 and #111 call it |
| 7 | the exec frame-order rule | **#111** | #112 adds its `hook` frame under it |

## Proposed order

**Phase 1 — the free wins, in parallel.** #186 first: one normalisation,
distance and threshold, replacing the two that exist
(`internal/diagnose/diagnose.go:417-455`, `internal/launcher/template.go:341-381`,
which disagree on transpositions). Then #109's `--explain` → tags →
normalisation/stemming → typo tolerance, and #111's first items: a `call` frame
type in the exec stream under the frame-order rule #111 owns (`docs/exec.md:137`),
and rung 1 near-miss detection. Note rung 1 needs two signals, not one: #186's
closeness for typos, and argument-shape fit for the note's own example —
`search`→`query` is edit distance 5, so no typo threshold finds it. Rung 0,
wiring `diagnose.CallError`, is #116 in the cross-cutting tracker (#177), in
flight with SURFACES; at 05c78b2 it still has no caller outside tests
(`internal/diagnose/diagnose.go:483`). When it lands, the structured diagnostic
it attaches is the shape #111's rungs read.

**Phase 2 — the vocabulary, before any dial is implemented.** #111's
`repair.level` (`off | explain | confirm | propose | retry | rewrite`) is the
same dial as #112's hook `effect` (`advise | transform | script | retry`) and
#113's `prompt.mode: plan`. Three children independently invented a
policy-with-named-stops. It is decided once, in the autonomy-dial decision
record SURFACES is writing under `pkgs/mcpx/docs/decisions/`, and carried by
#111; #112 and #113 adopt it. The floor/ceiling clamping (the daemon sets the
maximum autonomy, a caller may lower it and never raise it) is #185 — a
settings-registry feature, not an auth feature. Both precede #111's rungs 2–6,
#112's effects and #113's plan mode. The hook vocabulary (#81's decision
record) likewise precedes #112's per-call hooks.

**Phase 3 — #114 and #115, in parallel, both deterministic.** #114's view layer
(`from`, `pin`, `hide`) is the one-field change that answers the tailscale
request; script-backed tools are the highest-value missing piece and need no
model. Both sit on #83's tool-source interface, which owns namespaces and
collision rules — script-backed tools are #83's first ship step, recipes as
tools. #115's richer search metadata and the four example declarations are S
(its registry-dedup item is struck: mcpx pins `version=latest`,
`internal/registry/registry.go:158`, and never sees duplicates — #179), and
#115 concludes that an adapter spec over the local `tailscale` CLI is a better
answer than any third-party server — which makes #115 a consumer of #114's
generators and a proof of them. Both also want #109's tags (#115's miss log and
#109's failed-search record are the same record).

**Phase 4 — #110.** By now the deterministic halves are shipped and it is clear
exactly which five jobs want a model: query expansion (#109 rung 7), explain and
propose (#111 rungs 2–6), prompt hooks (#112), operation routing (#113), and
spec generation (#114). That is five one-shot completions, which is the evidence
for #110's Approach C (a thin `Provider` interface mcpx owns) over its Approach
B (a Go agent framework) — none of the five is an agent loop.

**Phase 5 — #112's prompt half, then #113's router.** #112 is the smaller of the
two and its `pre`/`post`/`onError` hooks exercise the provider layer at low
blast radius. #113 comes last because its Approach B (session operations,
force-detach, resume, `mcpx install`) depends on #76 and on settling what a
session even is (#6, #78), and its router cannot be better than the operation
surface it routes to.

**Explicitly deferred, from #113 itself:** arbitrary provisioning ("install any
language/tool/framework/library, clone whatever repo" by prompt) is the only
genuinely agentic operation in the theme and #113 defers it pending a
confinement answer. The declared-dependency and managed-provisioning rungs
below it belong with the runtimes-and-dependencies tracker (#103, #104), not
here.

## Ease / impact

| Issue | Ease | Impact | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #186 | S | med | one definition of "close" for search, diagnostics and the launcher; fixing a false positive once fixes it everywhere |
| #109 | M (S for tags + typos alone; M for the full lexical ladder; L if the semantic rung is included) | high | "search is the entry point to zero-context discovery, and a miss there costs an agent a full catalogue load" |
| #111 | L overall; the first two items (wire `diagnose.CallError` — now #116's, in flight — and add `call` frames) are **S** and should ship independently of everything else here | high | "the difference between 'it failed' and 'here is what worked, here is exactly what was wrong, here is the one-line fix'" |
| #185 | M | med (high once #111, #112 or #113 implements a dial) | one clamp in the resolver instead of one per dial |
| #114 | L overall; the tailscale-unblocking `toolViews.from`/`pin`/`hide` is **S–M**, script-backed tools **M**, virtual cross-server namespaces **M–L**, spec generation **L** | high | "turns mcpx from a router into a place where a personal tool surface is composed, and script-backed tools alone make recipes first-class" |
| #115 | M (S for richer metadata + the four example declarations — registry dedup struck, see #179; M for `mcpx registry add` end-to-end and the doctor recommendation; M for the feedback/miss store) | medium-high | "the doctor recommendation and the miss log are the parts that keep paying; the four servers are a day's config each once adapters are the route" |
| #110 | L (M for the `Provider` interface + one provider + settings; L including profiles, plugin backend and local sampling answers; XL if mcpx-as-an-OpenAI-proxy is in scope — it should not be, split it) | high | "every other issue in this theme depends on where the model comes from" |
| #112 | M (S for the deterministic half — much of it already ships as `script.*` launcher phases, so what remains is exposing them per call with a typed context; M with prompt hooks and effects; L if stop/resume gets its own machinery rather than reusing tasks) | medium-high | "what makes one script file portable across environments without the script knowing where it runs, which is the same goal #40 had for artifacts" |
| #113 | L overall; the session/detach operations are **M**, the prompt-routing layer is **M** given `/v1/intent` exists, `mcpx install` is **M**, and provisioning is **L–XL** and should be split out | medium-high | "mostly it makes an existing surface reachable by people who do not have the ops table memorised, which is the actual complaint" |

## Warnings

- **MCP Sampling is deprecated, and mcpx's own documentation recommends the
  opposite of the spec's migration.** Revision `2026-07-28` deprecates Roots,
  Sampling and Logging (SEP-2577) and names the migration explicitly:
  *integrate directly with LLM provider APIs instead of Sampling*.
  `pkgs/mcpx/docs/consumer.md:195-196` says a configured provider with an API
  key "was not built and should not be. It is the one that makes mcpx an agent."
  That conclusion is now inverted by the spec it was reasoning from. #110 must
  be read with this in mind, and the doc sentence must be corrected in the same
  change — otherwise the repo keeps an authoritative-sounding recommendation the
  protocol contradicts, which is exactly the #159 class.
- **mcpx's only existing model path cannot be answered by its primary
  consumer.** Neither opencode v1 nor v2 declares the `sampling` capability
  (`docs/opencode-plugin.md` §2.6 — v1 comments it out, v2 declares `roots` +
  `elicitation`). `prompt.sample` defaults to `never`
  (`internal/settings/consumer.go:105`), so today this is invisible rather than
  broken; it becomes visible the moment anyone sets it to `ask`. Any plan that
  treats sampling as the long-term channel is planning on a dead one. The
  upstream direction has the same gap: the daemon always installs its broker
  hook (`internal/daemon/hooks.go:69`), so it declares `sampling` to every
  upstream server (`internal/mcpclient/modern.go:46-57`) whether or not any
  caller can answer.
- **#116 is rung 0 of #111, it is S, and it is not a child here.**
  `diagnose.CallError` (`internal/diagnose/diagnose.go:483`) is built, tested
  and, at 05c78b2, called by nothing outside tests. #116 wires it at the
  daemon's call boundary and is in flight with SURFACES; it improves `/v1/call`,
  MCP `tools/call` and scripts at once. It belongs to the cross-cutting tracker
  (#177). #116 is choosing the structured-diagnostic shape as it lands; #111's
  rungs read that shape rather than defining another.
- **Three children independently invented the same dial.** `repair.level`
  (#111), hook `effect` (#112), `prompt.mode: plan` (#113). Shipping all three
  means a user learns three vocabularies for one concept: how much autonomy is
  mcpx allowed here. Owned: #111 carries it, decided in SURFACES's decision
  record (#181 collision 3); the ceiling is #185 (collision 5).
- **#113 is hard-blocked on #76.** The router's entire vocabulary is the ops
  table. Routing a sentence to operations that have no CLI command produces a
  capability reachable by prose and not by hand — the inverse of the parity rule
  the repo enforces with `internal/api/parity_test.go`. #76 is in flight with
  SURFACES. The op annotations #113's confirmation gate needs mostly exist
  already: `Op.Admin`/`Mutating`/`Destructive` (`internal/api/ops.go:59-67`)
  map to MCP `readOnlyHint`/`destructiveHint` (`:654-667`); what remains is an
  audit of which operations carry them.
- **#115's registry dedup was a false premise and is struck.** An earlier
  version of this tracker said `internal/registry` returns the same package up
  to nine times across versions. It does not: `Search` pins `version=latest`
  on every query (`internal/registry/registry.go:158`) and five live searches
  returned all-distinct names. The duplicates came from querying the raw API
  without the pin, which mcpx never does. The real registry gaps — an
  unreachable `registry.pageSize` and a dropped `nextCursor` — are #179's.
- **The scope guard needs to be a review item, not prose in one issue.** #110
  states it: *no mcpx operation may call a model on a path where a deterministic
  answer exists* — diagnostics before repair, recipe matching before generation,
  lexical search before query expansion. It is the only thing keeping this
  tracker from being "make mcpx an agent", and it is currently a sentence inside
  the issue most likely to be read last. Every child should be reviewable
  against "what happens when the provider returns an error", with the answer
  always "the deterministic result, plus a sentence saying the model was
  unavailable."
- **Tool renaming (#114) collides with everything that keys on a tool name.**
  `codegen.ToolFuncName`, `catalog-history.json`, `internal/diagnose`'s
  namespace filter and #111's diagnostics all key on names. A view must show its
  own name and record the target's, and those two must never be confused — or
  #111's schema-change diagnostics start naming tools the caller has never heard
  of. The namespace and collision rules themselves are #83's (#181 collision 4).
- **#109 warns against the obvious first move and it is worth repeating here.**
  Embedding search over the tool catalogue is the highest-cost, lowest-ratio
  rung: it needs a model, a cache keyed on the catalogue fingerprint (the
  `cacheVersion` trap in `docs/consumer.md` is a live source of silent
  wrongness), and it gives up determinism on a command people put in scripts,
  over a corpus of a few hundred short identifiers where the problem is
  vocabulary and not semantics.
- **#112's `pre` hook with `effect: script` is an execution back door if the
  effect declaration is not enforced.** "Make sure these dependencies exist
  where the job runs", resolved by a general agent, means installing packages —
  which is #113's deferred provisioning problem arriving through a convenience
  option. A hook must never be able to do what the script it wraps could not;
  `Options.Permissions` has to be inherited unchanged.

## Related

Related: #177 (cross-cutting: a promise and a behaviour that disagree), #173 (extensibility), #174 (surfaces). #116 (`diagnose.CallError` built, tested, never called — rung 0 of
#111, in flight, claimed by the cross-cutting "a promise and a behaviour that disagree"
tracker, referenced here and not a child), #179 (registry search gaps; disproved
#115's dedup premise), #102 (an adapted binary is not script-callable — same
tracker, and the structural reason behind #83 which #114 builds on), #83
(tool sources, namespaces and collision rules — owner of #181 collision 4), #81
(hook vocabulary — owner of collision 2), #6 (event store — the home for #115's
miss records and #113's session resume), #40 (closed, fixed in #57: artifacts
and ExecOptions — the vehicle for #111's proposed scripts and the home for
#112's hooks; "not a new method, an option" is the governing precedent for this
whole tracker), #41 (closed, fixed in #58: diagnose, recipes, `/v1/intent`,
elicitation defaults — #109, #111, #112 and #113 are all direct continuations
of it), #47 (opencode v2 plugin — `ctx.generate.text` is one of #110's
backends), #48 (harness-free plugin core), #52 (closed, fixed in #182: e2e
daemons are now stopped via the info files and exit after 60 s idle), #76 (CLI
for `/v1`-only ops — a hard prerequisite for #113; in flight), #77 (protocol
follow-ups — error-code renumbering in `2026-07-28` affects #111's `-32602`
catch, and Sampling's deprecation belongs there too), #78 (daemon state and
cache correctness — the schema-cache trap already silently disabled the
destructive-call policy once), #79 (faster CLI and exec — search must stay
instant and hooks must not regress exec latency), #80–#88 (extensibility and
surfaces; #83 in particular is the design #114's script-backed tools and #102
both belong to), #159 (docs that contradict the code — `docs/consumer.md`'s
provider recommendation is now an instance), #172 (undeclared `MCPX_*`
variables — every `model.*`, `repair.*` and hook setting proposed here must go
through the one registry).

code.body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#90 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #89

## Purpose

The platform every page stands on: which generator builds the book, how it reaches GitHub Pages, the subdomain it is
served from, and the agent-markdown twin of every page (llms.txt, a `.md` beside every `.html`, and a bot home page
that carries the install prompt).

## Original notes

> - documentation
>   - make a book using whatever is the most common and simple modern choice
>     - that thing all the rust/k8s people use is fine
>     - github static setup. separately, assign a subdomain
>     - specialized agent markdown all pages
>       - home page has install prompt built into the bot version

## Children

- [ ] #117 mcpx docs: choose the site generator (mdBook, MkDocs Material, Docusaurus, Starlight, Hugo)
- [ ] #118 mcpx docs: build the site in CI and deploy to GitHub Pages
- [ ] #119 mcpx docs: a custom subdomain for the site (DNS, CNAME, HTTPS)
- [ ] #120 mcpx docs: an agent-markdown twin of every page, and the bot home page carries the install prompt

## Proposed order

1. #117 first (S, a decision): everything else in the docs tree depends on its answer. Its recommendation: mdBook
   for the book, a hand-built static home page, and the extra logic (history, agent twin, reference output) as Go
   programs in this repo. MkDocs Material is excluded because it entered maintenance mode (end of life 2027-05-05).
   Only wanting whole-site versioned doc sets would reopen it.
2. #118 (Actions artifact deploy from this repo, `nix build .#mcpx-docs`), then #119 (`mcpx.drewrypope.com`; DNS is
   at Porkbun, and a wildcard record exists that an explicit CNAME overrides). #119's first step sets the custom
   domain on the repository's Pages site, which exists only once #118 has enabled it
   (`gh api repos/dezren39/nix/pages` still returns 404 at 05c78b2), so #119 follows #118 rather than running
   beside it.
3. #120 once there are pages to twin; its install procedure needs #158's channels.

## Ease and impact

| # | Title | Kind | Ease | Impact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #117 | choose the site generator | design | S | high |
| #118 | build + deploy to GitHub Pages | implement | M | high |
| #119 | custom subdomain | implement | S | med |
| #120 | agent-markdown twin, bot home page | design | M | high |

## Related

#49 (CI for every package: the docs site becomes a flake output), #144/#145 (generated reference feeds the build),
#150/#151 (history renderer runs in the build), #155 (home page), #158 (release and install channels). Docs checks
in CI: #95.

## Ease · Impact · Related

See the table above; related issues listed above.

code.title: mcpx: runtimes, languages and dependencies -- what runs a script, in what language, with which packages (tracker)
code.body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#175 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #181

## Purpose

Everything about what actually executes a script: which JavaScript runtime is
chosen and what each one does with the TypeScript it is handed, what a script is
allowed to be written in, where its third-party packages come from, how its
import graph is resolved before anything runs, and what environment it runs
inside. Today mcpx answers none of these in documentation and only one of them
(`script.runtime`) in configuration — the rest is whatever deno, bun or node
happens to do from the working directory. The theme's through-line is that the
runtime currently decides and mcpx has no opinion, no setting, and no way for a
caller to state one; these eight issues give mcpx an opinion at each stage, in
the one settings registry rather than in new endpoints. Three design objects are
shared across the whole set and should be settled once: the **preflight
pipeline** (`script.check` and its per-stage policy, from #100), the
**resolved dependency set** (from #103, filled in by #104, generalised by #105's
PEP 723 and #107's Nix vendoring), and the **cache mechanism** that holds what
#103, #104 and #107 prepare (#187). Everything else is an application of those
three.

## Children

- [ ] #100 mcpx: how the JavaScript runtime is chosen, what each does with TypeScript, and an automatic validate/compile step — first because it names `script.check`/`script.compile`/`script.checkOnUnsupported`, the vocabulary five of the others extend. Owns #181 collisions 1 (`script.typecheck` alias-vs-replace, before #79's default flip) and 11 (`auto` resolution and its test).
- [ ] #103 mcpx: where a script's packages come from -- npm/deno/bun dependency configuration chain — second and parallel to #100: it defines the resolved dependency set, which #104 fills in and #105/#107 reuse.
- [ ] #187 mcpx: one content-addressed cache for prepared dependencies, import graphs and flake resolutions — third and parallel to #100/#103: the one mechanism (layout, keys, byte/age eviction, leases, nix GC roots) that #103, #104 and #107 store into. Owns #181 collision 12; must be settled before the first of those three ships a cache.
- [ ] #104 mcpx: resolve a script's import graph statically and prepare missing dependencies — fourth, because it is the pipeline that populates #103's set, plugs into #100's preflight staging, and stores in #187's cache.
- [ ] #106 mcpx: exec should run any shebang, and resolve file scripts the same way local or remote — fifth: it defines the interpreter dispatch table with a hole for `script.language`, and independently closes a real CLI↔`/v1` divergence.
- [ ] #105 mcpx: Python as a first-class script language, 1:1 with TypeScript — sixth: XL, touches every package that names `.ts`, and fills the hole #106 leaves rather than forcing #106 to be revised. Split into a typed-client slice (M, can start any time) and a runner slice (L, the gated part).
- [ ] #107 mcpx: accept a flake ref as a program and as an execution environment — seventh: `exec.env` composes on top of #106's interpreter seam, and its "baked into binary" overlaps #103's vendored-cache reading.
- [ ] #101 mcpx: docs/runtimes.md -- compare the execution options and their features — last for content, first for its probe suite, which is the evidence base for #100's claims and the guard against them going stale.

## Proposed order

**Phase 0 — start now, blocks nothing.** The capability-probe harness from #101
(five one-line TypeScript files per runtime, plus package-resolution and
type-check probes). It is the measurement that #100's syntax table, #101's
generated matrix and #108's regression test all assert against, and it is worth
having before any of them is written. It can run in the existing mcpx CI job,
which already installs deno, bun and node (`.github/workflows/mcpx.yml:55-61`),
with the look-up-and-skip pattern the e2e runtime tests already use; #134's
matrix adds legs with fewer runtimes. Independently and in the other tracker:
#108's one-line flag change (in flight under #177), which is the cheapest fix in
this whole theme and should not wait for anything here.

**Phase 1 — the three shared design objects, in parallel.** #100, #103 and #187
touch different settings and different code and can proceed at the same time.
#100 settles the preflight pipeline and, critically, the `script.typecheck` →
`script.check` question that #79 is about to collide with (#100 owns #181
collision 1 and recommends an alias with a value map; #79's default change lands
on that decision). #103 settles the dependency chain, its precedence order, and
the resolved-set representation that travels on `ExecOptions`. #187 settles the
cache mechanism, so #103, #104 and #107 each define only what they store.

**Phase 2 — #104, gated on #103 and #187.** #104 says so itself: #103 "supplies
the dependency-set concept this pipeline fills in", and its graph and prepared
environments are #187 entries. It also needs #100's decision
about where in the preflight the graph stage sits (before a single server
starts, per `runner.Run`'s existing comment).

**Phase 3 — #106, parallel to phases 1–2 except for one field.** Shebang
dispatch, `script.interpreter` and `script.cwd` depend on nothing here. Moving
`resolveScript` out of `internal/cli` so the daemon resolves `file` the same way
depends on #76, not on this tracker. Only dispatch rank 3 (`script.language`)
waits for #105, and it waits as a documented hole, not as a blocker.

**Phase 4 — #105, gated on #100, #103 and #106.** Python is XL and is built
against `script.check`, the dependency chain and the dispatch table. Starting it
earlier means building it against setting names that then change. The
exception is #105's slice 1 (the codegen seam and a typed Python client),
which touches none of those and can be pulled forward.

**Phase 5 — #107, gated on #106.** `exec.env` and `script.interpreter` compose
(environment-then-interpreter), so the interpreter seam has to exist first. Part
1 of #107 (the `nix:` program spec and its resolve-to-store-path cache) is
independent of part 2 and can be pulled forward once #187 exists.

**Phase 6 — #101 finalised.** The comparison doc can only compare options once
they exist. Its prose sections (how to set the runtime, the decision list) can
be written in phase 1; the Python, environment and dependency rows land as their
issues do.

Cheap-first callouts, in order of ratio: #108's flag (#177, in flight, one line,
which also covers the `--experimental-strip-types` removal), #100's `auto`
test (four stub-`PATH` cases) and its `auto`-chose-X line, `mcpx run` as a
shebang interpreter in #106 (probably works already; needs a test), and #101's
prose sections.

## Ease / impact

| Issue | Ease | Impact | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #100 | M (S for the node flag fix and the docs; M for the check pipeline; L if `compile` lands too) | high | "it is the first question a user asks and the answer is currently only in source comments" |
| #103 | L — five sources, three runtimes, and a cache key | high | "without it a script cannot use a library, which is most of what scripts do" |
| #187 | M | med-high | "cheap now, expensive after the first of #103/#104/#107 ships its own" |
| #104 | L | high | "the difference between 'scripts may use libraries if you set the project up first' and 'scripts may use libraries'" |
| #106 | M (dispatch and cwd policy) / L (shared script resolution across CLI and daemon) | high | "turns `exec` from 'run TypeScript' into 'run a script', and it closes a real CLI-vs-`/v1` divergence of the kind #76 tracks" |
| #105 | XL — a second codegen backend, a second launcher, a second checker, and a parity checklist to hold it to (slice 1 M, slice 2 L) | high | "Python is where most MCP and data tooling already lives" |
| #107 | L | medium overall, high for this repository's own users | "'the environment a script runs in' is currently a fixed list chosen at build time" |
| #101 | S (Approach B) / M (Approach C, because of the probe suite) | medium | "the answer to the most-asked question and the guard against the docs going stale" |

## Warnings

- **#100 and #79 collide on a shipped setting** (#181 collision 1, **owned by
  #100**). #100 proposes widening `script.typecheck` into `script.check`; #79
  proposes changing `script.typecheck`'s default from `off` to `on` for `run`.
  `script.typecheck` is shipped and documented in `docs/configuration.md` (still
  `internal/settings/registry.go:244`, `Default: "off"`, at 05c78b2). Renaming it
  and changing its default in the same cycle is two breaking changes to one
  knob. Settle alias-vs-replace in #100 **before** #79 ships its default; #100
  now recommends an alias with a value map (an unknown config key only warns,
  so a plain replace silently turns checking off). #74 (closed, fixed in #75)
  is the precedent for how much this project dislikes a flag whose behaviour
  does not match its name.
- **#108 is the cheapest fix in this entire theme and it is not a child here.**
  `internal/runner/runner.go:100` still passes `--experimental-strip-types` (a
  no-op on node 24) instead of `--experimental-transform-types`, which is the
  whole difference between `enum` failing and `enum` working. It is one line
  plus a test. It is claimed by #177 ("a promise and a behaviour that
  disagree") and is in flight; do not let this tracker's phase 1 design block
  it.
- **`script.runtime = auto` hides the node breakage from anyone using a
  packaged install** (#181 collision 11, **owned by #100**; partly outdated).
  `runner.Detect` takes the first of deno, bun, node on `PATH`, and `package.nix`
  suffixes all three (`package.nix:96-103`), so on any Nix install `auto` always
  means deno; the container pins bun (`Containerfile:80`). The test suite is
  *not* blind, though: the e2e runtime tests pin each runtime explicitly
  (`internal/e2e/runtime_test.go:14,46`, `e2e_test.go:2478`) and CI installs all
  three. What remains is `auto` itself (no test asserts what it picks — #100
  owns a four-case stub-`PATH` test), non-erasable TypeScript under node
  (#108), and a CI leg with no deno at all (#134's matrix).
- **#104 makes Deno a hard dependency of import analysis for scripts that will
  not run on Deno.** `deno info --json` is the proposed graph oracle even when
  the selected runtime is bun or node. Deno's resolution is stricter
  (extensionless relative imports fail), so the analysis can report a problem
  that would not have occurred at run time — the same trap as #100's
  `onUnsupported: switch`. Both need `--sloppy-imports` or a
  demote-to-warning rule for that specific diagnostic class, and both need
  `docs/dependencies.md`'s bar applied to making deno mandatory.
- **Three children each introduce a new content-addressed cache, and none of
  them is sized like the existing one** (#181 collision 12, **owned by #187**). #103 (a prepared dependency directory),
  #104 (a prepared environment keyed by the resolved set) and #107 (resolved
  store paths and a captured devshell). `node_modules` and Nix closures are
  orders of magnitude larger than the generated client that `pruneWorkDirs` and
  `defaults.ExecWorkDirs` were sized for. Decide the cache design and the
  retention policy once, across the three, or #78 acquires a fourth instance of
  the same bug class. #187 is that decision; #103, #104 and #107 now defer to it
  and keep their own cache text as input.
- **#106 changes the meaning of a shipped wire field.** `POST /v1/exec
  {"file": ...}` today is `filepath.Abs` on the daemon (passed through at
  `internal/execsvc/execsvc.go:327`, resolved at `internal/runner/runner.go:293`);
  #106 makes it a search-path resolution.
  That is the behaviour #48's harness-free plugin needs and it is a behaviour
  change for anyone already sending an absolute path. It needs a compatibility
  decision (absolute paths keep working, names resolve) stated explicitly rather
  than discovered. #106 also records that a remote CLI run drops most exec flags
  (`--typecheck`, `--launcher`, the phases, `--env`, ...) because `runScript`
  hands off before reading them; #75 fixed that class only for the local path.
- **#107's naive form is an unbounded latency source.** `command: "nix"` with
  `nix run` already works today and is exactly the thing not to do — a flake
  evaluation on every server start, repeated by pool restarts, in a project that
  measures its exec path in tens of milliseconds (#79). The resolve-once-to-a-
  store-path cache is the point of the issue, not an optimisation to defer.
- **#105's runner slice cannot start early.** XL overall, and slice 2 touches
  `internal/runner`, `internal/settings`, `internal/preflight`,
  `internal/cli/scripts.go`, `internal/diagnose` and `docs/exec.md`, all of
  which #100 and #106 are about to change the shape of. Slice 1 (the codegen
  seam and a typed client) touches only `internal/codegen` and one route.
- **Setting names must not be both a value and a parent.** A nested config file
  cannot hold `script.check` as a string and as `{onError: ...}`; no declared
  setting path is both today. #100 and #104 were renamed to flat camelCase
  (`script.checkOnError`, `script.importsOnMissing`, ...). #107's working name
  `exec.env` collides in meaning with the shipped `script.env` (environment
  variables) and should change before it ships.

## Related

Related: #177 (cross-cutting: a promise and a behaviour that disagree), #173 (extensibility), #174 (surfaces). #102 and #108 (runtime-adjacent bugs — an adapted binary that is not
script-callable, and `--runtime node` passing an inert flag — both claimed by
the cross-cutting "a promise and a behaviour that disagree" tracker, referenced
here and not children), #5 (`paths.config` chain, the precedence model #103
follows), #7 (launcher placeholders, the declaration-to-command-line machinery
#103 and #107 must not duplicate), #40 (closed, fixed in #57 — ExecOptions,
which gains `deps` and `language`), #49 (CI for every flake package), #134 (CI
environment matrix — the per-runtime legs, including one without deno), #52
(closed, fixed in #182 — the e2e suite no longer leaks daemons), #74 (closed,
fixed in #75 — flags accepted and ignored, the precedent for #100's rename
question),
#76 (CLI ↔ `/v1` parity, a prerequisite for #106's shared script resolution),
#78 (daemon state and cache correctness — the new caches go through #187),
#79 (typecheck default and startup cost — lands on #100's collision-1 decision),
#83 (anything as an MCP server), #159 (docs that contradict the code — #101 is
the fix for this theme's share of it), #172 (undeclared `MCPX_*` variables —
every setting proposed here must go through the one registry).

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

code.title: mcpx docs: the book -- overview, manual and compendium (tracker)
code.body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#89 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #91

## Purpose

Top tracker for the mcpx documentation site: one book, three levels of detail (not book sections), a
machine-readable twin of every page for agents, and reference pages generated from the code so they cannot drift.
Top of the documentation tree. Its parent is the joint docs/testing strategy issue #91; the testing trackers under #91 own every docs check that runs in CI (#95 pipeline, #97 environments).

## Original notes

> - documentation
>   - make a book using whatever is the most common and simple modern choice
>     - 3 main things, not book sections jsut like levels of detail-

The rest of the section is quoted, line by line, in the children below. The closing sentence of the notes is the
brief for the whole site and is quoted here too:

> i'm not asking you to write a short science fiction story i'm asking for an overview intro and reference website and manual.

## The three levels, plus what they stand on

| Level | Reader | Tracker |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. The 30-second layer | skimming, three other things open; home -> overview -> quick start -> ctrl+w | #92 |
| 2. "ok i just installed this thing what even is it" | a new user who may assume this is all there is | #94 |
| 3. The compendium | anyone who wants everything, in any detail, including things that are not mcpx | #98 |
| Platform | generator, GitHub Pages, subdomain, agent-markdown twin | #90 |
| Generated reference | settings/env/flags, CLI, `/v1`, MCP tools, protocol and parity matrices | #96 |

## What exists today, mapped onto the levels

Checked against main (`d0b7e01`), re-checked at `05c78b2` (two docs and a `Containerfile` added by #171 and #182).
Nothing at level 1 exists: there is no home page, install page, quick start or release to download. Most of level 3
exists as design records; level 2 exists in fragments spread across them.

| File | Lines | What it is | Level |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `docs/story.md` (`README.md` symlinks to it) | 2615 | Above the table-of-contents marker: one agent, one prompt, one script, real output. Below: the feature list, one keyed entry per feature (`created`, `last-updated`, `increment`, `status`, ...), `## Proposed` | story -> 1 (overview source); feature list -> 3 |
| `AGENTS.md` | 109 | The agent instruction file: the loop, scripts, profiles, script contract | 2 + agent twin |
| `docs/landing.md` | 185 | **Not a landing page.** A PR landing checklist (items A-J) with "Guesses worth reviewing" and "Not done, and why" | 3 (decision record) |
| `docs/configuration.md` | 474 | Prose plus the "Every setting" table. The table is hand-regenerated and only presence-checked by `internal/settings/docs_test.go` | 2 prose + generated reference |
| `docs/parity.md` | 130 | CLI / plugin / `/v1` / MCP matrix; `internal/api/parity_test.go` enforces three columns | reference |
| `docs/protocol.md` | 384 | Every MCP revision, both directions | 2 (compatibility) + reference + 3 |
| `docs/exec.md`, `docs/consumer.md` | 353, 236 | exec, artifacts, diagnostics, recipes, intent | 2 + 3 |
| `docs/elicitation.md` | 685 | elicitation design | 3 |
| `docs/opencode-plugin.md`, `docs/plugin-discovery.md`, `plugin/opencode/README.md` | 451, 224, 355 | plugin, v1 vs v2, finding the daemon without the binary, plugin options | 2 (plugin pages) + 3 |
| `docs/proposals.md`, `docs/ideas.md` | 1395, 338 | open designs, unvetted intake | 3 (or stay repo-only) |
| `docs/release-runbook.md` | 173 | how the story stays true; key-block rules; per-release steps | maintainer docs; seed of the history design |
| `docs/dependencies.md` | 91 | libraries, external programs, Nix packaging | 2 (binary) + 3 |
| `docs/container.md` (#182) | 170 | what `pkgs/mcpx/Containerfile` builds (Debian slim, bun, git, 413 MB), what it deliberately leaves out, and the `CGO_ENABLED=0` static-build measurement | 2 (install: docker row) + 3 |
| `docs/declared-but-unread.md` (#171) | 245 | the settings audit: declared settings nothing read, what was wired or deleted, the guard tests | 3 (decision record) |
| `ASSESSMENT.md`, `OPENCODE-V2.md` | 306, 249 | lootbox audit; opencode code mode comparison (with a 2026-09-29 correction block) | 3 (history, comparisons) |
| generated: `mcpx help`, `mcpx man`, `mcpx completion`, `mcpx config --schema`, `mcpx schema --format ...`, `GET /v1/openapi.json` | - | one source each: `Commands()` in `internal/cli/manual.go`, the settings registry, the ops table | reference |

## Children

- [ ] #90 site platform -- generator, GitHub Pages, subdomain, agent markdown (tracker)
- [ ] #96 generated reference that cannot drift (tracker) -- includes #159, the bugs a generator would publish
- [ ] #92 level 1 -- the 30-second layer (tracker)
- [ ] #94 level 2 -- the "ok i just installed this thing" layer (tracker)
- [ ] #98 level 3 -- the compendium, release markers and section history (tracker)

## Proposed order

1. Decisions, in parallel: generator #117, generated-reference pipeline #144, release/install channels #158,
   history mechanism #150. #158 is the critical path: without a release there is no download link, no
   `curl | sh`, and nothing to stamp a version marker with. The one artifact recipe that already builds is
   `pkgs/mcpx/Containerfile` (#182); nothing publishes it yet.
2. Stand the site up: Pages deploy #118, subdomain #119, reference emitters #145.
3. Level 2 first (#146 page map, then #147 #148 #149), because level 1 links into it and level 2 must be
   complete on its own. Overview / quick start / install #157 alongside. Agent twin #120 once pages exist.
4. Home page #155, then the runnable example #156.
5. Compendium: structure and migration #152, history renderer #151, then the open-ended content #153 #154.
   #153's first cut is already in progress (the COMPARE architect is writing `docs/compare/`).

## Ease and impact

| Tracker | Children (ease / impact) | Ease | Impact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #90 platform | #117 generator (S/high), #118 Pages deploy (M/high), #119 subdomain (S/med), #120 agent twin (M/high) | M | high |
| #96 generated reference | #159 incomplete sources (M/high), #144 design (M/high), #145 emitters + drift check (L/high) | L | high |
| #92 level 1 | #158 release + install channels (L/high), #157 overview/quick start/install (M/high), #155 home page (M/high), #156 runnable example (S-M/med) | L | high |
| #94 level 2 | #146 page map + config (M/high), #147 interfaces (M/high), #148 plugins (S-M/med), #149 FAQ (S/med-high) | M | high |
| #98 compendium | #150 history design (M/med), #151 history impl (L/med), #152 structure + catalogue (L/med), #153 comparisons + history (M/med, in progress), #154 research + Nix (L/med) | XL | med |

## Warnings

- `docs/landing.md` is not a head start for the home page; it is a PR checklist. The only level-1 material is the
  story walk at the top of `docs/story.md`.
- The system-wide install form in the notes, `sudo $(curl <short> | sh)`, runs the installer unprivileged and
  executes its *output* as a root command. #155, #157 and #158 replace it with
  `curl -fsSL <short> | sh -s -- --system` (an unprivileged script that escalates only the copy), with
  `curl -fsSL <short> | sudo sh` as the plain fallback.
- "that thing all the rust/k8s people use" names two different tools: Rust uses mdBook, kubernetes.io uses Hugo
  (Docsy). #117 compares both and three others.
- The "single sources" are not all single: `Commands()` omits seven dispatched commands, dozens of `MCPX_*` variables
  are outside the settings registry (#172 owns the count and the allowlist), `mcpx init` writes an ignored key, and
  several docs contradict the code. A generator would publish all of it; #159 fixes the sources first.
- Docs checks (links, generated pages current, agent twin in sync, examples executed) belong in the CI pipeline;
  see #95 (CI pipeline) and #97 (integration/environments), under #91.

## Ease · Impact · Related

Ease: XL (sum of children) · Impact: high · Related: #49 (CI for every package), #44 (closed, fixed in #53), #47,
#48, #76, #77, #134 (container image; `Containerfile` from #182).

code.title: mcpx: surfaces -- reaching the daemon over ssh and the browser, and keeping what you reached (tracker)
code.body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#174 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #181

## Purpose

Everything about reaching a running daemon, and keeping what you reached alive long enough to use. Four issues sit under this theme because they are all consequences of one fact: the daemon is already a network service with 60 declared operations, SSE and MCP, and almost nothing exists to *reach* it except a local CLI. #88 is the foundation — a caller today cannot reliably name the socket of a daemon it did not start, which is a live bug in the CLI. It was the mechanism behind #52; #182 closed #52 by making the test harness resolve through the info files (`stop --all`), which is #88's approach applied to one command, and left the CLI itself unchanged. #85 and #86 are the two missing front doors, one for a terminal on another machine and one for a browser. #87 is what makes either of them worth opening: every expiring resource in mcpx is absolute-from-creation and un-renewable, so a browser tab or a remote TUI watching a 120-second elicitation loses it. Done looks like: any process that knows the state directory can find the daemon, `mcpx tui --daemon-endpoint ssh://host` works, `/ui/` serves a dashboard from the binary with no npm anywhere, and a resource stays alive while something is watching it.

Two of these issues have an explicitly rejected Approach A that is also the obvious phrasing of the ask — a built-in SSH server, and a vendored React SPA. Both are the expensive path. The theme's job is partly to stop those being rebuilt from the title alone.

## Children

- [ ] #88 mcpx: the socket-path fallback is deterministic but environment-dependent; resolve through the info file — first because it is the only `bug` here, both other surfaces need to name a socket, and it owns `MCPX_SOCKET` precedence (#181 collision 8). #52, which it explained, is closed (fixed in #182 for the test suite only).
- [ ] #87 mcpx: one convention for renewing TTLs -- touch-on-read, not a renew endpoint per resource — independent of the rest and a prerequisite for #86's real use case; a dashboard sitting on an elicitation is the motivating example in its own body. Owns the daemon lifetime rule for every surface (#181 collision 9).
- [ ] #85 mcpx: remote access over ssh -- TUI, RPC, reverse tunnels, and why not a built-in ssh server — its documentation slice is zero code and ships immediately; the `ssh://` endpoint scheme is the real work.
- [ ] #86 mcpx: a web frontend served by the daemon, without a second build system — last because the embedded frontend is the largest piece and it is the one that benefits most from the other three.

## Proposed order

**Phase 1 — fix discovery before adding two more things that have to name a socket.**

1. **#88.** `Paths.Resolve()` reads `<state>/daemon-<key>.json` and returns `info.Socket`, falling back to the computed path only when no record exists (the daemon's `/v1/resolve` already does this, `routes_resolve.go:110-121`; extract it); `NewClient` and `EnsureDaemon` use it; shutdown already unlinks the record (`server.go:387`) and should do so only when the record is still its own; `MCPX_SOCKET` applies to the process's own daemon and never to answers about other keys; log the relocation once at daemon start. Ease S for that core. It makes `mcpx stop` behave the way `mcpx stop --all` already does — #182 switched the e2e cleanup to `stop --all` for exactly this reason (`internal/e2e/e2e_test.go:72-83`) — aligns the Go CLI with the plugin ladder that `docs/plugin-discovery.md:61-64` already documents as correct, and gives #85's `ssh -L` recipe a path a human can actually read.

**Phase 2 — cheap slices, in parallel.**

2. **#85 slice 1 (documentation only, Ease S, zero code).** `ssh host mcpx tui` is already an SSH TUI. `command: ssh, args: [host, mcpx, serve, --transport, stdio]` is already MCP-over-ssh for any MCP host, and belongs in `docs/protocol.md` because it is free and nobody will guess it. `ssh -N -L 7777:<socket> host` plus `daemon.endpoint=http://127.0.0.1:7777` already works — and needs phase 1 to be usable, since you must know the remote socket path.
3. **#86 slice 1 (Ease S).** Add `daemon.ui` (bool, daemon scope, default off) and `daemon.uiDir` (string, default empty, serves a directory instead of embedded assets). `daemon.uiDir` must ship in this slice, not later: it is the escape hatch that makes "do not vendor a SPA" a real position rather than a refusal, and it is the dev loop for slice 2.
4. **#87.** Touch-on-read as the default expiry, an `<x>.maxAge` absolute ceiling paired with each idle `<x>.ttl`, an explicit `ttl` parameter on create only, and one vocabulary (`expiresAt` + `ttlRemainingMs`) echoed on every expiring resource — plus the daemon's own lifetime rule, which #85 and #86 apply. Step zero: `elicit.ttl` is a compiled-in default with no setting (`internal/defaults/defaults.json:63`), so it must be declared before it can be re-meant. Independent of the other three and can start any time; placed here because #86 slice 2 is not worth building without it and #85/#86 need its lifetime answer.

**Phase 3 — the two real surfaces.**

5. **#85 slice 2: the `ssh://` endpoint scheme.** `daemon.endpoint = ssh://user@host` installs a `DialContext` that spawns the system `ssh` running a stdio-proxy subcommand on the far side. Everything downstream is unchanged because it is all HTTP over a byte stream. **Prototype SSE over the ssh pipe before committing** — it is the one genuinely unknown behaviour in the design, and `/v1/events` is what a remote TUI lives on.
6. **#86 slice 2: the embedded no-build frontend.** Plain HTML/CSS/ES modules, `go:embed`, served at `/ui/` by the existing listener. Scope fixed at the TUI's six views read-only, plus elicitation forms — which is the one thing a browser does better than a terminal, and the thing #87 makes viable.

**Declined, and recorded as declined.**

7. **#85 Approach A** (a `charmbracelet/wish` SSH server) and **#86 Approach A** (a vendored React SPA bundled at build time). Both are documented in their issues with the reasoning. Neither should be built; if either is, it goes behind a build tag or a separate flake package with its own CI (#49), never linked into the default `mcpx`.

Parallelism: phase 2's three items are disjoint. Phase 3's two are disjoint from each other but both want phase 1 and #85 slice 2 makes #86's remote story work (`ssh -L` plus `/ui/` is a remote dashboard with nothing installed locally).

## Ease / impact

| Issue | Ease | Impact | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #88 | S for the resolve step and the relocation log; M once `Paths.Socket`'s call sites are audited | med | Lowered from high in the 2026-09-30 pass: #182 removed the test-suite leak (#52). Still silently produces false negatives from `mcpx stop`, `mcpx status` and every client command past a 100-byte state path, can start a second daemon for one key, and gets worse as more surfaces need to name a socket. |
| #87 | M | med | Mechanically small per store, but touches five subsystems and changes the meaning of documented settings. High for anything with a human in the loop, where `elicit.ttl = 120s` is the ceiling on how long a person may take. |
| #85 | S for the documentation and the `ssh host mcpx serve` recipe; M for the `ssh://` endpoint scheme and stdio proxy; L for a wish-based SSH server (A), mostly in policy rather than code | med | High for anyone with a remote or containerised daemon, nil for a single-laptop user. |
| #86 | S to serve a directory and add the settings; M for the embedded read-only frontend covering the TUI's six views; L if a bundled SPA (A) is chosen | med | High for demos, remote machines and anyone who will not open a terminal; low for the existing CLI-first user. |

As in the sibling tracker, these Ease values are **per-slice**. The S rows are the phase-1/phase-2 slices only.

## Warnings

- **Two of the four issues have an explicitly rejected Approach A that is exactly what the issue title sounds like.** "ssh server" summons `charmbracelet/wish`; "web frontend" summons a Vite/React SPA. Both are refused with reasons in the bodies. The wish path also costs ~15 modules including `go-git/go-git/v5`, `ProtonMail/go-crypto` and `cloudflare/circl` in a repo whose `pkgs/mcpx/package.nix:36-53` enumerates and justifies each of its five direct Go dependencies; the SPA path adds a second fixed-output hash (`npmDepsHash`) to a build where **#49 already records that the vendorHash repair step has never run on a real bot PR**. Do not let either be re-derived from the title.
- **#87 changes the meaning of documented settings.** `elicit.ttl`, `tasks.ttl`, `proto.askTTL` and `proto.stateTTL` currently mean absolute-from-creation; the recommendation re-means them as idle. That is a behaviour change on a documented surface, and the issue itself lists "new names with a deprecation, or just change it pre-1.0" as unresolved. Separately, #87's *middle* approach puts an `extend` parameter on `GET`, which breaks the `Mutating`/`Admin`/`Destructive` classification the ops table relies on (`internal/api/ops.go`) — the recommended path avoids it, but anyone who implements the B slice for expedience reintroduces a mutating read.
- **The symlink fix for #88 does not work, and this was measured.** macOS checks the length of the path you hand `bind()`/`connect()` *before* symlink resolution, so a symlink at `<state>/daemon-<key>.sock` is unusable in exactly the case that produced the fallback — that path is over 100 bytes by definition. The `chdir`-to-the-directory trick works but `chdir` is process-global and darwin has no `connectat()`. The measurement table is in #88's body and should end up in a code comment, or someone will spend an afternoon rediscovering it.
- **One lifetime rule, owned by #87 (#181 collision 9).** An open browser tab either keeps a daemon alive forever or gets killed under the user by `daemon.idleExit`; an `ssh://` endpoint with `ControlMaster` leaves a process behind. The rule: activity on any surface renews the daemon's idle deadline, and nothing else does; #85 and #86 apply it. The concrete open point is whether a *delivering* stream is activity — today the idle clock is stamped only when a request starts (`internal/daemon/server.go:344-368`), so an open `/v1/events` tab does not hold the daemon. The third case, leaked e2e daemons (#52), was fixed by #182.
- **`MCPX_SOCKET` precedence is #88's (#181 collision 8).** It overrides both the computed path and the info file for every key (`paths.go:104-106`). #78 dropped the item and links #88; #88's recommendation is that it names the process's own daemon only and never leaks into answers about other directories. It is also one of the undeclared `MCPX_*` variables in #172.
- **#88's fix adds a file read to the CLI fast path,** which is inside #79's startup budget. It is a `stat` plus a ~200-byte read in a directory about to be touched anyway, and it can be skipped when the computed path is already a live socket — but that has to be measured rather than assumed, because #79 is about tens of milliseconds.
- **#86's no-build frontend has a real scope cliff at view seven.** Hand-written DOM is fine for the TUI's six read-only views and an elicitation form and painful past that. `daemon.uiDir` is the stated mitigation and only works if it exists *before* the cliff is reached, which is why it is in phase 2 and not bundled into slice 2.
- **`.lootbox/ui` is not a starting point and should not be adopted.** 36 tracked files, one page, a committed prebuilt bundle, 279 MB of untracked `node_modules`, and #49 records that it is not built by the flake at all — the lootbox that actually runs comes from upstream (`flake.nix:388`). Its only reusable part is a regenerable shadcn component set. #49 owns whether it is deleted; this theme's input is only that it is not mcpx's frontend.
- **Both new surfaces make `/v1`-only operations more visible.** #76 and #113 are the existing parity backlog; a remote TUI and a browser dashboard both expose operations that have no CLI command, which will generate parity requests as a side effect of shipping either.

## Related

Related: #52 (closed, fixed in #182 — `stop --all` through the info files plus a 60s autostart idle exit in the test env; no `TestMain` sweep was needed) · #78 (two digests under one name in the same info file; its `MCPX_SOCKET` item moved to #88) · #183 (in flight: the `ForConfig` comment in `paths.go`) · #76 and #113 (CLI parity for `/v1`-only operations; every new surface makes the gaps more visible, and #87's new parameters must reach the CLI and the plugin, not just `/v1`) · #77 (protocol follow-ups — task status, cancellation and inline answers are exactly what a live dashboard and a touch-renewed task want) · #79 (client fast-path budget; #88 spends from it) · #49 (`.lootbox/ui` has no build check; any new build stage, build tag or flake package needs CI) · #6 (event store — expiry events from #87 belong there, and `/v1/events` is what both new surfaces live on; #6 owns the gap contract, collision 13, which is what a remote TUI or a browser `EventSource` is told when it falls behind — today a replay past 256 events is silently truncated) · #172 (`MCPX_SOCKET` is one of 44 undeclared `MCPX_*` variables) · #159 (docs that say what the code does not — #85's and #86's documentation slices are partly repayment on that) · #5 (`daemon.endpoint`, `daemon.address` and the new UI settings all resolve through the config chain).

Sibling tracker: #173 (extensibility / plugins).
