feat(agent-tool): allow agents to write project setup commands and project actions (decision on #152)
openchamber.body:
## Decision (Drew, 2026-11-23, on #152)

Agents may write setup commands and project actions in OpenChamber. PR #179 shipped `projects.setup` read-only because those commands run outside OpenCode's permission rules; Drew's call: allow the writes — setup and project actions are the point of the agent tool, and OpenCode's permission rules still govern execution. The 2026-10-22 adopted default (read-only stays) is superseded by this decision.

## Scope

- Add the write counterpart to `projects.setup`: agents can set/replace a project's setup commands through the openchamber tool, under the same save-lock discipline PR #194 established for project writes.
- Allow agent writes to project actions (create/update/remove), same lock discipline.
- Keep the enterprise-mode posture coherent with the existing rule: in enterprise mode, agent config writes stay closed (2026-10-22 default, not superseded) unless this issue's implementation records otherwise with a reason.
- Writes must be auditable the way other agent-tool mutations are (who/what/when in the action result).

## Acceptance

- An agent can write a project's setup commands and project actions via the tool, and the change is visible in the project configuration and takes effect on the next run of that setup/action.
- Enterprise mode still refuses these writes.
- Tests cover the write path, the lock behaviour, and the enterprise refusal.

Filed from the #152 tracker close-out (task 17623): the decision was that tracker's last open thread; the tracker closes with this issue as the implementation's home.

openchamber.title: Add atomic no-replace directory renames across supported platforms
openchamber.body:
## Context

Issue #2572 requires `/api/fs/rename` to preserve a concurrently created empty destination directory. `renameWithoutReplace` currently uses `fs.rename` for directory sources. POSIX rename may replace an empty destination directory, and Node does not expose the platform's exclusive-rename flags.

A precheck followed by `rename`, placeholder directory, or copy fallback cannot preserve the source and raced destination inodes atomically. Linux provides `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)`, macOS provides `renamex_np(RENAME_EXCL)`, and Windows provides a move without `MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING`. Node and Bun do not expose these operations directly.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add a supported native operation for atomic no-replace directory rename on the app's supported Linux, macOS, and Windows targets.
- Return an existing-path error when a destination appears before commit, leaving both directory paths and inodes unchanged.
- Fail closed when the platform or filesystem cannot provide the exclusive operation. Do not fall back to check-then-rename.
- Keep ordinary directory moves and same-path/case-only renames working.
- Add deterministic race coverage and verify the platform behavior in Linux, macOS, and Windows CI.
- Document native loading and any filesystem or platform constraint.
- Wire the helper into the existing `/api/fs/rename` route and complete issue #2572.

Related: #2572.

openchamber.title: fix(web): preserve a concurrently created empty directory in /api/fs/rename
openchamber.body:
## Evidence

Follow-up to #2375. The no-replace rename fix in `packages/web/server/lib/shared/atomic-rename.ts` intentionally keeps plain `rename()` for directory sources (`sourceKind.isDirectory`, lines 51-53); the comment says a directory rename onto an existing file or non-empty directory fails. But POSIX `rename(2)` replaces an existing **empty directory**.

The route's existence check is still separate from commit (`packages/web/server/lib/fs/routes.ts:2059-2079`): if `/api/fs/rename` observes the destination as absent and another process creates an empty directory there before `renameWithoutReplace` commits, the plain directory `rename()` replaces that newly created directory and returns success. A real Node filesystem probe confirmed the primitive: after creating an empty destination directory, `fs.rename(sourceDir, destinationDir)` succeeded and changed the destination inode to the source directory's inode. This is the directory-shaped residual explicitly left by #2375's implementation, not the regular-file race covered by that issue's regression test.

## Why it matters

A concurrent directory creation can be silently discarded, and callers receive success rather than the existing 409 conflict. The route promises not to overwrite a distinct destination; the no-replace behavior currently does not hold for this valid directory edge case.

## Acceptance criteria

- If a distinct empty destination directory appears after the route's lookup but before commit, return the existing 409 `already-exists` response and preserve both source and destination paths/inodes.
- Add a real-filesystem regression that injects empty-directory creation between the destination lookup and commit.
- Keep supported directory moves and same-path/case-only rename behavior working; document/test platform-specific semantics for supported OSes.

openchamber.title: fix(web): preview-grant serve route serves symlink-escaped files outside the grant root
openchamber.body:
## Summary
`GET /api/fs/preview/<grant>/<path>` enforces only lexical containment against `grant.base`, then `realpath`s and serves the canonical target with no canonical re-check — so a symlink inside the granted tree pointing outside the workspace is served with 200, including unauthenticated (the grant token is the credential on this route).

## Evidence
- Mint (`packages/web/server/lib/fs/routes.ts:1589-1613`): canonicalizes the page (`realpath(resolved.resolved)`), mints `{ base: resolved.base /* lexical */, readRoot /* canonical */ }`.
- Serve (`routes.ts:1626-1689`): `resolveWorkspacePath({ baseDirectory: grant.base })` is lexical-only, then `const canonicalPath = await fsPromises.realpath(resolved.resolved)` — but `canonicalPath` is never checked back against `grant.base`/`grant.readRoot`. The only use of `isPathWithinRoot(canonicalPath, grant.readRoot)` (:1674) gates the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null` header, not the serve.
- Sibling `POST /api/fs/reveal` (`routes.ts:2091-2098`) does the correct thing: `realpath` both sides and 403s when `!isPathWithinRoot(canonicalTarget, canonicalBase)`. The preview serve route skips this step.
- Live repro (vitest harness minting a grant for `site/index.html`, then `GET /api/fs/preview/<grant>/site/evil.txt` where `evil.txt -> <workspace>/../secret.txt`): **200 with the outside file's bytes** (`EVIL STATUS 200 BODY TOP-SECRET-OUTSIDE-WORKSPACE`). Repro file: `packages/web/server/lib/fs/preview-symlink-repro.test.js` (scratch only, not committed). Expected after fix: 403 (or 400) without serving bytes.

## Impact
Anyone holding/sharing a preview URL (grant-scoped, no session auth on the GET) can read arbitrary files the server process can read by planting or following a symlink inside the previewed tree — e.g. `secret.txt` adjacent to the workspace, or via a symlinked ancestor. The mint route's own canonicalization shows the codebase already treats this as a boundary; the serve route just doesn't re-enforce it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After `realpath` in the preview serve route, deny (403) when the canonical target is not within the canonical grant root (`grant.readRoot`, mirroring the reveal route's canonical-both-sides check), instead of serving.
- [ ] Regression test: grant rooted in dir A, symlink inside A pointing to a file outside A, asserts the serve returns 403/400 and never the outside bytes (plus a positive test that a normal in-root file still serves).
- [ ] Symlinked-ancestor escape (granted dir itself reached through a symlink pointing out) covered by the same check.

## Dedupe
- OPEN #2458 covers vscode bridge read/stat symlink escapes — different surface (extension bridge, no grant involved).
- CLOSED #1605 is preview-serve byte-cap accounting — different defect on the same route.
- CLOSED #2520 contained the sibling `/api/fs/reveal` route — this issue is the preview-serve route that was left open.
- No open PR touches the preview serve route (only open PR is #2535 ci token fallback).

openchamber.title: Model pool settings: follow-ups after the rebuild
openchamber.body:
Follow-ups to the model-pool settings rebuild. Everything listed here is open; nothing in it blocks the merged work.

Merged so far: #2469 (rebuild), #2486 (model defaults and lock, OpenCode model settings), #2489 (fixes found in a real browser), #2492 (last-model wait), #2493 (effort fixes for pools of pools), #2497 (docs: a pool moves on after a failure that follows output). OpenCode side: developing-today-forks/opencode#2674, #2676, #2679.

## 1. "Try the next pool model" takes the session off the pool (needs a decision)

After the button retries a reply, the chat box shows the member it used (for example `mock/okay`) instead of the pool, and the next message goes straight to that model. From then on the session has no failover until the pool is picked again.

- Seen in a browser on 2026-11-22: after the click, the composer read "Current model: mock/okay", and the next pick had to start from `okay`.
- Cause: `retryMessage` (`packages/ui/src/sync/session-ui-store.ts`) resends the prompt through `sendMessage` with the chosen model, and a send makes that model the session's model.
- Choices: keep it, or retry with the member once and keep the session on the pool. The pool-member pin (#2482, OpenCode #2672, both merged) already keeps a session on the pool with one member preferred, so the button could reuse it. That needs an installed OpenCode with #2672.
- My recommendation is the second. It is a product decision, so it is not built. #2126 is where the original ask lives ("configurable whether it force-stops or applies on the next message").

Since OpenCode #2679, OpenCode moves to the next member on its own after a failure that follows output. So the button now mostly matters with an older OpenCode, or when the user declined or interrupted a tool call.

## 2. Surfaces not verified

- The desktop app: the pool list and pool page. The server code is shared with web, but no one has opened them there.
- Touch drag to reorder pools and members, on hosted mobile and in the Capacitor app (390px touch viewport).
- Already verified in a browser: Arabic right-to-left layout of the pool list and pool page. The chevron and back arrow are mirrored, and mouse and keyboard reorder both save. VS Code has no Routing page, and its model-settings store reads OpenCode's 404 as "unavailable" (checked against OpenCode 2.0.30).

## 3. Pool order cannot be kept for pool IDs that look like integers

JavaScript lists integer-like object keys (`"1"`, `"42"`) first, in numeric order. A pool with such an ID therefore always sorts first, whatever order is saved, and the config writer cannot change that. Options: warn when a pool ID is integer-like, or add an explicit order key in OpenCode.

## 4. Re-check on the installed OpenCode after the pin bump

The installed OpenCode is 2.0.30, which has none of #2674, #2676 or #2679. After the bump, check that:

- the last model is kept past the first-output wait (#2676);
- "Each pool its own" works (#2674);
- OpenCode's own `defaultVariant`, `lockVariant` and `hidden` take effect (#2674);
- a failure after output continues on the next member (#2679).

## 5. Seen while testing, not caused by the pool work (for triage)

- On OpenCode 2.0.30 every send logs `[current-model] reading the pinned pool member failed: OpencodeApiError: session.routeTarget.list failed (404)`. The pool-member pin (#2482) calls an endpoint 2.0.30 does not have. It degrades to a warning.
- React warns "Cannot update a component while rendering a different component" from `VisibleSessionProjects`, `SyncAppEffects` and `WorkStatusPinnedSection`.

openchamber.title: Paired clients have no route scopes and no programmatic client kind (babysitter enrollment gap, code#1271)
openchamber.body:
## Gap — paired clients have no route scopes and no programmatic client kind

Found during the babysitter enrollment for developing-today/code#1271
(fleet queue task 16620, 2026-11-14): enrolling a paired OpenChamber
client named `babysitter-sandbox` for a sandbox babysitter process
(sandbox -> laptop :3000). The enrollment and all five babysitter
routes verified live, but two parts of the requested design are not
expressible in the current client-auth model:

1. **No route scopes.** `lib/client-auth/remote-clients.js` issues an
   unscoped bearer token (`oc_client_...`); a paired client can call
   every route its token authenticates, not a named subset. The
   babysitter design (code#1271) asked for a client scoped to five
   routes: session reads, session-activity, quota reads, message
   injection, plan/todo binding reads. There is no field on the client
   record, the pairing session, or the redeem call to declare or
   enforce that subset.
2. **No programmatic client kind.** Pairing restricts kinds to
   `mobile | desktop` (`VALID_CLIENT_KINDS` in
   `lib/client-auth/pairing.js`; redeem normalizes anything else to
   `mobile`). A headless babysitter had to enroll as kind `desktop`
   to be represented truthfully-ish in the device list.

Related observation from the same verification: the client-management
route's own-record scoping works as designed (with the babysitter
token, `GET /api/client-auth/clients` returned only its own record),
but requests arriving over the sandbox's trusted tunnel transport are
also session-trusted without a token, so on that transport the token
is not the operative credential. Worth a deliberate decision when
scopes are designed: scope enforcement should bind to the token, not
to the transport's trust.

Ask: add an optional `scopes` set on paired clients (route families,
enforced where client auth is resolved), and a `programmatic` (or
`service`) client kind allowed in pairing. Until then, paired-client
enrollments for automation are necessarily unscoped — documented in
the #1188 inventory (fleet goal workspace,
`openchamber-api-inventory-2026-10-26.md`, babysitter section
2026-11-14) and on code#1271.

could not create workflow dispatch event: HTTP 422: Actions has been disabled for this repository.

Meanwhile the workflows list and the permissions API still look healthy — `gh workflow list --all` reports every scheduled workflow `active`, and `gh api repos/developing-today-forks/openchamber/actions/permissions` returns `enabled:true` — so the blackout is silent to anyone reading only the workflow list. **Trust the dispatch error, not the API.** This is the same signature as #54 (closed 2026-10-18), which covered the 2026-10-14 → 2026-10-18 blackout and was resolved by re-enabling Actions. This is the second occurrence.

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-13)

- **Last run of any kind:** 2026-11-11T23:44:36Z, run `43122132629` (`pull_request_review_comment`, `pr-review`, skipped). Last scheduled run: `branch-cleanup` `43103379549`, success, 2026-11-11T21:28:41Z. Nothing after that — not even the usual `skipped` runs.
- **Main kept moving with zero checks.** `main` advanced past the last run (merge `072ba8c8e` 2026-11-12, `7b808f60e` 2026-11-13; repo `pushed_at` 2026-11-13T11:57:10Z), yet the head commit has no checks at all:
  - `gh api repos/.../commits/7b808f60e.../check-runs` → `total_count: 0`
  - `gh api repos/.../commits/7b808f60e.../status` → `state: pending`, 0 statuses
- **Eligible events produced no runs.** dezren39 issue comments on 2026-11-13 (11:29Z on #2272, 12:25Z on #224) would normally create `issue_comment` runs (even if `skipped`); none appeared. So the events are not being processed at all, not merely skipped.
- **Not a trigger edit.** `git log --since=2026-11-09 -- .github/workflows` is empty on `main`; the workflow files (with their `schedule:`, `issue_comment:` etc. triggers) are unchanged.
- **This repo only.** The sibling fleet repos all ran scheduled workflows on 2026-11-12/13: `developing-today/code` (e.g. `flake-inputs-update` 15:30Z, `id e2e nightly` 15:28Z), `developing-today-forks/opencode` (`repo-sweeper` 15:24Z), `dezren39/darwin-nix` (`flake checks build` 15:27Z).
- Note the repo is a **fork** (`dezren39/openchamber` ← `openchamber/openchamber`); #54's resolution and #1606 (repo move to `developing-today-forks`) are the relevant recent history.

## Impact

Every repo workflow is dark, not just one: `pr checks` (the nightly main-tier test gate), `main-broken watcher`, `repo sweeper`, `stale`, `agents` (bolt/palette/suggestions), `opencode-update`, `Jules Daily Upstream Sync`, and the `issue_comment`/`pull_request_review_comment` handlers (`bot-help`, `bot-summarize`, `oc integration`, `pr-review`, `opencode`). Recent merges landed with **zero verification** — e.g. #2270, #2272 and every queue PR since Nov 11 — and the loss is invisible in the PR UI because checks simply never appear.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A maintainer re-enables Actions for `developing-today-forks/openchamber` (Settings → Actions → General), or identifies the org/policy/repo-level condition disabling it (re-check after the org move to `developing-today-forks`).
- [ ] `gh workflow run workflow-audit.yml --repo developing-today-forks/openchamber --ref main` creates a run instead of returning `HTTP 422`.
- [ ] The next scheduled slots fire again: `agents` at 02:00/14:00 UTC, plus `repo sweeper`, `branch cleanup`, `stale`, `opencode-update`, `Jules Daily Upstream Sync`.
- [ ] **Add a durable tripwire so a silent blackout cannot again wait to be noticed by hand.** Because the API lies (workflows `active`, permissions `enabled:true`), the check must assert on observable run history or a dispatch — e.g. a heartbeat from a surface whose Actions still run (the fleet's main-CI watch lane or an external probe) that files an issue when this repo has had no completed run for more than a few hours.

## Cross-references

- #54 — previous identical blackout (2026-10-14 → 2026-10-18); closed after Actions was re-enabled. This is the recurrence.
- #51 — closed; the Jules daily sync that never ran during the #54 blackout.
- #1606 — closed; the org move to `developing-today-forks` left repository guards behind.

Repo: developing-today-forks/openchamber
Finding: Actions disabled since 2026-11-11T23:44:36Z; confirmed with `gh workflow run` 422 despite workflows reporting active and /actions/permissions enabled:true. Recurrence of closed #54. Selected this repo by rotation (its last creator filing was #2269 at 06:10Z, the oldest of the four).

-->

openchamber.title: Update the embedded OpenCode to a v2-based build (fleet OpenCode 2 migration)
openchamber.body:
Part of the fleet-wide OpenCode 2 migration tracked at https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/issues/374 (origin issue for the whole set).

OpenChamber embeds OpenCode, and the current release (v2.3.3) embeds a v1-based build. For the fleet to be exclusively on OpenCode 2, the embed has to move to a v2-based OpenCode. Upstream migration guide: https://dev.opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1/

## Scope / first steps

1. **Pin down how the embed is wired today** — where the OpenCode version/build is pinned in this repo, and whether the embed tracks our fork (developing-today/opencode) or upstream. This decides whether this issue waits on the fork rebase (item (a) in the origin issue) or can move independently.
2. **Server API contract change** — v2's server API and clients have new contracts (`/api/*`). Audit OpenChamber's calls into the embedded server against the v2 contracts and list what breaks.
3. **Plugin surface** — v1 plugins do not run in v2. Check how OpenChamber exposes/loads plugins and what that means for user-facing plugin support on a v2 embed.
4. Only after 1–3: the actual embed bump plus smoke tests (session create, message round-trip, plugin load) against the v2-based build.

Status: tracking entry only — not started. First step is (1).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The embed wiring is pinned down in a comment on this issue: where the OpenCode version/build is pinned, and whether the embed tracks the developing-today/opencode fork or upstream.
- [x] An audit list exists of OpenChamber's calls into the embedded server, marking each against the v2 `/api/*` contracts as works / breaks / removed.
- [x] The plugin surface on a v2 embed is documented: how plugins load, and what v1 plugins do (run, fail loudly, or are refused).
- [x] The embed is bumped to a v2-based build and smoke tests pass: session create, message round-trip, plugin load.

openchamber.title: Goal writer card says "The message was not sent." above reasons that say it may have been sent
openchamber.body:
Found while fixing a Codex thread on #216.

When a send of a goal writer job ends without a report, the server releases the job with a reason that says the message may have gone out:

- `RESTART_REASON` in `packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/spec-jobs.js`: "the server restarted while the message was being sent; check the session before sending it again"
- `CLAIM_EXPIRED_REASON` in the same file (new in #216): "the window sending the message did not report back, so it may have been sent; check the session before sending it again"

`GoalSpecJobCard.tsx` shows every send failure under the heading `chat.goal.writer.card.sendFailed`, "The message was not sent.", so the card states both that the message was not sent and that it may have been. A user who reads only the heading can send it a second time.

Fix shape: the job says when the outcome is unknown (an optional field such as `sendUncertain`, set by those two releases and kept in the jobs file), and the card shows a heading such as "The message may have been sent." for it, in all 15 locales. A job without the field keeps today's heading, so older files and servers read as before.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Sends released for the restart or expired-claim reasons show a heading such as "The message may have been sent." (in all 15 locales), not "The message was not sent."
- [ ] The job record carries the uncertainty explicitly (e.g. a `sendUncertain` field set by those two release paths and preserved in the jobs file); jobs without the field keep the existing heading.
- [ ] Older jobs files and servers without the field read exactly as before.
- [ ] Tests cover both uncertain release reasons and the certain-failure case.

openchamber.title: Back to edit on a new chat can replace the session the user moved to with a new draft
openchamber.body:
Raised in review of #216 ([comment](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/216#discussion_r4338000764)).

> **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recheck the selected session before opening the replacement draft**
> 
> When the user navigates to another session while `deleteSession` is awaiting the server or chat-directory cleanup, the earlier `emptyOnScreen` check is no longer authoritative, but this call still opens a new-session draft unconditionally. Because deletion only clears the current session when it still matches the deleted ID, the newly selected session remains valid and is then unexpectedly replaced by this draft; recheck the runtime and current session after deletion before navigating.
> 
> Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
> 
> <!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

From Codex's review of #216 (https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/216#discussion_r4338000764, `packages/ui/src/components/chat/goalSpecJobEdit.ts`, `replaceEmptySessionWithDraft`).

Back to edit on a new chat's goal writer job removes the empty session and opens a new-session draft for the message. The window is checked before the removal, but if the user switches to another session while `deleteSession` is in flight, `openNewSessionDraft` still runs afterwards and replaces the session they moved to with the draft.

Why it was not fixed in #216: the message needs a home either way. Opening the draft takes over the user's screen, and skipping it leaves the composer edit aimed at a session that was just removed, so the message would sit in `pendingComposerEdits` with no composer to take it. A fix needs a way to hand the message to a new-session draft without showing it, or a decision that the draft should open anyway with a notice.

What done looks like: after the removal, a user who is still on the removed session gets the draft as today; a user who moved elsewhere stays where they are, and the message is still recoverable from a draft or composer they can find.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After the removal, a user who is still on the removed session gets the draft as today; a user who moved elsewhere stays where they are, and the message is still recoverable from a draft or composer they can find.
- [ ] If the successor goal-edit flow has no delete-then-open-draft sequence, this is met by absence and the issue can be closed as obsolete with that noted.

openchamber.title: Learn from manual model and effort choices: notes for the classifier and Settings suggestions
openchamber.body:
## What I want

When I pick a model or an effort level by hand (the goal writer, the composer, a pool), OpenChamber should remember that choice and what it was for. Over time those notes should feed the classifier that picks models in Auto mode, and Settings should be able to suggest changes from them.

My words: "automatically track which models are chosen when over time and create notes that can be fed to classifier and used for settings recs. maybe allow settings changes propose and then approve/decline when in single mode in settings ui? over time then a small model would get better because can provide feedback and auto model picker for auto mode would understand user intent a bit better."

## What exists today

- The goal writer can now take a model and effort picked in the goal window (PR for the goal editor rework, branch `feat/goal-editor-rework`). A pick applies to that goal only, unless the user presses Remember or turns on `sessionGoalWriterRememberChoice`.
- `recentModels` and `recentEfforts` in settings record what was picked, but not why or for what.
- `plan_info` notes record what the user says about plans; nothing records choices made in the UI.

## Proposal

1. Record each manual model or effort choice as an event: where it was made (goal writer, composer, pool, Settings), the default it replaced, the session's model, and the length of the input it was for.
2. Summarize the events into short notes, such as "picks low effort on Opus for goal specs", and keep them where the classifier prompt and Settings can read them.
3. In Settings, while a single model is in use, show a proposed change built from the notes, with Approve and Decline. A decline is recorded too.
4. Give those notes to Jev and the small model when they choose a model in Auto mode.

## Open questions

- Where the events are stored and how long they are kept.
- Whether recording is on by default. Recording choices is a privacy question even when it stays local.
- How a proposal is shown without becoming a nag.

Related: route pool descriptions for classification (separate issue).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Manual model/effort choices are recorded as events with surface (goal writer, composer, pool, Settings), the default replaced, the session model, and input length.
- [ ] Events are summarized into short notes readable by the Auto-mode classifier prompt and by Settings.
- [ ] Settings (single-model mode) can propose a change built from the notes with Approve/Decline, and declines are recorded too.
- [ ] The body's open questions (retention/privacy of choice history, note format) are answered or explicitly deferred with a named owner.

openchamber.title: Upgrade without dropped sessions: supervisor that owns the listener and the managed OpenCode children
openchamber.body:
This comes from the first item in `TODO.md`. It is a proposal that needs the maintainer's decision before code, per `CLAUDE.md`.

## Problem

Upgrading or restarting OpenChamber can drop OpenCode sessions or change the port. Today this works through detached OpenCode adoption (`state.json`) and optional socket activation (`LISTEN_FDS`). Socket activation still needs a systemd `.socket` unit and `KillMode=process`.

## Idea

A small supervisor process owns the managed OpenCode children and the listening socket. OpenChamber then restarts without dropping sessions or moving ports.

## Open questions (from `TODO.md`)

- Who owns the socket across an OpenChamber version change?
- How does the new process prove it speaks the same OpenCode protocol before taking over?
- How does a failed handoff roll back?

The OpenCode fork already implements the server side of a handover (`developing-today/opencode`, `TODO.md`, listener inheritance, drain and `READY=1`). Whatever is built here should use that contract, and the systemd check in the opencode issue for the real-systemd test applies to it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The maintainer approves a design.
- [ ] A handoff test shows an upgrade with no refused request, and a failed handoff restores the predecessor.

openchamber.title: Handoff: release and live-validate the openchamber fork's work since v2.2.0 as an orchestrator using subagents
openchamber.body:
> **Picking this up with no context?** Everything you need is linked here. Read "Your role" first, then "Current state" and "Read first".

## Goal

A release of this fork newer than `v2.2.0` is published on [developing-today/openchamber releases](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/releases). The user's Mac runs a build of the fork's `main`. Everything merged since 2026-10-14 has been used once in that running app, and the results are written on this issue: the new agent control actions, worktree-by-default, the Auto-create worktree switch, the new sidebar layout ([#20](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/20)), and worktree start points and branch templates ([#23](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/23)). Every defect found is either fixed in a merged PR or filed as its own issue.

This repository has no design or feature packages. **This issue is the tracker.** The sources are the PRs and commits listed under "Read first".

## Current state (verified 2026-10-16T20:11:12Z)

**What was released and what is installed**

- **Latest fork release:** `v2.2.0`, published 2026-10-14T00:58:46Z (`gh release list -R developing-today/openchamber`). It was cut by a manual `workflow_dispatch` of `release.yml` (run [38492608995](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/actions/runs/38492608995)) at commit `1aff2691c`. Its assets are Linux AppImages and Android only: `OpenChamber-2.2.0-linux-{x86_64,arm64}.AppImage`, `latest-linux*.yml`, and the Android `.apk` and `.aab`. **The macOS and Windows builds were skipped.** PR [#7](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/7) made them opt-in.
- **No fork release has ever had a macOS build.** The fork has no Apple signing secrets: `gh secret list` shows only the four `ANDROID_*` secrets. The macOS jobs in `release.yml` and in `build-macos-arm64-dmg.yml` both need `APPLE_CERTIFICATE`, `APPLE_ID`, `APPLE_PASSWORD` and `APPLE_TEAM_ID`, and electron-builder's config has `"notarize": true` (`packages/electron/package.json` → `build.mac`).
- **The installed app is upstream's, not the fork's.** `/Applications/OpenChamber.app` reports `CFBundleShortVersionString` 2.1.0 and TeamIdentifier `5J7WJGPA2Q`, and its `Contents/Resources/app-update.yml` says `owner: openchamber, repo: openchamber`. That is the upstream signed build, and its updater follows upstream, not this fork. **So "install the fork release" on this Mac means replacing upstream's app with a locally built, unsigned fork build.** The earlier notes said only "installed app is 2.1.0". They did not say that build is upstream's.
- **The agent tool this session can call is the old one.** It exposes 14 actions (`projects.list` … `file.open`), while `origin/main` defines more than 50.

**What is merged on `main` (`9a7ca5901`) but has never run live** (296 commits after `v2.2.0`; `git log --oneline v2.2.0..origin/main | wc -l`, which includes an upstream merge, `8f9956331`)

1. **Agent control actions.** Commits `865d470be` (2026-10-15T04:18Z, `projects.add`/`projects.remove`) and `a16d8e79d` (2026-10-15T05:11Z, 62 files, +4954). They live in `packages/web/server/lib/openchamber-control/`:
   - `actions.js`: `projects.add`, `projects.remove`, `schedule.get`, `schedule.update`.
   - `session-actions.js`: `session.rename`, `session.model` (model and effort), `session.agent`, `session.goal`, `session.retry`, `session.pin`, `session.abort`.
   - `provider-actions.js`: `providers.list`, `providers.toggle`, `models.available`, `models.toggle`, `models.default`, `models.cost`, `provider.models.add`, `provider.models.remove`.
   - `config-actions.js`: `settings.get`, `settings.keys`, `settings.set`, `opencode.config.get`, `opencode.config.set`, `opencode.reload`, `openchamber.restart`.
   - `integration-actions.js`: `mcp.list`, `mcp.toggle`, `skills.list`, `skills.toggle`, `tools.list`, `tools.toggle`, `integration.use`.

   The session that wrote them said: "None of it has been tried in a running app or against a live OpenCode yet." Their unit tests passed (348 across the affected suites). The module doc is [`openchamber-control/DOCUMENTATION.md`](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/blob/main/packages/web/server/lib/openchamber-control/DOCUMENTATION.md).
2. **Worktree-by-default for agents and the Auto-create worktree switch** (also `a16d8e79d`):
   - `session.create` makes a worktree unless the caller passes a `worktree` name or `newWorktree: false`.
   - With no name, a model names the worktree from the prompt, with a 20 s limit, and falls back to a random name. The model is `worktreeNameModel` if given, else the session's model, else the default model, else OpenCode's small model.
   - The new-session page has an "Auto-create worktree" switch (setting `autoCreateWorktree`, also under Settings → Sessions). In the UI, naming has a 15 s limit.
   - A name starting with `/` is used as an exact path. This also changed the existing New worktree dialog.
   - **The switch's default value is not established:** the registry field at `packages/ui/src/lib/settings/registry.ts:470` declares no default.
3. **Sidebar layout, PR [#20](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/20)** (squash `278eb1518`, merged 2026-10-16T15:20:31Z):
   - attention sections (Approvals, Questions, Errors, Stopped);
   - movable sections;
   - a held open session;
   - a merged "All sessions" list;
   - Classic layout one menu click away.

   Its "Not verified" line reads: "Approvals, Questions and Errors with real requests (unit tests only), light theme, Arabic and Hebrew layout, Electron, and performance measurement." **It merged with no completed review.** It has zero review records (`gh pr view 20 --json reviews` → `[]`), and CodeRabbit's only comment is the in-progress summary. The merging session said "CodeRabbit's review of #20 was still running when I merged."
4. **Worktree start points and branch templates, PR [#23](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/23)** (squash `b76693e98`, merged 2026-10-16T19:19:43Z):
   - new worktrees start from the default remote's default branch (for example `origin/main`), with an override for each place that creates worktrees;
   - a worktree can branch off a pull request instead of checking it out;
   - branch-name templates (`{name}`, `{name}-from-pr-{pr}`).

   It had Copilot and CodeRabbit rounds, and all threads were resolved. Its "Not verified" line reads: "a real GitHub or GitLab PR end to end, including branching off in a fork checkout; Electron; VS Code; phones; light theme; Arabic and Hebrew layout." The merging session listed three checks to run after merge, and they are carried into "Where to start".
5. **Also merged in the window:** [#17](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/17), which restores a brace in the control `service.js`; without it the server does not start. [#24](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/24) fixes `check:changed` lint, dead-code and type errors (squash `9a7ca5901`). A daily upstream-sync workflow (`jules-daily-upstream-sync.yml`, commit `bdecf4906`) is also in.

**Changes users will notice on upgrade.** These come from the PR bodies and session final texts:

- new worktrees start from `origin/main`, not from the project root's branch;
- agents create worktrees by default;
- agents' unnamed branches lose the `openchamber/` prefix (set the template to `openchamber/{name}` to keep it);
- the new sidebar layout is on by default.

The upstream merge also changed things. One example: the sidebar question badge no longer shows a count (upstream commit `cfef4b938`). The user asked about that, and in session `ses_ebabbdd86` they chose to keep upstream's behavior.

**CI on this fork has gone quiet. Investigate this before relying on it.**

- Since 2026-10-14T20:00Z, the only Actions runs in the repo are four Copilot review runs, all with an empty conclusion: `gh api "repos/developing-today/openchamber/actions/runs?created=>2026-10-14T20:00:00Z"` → `{"dynamic":4}`.

**State of the repository**

- `main` is not protected (`branches/main/protection` → 404; `rules/branches/main` → `[]`).
- Open PRs: none.
- Open issues: [#2](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/issues/2), [#14](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/issues/14), [#15](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/issues/15), [#16](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/issues/16), [#18](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/issues/18), [#19](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/issues/19), [#21](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/issues/21), [#22](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/issues/22). They are feature requests and none of them covers release or validation.

## Your role: orchestrator, not implementer

The user's instruction: "it's orchestrating/planning/managing and it should use subagents to implement/review/validate and only handle itself when it can't use a subagent somehow. it should make parallel subagents for any portions that can be broken apart."

You plan, dispatch, track and decide. **Subagents do the work:**

- **Design.** Subagents verify a design's claims against the code, research alternatives and draft revisions. The user approves designs; you don't.
- **Implement.** One subagent owns each phase and its PR. When a phase has independent parts, each part gets its own subagent in parallel, and one of them assembles the PR.
- **Review.** Before anything merges, a separate subagent with fresh context reviews every PR against the phase's steps and success criteria, its specs in `TESTING.md`, and the design sections it cites. An implementer never reviews its own work.
- **Validate.** Subagents run the targeted tests, read CI, do the manual validations (browser checks, checks on the development environment) and record the evidence in the feature package.
- **Copilot rounds.** Subagents check each Copilot finding against the code (the `review-pr-comments` skill), then fix it or explain why it's wrong. You decide what gets pushed and replied.
- **Research.** Read-only `explore` subagents answer "how does X work" questions.

**Run subagents in parallel whenever work can be split:** independent phases, independent parts of one phase, reviews and validations of different PRs, separate Copilot threads. Partition by file before any writer starts: two writers on one file clobber each other.

Do work yourself only when a subagent can't: talking to the user, making decisions, merging, or using a tool subagents lack. In OpenCode, `general` handles one task that needs judgment, `general-deep` follows one long thread, `general-wide` and `general-2wide` handle batches, and `explore*` does read-only research. Subagents may not be able to spawn subagents of their own, so every brief must be doable alone.

**Every subagent starts with no context.** Each prompt must include:

- the repository path, plus the branch and worktree to use;
- the phase's full text: its steps, success criteria and test specs;
- the design sections it cites;
- the rules below that apply;
- exactly what to return: the PR URL, the commands it ran with their real output, evidence, open questions, and changes needed in files it doesn't own.

Re-verify what a subagent reports before relaying or building on it — check `git status`, `git log origin/main..HEAD` and the pushed branch, because a final message is not proof the work landed — and carry its hedges forward. Before the first dispatch, read the repo's root [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/blob/main/AGENTS.md) and the skills in [`.agents/skills/`](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/tree/main/.agents/skills) that the work touches: `openchamber-change-discipline` for any source change, `pr-review` for the post-merge review of #20, `rtl-layout` for the Arabic and Hebrew checks, `desktop-shell` for Electron, and `update-changelog` for release notes. **This repo's `AGENTS.md` says "Do not run git or GitHub commands unless the user explicitly asks".** This issue is that ask for the commands listed here. Put it in every brief.

**Give each branch its own git worktree, cut from `origin/main`,** so parallel subagents never share a working tree. This repo keeps its worktrees under `~/git/openchamber/.worktrees/`:

```sh
git -C ~/git/openchamber fetch origin
git -C ~/git/openchamber worktree add -b <branch> .worktrees/<name> origin/main
cd ~/git/openchamber/.worktrees/<name> && bun install --frozen-lockfile
```

Remove the worktree after its PR merges. The existing worktrees `fix-control-service-brace`, `sidebar-attention-groups` and `worktree-source-branch` belong to merged PRs. Ask the user before removing them.

**What can run in parallel here:**

- The release cut is serial and needs the user's go-ahead.
- These need no release and can start at once: the fresh review of #20, the CI investigation, and the three groups of live checks against an isolated dev server (see "Where to start").
- The checks inside the installed desktop app (Electron-only behavior) wait for the install.
- All fixes go through **one writer** per area, each in its own worktree.

## Read first, in this order

1. [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/blob/main/AGENTS.md). Its rules bind every agent: no git or GitHub without an explicit ask, `bun run check:changed` before every source commit, `changelog/` is read-only except through `update-changelog`, and report exactly what was and was not validated.

PR #23's author declined to run a second server on the real settings folder because "it writes to it on startup".

## Where to start

**Stream 0, do this first (you, with read-only subagents): the CI silence and the release plan.**

**Stream 1, the release cut (serial, only after the go-ahead).** This follows how `v2.2.0` was cut:

3. **Replacing upstream's installed app with an unsigned local fork build.** It loses upstream's auto-update, shares the same settings folders and bundle ID (`dev.openchamber.desktop`), and needs a manual rebuild for each later fork release. ## Traps and risks

- **The installed app is upstream's** (see "Current state"). Validating there validates upstream 2.1.0, not this fork. Upstream's updater may also replace it with upstream 2.3.x at any time.
- **CI has not run since 2026-10-14T20:00Z.** #17, #20, #23 and #24 merged without the `pr checks` workflow running. Treat their "tests passed" claims as local runs reported by agents, and re-run `bun run test` / `bun run check:changed` on `9a7ca5901` before cutting.

- **Tag name clash in the local clone.** `~/git/openchamber` has an `upstream` remote and already holds upstream's `v2.3.3` tag. If the fork creates its own `v2.3.3` at a different commit, `git fetch origin --tags` will refuse to overwrite it, and local tags will point at the wrong tree. Compare with `git ls-remote --tags origin`.
- **Real settings get written.** The OpenChamber server writes to its data folder on startup, which is the reason #23's author did not test the real-PR path. Isolate HOME and `OPENCHAMBER_DATA_DIR` for every live check that is not in the installed app. Do not point a dev server at `~/.config/openchamber`.

- **The macOS build is unsigned.** Gatekeeper and quarantine will interfere, auto-update on macOS will not work, and `notarize: true` may fail a local build that has no Apple credentials (unverified).

## Repository mechanics

- **Checkout:** `~/git/openchamber`, remote `origin` = `developing-today/openchamber`, remote `upstream` = `openchamber/openchamber`. On GitHub, the fork's parent is `dezren39/openchamber`. The main checkout is on `main`; never switch branches or commit there, and work only in worktrees you created under `.worktrees/`. `gh` is signed in as the user, who has admin on the repo. The machine is a shared macOS host (zsh), so a slow or timed-out command may be contention: re-run it before believing it.
- **Binding rules:** [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/blob/main/AGENTS.md) and the skills in `.agents/skills/`, starting with `openchamber-change-discipline` for any source change. Read the nearest `DOCUMENTATION.md` under `packages/**` for each module you change. `CONTRIBUTING.md` treats any changed default, new setting or new control as a product decision for the user.
- **Install, build, test:** `bun install --frozen-lockfile`. Tests run with `bun run test`, the whole repo, or per package, for example `node ../../scripts/run-isolated-tests.mjs <dirs>` in `packages/ui` or `bun test <file>` in `packages/web`. Builds: `bun run build`, or `bun run build:web` for the web build. **Before every source commit, `bun run check:changed` must pass.** It covers type-check, lint, Knip dead code and the anti-slop ratchet, and it compares against `origin/main`. Live runs: `bun run dev` (web with hot reload), `bun run electron:dev`, and `bun run profile:serve` (isolated server with a fixture provider).
- **CI:** the `pr checks` workflow (`.github/workflows/oc-review.yml`) runs type-check, lint plus changelog check, tests, and the web build on GitHub-hosted runners for `pull_request`. **It has not run since 2026-10-14; see "Traps".** Nothing is a required check. CodeRabbit and the Copilot reviewer also review PRs.
- **Merging:** `main` has no branch protection and no rulesets. The fork's PRs have been squash-merged (`gh pr merge <n> --squash`). Merge only with CI green on the head commit, or, while CI is down, with the local `check:changed` and test output recorded on the PR, and with no open correctness or data-loss thread.
- **Releases:** see Stream 1 above. These are manual `workflow_dispatch` runs of `release.yml`. Only `finalize-release` publishes, so a failed run leaves a draft. Pushing a `v*` tag also starts the workflow. `publish-npm` runs only in upstream.
- **Copilot** reviews every push. Reply "Fixed in <sha>" only after confirming the pushed commit contains the change. Out-of-scope findings: open an issue, link it in the reply, resolve the thread.
- **Git history:** never force-push and never rewrite shared history. To update a branch, merge `main` into it.
- **Datetimes:** RFC 3339 UTC everywhere (`2026-10-16T19:30:00Z`).

openchamber.title: Sidebar view mode without headers that keeps the section order
openchamber.body:
A view mode that keeps the sidebar's order but draws no headers at all: no section headers (Approvals, In work, Chats, All sessions, and the rest), no project headers, no worktree headers. The sessions come one after another in exactly the order the current layout gives them (#20): the attention sections first in their configured order, then Pinned, In work, the other sections, then Chats and the projects, each in its own order.

Why: once the order itself says what needs me (attention first, then what I work on, then everything else), the headers cost a row each and the list could be read top to bottom like an inbox.

Things to settle before building:

- **Where the boundaries go.** With no headers, nothing shows where Questions ends and In work starts. Options: nothing at all, a thin divider, or a per-row mark (the section's icon in the row's slot).
- **Duplicates.** A session in a zone is also listed under its project today. Without headers the same row would show twice; the headerless mode probably lists every session once, at its first place.
- **What collapse and Show more mean.** Both hang off headers today. Probably: no collapsing, and one reveal limit for the whole list or per section.
- **Where the project shows.** Rows under a project header leave the project out; without the header every row needs its project's icon (the zone rows' `'timeline-mixed'` / `'mixed-flat'` forms already do this).
- **Tree vs List.** Whether this is a third view next to Tree and List, or a toggle that applies to both.
- **Phone.** Whether the phone sheet gets it with #18.

Code pointers: the row model draws sections in `sectionOrder` (`components/session/sidebar/sessionSidebarRowModel.ts`), and sticky headers, drag and the Done/Archive navigation all key off the header rows, so each needs a defined behavior without them.

## Acceptance criteria

- A view mode exists that renders sessions in exactly the current layout's order with no section, project, or worktree headers drawn.
- Each session appears once, at its first position in the order (no zone/project duplicates).
- Collapse and "Show more" have defined behavior in this mode (or are explicitly absent), and every row shows its project's icon since no header carries it.
- Sticky headers, drag, and Done/Archive navigation — which key off header rows today — have defined behavior without headers.
- Whether the mode is a third view or a toggle over Tree/List, and whether the phone sheet gets it, is decided and recorded on the issue.

fleet.title: fleet-command executor: ring/aws-lc-sys build-script binary fails to execute (os error 2) — native build-script dependency trees unbuildable
fleet.body:
## Defect

fleet-command runs on the baked executor image cannot build dependency trees containing `ring` (and by the same shape, `aws-lc-sys`): the `ring` build-script binary fails to execute.

## Evidence — two runs, identical failure, before any test ran

- https://github.com/developing-today/fleet/actions/runs/45249821636
- https://github.com/developing-today/fleet/actions/runs/45255497015

Both runs attempted the same command (developing-today/code, branch `felix/787-kitty-slice-e-f`, from `pkgs/id`):

```
cargo test -p id-worlds --lib --features ssh
```

Both failed deterministically with:

```
error: failed to run custom build command for ring v0.17.14
could not execute process …/build-script-build (never executed)
No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

`aws-lc-sys` compiles in the same dependency tree.

## Triggering tree

`id-worlds --features ssh` → `russh` → `ring`. Any crate whose dependency tree includes a native build-script dependency of this class (ring, aws-lc-sys) hits the same wall: the build-script binary is produced but cannot be executed in the executor environment (os error 2 on exec).

## Consequence

Any such crate is unbuildable — and therefore untestable — in the fleet-command executor until this is fixed. This is the same family as the earlier executor-environment defects tracked in developing-today/code#13331 (closed after the image fixes in this repo's PRs #105/#106); the image source of record is `containers/fleet-build/Containerfile` here.

## Workaround in use

For the one gated suite (developing-today/code PR #13267), the evidence run is being executed on the laptop (amd-6) instead, with the venue change and the reason recorded on that PR.

fleet.title: sync-upstream cannot run on new org forks: app-id 5454422 vs fleet-app key, and the app isn't installed there
fleet.body:
## Problem

`sync-upstream.yml` cannot run on the ~100 new org fleet forks created 2026-11-06 (org saturation program, developing-today/code#6645), for two stacked reasons found by live proof (dezren39-dev/fleet run 42328445423, job "pull upstream main", 401 "A JSON web token could not be decoded"):

1. **Key/app mismatch.** The workflow hardcodes `app-id: 5454422` (the *developing.today* app) and reads `secrets.FLEET_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`. The org-level `FLEET_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` now set on all admin orgs holds the **fleet app's (5612056)** key (BWS `github-app.developing-today-fleet.private-key`) — a JWT for app 5454422 signed with 5612056's key is rejected. BWS holds **no** private key for app 5454422 (only the backup app 5562183 and fleet app 5612056 keys); the working repo-level secret on developing-today/fleet + dezren39/fleet was set 2026-11-04 from a source not in BWS.
2. **App not installed.** Even with the right key, the sync mints a token for app 5454422, which is installed only on developing-today / -forks / -vendored / -fork. On the other ~99 orgs neither 5454422 nor 5612056 is installed, so app-token sync cannot authenticate there at all. (Installs are browser/sudo-gated; tracked on code#6645.)

## Options

- **A. Re-point sync to the fleet app (5612056)** — change `app-id` to 5612056 so it matches the org-level key already everywhere; still needs the fleet app installed per org (same browser trip as Blacksmith/CodeRabbit).
- **B. Re-point sync to the GHCR_ORG_PAT** (classic PAT, repo+workflow scope — the `workflow` scope exists precisely to allow pushing workflow files). Works on every org today with zero installs; loses the app-identity/ruleset-bypass properties the current design comments describe.
- **C. Vault the 5454422 key in BWS** and install app 5454422 on all orgs — most faithful to the current design, most browser work.

Until one lands, new org forks are current only as of their fork time (all contain the post-PR#86 fleet-run; forks created before the #86 merge carry the pre-#86 file and also cannot sync). Proof that the forks otherwise run fleet jobs: dezren39-dev/fleet runs 42328489467 + 42330094546, sleep-atomic/fleet run 42328728480 (all success, GitHub leg).

Context: org saturation run 2026-11-06 (code#6645 comment has the full matrix).
